P0003.t: Influence of abutment disconnection on peri‐implant marginal bone loss: A randomized clinical trial
P0003.kf: RCT of 24 participants with single implants: definitive abutment at surgery vs healing abutments disconnected/reconnected three times. At 2 years cumulative bone loss was −0.61 ± 0.10 mm vs −0.81 ± 0.15 mm, with no statistical difference between groups.

P0004.t: Influence of Transmucosal Area Morphology on Peri-implant Bone Loss in Tissue-Level Implants
P0004.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0004.kf: Prospective study of 21 patients each receiving one convergent and one divergent transmucosal tissue-level implant (n = 42): at 24 months after loading, bone loss was 0.29 ± 0.34 mm vs 0.60 ± 0.63 mm (P = .031).

P0005.t: 13-year follow-up of a randomized controlled study on zirconia and titanium abutments
P0005.kf: 13-year follow-up of a trial randomizing 40 posterior implants (22 patients) to customized zirconia or titanium abutments; 15 patients with 21 abutments were examined: abutment and crown survival were 100%, with similar biological and esthetic outcomes.

P0007.t: A Biologically Driven Concept to Design the Emergence Profile Around Dental Implants: Surgical and Prosthetic Considerations to Optimize Hard and Soft Tissue Integration
P0007.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0007.kf: Narrative paper proposing a biologically driven prosthetic concept for designing the implant emergence profile, considering material properties and clinical approach, to optimize soft-tissue integration and protect peri-implant bone.

P0009.t: A multicenter cohort study on the association of the one-abutment one-time concept with marginal bone loss around bone level implants
P0009.kf: Retrospective multicenter cohort of 160 patients/344 bone-level implants (mean follow-up 20 months): one-abutment one-time was not related to presence of MBL but reduced its magnitude by 0.300 mm vs healing abutments (p = .023) where MBL occurred; 98% of implants survived.

P0014.t: Additively and subtractively manufactured implant-supported fixed dental prostheses: A systematic review
P0014.kf: Systematic review of additively vs subtractively manufactured implant-supported FDPs: of 2'184 citations, no clinical study and only six in vitro studies were eligible, with inconclusive results on marginal/internal discrepancies and mechanical properties.

P0024.t: Cemented versus screw-retained posterior implant-supported single crowns: A 24-month randomized controlled clinical trial
P0024.kf: RCT of 41 subjects (56 implants) with cemented vs screw-retained monolithic lithium-disilicate posterior implant crowns: mucositis at 12 months was 17.9% vs 14.2%, bone loss did not differ, and no restoration failed by 24 months.

P0025.t: Cemented versus screw-retained zirconia-based single-implant restorations: 5-year results of a randomized controlled clinical trial
P0025.kf: RCT of 34 single-implant patients with cemented vs screw-retained one-piece zirconia-based restorations: at 5 years (26 re-examined) implant survival was 100%, restoration survival 82.4% and technical complications 15.4% in both groups, with no intergroup bone-level difference.

P0026.t: Clinical Advantages of Immediate Posterior Implants With Custom Healing Abutments: Up to 8-Year Follow-Up of 115 Cases
P0026.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P0026.kf: Retrospective case series of 115 patients with posterior immediate implants and chair-side custom healing abutments: overall survival was 98.26% (3 failures) at up to 8 years (median follow-up 1 year), 100% in the maxilla and 96.08% in the mandible.

P0027.t: Limited marginal bone loss in implant-supported fixed full-arch rehabilitations after 5 years of follow-up
P0027.kf: Retrospective cohort of 160 conical-connection implants in 19 patients with fixed full-arch metal-ceramic restorations: no failures at 5 years and 8.75% with >2 mm MBL; abutment height and implant diameter were associated with MBL (more with 1 mm abutments and narrow implants).

P0028.t: Association of crown emergence angle and profile with dental plaque and inflammation at dental implants
P0028.kf: Cross-sectional study of 122 subjects with single screw-retained implant crowns: platform-level emergence angle, profile and mucosal tunnel depth were significantly associated with plaque (p < .01) and bleeding on probing (p < .02); profiles were convex in 59%.

P0029.t: Effect of CAD/CAM Abutment Morphology on the Outcomes of Implant Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
P0029.kf: RCT of concave vs linear divergent CAD/CAM zirconia abutments in the anterior maxilla (54 of 60 subjects completed): at 1 year implant survival was 100%, with no substantial differences in peri-implant soft-tissue dynamics or health indicators.

P0030.t: Clinical performance of single implant prostheses restored using titanium base abutments: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0030.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis including 23 prospective and retrospective studies (857 single implant prostheses on titanium base abutments): estimated 1-year survival 98.6% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.4%); mean follow-up 31.2 ± 16.9 months.

P0032.t: Comparison of external, internal flat-to-flat, and conical implant abutment connections for implant-supported prostheses: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
P0032.kf: Network meta-analysis of RCTs (2009–May 2020) comparing implant-abutment connections: at 12 months conical connections had less marginal bone loss (P=.011) and fewer prosthetic complications (P=.038) than external hexagonal ones; survival and biologic complications did not differ.

P0039.t: Effect of abutment height on interproximal implant bone level in the early healing: A randomized clinical trial
P0039.kf: RCT of 22 patients (44 platform-switched bone-level implants) with 1 mm vs 3 mm definitive abutments: at 6 months interproximal bone loss was 0.91 ± 0.19 vs 0.11 ± 0.09 mm; only smoking among other variables was related to bone loss.

P0041.t: Effect of different angulations and collar lengths of conical hybrid implant abutment on screw loosening after dynamic cyclic loading
P0041.kf: In vitro study of 90 conical hybrid connection implant-abutment sets (0°, 15°, 25° angulation; 2 or 4 mm collar) after 100,000 eccentric load cycles: removal torque loss increased with angulation to 33.4 ± 3.7% (15°) and 40.1 ± 5.1% (25°); angulation and collar length significantly affected screw loosening.

P0043.t: Effect of internal connection type and screw channel angle on the screw stability of anterior implant-supported zirconia crowns
P0043.kf: In vitro study of 44 implants with Torcfit or Crossfit connection and straight or angled screw channel titanium-base abutments, cyclically loaded (2.4 million cycles, 98 N): Crossfit gave higher removal torque values, but no screw loosening occurred and channel angle did not affect stability after loading.

P0047.t: Definitive Abutment–Driven Stage- Two Surgery as a Means to Reduce Peri-implant Soft Tissue Changes: Introduction of a New Concept
P0047.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0047.kf: Technique report, illustrated with two clinical cases, in which the soft-tissue morphology is registered at implant uncovery and a lab-made customized definitive abutment is inserted at stage-two surgery to guide the peri-implant soft tissue.

P0049.t: Evaluation of resistance against bacterial microleakage of a new conical implant-abutment connection versus conventional connections: an in vitro study
P0049.kf: In vitro test of 80 implants (eight internal connection groups) inoculated with Escherichia coli: controls showed significant contamination by 24 hours (>100.000 CFU/μl), whereas 7 of 10 double-taper conical test implants showed no contamination even after 96 hours (p<0.05).

P0051.t: Five-year randomized controlled clinical study comparing cemented and screw-retained zirconia-based implant-supported single crowns
P0051.kf: RCT of 44 patients with single esthetic-zone implants randomized to screw-retained or cemented all-ceramic crowns: 5-year restorative survival was 81.2%; cemented crowns had higher biological (36.8% vs 0.0%) and overall complication rates (68.4% vs 22.7%).

P0053.t: Histological evaluation of different abutments in the posterior maxilla and mandible: an experimental study in humans
P0053.kf: Parallel-group trial randomizing 30 patients' posterior implants to machined, hydrophilic modMA Ti or modMA TiZr healing abutments; per-protocol histology (18 patients) at 8 weeks showed greater epithelial and connective tissue contact on modMA surfaces.

P0056.t: Immediate provisionalization of bone level implants with a hydrophilic surface. A 5-year follow-up of a randomised controlled clinical trial
P0056.kf: 5-year follow-up of a randomized single-blind trial (16 of 24 patients) of immediately provisionalized (n = 7) vs conventionally restored (n = 9) hydrophilic bone-level single implants in the esthetic area: bone loss at 60 months was -0.42 ± 0.17 mm vs -0.37 ± 0.35 mm.

P0058.t: Impact of Concave/Convergent vs Parallel/ Divergent Implant Transmucosal Profiles on Hard and Soft Peri-implant Tissues: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analyses
P0058.kf: Systematic review (5 studies, 4 meta-analysed) found significantly less marginal bone loss with concave/convergent than divergent/parallel transmucosal profiles (mean difference 0.772; 95% CI: 0.450 to 1.095), significant with platform switching but not platform matching.

P0059.t: Impact of implant-abutment connection design on biological and mechanical outcomes in posterior single-tooth restorations: A randomized clinical trial
P0059.kf: Three-arm RCT of 75 participants (105 posterior implants) with identical implant design but external hexagon, internal hexagon or conical connections: after 1 year of loading, interproximal bone levels were similar across groups (P=.152), with 7 failures (P=.356).

P0062.t: Implant prosthodontic design as a predisposing or precipitating factor for peri‐implant disease: A review
P0062.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0062.kf: Narrative review of prosthodontic design factors and peri-implant disease: malpositioned implants produce emergence profiles that restrict hygiene access, and poor cleansability influenced by restorative contours is reported as a precipitating factor for mucositis and peri-implantitis.

P0065.t: Implant-abutment connections on single crowns: a systematic review

P0066.t: Implant-abutment interface: biomechanical study of flat top versus conical
P0066.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0066.kf: Axisymmetric finite element analysis of an axially loaded mandibular titanium implant: a conical implant-abutment interface decreased peak bone-implant interfacial shear stress and moved it apically compared with a flat-top interface.

P0070.t: In vitro evaluation of the implant abutment connection sealing capability of different implant systems
P0070.kf: In vitro toluidine blue leakage test of Nobel Replace Select, Straumann and Intra-lock implant-abutment connections (five each) over 144 h: all showed increasing leakage over time, with significantly more from Straumann and Nobel Replace Select (P < 0.0001).

P0071.t: Influence of abutment macro- and micro-geometry on morphologic and morphometric features of peri-implant connective tissue
P0071.kf: Human study of 30 posterior single implants with divergent machined, convergent machined or convergent ultrathin-threaded healing abutments: at 3 months convergent abutments showed significantly greater connective tissue vertical dimension, and the ultrathin-threaded surface showed denser collagen bundles.

P0072.t: Influence of abutment material and modifications on peri-implant soft-tissue attachment: A systematic review and meta-analysis of histological animal studies
P0072.kf: Systematic review of histological animal studies (18 of 1187 included, 4 meta-analysed, none low risk of bias): attachment dimensions were comparable, except a higher aJE-CBI distance for chemically modified acid-etched vs machined titanium surfaces.

P0075.t: Influence of Implant Connection, Abutment Design and Screw Insertion Torque on Implant-Abutment Misfit
P0075.kf: In vitro study of 120 implants (external vs Morse taper connection; straight vs angulated abutments; 10, 20, 30 Ncm) after thermal and cyclic loading: Morse taper connections showed the lowest misfit (0.6 µm), and misfit decreased as torque increased.

P0076.t: Influence of implant neck design on facial bone crest dimensions in the esthetic zone analyzed by cone beam CT: a comparative study with a 5-to-9-year follow-up
P0076.kf: Comparative CBCT study of 61 esthetic-zone single implants after 5–9 years: bone-level platform-switched implants (n = 20) had the facial bone crest 0.2 mm above the shoulder vs 1.6 mm below for soft-tissue-level butt-joint implants (n = 41); soft tissues and PES did not differ.

P0077.t: Influence of implant restorative emergence angle and contour on peri-implant marginal bone loss: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0077.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0077.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 studies (912 implants, 397 participants, 3.8–10.9 years): emergence angle >30° vs ≤30° did not significantly affect marginal bone change (mean difference 0.80; 95% CI -0.13 to 1.72), but convex profiles had more peri-implantitis (57.8% vs 21.3%; risk ratio 2.32).

P0078.t: Influence of platform switching on bone-level alterations: a three-year randomized clinical trial
P0078.kf: RCT with intraindividual randomization in 25 patients (two posterior mandibular implants each, platform-switched 3.3 mm vs standard 4 mm platform): at 3 years bone loss was 0.69 ± 0.43 mm vs 0.74 ± 0.57 mm, with no effect of platform type (p = .363).

P0079.t: Influence of straight versus angulated screw channel titanium bases on failure loads of two-piece ceramic and titanium implants restored with screw-retained monolithic crowns: An in-vitro study
P0079.kf: In vitro study of 32 screw-retained monolithic zirconia anterior crowns on two-piece ceramic or Ti-Zr implants with straight or 25° angulated-screw-channel titanium bases: all survived 1.2 million fatigue cycles; ASC bases (p = .001) and ceramic implants (p < .001) had higher bending moments, but ceramic implants …

P0083.t: Leakage of Microbial Endotoxin through the Implant-Abutment Interface in Oral Implants: An In Vitro Study
P0083.kf: In vitro test of 27 implant-abutment connections inoculated with E. coli endotoxin: all 6 external connections leaked, while 9 of 21 internal connections showed no measurable leakage; external connections had significantly higher endotoxin levels (p = 0.015).

P0086.t: Marginal changes at bone-level implants supporting fixed screw-retained partial implant prostheses with or without intermediate standardised abutments: 1-year results of a randomised controlled clinical trial
P0086.kf: RCT of 36 partially edentulous patients (72 bone-level implants) with screw-retained partial prostheses connected directly to the implant or via 3-mm standardised abutments: 12-month marginal bone loss was 0.17 ± 0.24 vs 0.09 ± 0.15 mm, not significantly different.

P0087.t: Mechanical stability and technical outcomes of monolithic CAD/CAM fabricated abutment-crowns supported by titanium bases: An in vitro study
P0087.kf: In vitro study of 60 conical implants with five abutment-crown designs after thermocycling and 1,200,000 chewing cycles: survival was 100% for lithium disilicate on custom titanium abutments or Ti-bases, 91.7% for PFM, 66.7% for zirconia and 58.3% for PICN on Ti-bases.

P0088.t: Mechanics of the implant-abutment connection: an 8-degree taper compared to a butt joint connection
P0088.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0088.kf: Three-dimensional non-linear finite element comparison of an 8-degree Morse taper and a butt joint implant-abutment connection under a regulatory dynamic test loading configuration indicated superior mechanics of the conical connection.

P0091.t: Microleakage assessment of CAD-CAM Cobalt-Chrome and Zirconia abutments on a conical connection dental implant: A comparative in vitro study
P0091.kf: In vitro study of 64 conical connection implants with milled, laser-sintered or cast Co-Cr and milled zirconia abutments after aging: 30 (47%) showed microleakage, with lowest bacterial counts for milled Co-Cr and zirconia and highest for cast and laser-sintered Co-Cr.

P0092.t: Microleakage at the Different Implant Abutment Interface: A Systematic Review
P0092.j: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
P0092.kf: Systematic review of 30 studies on microleakage at the implant-abutment interface: almost all showed some microleakage; it was least with Morse taper connections, external hexagon connections failed to prevent it, and leakage increased under dynamic loading.

P0093.t: Microleakage of bacteria in different implant-abutment assemblies: an in vitro study
P0093.j: Journal of Applied Biomaterials & Functional Materials
P0093.kf: In vitro study of two implant connection types (ten specimens each) inoculated with Enterococcus faecalis or Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans over 14 days: no leakage occurred, with microgaps ranging from 0.008 to 2.009 μm.

P0094.t: Multi unit abutments recommended in prosthetic and surgical implantology treatment (case report)
P0094.kf: Single case report of a 45-year-old man with a partially edentulous maxilla and a failed bridge, treated with two implants (one tilted distally along the sinus wall) and a 30-degree multi-unit abutment; the authors report a well-functioning final PFM prosthesis, no pain, and no sinus grafting needed.

P0096.t: Performance of CAD/CAM monolithic ceramic Implant-supported restorations bonded to titanium inserts: A systematic review
P0096.kf: Systematic review (25 of 505 articles, 2000–2016) on CAD/CAM monolithic ceramic implant restorations bonded to titanium inserts: no clinical studies were found; laboratory data indicate Ti inserts improve fracture strength, protect the connection from wear and improve marginal fit vs all-ceramic abutments.

P0103.t: Randomized clinical trial of zirconia and polyetheretherketone implant abutments for single-tooth implant restorations: A 5-year evaluation
P0103.kf: RCT of 40 participants with maxillary anterior/premolar implants randomized to titanium-supported PEEK or zirconia abutments with lithium disilicate crowns: at 5 years both had 100% survival with similar probing depth, bleeding, bone levels and esthetic outcomes.

P0105.t: Recommendations for Implant-Supported Full-Arch Rehabilitations in Edentulous Patients: The Oral Reconstruction Foundation Consensus Report
P0105.kf: Oral Reconstruction Foundation consensus report in which six working groups, based on six systematic/narrative reviews, formulated consensus statements and clinical recommendations on implant-supported full-arch rehabilitation of edentulous patients.

P0107.t: Restorative Emergence Profile for Single-Tooth Implants in Healthy Periodontal Patients: Clinical Guidelines and Decision-Making Strategies
P0107.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0107.kf: Review providing decision-making guidance for implant restorative emergence profile design: subgingival contours should mimic the root where possible, a convex critical contour is often needed facially for palatally positioned implants, and flat or concave contours if the implant is too facial.

P0108.t: Retrospective evaluation of crestal bone changes around implants with reduced abutment diameter placed non-submerged and at subcrestal positions: the effect of bone grafting at implant placement
P0108.kf: Retrospective comparison of 50 patients with subcrestal implants grafted with xenograft vs 50 without grafting: mean marginal hard-tissue loss was 0.11 ± 0.30 mm vs 0.08 ± 0.22 mm, with no statistically significant difference.

P0109.t: Review of the Mechanical Behavior of Different Implant-Abutment Connections
P0109.j: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
P0109.kf: Literature review (19 articles and 1 systematic review) on implant-abutment connection mechanics: conical abutments appeared to have fewer mechanical complications and better torque preservation, and internal conical connections showed less microleakage under dynamic loading.

P0111.t: Soft tissue stability at the facial aspect of gingivally converging abutments in the esthetic zone: a pilot clinical study
P0111.kf: Pilot study of 54 esthetic-zone implants in 41 patients with concave gingivally converging titanium or zirconia abutments and immediate provisionals: no recession or vertical gain in 87% of situations, no recession greater than 0.5 mm, and stable gingival levels up to 24 months.

P0114.t: Soft tissue response to different abutment materials: A controlled and randomized human study using an experimental model
P0114.kf: Randomized split-mouth study of 40 experimental healing abutments (titanium, zirconia, feldspar-veneered zirconia, PEEK) in 20 patients: after 3 months there were no significant differences in clinical, microbiological, cytokine or bone-level outcomes; veneered zirconia showed fewer mononuclear inflammatory cells than …

P0120.t: The effect of different abutment materials on peri-implant tissues-A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0120.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (12 articles) comparing alternative abutment materials with titanium: no differences in marginal bone level or probing depth for zirconia or alumina after 1 year or 5 years; ceramic abutment fractures and veneer chipping were the main technical findings.

P0127.t: The impact of the type and configuration of abutments and their (repeated) removal on the attachment level and marginal bone
P0127.kf: Review of transmucosal component composition, type, design and disconnection: animal data suggest only titanium, aluminium and zirconium oxides allow proper soft-tissue interface formation, while clinical evidence on disconnection, platform switching and connection type is limited and controversial.

P0128.t: The influence of titanium abutment surface roughness on plaque accumulation and gingivitis: short-term observations
P0128.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0128.kf: Six partially edentulous patients each received four titanium abutments of different surface roughness in random placement: after 3 months microbiological composition showed no major differences, spirochetes appeared only at the roughest abutments, and the roughest showed 0.2 mm attachment gain vs 0.8 to >1 mm loss at …

P0131.t: The Prosthetic-Biologic Connection and Its Influence on Peri-implant Health: An Overview of the Current Evidence
P0131.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0131.kf: Overview of prosthetic factors and peri-implant disease: implant spatial position, abutment height, residual cement and splinting were associated with peri-implant disease pathogenesis, while excessive occlusal forces related mainly to prosthetic complications.

P0133.t: The "hybrid abutment": a new design for implant cemented restorations in the esthetic zones
P0133.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0133.kf: Article proposing a 'hybrid abutment' design for cemented implant restorations in esthetic zones, combining a feather edge on the buccal side with a chamfer finish line on the lingual side, with a rationale for different designs in different situations.

P0137.t: Volumetric Calculation of Supraimplant Submergence Profile After Soft Tissue Conditioning with a Provisional Restoration
P0137.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0137.kf: Digital analysis of 20 patients' casts after soft-tissue conditioning with implant provisionals: emergence profile extension averaged 41.9 mm3 for central and 25.8 mm3 for lateral incisor sites, more than double the initial healing-abutment profile.

P0138.t: Early peri‐implant bone loss as a predictor for peri‐implantitis: A 10‐year prospective cohort study
P0138.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0138.kf: Prospective cohort of 407 patients with 1482 implants followed for an average of 10.66 years: implant survival was 94.74%; early bone loss thresholds were analysed as predictors of peri-implantitis together with smoking and periodontitis history.

P0140.t: Implant-Abutment Connections: A Review of Biologic Consequences and Peri-implantitis Implications
P0140.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0140.kf: Review of implant-abutment crestal connections: 1.5 to 2.0 mm of bone loss occurred around bone-level butt-joint connections attributed to bacterial microgap colonization, not seen with no-interface (tissue-level) implants, and platform-switched connections showed less marginal bone resorption.

P0143.t: Papillary fill response in single‐tooth implants using abutments of different geometry
P0143.kf: Within-patient randomized study of 26 subjects with two esthetic-zone implants restored with conventional or curved abutments: papilla fill at 12 months did not differ (P = 0.25) and correlated with the bone level between implant and adjacent root.

P0146.t: Chemical Interaction of Phosphoric Acid Ester with Hydroxyapatite
P0146.kf: Laboratory NMR and x-ray diffraction study of MDP interaction with hydroxyapatite: MDP leached Ca to form a layered MDP-calcium salt on the surface, with CaHPO4·2H2O precipitating on top after longer interaction.

P0147.t: Which adhesive strategy for non-carious cervical lesions?
P0147.kf: Summary of a systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 RCTs on non-carious cervical lesions: bonding strategy did not influence postoperative sensitivity (RR 1.04; 95% CI 0.81 to 1.34) or retention, while etch-and-rinse produced less marginal discoloration at 18 months to 2 years and 4 to 5 years.

P0148.t: Resin-ceramic bonding: a review of the literature
P0148.kf: Literature review of in vitro studies (1966–2001) on resin bonding to dental ceramics: bonding to silica-based ceramics is well documented, but bonding to high-strength ceramics is less predictable and requires substantially different methods.

P0149.t: From Buonocore's Pioneering Acid-Etch Technique to Self-Adhering Restoratives. A Status Perspective of Rapidly Advancing Dental Adhesive Technology
P0149.kf: Literature-based opinion paper on dental adhesive technology covering 14 items, recommending a 3-step full etch-and-rinse route and a preferred 3-step combined selective enamel etch with 2-step self-etch route, and appraising bond degradation and universal adhesives.

P0151.t: A 15-year study of osseointegrated implants in the treatment of the edentulous jaw
P0151.kf: 15-year clinical series (1965–1980) of 2768 fixtures in 410 edentulous jaws: in the 5–9-year standardized group (895 fixtures), 81% of maxillary and 91% of mandibular fixtures remained stable; bone loss averaged 1.5 mm in the first year and 0.1 mm annually thereafter.

P0156.t: Ten-year survival rates of fixed prostheses on four or six implants ad modum Brånemark in full edentulism
P0156.kf: Retrospective study of 156 consecutive fully edentulous patients with fixed prostheses on 4 or 6 Brånemark implants, all with 10-year follow-up: despite a tendency to more failures with 4 implants, implant and prosthesis survival were the same in both groups at 10 years.

P0163.t: Clinical protocol with digital cad/cam chairside workflow for the rehabilitation of severely worn dentition patients
P0163.kf: Report of 4 consecutive patients with severely worn dentitions rehabilitated using a digital CAD/CAM chairside workflow: good aesthetic and functional results with almost 100% cumulative survival at two-year follow-up.

P0167.t: Comparison between CAD/CAM-milled and cast hybrid full-mouth restorations on dental implants: A novel approach to full-mouth rehabilitation
P0167.kf: Prospective clinical study of 10 edentulous patients (58 implants) with immediately loaded hybrid bridges, followed on average 40 months: 100 per cent implant success; prosthetic complications (screw fracture/loosening, chipping, debonding) occurred only with cast frameworks, none with CAD/CAM-milled frameworks.

P0168.t: A systematic approach to full-mouth reconstruction of the severely worn dentition
P0168.kf: Technique report with a single case (55-year-old man, severely worn dentition): seating the condyles in centric relation gained 2.38 mm of anterior restorative space without appreciably stretching the elevator muscles, so VDO did not need to be opened; full-coverage PFM restorations were made.

P0169.t: Immediate loading of three (fixed-on-3) vs four (fixed-on-4) implants supporting cross-arch fixed prostheses: 1-year results from a multicentre randomised controlled trial
P0169.kf: Multicentre RCT of 48 edentulous patients with immediately loaded cross-arch prostheses on three (Fo3) vs four (Fo4) implants: at 1 year implant losses (1 vs 3 patients) and complications did not differ significantly; Fo3 lost less bone (0.22 ± 0.20 vs 0.40 ± 0.21 mm, P = 0.005).

P0175.t: Number of implants placed for complete‐arch fixed prostheses: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P0175.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis: fewer than five implants per arch for a one-piece complete-arch fixed prosthesis showed implant and prosthesis survival similar to five or more implants, with no statistically significant difference (median follow-up 8 years, range 1 to 15). Posterior tilting of distal implants did …

P0179.t: Effect of cantilever length and alloy framework on the stress distribution in peri-implant area of cantilevered implant-supported fixed partial dentures
P0179.kf: In vitro strain-gauge study on a polyurethane mandible model with two implants and CoCr or PdAg cantilevered frameworks loaded with 300 N at 5, 10 and 15 mm: peri-implant deformation increased with cantilever length, and CoCr showed larger compression than PdAg.

P0185.t: The Efficacy of 4% Articaine Versus 2% Lidocaine in Inducing Palatal Anesthesia for Tooth Extraction in Different Maxillary Regions
P0185.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P0185.kf: Double-blind RCT of 300 patients undergoing single maxillary extraction: buccal infiltration achieved palatal anesthesia in 82.7% with 4% articaine vs 1.3% with 2% lidocaine (P < .001), with no difference between maxillary regions.

P0186.t: Finishing procedures in Orthodontics: dental dimensions and proportions (microesthetics)
P0186.kf: Narrative special article describing ideal dental dimensions and proportions (white esthetics) and their relation to the periodontium (pink esthetics) for orthodontic finishing. The authors conclude that excellence is the sum of many details and that many aspects depend on periodontists and prosthodontists, so …

P0187.t: A Technique to Transfer the Emergence Profile Contours of a Provisional Implant Crown to the Definitive Impression
P0187.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0187.kf: Clinical report describing an indirectly fabricated modified impression post, made from a polyvinyl siloxane index of the provisional screw-retained crown and acrylic resin, to transfer the emergence profile to the definitive impression.

P0188.t: Gingival Zenith Positions and Levels of the Maxillary Anterior Dentition
P0188.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0188.kf: Cross-sectional measurement of 240 sites in 20 healthy patients: mean gingival zenith position distal to the tooth's vertical midline was about 1 mm for central incisors, 0.4 mm for lateral incisors and 0 mm for canines; lateral incisor zenith level was approximately 1 mm coronal to the line joining central incisor …

P0189.t: Public Preferences for Anterior Tooth Variations: A Web-Based Study
P0189.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0189.kf: Web-based survey of anterior tooth variations with 1934 valid US/Canadian respondents analysed: strongest preferences concerned diastema and midline shift, weakest whiteness and proportion; females had stronger preferences, and age, gender and race produced significant differences.

P0190.t: Digital Smile Design: A Tool for Treatment Planning and Communication in Esthetic Dentistry
P0190.kf: Technique report describing the Digital Smile Design (DSD) protocol: reference lines and shapes drawn over facial and intraoral photographs in presentation software, then transferred to the cast and wax-up. The authors conclude it improves the team's diagnostic vision, understanding of esthetic issues and patient …

P0191.t: Dentists' preferences of anterior tooth proportion--a web-based study
P0191.kf: Web-based survey of 549 dentists from 38 countries rating computer-manipulated anterior tooth proportions: the 80% proportion was judged best for very short and short teeth and the golden proportion for very tall teeth, with no clear best for normal height or tall teeth.

P0192.kf: Cast-measurement study (58 images of casts, 52 directly measured casts): the 1.618:1 golden proportion was found in the perceived maxillary central:lateral incisor width in 10 of 58 images (17%) and not between maxillary lateral incisor and canine; it was absent for maxillary central to mandibular lateral incisor and …

P0197.t: The Possible Role of Dental Implants in the Etiology and Prognosis of Osteomyelitis: A Retrospective Study
P0197.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0197.kf: Retrospective review of 54 patients with jaw osteomyelitis in three departments (2009–2014): 40 had complete remission and 14 needed aggressive surgery; a previous dental implant was an independent factor for primary treatment failure (P = .0001).

P0201.t: Self-reported allergy to penicillin and clindamycin administration may be risk factors for dental implant failure: A systematic review, meta-analysis and delabeling protocol
P0201.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 studies: patients given clindamycin for self-reported penicillin allergy had higher implant failure (OR = 3.30, 95% C.I. 2.58-4.22), with cumulative failure 11.0% vs 3.8% in amoxicillin patients.

P0204.t: Abutment height influences the effect of platform switching on peri-implant marginal bone loss
P0204.kf: Retrospective study of 228 conical-connection implants in 108 patients with the same uni-abutment (different mismatch): at 6 and 18 months MBL was greater for short vs long abutments, grafted vs pristine bone, heavier smoking and 5.0 vs 4.5 mm diameter implants.

P0207.t: Inter-implant distance and buccal bone thickness for a novel implant design: a preclinical study
P0207.kf: Minipig study of fully tapered implants: inter-implant bone height was maintained at thread-peak distances of 1, 2 or 3 mm, while buccal bone resorption was significant when thread-peak distance to outer buccal bone was < 0.5 mm.

P0211.t: Fixed Prosthetic Restorations and Periodontal Health: A Narrative Review
P0211.kf: Narrative review (literature 1981–2021) of fixed prostheses and periodontal health: marginal discrepancies promote biofilm, microleakage, caries and periodontal lesions; CAD/CAM zirconia restorations showed better marginal fit and periodontal outcomes, and supragingival margins favored hygiene.

P0213.t: The effect of subcrestal placement of the polished surface of ITI implants on marginal soft and hard tissues
P0213.kf: Within-patient study of 11 patients each receiving two ITI implants, randomly assigned to standard placement or the polished-surface border 1 mm subcrestal: over the first year test implants lost 2.26 mm vs 1.02 mm of bone height, ending 0.38 mm lower.

P0215.t: Hard and soft tissue healing around implants with a modified implant neck configuration: An experimental in vivo preclinical investigation
P0215.kf: Preclinical study in 8 animals with 16 tissue-level convergent-neck test implants and 16 bone-level controls randomly allocated: at 4 and 12 weeks no statistically significant differences in peri-implant hard and soft tissue height and thickness.

P0220.t: Influence of Soft Tissue Thickness on Peri-Implant Marginal Bone Loss: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P0220.kf: Systematic review (8 articles, 5 meta-analysed) of soft tissue thickness and early marginal bone loss: thick peri-implant soft tissue showed less MBL (WMD -0.80 mm; 95% confidence interval -1.18 to -0.42 mm).

P0222.t: Initial implant position determines the magnitude of crestal bone remodeling
P0222.kf: Study of one-piece non-submerged implants in 42 patients followed up to 5 years: bone remodeling of 1.10 mm occurred by 6 months with virtually no later change; implants with the rough-smooth border below the crest remodeled more (1.72 mm) than at the crest (0.68 mm).

P0223.t: Interproximal contact loss at implant sites: a retrospective clinical study with a 10-year follow-up
P0223.kf: Retrospective study of 39 patients with 80 implants re-examined at least 10 years after restoration: interproximal contact loss occurred at 50% of implants, more often mesially (RR = 1.79) and with 2-implant FDPs, and was associated with increased probing depth (+0.46 mm).

P0232.t: The esthetic biological contour concept for implant restoration emergence profile design
P0232.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0232.kf: Concept article describing the esthetic biological contour (EBC) concept, which divides the implant restoration emergence profile into zones with specific functions and recommended designs related to implant position, implant design and soft tissue thickness.

P0233.t: The influence of new immediate tissue level abutment on crestal bone stability of subcrestally placed implants: A 1-year randomized controlled clinical trial
P0233.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0233.kf: RCT of 64 patients with subcrestal platform-switched implants: immediate tissue level abutments (no disconnection) vs healing abutments with four disconnections; early bone loss was 0.14 ± 0.27 vs 0.64 ± 0.64 mm (p = .0001), but the 1-year late-loss difference was not significant (p = .22).

P0234.t: The Long-Term Efficacy of Currently Used Dental Implants: A Review and Proposed Criteria of Success
P0234.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0234.kf: Narrative review of the long-term data on dental implants in use in 1986 that proposes criteria of success. Of the systems reviewed, the authors found only two meeting their criteria, the Branemark osseointegrated screw and the Small transosteal staple, each with over 10 years of results based on every inserted …

P0236.t: The use of implant-level connection in screw-retained fixed partial dentures: A 3-year randomised clinical trial
P0236.kf: RCT of 50 patients (119 internal conical connection implants) with screw-retained FPDs on abutment-level vs implant-level connection: MBL change did not differ at any point (3 years: 0.18 ± 0.39 vs 0.15 ± 0.21 mm); technical, biological and prosthetic complication rates were 5.04%, 3.36% and 16.00%.

P0240.t: Crestal Bone Stability around Implants with Horizontally Matching Connection after Soft Tissue Thickening: A Prospective Clinical Trial
P0240.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0240.kf: Prospective study of 103 patients with internal hex regular-connection implants in thin, thin-thickened (allogenic membrane) or thick tissues: at 1 year bone loss was 1.65 ± 0.08 mm mesially in thin, 0.31 ± 0.05 mm in thickened and 0.44 ± 0.06 mm in thick tissues.

P0241.t: Influence of thin mucosal tissues on crestal bone stability around implants with platform switching: a 1-year pilot study
P0241.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P0241.kf: Pilot study of 12 implants in 4 patients with thin mucosa (≤2 mm): at 1 year bone loss was 1.81 ± 0.39 mm mesially for platform-switched vs 1.60 ± 0.46 mm for matching connections, with no significant difference.

P0243.t: The influence of mucosal tissue thickening on crestal bone stability around bone-level implants. A prospective controlled clinical trial
P0243.kf: Prospective controlled study of 97 bone-level implants in thin, thin-thickened (allogenic membrane) or thick mucosa: at 1 year mesial bone loss was 1.22 ± 0.08 mm (thin), 0.24 ± 0.06 mm (thickened) and 0.22 ± 0.06 mm (thick).

P0244.t: The influence of soft tissue thickness on crestal bone changes around implants: a 1-year prospective controlled clinical trial
P0244.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0244.kf: Prospective controlled study of 46 implants in 19 patients: supracrestal test implants lost 1.61 ± 0.24 mm mesially with thin mucosa vs 0.26 ± 0.08 mm with thick mucosa at 1 year; bone-level controls lost 1.8 ± 0.164 mm mesially.

P0246.t: The Evolution of Surgical Techniques and Biomaterials for Periodontal Regeneration
P0246.kf: Narrative review of periodontal regeneration. Authors conclude that techniques evolved from papilla-preserving flaps for barrier membranes to minimally invasive flaps combined with biologic agents, which can reduce papilla dehiscence/necrosis and postoperative morbidity and enhance outcomes; newer techniques also …

P0250.t: Advanced Scaffolds for Dental Pulp and Periodontal Regeneration
P0250.kf: Narrative review of advanced scaffolds for dental pulp and periodontal regeneration. The authors state that no current therapy regenerates the pulp-dentin complex in necrotic pulp, antibiotic pastes harm stem cell survival, and antibiotic-eluting nanofibers with injectable scaffolds may improve the likelihood of pulp …

P0253.t: Relative performance of various biomaterials used for maxillary sinus augmentation: A Bayesian network meta‐analysis
P0253.kf: Bayesian network meta-analysis of 34 RCTs (842 two-stage lateral sinus augmentations) on histomorphometric new bone percentage: bovine xenograft plus bone marrow concentrate ranked most effective (81%).

P0255.t: Bone grafts: which is the ideal biomaterial?
P0255.kf: Narrative review on bone graft biomaterials: bovine xenografts, followed by synthetic materials lacking documented predictability, dominate the cranio-maxillofacial market, and only a handful of new substitutes are clinically available despite extensive laboratory research.

P0264.kf: Narrative review of biomaterials for craniofacial bone regeneration. The authors state that calcium phosphate bioceramics remain among the most widely used biomaterials with a long clinical track record, polymers offer biologic advantages despite lower rigidity, and 3D printing is likely to feature in the next …

P0269.t: Guided tissue regeneration with and without decalcified freeze-dried bone in mandibular Class II furcation invasions
P0269.kf: Study of 6 patients with 17 mandibular Class II buccal furcations randomly assigned to ePTFE GTR with DFDBA (10) or ePTFE alone (7): at 6-month re-entry, vertical defect fill was 5.0 vs 3.8 mm and PD reduction 2.2 vs 1.5 mm, with no statistically significant differences.

P0271.t: A systematic approach to deep caries removal end points: the peripheral seal concept in adhesive dentistry
P0271.kf: Literature-based protocol (since 1980) combining anatomical and histologic knowledge with caries-detecting dye and DIAGNOdent laser fluorescence to define caries removal end points that create a peripheral seal zone for adhesive restorations without exposing vital pulps.

P0276.t: Biomechanical considerations for the restoration of endodontically treated teeth: a systematic review of the literature, Part II (Evaluation of fatigue behavior, interfaces, and in vivo studies)
P0276.kf: Systematic literature review (PubMed 1990–2005) of interfaces, fatigue and clinical studies of restored endodontically treated teeth: composite resin with or without fiber posts resisted fatigue tests, with less severe failures than rigid metal or ceramic posts, though root adhesion remains challenging.

P0277.t: Biomechanical considerations for the restoration of endodontically treated teeth: a systematic review of the literature--Part 1. Composition and micro- and macrostructure alterations
P0277.kf: Systematic literature review (PubMed 1990–2005) of endodontically treated teeth: vitality loss and endodontic therapy caused only negligible composition changes and limited biomechanical effects, while tooth strength decreased in proportion to coronal tissue loss.

P0278.t: Biomimetic Aspects of Restorative Dentistry Biomaterials
P0278.kf: Narrative review of biomimetic restorative biomaterials and tissue-engineering approaches in dentistry. The authors conclude that biomimetic restorative materials are still at a preliminary stage, tissue-engineering progress needs further research before clinical translation, and implementation at larger scale may …

P0279.t: Biomimetic Dentistry: Basic Principles and Protocols
P0279.kf: Review of biomimetic dentistry principles, dividing restorative protocols into stress-reducing and bond-maximizing protocols and highlighting minimally invasive caries management and bioactive agents for remineralization.

P0280.j: Journal of Oral Research and Review
P0280.kf: Short narrative review of biomimetic dentistry covering its history, biomaterials, restorative principles and regenerative approaches (pulp, dentin, enamel, tooth, salivary gland). The author concludes biomimetics is a very useful concept and that further, firmer multidisciplinary research is needed.

P0282.t: Clinical Evaluation of Stress-reducing Direct Composite Restorations in Structurally Compromised Molars: A 2-year Report
P0282.kf: Randomized clinical trial of 50 patients (75 vital molars with large class II cavities) restored with stress-reducing direct composite and one of three etch-and-rinse adhesives (25 teeth per group): no failures and no postoperative sensitivity at 2 weeks or 2 years; performance did not differ between adhesives.

P0283.t: Clinical performance of anterior resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses with different framework designs: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0283.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 1 RCT and 4 cohort studies (all high risk of bias) on anterior resin-bonded FDPs: single-retainer cantilever designs had lower failure than two-retainer fixed-fixed designs (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.19-0.94), while debonding did not differ.

P0284.t: Clinical presentations of stress distribution in teeth and the significance in operative dentistry
P0284.kf: Narrative article using Moire fringe stress findings to describe how conventional extension-for-prevention cavities disrupt the peripheral rim of enamel and occlusal cross-bracing structures, leading to compressive and tension fractures and occlusal-effect interproximal caries. The authors conclude cavity designs …

P0286.kf: Article explaining that immediately sealing dentin and allowing the hybrid layer to mature ('decoupling with time') improves bond strength and prevents shrinkage-stress debonding, with deep margin elevation, stress-reduced layering and fiber reinforcement also leveraging this principle.

P0288.t: Does the use of preheated restorative resin composite as a luting agent influence the adaptation of fixed dental prostheses? A systematic review
P0288.kf: Systematic review of preheated restorative composite as a luting agent: of 2109 articles, 4 in vitro studies were included; three found greater mismatch than resin cement and one found improved adaptation; meta-analysis was precluded by heterogeneity.

P0289.t: Efficacy of a resin coating on bond strengths of resin cement to dentin
P0289.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0289.kf: In vitro microtensile study on human premolar dentin: a resin coating (dentin bonding system plus flowable composite) significantly improved Panavia F bond strength in indirect restorations, highest with Clearfil SE Bond plus Protect Liner F, but direct composite bonds remained strongest.

P0290.t: Evidence-based concepts and procedures for bonded inlays and onlays. Part I. Historical perspectives and clinical rationale for a biosubstitutive approach
P0290.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0290.kf: Concept article presenting a protocol for bonded inlays/onlays: adhesive base/liner (Dual Bonding, Cavity Design Optimization), cervical margin relocation when needed, and highly filled light-curing restorative material for cementation.

P0292.t: Evidence-based concepts and procedures for bonded inlays and onlays. Part II. Guidelines for cavity preparation and restoration fabrication
P0292.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0292.kf: Evidence-based update on cavity preparation and material selection for bonded inlays/onlays: CAD/CAM composites or lithium disilicate are often recommended for bruxism or fragile teeth mainly on scarce in vitro evidence, and cusp coverage requires multifactorial analysis.

P0293.t: Evidence-based concepts and procedures for bonded inlays and onlays. Part III. A case series with long-term clinical results and follow-up
P0293.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0293.kf: Case series of 25 indirect or semidirect composite inlays/onlays with 6- to 21-year follow-ups: no clinical failure was reported; a few showed discrete marginal discoloration (n = 4) or occlusal wear (n = 7).

P0295.t: From 'Direct Versus Indirect' Toward an Integrated Restorative Concept in the Posterior Dentition
P0295.kf: Narrative review on direct versus indirect posterior restorations. Citing prospective reviews, annual failure rates of 1% to 2% for direct composites, indirect restorations and crowns, the authors conclude longevity no longer justifies choosing indirect over direct, recommend minimally invasive adhesive techniques …

P0296.t: Gingival microleakage of Class II resin composite restorations with fiber inserts
P0296.kf: In vitro study of 54 molars with Class II slot cavities (gingival margins on root) restored with or without glass or polyethylene fiber inserts and three adhesives: fiber inserts reduced gingival microleakage, and Clearfil SE Bond/Filtek P-60 gave the lowest scores.

P0300.t: Influence of preparation design and ceramic thicknesses on fracture resistance and failure modes of premolar partial coverage restorations
P0300.kf: In vitro study of 144 human premolars with lithium-disilicate palatal onlays, occlusal onlays or complete veneers at three thicknesses after fatigue: all survived fatigue; ultrathin palatal onlays had higher fracture resistance than standard (P=.015), whereas standard complete veneers outperformed thin and ultrathin.

P0301.t: Clinical and Biomechanical Performance of Occlusal Veneers: A Scoping Review
P0301.j: The Journal of Contemporary Dental Practice
P0301.kf: Scoping review of 42 articles (35 in vitro, 7 clinical) on occlusal veneers: ceramic thicknesses of 0.7–1.0 mm and polymeric materials below 0.7 mm are recommended, with load resistance exceeding 2000 N in most studies.

P0302.t: Longitudinal analysis on the effect of insertion torque on delayed single implants: A 3-year randomized clinical study
P0302.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0302.kf: Randomized clinical study of 116 single implants in healed sites over 3 years: survival 96.5%; cumulative success 91.3% with high insertion torque (≥50 Ncm) vs 98.2% regular torque, with significantly greater marginal bone loss and facial recession for high torque and in the mandible.

P0303.t: Management of large class II lesions in molars: how to restore and when to perform surgical crown lengthening?
P0303.kf: Narrative article reviewing 7 clinical scenarios of deep class II lesions in molars: deep margin elevation when the healthy margin lies at sulcus/epithelium level, crown lengthening when caries reaches connective tissue or bone crest, and endocrowns for advanced structural loss.

P0304.t: Microleakage in overflared root canals restored with different fiber reinforced dowels
P0304.kf: In vitro study of 40 premolars with overflared canals restored with four adhesively luted fiber-reinforced dowels: all groups showed considerable leakage, and the individually shaped polyethylene-reinforced dowel (Ribbond) showed the least overall leakage.

P0305.t: Minimally Invasive Direct Restoration of Worn Teeth: A Simplified Technique
P0305.kf: Technique report with a single case (63-year-old woman with tooth wear): full-mouth direct composite rehabilitation using a progressive diagnostic wax-up, transparent silicone templates and heated composite at an increased vertical dimension; the author reports an excellent esthetic outcome with reduced chair time and …

P0308.t: Nonretentive Bonded Ceramic Partial Crowns: Concept and Simplified Protocol for Long-lasting Dental Restorations
P0308.kf: Concept and protocol article for nonretentive bonded ceramic partial crowns: rounded, gently sloping preparations with margins inclined toward the tooth center, monolithic lithium disilicate, and composite cement bonded to HF-etched, silanized ceramic.

P0309.t: Posterior indirect adhesive restorations (PIAR): preparation designs and adhesthetics clinical protocol
P0309.kf: Narrative review of posterior indirect adhesive restorations and preparation designs, emphasizing minimal preparation, preservation of intact enamel and dentin, and increasing bonding surface area to improve adhesive bond quality and durability.

P0311.t: Post placement and restoration of endodontically treated teeth: a literature review
P0311.kf: Narrative literature review on post placement and restoration of endodontically treated teeth. The author concludes that high clinical success is achievable with most current systems if basic principles are followed: avoid canal contamination, give posterior teeth cuspal coverage, preserve tooth structure, use …

P0312.t: Postendodontic Restoration: Endodontic Post-and-Core or No Post At All?
P0312.kf: Systematic review of 14 clinical studies (11 RCTs): 10 of 14 failed to show a positive effect of post placement on endodontically treated teeth; a post effect is possible when no cavity wall is present.

P0313.t: Posterior indirect adhesive restorations: updated indications and the Morphology Driven Preparation Technique
P0313.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0313.kf: Technique article presenting the Morphology Driven Preparation Technique: continuous inclined-plane margins (hollow chamfer or concave bevel) coronal to the equatorial line, a 1.2 mm butt-joint when margins are apical to it, and avoidance of shoulders, slots and pins.

P0314.t: Pre-endodontic restoration of structurally compromised teeth: current concepts
P0314.kf: Narrative review of pre-endodontic restoration of structurally compromised teeth (cervical margin relocation, doughnut, canal projection, open sandwich, crown lengthening, orthodontic and surgical extrusion) with a decision flowchart. The authors conclude pre-endodontic restoration has many advantages for …

P0315.t: Proximal box elevation with resin composite and the dogma of biological width: clinical R2-technique and critical review
P0315.kf: Technique report with critical review: a single case (75-year-old woman, tooth 45) restored with the two-step R2-technique (proximal box elevation, then direct composite) with the margin 0.5 to 1.0 mm from the alveolar crest; at 12 months the tooth was vital, probing depth 2 mm, no bleeding on probing and only minimal …

P0316.t: Rationalization of shape and related stress distribution in posterior teeth: a finite element study using nonlinear contact analysis
P0316.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0316.kf: 2-D nonlinear contact finite element analysis of opposing molars loaded to 200 N: vertical loading generated no harmful stress concentrations, whereas working and nonworking micromotions produced inverted stress patterns, with tensile stresses in nonsupporting cusps and the maxillary central groove.

P0317.t: Reduced light energy density decreases post-gel contraction while maintaining degree of conversion in composites
P0317.kf: In vitro study of a composite cured at attenuated light intensities: a 20 s at 71% plus 20 s at 100% cure showed a 21.8% reduction from predicted contraction strain, and sub-maximal intensity significantly reduced post-gel contraction strain without significantly affecting degree of conversion.

P0319.t: Shrinkage stress in light-cured composite resins: influence of material and photoactivation mode
P0319.kf: In vitro study of five composites: maximum shrinkage stress ranged from 1.51 MPa (Solitaire) to 0.92 MPa (Clearfil AP-X) with standard curing; an exponential light ramp reduced maximum shrinkage stress by 3.9% and stress rate by 11%.

P0325.t: The effect of c-factor and flowable resin or fiber use at the interface on microtensile bond strength to dentin
P0325.j: Journal of adhesive dentistry/The journal of adhesive dentistry
P0325.kf: In vitro microtensile study of 24 molars (high c-factor Class I cavities vs flat dentin; bulk, flowable, glass-fiber or polyethylene-fiber techniques): flowable composite decreased bond strength in high c-factor cavities, everStick NET gave stable values, and Ribbond increased bond strength.

P0326.t: The effect of fiber placement or flowable resin lining on microleakage in Class II adhesive restorations
P0326.kf: In vitro dye-penetration study of Class II cavities in 40 molars: flowable resin alone or combined with polyethylene (Ribbond) or glass (everStick NET) fibers significantly reduced leakage at occlusal enamel margins, with no significant difference among groups at cervical dentin margins.

P0329.t: The role of functional monomers in bonding to enamel: acid-base resistant zone and bonding performance
P0329.kf: In vitro study on premolar enamel of two-step self-etch adhesives varying MDP and Phenyl-P: an acid-base resistant zone formed with all systems containing MDP in primer or bond but not Phenyl-P only, and the all-MDP combination gave significantly higher micro-shear bond strength.

P0332.t: Some Myths in Dentin Bonding: An Evidence-Based Perspective
P0332.kf: Critical narrative review of dentin-bonding 'myths' based on randomized trials and systematic reviews. The authors report that RCTs found no clinical superiority of wet bonding, chlorhexidine application, rubber dam, sclerotic-dentin roughening, or adhesive strategy/steps, and that OptiBond FL and Clearfil SE Bond …

P0337.kf: In vitro microtensile study: delayed light-activation of composite (20 min) significantly lowered dentin bond strengths of all six single-step adhesives but not the three-step control, and the effect was absent on dehydrated dentin or processed composite.

P0338.t: A clinical evaluation of Class II composites placed using a decoupling technique
P0338.kf: Single-center practice-based clinical trial of 43 Class II hybrid-composite restorations placed with a decoupling technique: 31 (74%) reviewed at 3 to 4 years, none showed significant deterioration, and no secondary caries or postoperative sensitivity was recorded.

P0339.kf: Narrative review of adhesion to porcelain and metal (sandblasting, tin plating, adhesive monomers, hydrofluoric acid etching and silane) with clinical examples. The author concludes that adhesives and adherend modification allow enamel-like bonds to metal and porcelain, with maximum tooth conservation as the …

P0340.t: Assessment of the nanostructure of acid-base resistant zone by the application of all-in-one adhesive systems: Super dentin formation
P0340.kf: In vitro SEM/TEM study of two all-in-one adhesives on premolar dentin: after acid-base challenge, a hybrid layer under 1 µm and an underlying mineral-containing acid-base resistant zone formed with both, with material-dependent thickness.

P0341.t: Bonded indirect restorations for posterior teeth: from cavity preparation to provisionalization
P0341.kf: Technique report with two clinical cases describing the first appointment for bonded indirect posterior restorations: conservative preparation, immediate dentin sealing with a self-etch adhesive and thin composite layer (relocating subgingival margins), impression, and a non-luted provisional. The authors state this …

P0344.t: Bonding Performance of Universal Adhesives: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P0344.kf: Meta-analysis of 59 in vitro studies: etch-and-rinse improved enamel bond strength of universal adhesives, and in dentin benefited ultra-mild and intermediately strong adhesives; intermediately strong adhesives lost bond strength after aging, while mild adhesives were stable with both strategies.

P0346.t: Classification review of dental adhesive systems: from the IV generation to the universal type
P0346.kf: Narrative review classifying dental adhesive systems from the 4th generation to universal adhesives (etch-and-rinse, self-etch, resin-modified glass-ionomer strategies). The authors note universal adhesives have broader applications than 7th-generation systems, while simplified adhesives are associated with lower in …

P0348.t: Collagen degradation by host-derived enzymes during aging
P0348.kf: In vitro study of demineralized human dentin collagen matrices in artificial saliva: matrices were almost completely destroyed at 250 days but not with protease inhibitors or mineral oil, and dentin collagenolytic activity was inhibited by protease inhibitors or 0.2% chlorhexidine.

P0349.t: Composite-to-composite microtensile bond strength in the repair of a microfilled hybrid resin: effect of surface treatment and oxygen inhibition
P0349.kf: In vitro microtensile study of composite-to-composite repair of a microfilled hybrid resin: air abrasion gave the strongest bond regardless of curing atmosphere, other surface treatments were comparable, and curing in air vs nitrogen did not significantly influence interfacial strength.

P0351.t: Dentine disorders and adhesive treatments: A systematic review
P0351.kf: Systematic review of 37 studies (164 teeth) on dentine disorders: dentine was damaged in dentinogenesis imperfecta and osteogenesis imperfecta, with reduced mineral density, hardness and elastic modulus, altered dentine-enamel junction, and enamel also affected in dentinogenesis imperfecta.

P0352.t: Development of Dentin Bonding Systems from Past to Present
P0352.kf: Narrative review of the development and classification of dentin bonding systems (historical generations; etch-and-rinse, self-etch and multi-mode adhesives). The authors conclude that etch-and-rinse may suit anterior teeth where enamel predominates, and that for posterior teeth active application of 10-MDP-based …

P0353.t: Direct comparison of the bond strength results of the different test methods: a critical literature review
P0353.kf: Critical literature review pooling dentin bond strength data from 147 references for six adhesives and four test methods: scatter remained high (coefficients of variation 20-50%), cohesive failures were frequent, and product ranking depended on the test used.

P0354.t: Evaluation of dentin bonding performance and acid-base resistance of the interface of two-step self-etching adhesive systems
P0354.kf: In vitro study of three two-step self-etch adhesives on molar dentin: Clearfil SE Bond had significantly higher μTBS than the fluoride-releasing FL-Bond and FL-Bond II, and an acid-base resistant zone formed in all groups with material-dependent formation.

P0356.t: Hydromechanics in dentine: role of dentinal tubules and hydrostatic pressure on mechanical stress-strain distribution
P0356.kf: Finite element models plus compression testing and FTIR of dentine: simulated hydrostatic pressure produced residual tensile stresses counteracting applied loads; partially dehydrated dentine had higher fracture stress (p=0.014) and hydrated dentine higher fracture strain (p=0.037).

P0357.t: Impact of Different Etching Strategies on Margin Integrity of Conservative Composite Restorations in Demineralized Enamel
P0357.kf: In vitro study of Class V composite restorations in bovine enamel (14 groups, n = 10) with two self-etch adhesives: phosphoric acid etching significantly increased continuous margins in demineralized and sound enamel, with longer etching (60-120 s) needed for iBond Self Etch.

P0359.t: External gap progression after cyclic fatigue of adhesive overlays and crowns made with high translucency zirconia or lithium silicate
P0359.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0359.kf: In vitro micro-CT study of endodontically treated molars restored with high-translucency zirconia or zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate overlays or crowns: crowns showed significantly less external gap progression than overlays after chewing simulation, and ZLS less than HTZ (p < 0.01).

P0361.t: Mechanisms of degradation of the hybrid layer in adhesive dentistry and therapeutic agents to improve bond durability--A literature review
P0361.kf: Literature review of 148 articles (1982-2015) on hybrid layer degradation: bond degradation involves hydrolysis of resin and collagen, with collagen vulnerable to fatigue and host-derived proteases (MMPs and cysteine cathepsins).

P0362.t: Meta-analytical Review of Parameters Involved in Dentin Bonding
P0362.kf: Systematic collection of 2,157 dentin bond-strength tests from 298 papers analyzed with a neural network model: micro-tensile tests showed greater discriminative power than macro-shear, and research group and adhesive brand were the most determining variables.

P0363.t: Microtensile bond strength of total-etch and self-etching adhesives to caries-affected dentine
P0363.kf: In vitro microtensile study of four adhesives on carious molars: total-etch adhesives yielded higher bond strengths than self-etch systems, Prompt L-Pop was significantly lowest, and all bonded better to normal than caries-affected dentine (significant for Prime & Bond NT and Clearfil SE Bond).

P0364.t: Monomer-Collagen Interactions Studied by Saturation Transfer Difference NMR
P0364.kf: Saturation transfer difference NMR study of functional monomers with atelocollagen: high STD intensities were detected for the aliphatic protons of MDP but not for 4-META, implying relatively stable hydrophobic MDP-collagen interaction.

P0369.t: Self-etch adhesive systems: a literature review
P0369.kf: Literature review of self-etch adhesives covering history, bonding mechanism, properties, acid-base resistant zone formation, classification by steps and acidity, durability and clinical importance.

P0370.t: Setting Stress in Composite Resin in Relation to Configuration of the Restoration
P0370.kf: Laboratory study of composite setting stress in cylindrical specimens of varying configuration factor (C, bonded to unbonded surface ratio): in most clinically relevant cavity configurations, stress-relieving flow was not sufficient to preserve adhesion to dentin.

P0375.t: The dual bonding technique: a modified method to improve adhesive luting procedures
P0375.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0375.kf: Technique report introducing the 'dual bonding technique': the dentin bonding agent is applied and cured right after preparation and applied again at final cementation. The authors report this practically doubled in vitro dentin bond strengths (mean values between 13 and 19 MPa) even with eugenol-containing temporary …

P0376.t: Ultramorphological evaluation of the dentin acid-base resistant zone of two-step self-etching systems after long-term storage in water
P0376.kf: In vitro SEM study of two two-step self-etch adhesives on dentin stored in water up to 6 months: outer lesion thickness grew from 10-15 µm to about 30 µm, and an acid-base resistant zone persisted in both, thinning over time with SE Bond and remaining more stable with Protect Bond.

P0377.t: Ultrastructure of the dentin-adhesive interface after acid-base challenge
P0377.kf: In vitro SEM study of four adhesive systems in bovine root dentin after acid-base challenge: the fluoride-releasing system showed a thick acid-resistant zone but partial resin degradation, self-etch systems a thin (<1 µm) resistant band beneath the hybrid layer, and the wet-bonding system partial hybrid layer …

P0378.kf: Narrative review of enamel bonding strategies. The authors conclude that universal adhesives simplify procedures and reduce chair time without necessarily optimizing the bonding strategy, selective enamel etching is recommended before (ultra) mild self-etch adhesives, and prior etching improves the quality of the …

P0380.t: Cuspal movement related to different bonding techniques using etch-and-rinse and self-etch adhesive systems
P0380.kf: In vitro study of Class II composite restorations in premolars with etch-and-rinse or self-etch adhesives: selective bonding gave lower cuspal movement than total bonding for all systems, and a flowable intermediate layer had no influence.

P0381.t: Evaluation of a new caries detecting dye for primary and permanent carious dentin
P0381.kf: Study of primary and permanent teeth with dentin caries using two acid-red dyes and DIAGNOdent: after caries removal readings were higher with complete removal of Caries Check-stained dentin than with Caries Detector, significantly in permanent teeth only; correlations with clinical parameters were low.

P0382.t: Mechanism of Differential Staining in Carious Dentin
P0382.kf: In vitro study: a 1.0% acid red caries detector failed to stain EDTA-demineralized bovine dentin matrix but stained the same matrix after lactic acid treatment above 0.01 M.

P0383.t: Cracked tooth syndrome: Overview of literature
P0383.j: International Journal of Applied and Basic Medical Research
P0383.kf: Narrative overview of cracked tooth syndrome: definition, AAE classification (craze line, fractured cusp, cracked tooth, split tooth, vertical root fracture), multifactorial etiology, clinical features, diagnostic methods (bite tests, transillumination, dyes, magnification) and treatment by crack extent. The authors …

P0384.t: Cracked tooth syndrome. Part 1: aetiology and diagnosis
P0384.kf: Narrative CPD review (part 1) of cracked tooth syndrome covering signs and symptoms, epidemiology, multifactorial etiology and diagnostic methods. It reports prognosis depends on crack location and extent (excellent for dentine-confined cracks, poor if both marginal ridges or pulp are involved) and that root-filled …

P0385.t: Cracked tooth syndrome. Part 2: restorative options for the management of cracked tooth syndrome
P0385.kf: Narrative CPD review (part 2) of restorative options for cracked tooth syndrome (immediate therapy, direct and indirect restorations with or without cuspal coverage). The authors conclude there is only very limited clinical evidence to substantiate any restoration, prognosis depends on crack extent, timing and …

P0386.t: Review of Cracked Tooth Syndrome: Etiology, Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention
P0386.kf: Narrative review of cracked tooth syndrome covering etiology, diagnosis (including newer technologies such as swept-source OCT), management and prevention. The authors conclude it is a common, clinically significant fracture, that diagnostic accuracy is advancing, and that most clinicians recommend full crown …

P0387.j: Journal of the Canadian Dental Association
P0387.kf: Narrative review of cracked tooth syndrome, an incomplete fracture of a vital posterior tooth typically causing pain on chewing hard foods that ceases on release; management options include monitoring, occlusal adjustment, cast restoration and endodontic treatment.

P0389.t: Adhesive strategies in cervical lesions: systematic review and a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
P0389.kf: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized trials in non-carious cervical lesions (66 eligible, 57 meta-analyzed): no significant differences between adhesive strategies (3ER, 2ER, 2SE, 1SE) except 2ER vs 3ER at the shortest follow-up; 2SE ranked highest but differed only slightly.

P0390.t: Cervical margin relocation in indirect adhesive restorations: A literature review
P0390.kf: Literature review of cervical margin relocation before indirect adhesive restorations identified 7 in vitro studies and 5 clinical reports, mostly on marginal adaptation, and no randomized, prospective or retrospective clinical studies.

P0391.t: Clinical and histological reaction of periodontal tissues to subgingival resin composite restorations
P0391.kf: Clinical-histological study of 29 subjects receiving deep margin elevation with composite: plaque, bleeding and probing depth decreased significantly at 3 months with apparent attachment gain, and gingival inflammation adjacent to composite was similar to that adjacent to natural root surfaces.

P0392.t: Up to 12 years clinical evaluation of 197 partial indirect restorations with deep margin elevation in the posterior region
P0392.kf: Retrospective evaluation of 197 partial indirect restorations with deep margin elevation in 120 patients: 8 absolute failures, cumulative survival 95.9% up to 12 years (mean 57.7 months); composite restorations degraded more than ceramic, and endodontic treatment increased fractures.

P0394.t: Current clinical concepts for adhesive cementation of tooth-colored posterior restorations
P0394.kf: Narrative continuing-education article reviewing concepts for adhesive cementation of tooth-colored posterior restorations. The authors conclude that immediate dentin sealing with a flexible adhesive base lining, plus highly filled viscous luting composites, improves safety and predictability and avoids complications …

P0396.t: Deep Margin Elevation: A Paradigm Shift
P0396.j: The American Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0396.kf: Technique article proposing deep margin elevation: a modified curved matrix, immediate dentin sealing and a direct composite base to raise subgingival proximal margins above the gingiva before indirect restorations. Two cases are shown with 9- and 12-year follow-up; the authors conclude more research is needed to …

P0397.t: Deep margin elevation versus crown lengthening: biologic width revisited
P0397.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0397.kf: Literature overview with three clinical cases comparing deep margin elevation and crown lengthening, extrapolating from root-coverage healing on restored roots; authors hypothesize that DME seems well tolerated by the periodontium clinically and histologically.

P0400.t: Effect of Smear Layer Thickness and pH of Self-etching Adhesive Systems on the Bond Strength and Gap Formation to Dentin
P0400.kf: In vitro study of three self-etch and two etch-and-rinse adhesives on thick or thin dentin smear layers: smear layer thickness did not affect microtensile bond strength but thick smear layers increased gap width; etch-and-rinse systems showed higher bond strength and lower gaps.

P0401.t: Evaluation of the In Vitro Effects of Cervical Marginal Relocation Using Composite Resins on the Marginal Quality of CAD/CAM Crowns
P0401.kf: In vitro study of 40 molars with CAD/CAM resin or lithium-disilicate crowns and a proximal box 2.0 mm below the CEJ: cervical margin relocation with conventional or flowable composite produced no significant difference in marginal quality before or after thermomechanical loading.

P0403.t: Immediate dentin sealing improves bond strength of indirect restorations
P0403.kf: In vitro microtensile study of 15 molars: immediate dentin sealing (58.25 MPa) did not differ from direct bonding (55.06 MPa), while delayed dentin sealing was significantly lower (11.58 MPa), with mostly interfacial failures and a disrupted hybrid layer.

P0404.t: Immediate dentin sealing supports delayed restoration placement
P0404.kf: In vitro microtensile study of 50 molars with two adhesives: immediate dentin sealing with 2-, 7- or 12-week provisional phases matched direct bonding (above 45 MPa), whereas delayed dentin sealing was much lower (1.81 MPa SE Bond, 11.58 MPa Optibond FL).

P0405.t: Influence of a proximal margin elevation technique on marginal adaptation of ceramic inlays
P0405.kf: In vitro study of 40 molars with MOD cavities and Cerec ceramic inlays: after thermomechanical loading, proximal margin elevation with composite produced marginal integrity not significantly different from inlay margins placed directly in dentin.

P0406.t: Influence of cervical margin relocation (CMR) on periodontal health: 12-month results of a controlled trial
P0406.kf: Controlled clinical study of 35 posterior teeth with lithium-disilicate restorations: at 12 months cervical margin relocation showed higher bleeding on probing than shoulder preparations (53.0% vs 31.5% per site), with no differences in gingival or plaque index.

P0407.t: Influence of cervical margin relocation and adhesive system on microleakage of indirect composite restorations
P0407.j: SMILE – School of dental Medicine dIgitaL archivE (University of Belgrade, School of Dental Medicine)
P0407.kf: In vitro study of 20 molars with CAD/CAM composite overlays and margins 1 mm below the CEJ: with a universal adhesive, relocated margins leaked significantly more than non-relocated ones, whereas with a three-step total-etch adhesive there was no significant difference.

P0408.t: M-i-M for DME: matrix-in-a-matrix technique for deep margin elevation
P0408.kf: Technique report describing the matrix-in-a-matrix method for deep margin elevation: a sectional matrix is placed inside a modified circumferential matrix with Teflon tape packed between them to seal deep subgingival margins, followed by bonding and 1 to 3 increments of composite. The author states this may avoid …

P0410.t: Marginal sealing of relocated cervical margins of mesio-occluso-distal overlays
P0410.kf: In vitro silver nitrate leakage study of 39 molars with CAD/CAM composite MOD overlays: leakage at the dentin-CMR interface did not differ between hybrid and flowable composites but was significantly lower without CMR, and dentin interfaces leaked more than enamel.

P0411.t: No correlation between two methodological approaches applied to evaluate cervical margin relocation
P0411.kf: In vitro study of cervical margin relocation under CAD/CAM overlays: microleakage scores and SEM marginal integrity showed no significant correlation; non-relocated margins leaked less than relocated ones, and universal adhesive with bulk-fill flowable leaked less than total-etch with flowable.

P0418.t: Fabrication and characterisation of biomimetic nacre-like ceramic/polymer composite a potential CAD/CAM dental material
P0418.j: University of Bristol (PhD thesis, Bristol Dental School)

P0421.t: Composite resin reinforced with pre-tensioned glass fibers. Influence of prestressing on flexural properties
P0421.kf: In vitro three-point bending study of two composite resins with unidirectional glass fibers, with and without pre-tensioning: prestressing significantly increased flexural strength (Adoro 443.46 to 569.15 MPa; Quixfil 425.47 to 568.00 MPa) and deflection at initial failure.

P0422.t: Effects of fiber reinforcement on adaptation and bond strength of a bulk-fill composite in deep preparations
P0422.kf: In vitro SS-OCT and microtensile study of a bulk-fill flowable in deep cavities: cavity-floor gaps were largest without adhesive (2.00), then bulk (0.74) and incremental (0.02), and gap-free with a polyethylene fiber base; MTBS was 13.8 (bulk), 31.7 (incremental) and 28.3 MPa (fiber).

P0426.t: Effect of immediate and delayed dentin sealing on the fracture strength, failure type and Weilbull characteristics of lithiumdisilicate laminate veneers
