P0426.kf: In vitro study of 50 incisors with lithium-disilicate laminate veneers after thermocycling: complete dentin exposure with delayed dentin sealing gave significantly lower fracture strength (314 N) than complete dentin with immediate dentin sealing (576 N; p=0.034).

P0427.t: Immediate Dentin Sealing for Adhesive Cementation of Indirect Restorations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P0427.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 in vitro studies (22 in qualitative analysis; searches to January 2022): immediate dentin sealing improved bond strength to dentin versus delayed sealing for immediate (p < 0.001) and aged (p = 0.001) bond strength. The aged-bond benefit appeared only with three-step …

P0429.t: Immediate Dentin Sealing: A Literature Review
P0429.kf: Literature review of 88 articles (1990-2020) on immediate dentin sealing: IDS appears advantageous for bond strength, gap formation, bacterial microleakage and dentin hypersensitivity, while interactions with impression materials, provisionals and conditioning need further study.

P0430.t: Immediate dentin sealing for indirect bonded restorations
P0430.kf: Review of more than 40 articles on immediate dentine sealing for indirect bonded restorations: IDS appears to achieve improved bond strength, fewer gaps, decreased bacterial leakage and reduced post-cementation sensitivity compared with delayed sealing.

P0433.t: Performance of ceramic laminate veneers with immediate dentine sealing: An 11 year prospective clinical trial
P0433.kf: Prospective 11-year trial of 384 feldspathic laminate veneers in 104 patients: 19 failures (15 fractures, 3 debondings, 1 extraction); with more than 50% dentin exposure, survival was significantly higher with immediate dentin sealing (96.4% vs 81.8%).

P0435.t: Treatment of deep carious lesions by complete excavation or partial removal: a critical review
P0435.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P0435.kf: Critical review of 23 relevant reports from five databases on partial vs complete removal of deep carious lesions: three randomized trials, one with 10-year follow-up, supported leaving infected dentin where removal would risk pulp exposure.

P0437.t: Survival of extensively damaged endodontically treated incisors restored with different types of posts-and-core foundation restoration material
P0437.kf: In vitro fatigue study of 60 decoronated bovine incisors without ferrule restored with glass-fiber or titanium posts and different cores under glass-ceramic crowns: fiber post with bulk-fill core outperformed titanium-post groups, but none matched the 2 mm ferrule group (72667 cycles).

P0439.t: Influence of Alumina Air-Abrasion on Flexural and Shear Bond Strengths of CAD/CAM Composite
P0439.kf: In vitro study of two CAD/CAM composites: alumina air-abrasion significantly increased shear bond strength to resin cement and significantly decreased flexural strength of single bars, but not of bonded double-bar specimens.

P0440.t: Influence of Dentine Pre-Treatment by Sandblasting with Aluminum Oxide in Adhesive Restorations. An In Vitro Study
P0440.kf: In vitro curve test on 32 bovine dentin bars: sandblasting with 50 µm aluminum oxide significantly increased tensile stress at maximum load (84.300 vs 35.071 MPa) and fracture strength (18.543 vs 8.186 MPa) of adhesive restorations versus no sandblasting.

P0441.t: Impact of mucosal phenotype on marginal bone levels around tissue level implants: A prospective controlled trial
P0441.kf: Prospective 1-year study of 30 patients with single tissue-level implants grouped by thin (≤2 mm) or thick (>2 mm) vertical mucosa: 26 completed, survival was 100%, and no significant differences were found in clinical parameters or radiographic marginal bone levels.

P0442.t: American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons position paper on medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw—2014 update
P0442.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P0442.kf: AAOMS 2014 position paper (special committee consensus): proposes renaming to medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) and defines it as exposed or probeable jaw bone persisting over eight weeks in a patient with antiresorptive or antiangiogenic exposure and no jaw radiotherapy or obvious jaw metastasis; it …

P0443.t: American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons’ Position Paper on Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaws—2022 Update
P0443.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P0443.kf: AAOMS 2022 position paper (working-group consensus update): the literature reaffirms MRONJ risk is significantly greater in cancer patients on antiresorptives than in osteoporosis patients, in whom risk remains very low regardless of drug type; the working group could not agree on drug holidays, and both operative and …

P0445.t: Current bonding systems for resin-bonded restorations and fixed partial dentures made of silver–palladium–copper–gold alloy
P0445.kf: Mini narrative review of bonding systems (thione/thiol primers, 4-META/MMA-TBB resin) for restorations and fixed partial dentures made of silver-palladium-copper-gold alloy. The authors conclude clinical performance is overall excellent with currently available noble metal bonding systems, citing case reports with 3 …

P0446.t: Performance of Adhesives and Restorative Materials After Selective Removal of Carious Lesions: Restorative Materials with Anticaries Properties
P0446.kf: Narrative review of restorative materials after selective carious tissue removal: a tight seal over hard dentin and sound enamel is essential, and high-viscosity glass-ionomer cements have the best clinical evidence of caries-arresting effect and sufficient longevity as long-term provisionals.

P0447.t: Does the application of an adhesive layer improve the bond strength of etched and silanized glass-ceramics to resin-based materials? A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0447.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 in vitro studies: an adhesive layer after HF etching and silanization did not significantly change shear/microshear bond strength, and microtensile values were higher without the adhesive in nonaged and aged specimens.

P0448.t: Hybrid layer difference between sixth and seventh generation bonding agent

P0449.t: An Overview of Dental Adhesive Systems and the Dynamic Tooth–Adhesive Interface
P0449.kf: Narrative review of dental adhesive systems and the tooth-adhesive interface. The authors state that adhesive systems remain technique sensitive, resin-tooth interfaces are highly susceptible to degradation (bacteria, endogenous enzymes, resin chemistry), and clinicians must tailor adhesive choice and technique to …

P0450.t: Is Adhesive Bond Strength Similar in Primary and Permanent Teeth? A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
P0450.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 37 in vitro studies: permanent teeth showed higher adhesive bond strength than primary teeth (p = 0.0005), with the same trend in dentin (p = 0.002) but no significant difference in enamel (p = 0.11); most studies had high risk of bias.

P0451.t: What's New in Dentine Bonding?: Universal Adhesives
P0451.kf: Narrative article describing universal bonding agents usable for direct and indirect restorations in self-etch, etch-and-rinse or selective enamel etch modes; laboratory and initial clinical studies are described as promising.

P0454.t: Bond strength of a universal bonding agent and other contemporary dental adhesives applied on enamel, dentin, composite, and porcelain
P0454.kf: In vitro bond strength study (bovine enamel/dentin, composite and porcelain): the universal adhesive was comparable to other contemporary adhesives on enamel and mostly on dentin (lower than Single Bond 2 on dentin, p <= 0.045), matched the silane-plus-adhesive control on composite (28.4 vs 29.5 MPa), and exceeded it …

P0455.t: Dental Cements for Luting and Bonding Restorations: Self-Adhesive Resin Cements
P0455.kf: Narrative review of self-adhesive resin cements. The author states they are popular luting materials with advantages in ease of use, that acidic monomers must be neutralized during setting, and that clinical studies are still insufficient, with early short-term studies suggesting performance similar to conventional …

P0456.t: Universal Adhesives: Setting Characteristics and Reactivity with Dentin
P0456.kf: In vitro study of six universal adhesives: degree of conversion ranged 67.2-82.5%, oxygen inhibition 5.6-18.6 µm, dentin demineralization from 69.3% (G-Premio Bond) to about 10-16% for others, and shear bond characteristic strength 29.3-16.6 MPa.

P0458.kf: Narrative review: caries-affected dentin left after removal of infected dentin differs morphologically, chemically and physically from normal dentin, producing lower bond strength and a poorer-quality hybrid layer prone to hydrolysis.

P0460.kf: Narrative review of ceramic and adhesive technologies. The authors state that ceramic systems have varying degrees of research support, that the role of cement in crown survival is unclear (laboratory data favor resin cements but several clinical studies found survival not influenced by cement type), and that …

P0461.t: Silane Coupling Agents are Beneficial for Resin Composite Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of In Vitro Studies
P0461.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 in vitro studies on direct composite repair: silane before adhesive produced significantly higher repair bond strengths than adhesive alone (p=0.003), with a larger effect for nonhydrolyzed silanes (7.30); heterogeneity was high.

P0462.t: Strength of a Zirconia-Reinforced Lithium Silicate Ceramic: Acid-Etching Time and Resin Cement Application Effects
P0462.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0462.kf: In vitro biaxial flexural study of ZLS discs: without cement, strength increased with HF etching time (250.8, 278.4 and 342.9 MPa at 20, 40 and 60 s), and a resin-cement layer raised 20 s specimens to 341.8 MPa; roughness was unaffected.

P0463.t: Primer for bonding resin to metal
P0463.kf: In vitro study of resin bonded to Ag-Pd, Au-Ag, Co-Cr and titanium with modified primers after 2,000 thermocycles: thiophosphoric or phosphoric methacrylates alone lost Ag-Pd bond strength, while their combination with benzoyl peroxide and heat kept bond strengths over 20 MPa.

P0464.t: Influence of Application Time and Etching Mode of Universal Adhesives on Enamel Adhesion
P0464.kf: In vitro study of five universal adhesives on bovine enamel: etch-and-rinse mode gave significantly higher shear bond strength and roughness than self-etch mode regardless of application time or adhesive, and surface free energy varied with mode, time and adhesive.

P0465.t: Universal Adhesives: The Next Evolution in Adhesive Dentistry?
P0465.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P0465.kf: Continuing-education narrative review of universal adhesives (origin, chemistry, strengths and weaknesses). The author concludes that proper management of the adhesive interface requires understanding the materials, substrate and protocol, and that universal adhesives represent an exciting, promising new class that …

P0466.t: Effect of two metal primers on adhesive bonding with type IV gold alloys
P0466.kf: In vitro study of an adhesive resin bonded to a type IV gold alloy and an age-hardenable gold alloy: both a vinyl-thiol and a thiophosphate metal primer effectively enhanced the resin-alloy bond.

P0471.t: Influence of soft tissue thickness on marginal bone level around dental implants: A systematic review with meta-analysis and trial-sequential analysis
P0471.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis of 6 controlled studies (354 implants, 10-14 months): implants with <2 mm soft tissue thickness had significantly more marginal bone loss than ≥2 mm (0.54; p = .027), with high heterogeneity.

P0474.t: Peri-implant soft tissue phenotype modification and its impact on peri-implant health: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
P0474.kf: Systematic review of 52 articles with network meta-analysis of 23 RCTs on peri-implant soft tissue phenotype modification: bilaminar CTG or ADM gave the greatest mucosal thickness gain, and apically positioned flap with FGG was most effective for keratinized mucosa width.

P0475.t: Relationship between cortical bone thickness and implant stability at the time of surgery and secondary stability after osseointegration measured using resonance frequency analysis
P0475.kf: Retrospective study of 229 implants in 113 patients: mean ISQ was 69.34 at placement and 75.99 after osseointegration; mandibular and non-augmented sites had significantly higher ISQ, and cortical bone thickness correlated weakly and positively with stability.

P0478.t: The Effect of Inter-Implant Distance on the Height of Inter-Implant Bone Crest
P0478.kf: Radiographic study of 36 patients with two adjacent implants: lateral bone loss was 1.34-1.40 mm from the implant shoulders, and crestal bone loss was 1.04 mm when implants were 3 mm or less apart versus 0.45 mm when more than 3 mm apart.

P0480.t: Bone loss-related factors in tissue and bone level dental implants: a systematic review of clinical trials
P0480.j: Journal of the Korean Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
P0480.kf: Systematic review of 38 clinical studies on bone changes around bone-level and tissue-level implants (18 bone-level only, 10 tissue-level, 10 both): methodologies, follow-ups and bone-loss factors varied so widely that direct comparison was impossible.

P0482.t: Analogical and Digital Workflow in the Design and Preparation of the Emergence Profile of Biologically Oriented Preparation Technique (BOPT) Crowns over Implants in the Working Model
P0482.kf: Technical note describing analogical (plaster) and digital workflows for designing the emergence profile of BOPT crowns over implants on the working model. The authors report chair time was about 8% higher with the analogical workflow, and conclude the digital approach is the most realistic option while the analogical …

P0484.t: Comparison of horizontal and vertical methods of tooth preparation for a prosthetic crown
P0484.j: Journal of Pre-Clinical and Clinical Research
P0484.kf: Narrative review comparing horizontal finish lines and vertical (verti prep) tooth preparations for crowns, noting that the choice of finish line depends on pulp vitality, tooth location and inclination, restorative material, crown convexity and patient age.

P0485.t: Influence of Biologically Oriented Preparation Technique on Peri-Implant Tissues; Prospective Randomized Clinical Trial with Three-Year Follow-Up. Part I: Hard Tissues
P0485.kf: Prospective RCT of 75 single posterior implants restored with screw-retained crowns, cemented BOPT crowns without finishing line, or conventional cemented crowns: after 3 years of loading, BOPT crowns showed the least peri-implant bone loss (p < 0.01).

P0486.t: Biologically oriented preparation technique (BOPT): a new approach for prosthetic restoration of periodontically healthy teeth
P0486.j: The European Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0486.kf: Technique article presenting the biologically oriented preparation technique (BOPT), a vertical feather-edge preparation without a finish line for periodontally healthy teeth. The authors report, from up to 15 years of their own clinical experience, stable pericoronal soft tissues in anterior and posterior areas on …

P0489.t: Biologically oriented preparation technique (BOPT) for implant-supported fixed prostheses
P0489.j: Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry
P0489.kf: Case report (58-year-old patient) applying BOPT to three conical-collar implants and prepared teeth with cemented metal-ceramic and zirconia restorations; at follow-ups of 3, 6, 12 and 24 months no mechanical, esthetic or biological complications were noted, with excellent peri-implant tissue health at 6 months.

P0491.t: Periodontal and prosthetic outcomes on teeth prepared with biologically oriented preparation technique: a 4-year follow-up prospective clinical study
P0491.kf: Prospective 4-year study of 149 teeth prepared with BOPT and restored with zirconia-ceramic crowns or FPDs: restoration survival 96.6%, marginal stability 98.6%, gingival thickening increased 32.5%, bleeding on probing in 12%, and complications 2% biological and 1.4% mechanical.

P0496.t: Adhesion of Veneering Porcelain to Zirconium Dioxide Ceramic as Determined by the Strain Energy Release Rate
P0496.kf: In vitro four-point bending delamination test of 5 VITA VM 9 porcelain-zirconia bilayers: mean strain energy release rate was 12.4 J/m2, with cracks running straight along the interface in all specimens, indicating adhesive fracture.

P0500.t: Implementing Digital Dentistry into Your Esthetic Dental Practice
P0500.kf: Narrative review of implementing digital dentistry (intraoral scanners, digital radiography, 3D printing, milling, digital smile design) in an esthetic practice. The authors conclude digital dentistry could be a great addition but has drawbacks (cost, lack of standardized workflows), and cite increased communication, …

P0501.t: Influence of scan body design and digital implant analogs on implant replica position in additively manufactured casts
P0501.kf: In vitro study of AM polymer casts from three scan body/digital replica systems versus conventional stone casts (n=10 each): AM groups had lower 3D discrepancies, conventional casts were better apicocoronally, and scan body design influenced only angular accuracy.

P0503.t: The potential of additive manufacturing technologies and their processing parameters for the fabrication of all-ceramic crowns: A review
P0503.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0503.kf: Literature review of additive manufacturing for all-ceramic crowns covering five technologies (stereolithography, material extrusion, powder-based fusion, direct inkjet printing, binder jetting) and their processing parameters and experimental outcomes.

P0507.t: Zirconia-Based Ceramics: Material Properties, Esthetics, and Layering Techniques of a New Veneering Porcelain, VM9
P0507.kf: Technique and materials article on zirconia frameworks and the VM9 veneering porcelain. The authors report from in-house laboratory testing that finer-grained veneering porcelains (VM9, VM7, Omega 900) showed lower enamel wear and higher flexural strength than other veneering porcelains, and describe core design and a …

P0508.t: Dental implant treatment in patients with cancer on high-dose antiresorptive medication: A prospective feasibility study with 2 years follow-up
P0508.kf: Prospective feasibility study of 22 cancer patients on high-dose antiresorptive medication with 39 implants: 13 patients (23 implants) completed 2 years, with 100% survival and 97.4% success; quality of life improved and two MRONJ cases were unrelated to implants.

P0509.t: Clinical and radiographic outcomes of implant‐supported fixed dental prostheses with cantilever extension. A retrospective cohort study with a follow‐up of at least 10 years
P0509.kf: Retrospective cohort of 26 patients with 30 posterior cantilevered implant FDPs on 60 implants after a mean 13.3 years: one diameter-reduced implant fractured (patient-based survival 96.2%), and mean marginal bone level change was not statistically significant (1.2 to 1.6 mm).

P0513.t: Influence of crown-implant ratio on implant success rates and crestal bone levels: A 36-month follow-up prospective study
P0513.kf: Prospective study of 259 sintered porous-surface implants in 136 patients over 36 months: success rate 98.1% and mean peri-implant bone loss 0.48 mm; C/I ratio correlated significantly with success and bone loss, with thresholds of 3.10 (anatomical) and 3.40 (clinical).

P0514.t: Clinical and radiographic changes at implants supporting single‐unit crowns (SCs) and fixed dental prostheses (FDPs) with one cantilever extension. A retrospective study
P0514.kf: Retrospective study of 19 implant-supported single crowns and 21 two-implant FDPs with one cantilever extension in posterior jaws (mean 78.2 and 67.8 months): no implant loss occurred, giving 100% survival.

P0515.t: Does the Presence of a Cantilever Influence the Survival and Success of Partial Implant-Supported Dental Prostheses? Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P0515.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0515.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 clinical studies: cantilevers did not compromise marginal bone loss or survival of partial implant-supported fixed prostheses, while prostheses without cantilevers showed significantly more minor complications (P = .008).

P0516.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0516.kf: Systematic review of 19 articles (14 human clinical studies, 1-10 years) on distal cantilevers in fixed complete implant prostheses: weighted prosthetic survival was 95% over 7.3 years, and screw loosening was the most frequent complication.

P0518.t: Implant supported cantilevered fixed dental rehabilitations in partially edentulous patients: Systematic review of the literature. Part I.
P0518.kf: Systematic review of 9 papers on cantilevered implant fixed restorations in partially edentulous patients (≥5-year follow-up): estimated 5-10-year survival was 98.4% for implants and 99.2% for rehabilitations, with cumulative complication rates of 28.66% (patients) and 26.57% (prostheses).

P0519.t: The impact of cantilevers on biological and technical success outcomes of implant‐supported fixed partial dentures. A retrospective cohort study
P0519.kf: Retrospective cohort comparing 128 cantilever FDPs (132 implants) with 144 non-cantilever FDPs (203 implants) over about 4 years: implant survival/success 96.7%/87.9% vs 99.5%/92.6%, with no significant overall bone-loss difference but more bone loss for cantilever implants in the posterior mandible.

P0520.t: An In Vivo Study on Load Distribution in Different Implant Configurations for Supporting Fixed Partial Dentures
P0520.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0520.kf: In vivo measurement with piezoelectric transducers in one patient with three mandibular implants, testing four three-unit FPD configurations: loads were evenly distributed with three implants and central pontic, while high loads occurred on the first molar with posterior or anterior cantilevers.

P0521.t: Systematic review of the survival rate and the biological, technical, and aesthetic complications of fixed dental prostheses with cantilevers on implants reported in longitudinal studies with a mean of 5 years follow-up
P0521.kf: Systematic review of 6 studies (≥5-year mean follow-up) on implant cantilever FDPs: implant survival 98.9% and prosthesis survival about 97.1%; 5-year biological complications 5.7%, veneer fractures 10.1%, screw loosening 7.9% and implant fracture 0.7%.

P0522.t: Accuracy of implant placement in the posterior maxillary region depending on the alveolar residual bone height and sinus morphology: An in vitro study
P0522.kf: In vitro study of 180 implants placed free-handed or with static computer-assisted placement in maxillary models with three residual bone heights and different sinus morphologies: guided placement was more accurate and unaffected by anatomy, whereas free-hand accuracy was affected by bone height and sinus morphology.

P0523.t: Should Cone Beam Computed Tomography Be Routinely Obtained in Implant Planning?
P0523.kf: Narrative review: CBCT provides 3-D visualization of the alveolar ridge with accurate linear measurements at lower radiation dose than conventional CT, aiding diagnosis and planning, particularly in complex implant cases.

P0524.t: Effect of cementation and aging on the marginal fit of veneered and monolithic zirconia and metal-ceramic CAD-CAM crowns
P0524.kf: In vitro SEM study of 72 metal-ceramic, veneered zirconia and monolithic zirconia CAD-CAM crowns: marginal discrepancy did not differ among groups or with cementation or aging; after 20 h aging monoclinic phase rose to 8.3% (veneered) and 3.1% (monolithic).

P0526.t: Evaluation of the Effect of Fluoride-containing Luting Cements on Titanium and Its Effect on the Shear Bond Strength
P0526.kf: In vitro shear bond study of commercially pure titanium grades and Ti-6Al-4V luted to molar dentin with zinc polycarboxylate, glass ionomer or zinc phosphate cement: polycarboxylate gave high shear bond strength but corrosion of the titanium alloy was observed.

P0527.t: Effect of seating force, margin design, and cement on marginal seal and retention of complete metal crowns
P0527.kf: In vitro study of silver-palladium crowns on chamfer, shoulder and beveled-shoulder dies cemented with zinc phosphate or glass ionomer at 25-300 N: higher seating force improved seating but not retention; shoulder finish lines and glass ionomer gave greater retention.

P0529.t: Effects of cement, cement space, marginal design, seating aid materials, and seating force on crown cementation
P0529.kf: In vitro study of cast crowns on shoulder and beveled-shoulder dies: die spacer, a heavier 30 lb seating force and glass ionomer cement significantly improved crown seating, and the beveled preparation gave superior seating with heavier force or glass ionomer.

P0530.t: Resin composite cements: Current status and a novel classification proposal
P0530.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0530.kf: Literature and market review of resin composite cements proposing a classification: (1) adhesive/multi-step, (2) self-adhesive/one-step, and (3) universal cements, defined as those paired with a universal adhesive usable as tooth and restorative primer.

P0531.t: Influence of Novel Experimental Light-Cured Resin Cement on Microtensile Bond Strength
P0531.kf: In vitro study bonding CAD/CAM resin blocks to 18 molar dentin surfaces: resin cement type significantly affected immediate and 7-day microtensile bond strength, and the experimental light-cured cement showed higher Knoop hardness than Panavia V5.

P0532.t: Effects of precementation on minimizing residual cement around the marginal area of dental implants
P0532.kf: In vitro study of 50 Co-Cr abutment/crown pairs: precementation abutments reduced by 50 µm or more gave higher cement weight in the cement space and better marginal sealing than 25 µm, and 50 µm precementation reduced subgingival residual cement without affecting retention.

P0533.t: Influence of collar height of definitive restoration and type of luting cement on the amount of residual cement in implant restorations: A clinical study
P0533.kf: Clinical study of 30 single premolar implants grouped by collar height (<2, 2-4, >4 mm), each tested with three cements: residual excess cement rose from 0.08-0.33 mm (low) to 1.31-2.33 mm (high collar), and zinc oxide noneugenol left significantly less than resin or GIC.

P0536.t: An Overview of the Development and Strengthening of All-Ceramic Dental Materials
P0536.kf: Literature review of the development and strengthening of all-ceramic materials and systems for fixed partial dentures, covering materials, technologies, survival, strength, color and esthetics.

P0541.t: Evolution of Dental Ceramic from the Platinum Foil to CAD-CAM Technologies: Review
P0541.j: International Journal of Dentistry and Oral Science
P0541.kf: Narrative historical review of dental ceramics from platinum foil to CAD-CAM. The authors conclude that advances in composition, high-strength ceramics and fabrication methods have increased the longevity of ceramic restorations while maintaining acceptable esthetics, allowing metal-free restorations in anterior and …

P0542.t: A new classification system for all-ceramic and ceramic-like restorative materials
P0542.kf: Classification proposal grouping ceramic and ceramic-like restorative materials into three families by phase composition: glass-matrix ceramics, polycrystalline ceramics and resin-matrix ceramics, each with subfamilies, plus manufacturers' indications and fabrication methods.

P0543.t: The Platinum Foil Technique: History, Indication, Fabrication, and Adaptation
P0543.kf: Technique report on the platinum foil technique for porcelain veneers (history, indications, fabrication, adaptation) illustrated with four clinical cases. The authors state, citing earlier studies, that platinum foil restorations show marginal fit equal to or better than pressed, milled or refractory-die veneers and …

P0546.t: Lithium Silicate-Based Glass Ceramics in Dentistry: A Narrative Review
P0546.kf: Narrative review of novel lithium silicate-based glass ceramics: considerable evidence supports mechanical and esthetic competency of zirconia-reinforced lithium silicates and lithium-aluminium disilicates, while biocompatibility data are scarce; acid neutralisation and plasma treatment showed promising adhesion.

P0549.t: Overview of Several Typical Ceramic Materials for Restorative Dentistry
P0549.kf: Narrative review comparing resin-based ceramics, polycrystalline ceramics and silicate ceramics for prosthodontics, with their advantages, disadvantages and indications.

P0550.t: Dental Ceramics for Restoration and Metal Veneering
P0550.kf: Narrative review of dental ceramics for restoration and metal veneering (history, porcelain, glass-ceramics, polycrystalline ceramics, design considerations). The authors state that composition, microstructure and properties determine clinical indications and that successful ceramic restorations ultimately depend on …

P0552.t: Prospective randomized clinical trial evaluating the effects of two different implant collar designs on peri‐implant healing and functional osseointegration after 25 years
P0552.kf: Clinical trial of 22 participants (110 interforaminal implants under full-arch prostheses) after 23-26 years: microtextured implants with a 3.6 mm machined collar lost significantly more bone (-1.77 mm) than implants with a 1.2 mm collar, machined (-0.85 mm) or microtextured (-1.00 mm).

P0553.t: Impact of design elements of the implant supracrestal complex (ISC) on the risk of peri‐implant mucositis and peri‐implantitis: A critical review
P0553.kf: Critical review of seven focus questions on implant supracrestal complex design: emerging evidence links emergence angle with convex emergence profile to peri-implantitis at bone-level implants, sulcus depth ≥3 mm reduces mucositis treatment effectiveness, and prosthesis contour modification aids mucositis treatment.

P0554.t: A New Definition of Attached Gingiva Around Teeth and Implants in Healthy and Diseased Sites
P0554.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0554.kf: Proposes a two-part definition of attached gingiva: with supracrestal biologic width (healthy teeth, tissue-level implants) measured from sulcus base to the mucogingival junction, and with subcrestal biologic width (infrabony defects, bone-level implants) measured from the bone crest.

P0555.t: A comparison of ceramic crown color difference between different shade selection methods: Visual, digital camera, and smartphone
P0555.kf: Clinical study of 45 patients receiving lithium-disilicate crowns: mean color difference to the adjacent tooth was 5.32 with visual shade selection versus 2.75 with digital camera and 2.34 with smartphone plus light-correcting device (both significantly lower, not different from each other).

P0556.t: Dimensional changes of complete dentures fabricated by milled and printed techniques: An in vitro study
P0556.kf: In vitro study of maxillary and mandibular complete dentures: CAD-CAM-milled dentures showed the smallest dimensional deviations and best reproducibility, while 3D-printed dentures varied with build angle and postprocessing, a 90-degree build with light polymerization on the cast performing best.

P0560.t: Occurrence and clustering of complications in implant dentistry
P0560.kf: Cohort of 596 patients with implant-supported reconstructions followed for 9 years: 42% had technical and/or biological complications; partial (HR 2.5) and full-jaw restorations (HR 3.9) and periodontitis history (HR 1.6) were risk factors, and peri-implantitis and implant loss clustered with other complications.

P0562.kf: Narrative review of light curing in dentistry. The author states that undercuring decreases bond strengths, increases bulk fracture and wear and raises leached chemicals, that many clinicians lack understanding of what is needed for successful curing, and gives selection criteria for curing lights and 7 clinical …

P0563.t: Gingival phenotype modification therapies on natural teeth: A network meta‐analysis
P0563.kf: Network meta-analysis of 105 RCTs (95 root coverage, 3,539 recessions; 10 non-root coverage, 699 sites). Any graft increased gingival thickness; keratinized tissue rose with CTG and ADM in root coverage, and with ADM, CM, FGG and LCC in non-root coverage; autogenous grafts (CTG/FGG) were superior for both outcomes.

P0575.t: Editorial: Significance of Peri-implant Keratinized Mucosa Width and Soft Tissue Thickness
P0575.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0575.kf: Editorial reviewing evidence on peri-implant keratinized mucosa and soft tissue thickness; it argues keratinized mucosa aids hygiene and peri-implant health and advises a minimum soft tissue thickness of 2 mm to prevent dehiscence.

P0580.t: Design of customized soft tissue substitutes for posterior single-tooth defects: a proof-of-concept in vitro study
P0580.kf: Proof-of-concept digital study of 33 casts from 30 patients designing soft-tissue substitutes for single posterior defects; three average shapes were identified, with highest thickness (median 2 mm) buccally above the ridge and 0.2 mm at the edges.

P0582.t: Do soft tissue augmentation techniques provide stable and favorable peri-implant conditions in the medium and long term? A systematic review
P0582.kf: Systematic review of 15 prospective studies with ≥36 months follow-up after peri-implant soft tissue augmentation; survival was high, peri-implant mucositis ranged 0–50% and peri-implantitis 0–7.14%, and soft tissue margin and bone levels were mostly stable.

P0584.t: Effect of peri-implant mucosal thickness on esthetic outcomes and the efficacy of soft tissue augmentation procedures: Consensus report of group 2 of the SEPA/DGI/OF workshop
P0584.kf: SEPA/DGI/OF consensus report (group 2) based on two systematic reviews on peri-implant mucosal thickness and soft tissue augmentation; it found a tendency toward superior esthetic outcomes with thick peri-implant mucosa.

P0585.t: Effectiveness of soft tissue augmentation procedures for coverage of buccal soft tissue dehiscence around dental implants. A systematic review
P0585.kf: Systematic review of 7 articles (one high-risk-of-bias RCT) on coverage of buccal soft tissue dehiscence at implants; exploratory meta-analyses showed complete coverage in 70% of cases at 1 year (2 studies, n = 36) and 5 years (3 studies, n = 54).

P0588.t: Effects of soft tissue augmentation procedures on peri-implant health or disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0588.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis (4 keratinized tissue studies, 6 mucosal thickness studies); keratinized tissue grafting improved gingival index (WMD = 0.863) and APF plus autogenous graft gave higher bone levels, while thickness grafting reduced marginal bone loss (WMD = 0.110) without improving bleeding indices.

P0596.t: Immediate Implant Placement and Provisionalization With and Without a Connective Tissue Graft: An Analysis of Facial Gingival Tissue Thickness
P0596.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0596.kf: Comparative study of immediate implant placement and provisionalization in the anterior maxilla with or without subepithelial CTG; facial gingival tissue thickness at prosthesis delivery and its change were significantly greater in the CTG group.

P0598.t: Influence of soft tissue augmentation procedures around dental implants on marginal bone level changes-A systematic review
P0598.kf: Systematic review of 20 publications (16 comparisons, two meta-analyses); soft tissue augmentation inconsistently affected marginal bone level changes vs none but consistently improved secondary outcomes, and combined soft and hard augmentation reduced soft tissue recession without bone-level difference.

P0600.t: Evidence‐based knowledge on the aesthetics and maintenance of peri‐implant soft tissues: Osteology Foundation Consensus Report Part 3—Aesthetics of peri‐implant soft tissues
P0600.kf: Osteology Foundation consensus (Working Group 2) based on two systematic reviews; for single implants (12 studies) the crestal bone to contact point distance ranged from 2 to 11 mm and papilla fill was reached in 56.5% to 100% of cases.

P0604.t: Minimal invasiveness in soft tissue augmentation at dental implants: A systematic review and meta-analysis of patient-reported outcome measures
P0604.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 studies comparing soft tissue substitutes with SCTG at implants; substitutes reduced pain, painkiller use (WMD = 1.56 tablets) and surgery time (WMD = 10.9 minutes), with no differences in satisfaction, esthetics or OHIP-14.

P0612.t: Soft tissue contour changes at implant sites with or without soft tissue grafting in the esthetic zone: A retrospective case–control study with a 12-year follow-up
P0612.kf: Retrospective comparison of 18 patients with esthetic-zone implants and GBR, with (8) or without (10) subsequent SCTG, re-assessed after a median 144.5 months; mid-buccal contour reduction was -0.81 mm vs -0.56 mm (p = .607) and no peri-implantitis occurred.

P0621.t: Volumetric analysis on the use of customized healing abutments with or without connective tissue graft at flapless maxillary immediate implant placement: A randomized clinical trial
P0621.kf: RCT of 32 patients with flapless maxillary immediate implants and customized healing abutments, with or without CTG; at 12 months no significant group differences overall, but with buccal bone ≤1 mm buccal volume change was -14.18% (control) vs -8.30% (CTG) (p = .033).

P0626.t: Crestal Bone Changes Around Implants With Reduced Abutment Diameter Placed Non‐Submerged and at Subcrestal Positions: A 1‐Year Radiographic Evaluation
P0626.kf: Retrospective review of 50 consecutive partially edentulous patients with non-submerged implants placed about 1.37 mm (mesial) and 1.28 mm (distal) subcrestally; at 1 year survival was 100% and mean marginal hard tissue loss 0.11 ± 0.30 mm.

P0627.t: Effects of implant diameter, implant-abutment connection type, and bone density on the biomechanical stability of implant components and bone: A finite element analysis study
P0627.kf: 3D finite element analysis of 12 mandibular first molar models varying bone density, connection type (tissue-level vs bone-level internal) and diameter (3.5–4.5 mm); bone-level connection increased implant/abutment peak stress, smaller diameter concentrated stress, and low-density bone increased strain.

P0630.t: Marginal bone level changes in association with different vertical implant positions: a 3-year retrospective study
P0630.kf: Retrospective radiographic study of 143 implants in 61 patients; at 36 months after loading marginal bone change was 0.99±1.45, 1.13±0.91 and 1.76±0.78 mm for implant-abutment interface above, at and below bone level, greater for the subcrestal group.

P0632.t: Cone Beam Computed Tomographic Evaluation of Implants with Platform-Switched Morse Taper Connection with the Implant-Abutment Interface at Different Levels in Relation to the Alveolar Crest
P0632.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0632.kf: CBCT analysis of 30 patients randomized to platform-switched Morse taper implants at crest level or 1 or 2 mm subcrestally; at 12 months buccal bone remodeling was -0.08 mm (crestal) vs -0.65 and -0.85 mm (subcrestal), with no difference in first bone-to-implant contact.

P0634.t: Mechanical complications of implant-supported restorations with internal conical connection implants: A 14-year retrospective study
P0634.kf: Retrospective 14-year study of 428 patients with 898 internal conical connection implants; mechanical complications affected 47.9% of implants, mainly screw loosening (46.4%), with highest risk for molar restorations (HR 12.82) and men (HR 2.00).

P0635.t: Effect of the geometry of butt-joint implant-supported restorations on the fatigue life of prosthetic screws
P0635.kf: In vitro ISO 14801 fatigue testing (48 tests) of four BTI butt-joint designs; a 1 mm larger implant body diameter gave an average 3.5-fold longer prosthetic screw fatigue life and a 1.4 mm larger connection diameter about 7-fold, with no internal vs external connection difference.

P0640.t: Performance of conical abutment (Morse Taper) connection implants: A systematic review
P0640.j: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research Part A
P0640.kf: Systematic review of 52 in vitro and in vivo studies comparing conical vs non-conical implant-abutment connections (no meta-analysis due to heterogeneity); both resisted bending and fatigue in vitro, while conical abutments were superior in seal, microgap, torque maintenance and abutment stability.

P0641.t: Micro-leakage at the implant-abutment interface with different tightening torques in vitro
P0641.kf: In vitro study of external hexagon implant-abutment assemblies inoculated with bacteria and tightened at 10, 20 or 32 Ncm (n = 9 each) over 14 days; torque did not significantly affect microleakage, though no 32 Ncm sample was contaminated.

P0646.t: Dental implant suprastructures using cobalt–chromium alloy compared with gold alloy framework veneered with ceramic or acrylic resin: a retrospective cohort study up to 18 years
P0646.kf: Retrospective chart audit of 198 patients with 270 implant-supported FDPs on 1117 implants (mean follow-up 120 months, up to 220) comparing cobalt-chromium vs type 3 gold frameworks veneered with ceramic or acrylic; success, survival and complication rates were similar.

P0650.t: Dental care during COVID‐19 pandemic: Survey of experts’ opinion
P0650.kf: Anonymous online survey of 27 oral surgery experts from European countries (April–May 2020); all but two considered SARS-CoV-2 transmission risk high for aerosol-generating procedures, and more than 80% recommended face protection and caps for every treatment.

P0652.t: Sources of SARS-CoV-2 and Other Microorganisms in Dental Aerosols
P0652.kf: Microbiome and RT-qPCR study of aerosols from ultrasonic scaling, implant osteotomy and restorative procedures; 78% of microbiota in condensate traced to the dental irrigant, saliva contributed a median 0%, and only low copy numbers of SARS-CoV-2 were identified.

P0657.t: ADA Return to Work Interim Guidance Toolkit
P0657.kf: Interim toolkit from the ADA Advisory Task Force on Dental Practice Recovery (updated 4/24/2020) for reopening for non-emergent care: patient pre-screening and in-office screening, reception and chairside checklists, staff protection strategies, and a shopping list.

P0660.t: COVID‐19: Review of European recommendations and experts’ opinion on dental care. Summary and consensus statements of group 5. The 6th EAO Consensus Conference 2021
P0660.kf: EAO consensus (group 5) based on a comparison of European national guidelines and an expert survey on infection control in dentistry during COVID-19; guidelines were rapidly updated and not based on solid evidence, so were supplemented by expert opinion.

P0662.t: Dental care during COVID‐19 pandemic: Follow‐up survey of experts' opinion
P0662.kf: Follow-up online survey of 26 European oral surgery experts during the second wave (Nov 2020–Feb 2021); overall transmission risk was rated significantly lower than in the first survey, though aerosol-generating procedures were still considered high risk and 80.8% recommended FFP2/FFP3 masks.

P0663.t: Summary of European guidelines on infection control and prevention during COVID‐19 pandemic
P0663.kf: Comparison of COVID-19 dental infection-control guidelines from 30 European countries with WHO, ECDC and CDC recommendations; all 30 recommended triage and postponing non-urgent care, 24/30 recommended 1%–1.5% hydrogen peroxide mouth rinse, and 25/30 FFP2/FFP3 masks for AGP.

P0666.t: Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities, 2008 (Update: May 2019)
P0666.j: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (HICPAC)
P0666.kf: CDC/HICPAC evidence-based guideline on cleaning, disinfection and sterilization of patient-care devices and the healthcare environment. It states that, properly used, these processes can reduce infection risk from invasive and noninvasive devices, and that choice of disinfectant, concentration and exposure time …

P0675.t: Persian-language guide to dental practice during the COVID-19 epidemic (update 1, 'In memory of Dr. Albert Bruce Sabin')

P0678.t: Reopening dentistry after COVID-19: Complete suppression of aerosolization in dental procedures by viscoelastic Medusa Gorgo
P0678.kf: Laboratory and mannequin fluid-mechanics study: adding a high molecular weight FDA-approved polymer (e.g., PAA) to irrigation water gives viscoelastic solutions that markedly suppress or completely eliminate aerosol (droplet) generation from an ultrasonic scaler and dental handpiece compared with water.

P0682.t: The effectiveness of an aerosol reduction device for ultrasonic scalers
P0682.kf: Randomized split-mouth study in 12 adults of 5-minute ultrasonic scaling with or without an aerosol reduction device; mean CFUs 6 inches from the mouth were 45.1 ± 28.9 without vs 2.6 ± 3.6 with the device (P < 0.001), with no face-shield difference.

P0688.t: Evaluation of the effect of hydrogen peroxide as a mouthwash in comparison with chlorhexidine in chronic periodontitis patients: A clinical study
P0688.j: Journal of International Society of Preventive and Community Dentistry
P0688.kf: Clinical study of 45 patients with mild to moderate chronic periodontitis treated with SRP alone, SRP plus 0.2% CHX or SRP plus 1.5% H2O2 mouthwash for 10 days; both mouthwashes reduced gingival index more than control and similarly to each other.

P0689.t: Airborne hydrogen peroxide for disinfection of the hospital environment and infection control: a systematic review
P0689.kf: Systematic review of ten studies on airborne hydrogen peroxide (vapour or dry mist) for hospital disinfection; contaminated sites fell from 39.0% before cleaning to 28.3% after terminal cleaning and 2.2% after airborne hydrogen peroxide.

P0698.t: Hydrogen Peroxide: A Review of Its Use in Dentistry
P0698.kf: Review of hydrogen peroxide safety in oral hygiene; daily use of 3% H2O2 or less for up to 6 years produced only occasional transitory irritation, whereas high-level bleaching agents can cause localized oral toxicity with sustained exposure if mishandled.

P0701.t: Antiviral Effect of Chlorine Dioxide against Influenza Virus and Its Application for Infection Control
P0701.kf: Review by a manufacturer's authors of chlorine dioxide against influenza: in vitro, 10 ppm solution gave 99.999% or greater inactivation in 1% serum; in mice, 0.03 ppm gas lowered lung virus titre and mortality was 0/10 versus 7/10 in controls (P=0.002).

P0706.t: Living with a killer: the effects of hypochlorous acid on mammalian cells
P0706.kf: Review of how hypochlorous acid produced by phagocytes interacts with mammalian cells; higher doses cause necrosis and lower doses apoptosis or growth arrest, with glutathione and protein thiols as preferred targets of sublethal amounts.

P0718.t: A 10-year prospective study on single immediate implants
P0718.kf: Prospective study of 22 consecutive patients with flapless single immediate implants and DBBM socket grafting in the esthetic zone (18 re-examined at 10 years); marginal bone loss was 0.31 mm, but 33% showed ≥1 mm mid-facial recession and 17% had no visible buccal bone on CBCT.

P0719.t: Anterior implant restorations with a convex emergence profile increase the frequency of recession: 12-month results of a randomized controlled clinical trial
P0719.kf: RCT of 47 patients with single anterior implants allocated to convex or concave provisional/crown profiles or no provisional; at 12 months mucosal recession occurred in 64.3% (convex), 14.3% (concave) and 31.4% (control), with convex profile OR 12.6 vs concave.

P0720.t: Assessment of Peri-implant Soft Tissue Adaptive Pressure and Time After Provisional Restorations
P0720.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0720.kf: Clinical video study of 25 single implant sites receiving interim restorations 2 weeks after stage-two surgery; gingival colour changes at 10 min vs 0 min and vs adjacent tooth gingiva were within clinically acceptable colour difference.

P0721.t: Association of prosthetic features and peri-implantitis: A cross-sectional study
P0721.kf: Cross-sectional analysis of 169 patients (349 implants) with radiographs at 1 and 5 years; emergence angle correlated with bone loss, and peri-implantitis was more prevalent with EA ≥ 30 degrees, convex profile and middle splinted bone-level implants, but not tissue-level implants.

P0723.t: Considerations of Implant Abutment and Crown Contour: Critical Contour and Subcritical Contour
P0723.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0723.kf: Pilot case series and clinical observations defining critical and subcritical contour of implant abutments and crowns: changes to subcritical contour within a physiologic range did not significantly alter gingival margin level, whereas critical contour changes did; convex subcritical contour increased papilla height …

P0726.t: Effects of crown contour on artificial biofilm removal efficacy with interdental cleaning aids: An in vitro study
P0726.kf: In vitro study in which 30 volunteers cleaned artificial biofilm from concave, straight and convex implant crowns on mandibular models; concave crowns were cleaned best at the basal surface, and floss (43.02%) and superfloss (42.51%) outperformed other aids, with the water flosser lowest (9.72%).

P0734.t: Systematic review of the survival rate and the incidence of biological, technical, and aesthetic complications of single crowns on implants reported in longitudinal studies with a mean follow-up of 5 years
P0734.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 46 studies on implant-supported single crowns; implant survival was 97.2% at 5 years and 95.2% at 10 years, crown survival 96.3% and 89.4%, with 5-year screw-loosening 8.8% and aesthetic complications 7.1%.

P0735.t: The Impact of 3D Implant Position on Emergence Profile Design
P0735.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0735.kf: Narrative review with one clinical scenario: abutment emergence profile design is influenced by implant depth, interproximal position, bodily position and axial inclination (Table 1 links each position to a design); the authors conclude implant position and soft tissue conditions determine emergence profile design.

P0737.t: Full digital workflow for crown lengthening by using a single surgical guide
P0737.kf: Technique report: a free-software digital workflow (intraoral scan, CBCT and designed tooth shape superimposed) produces one 3D-printed guide whose 3-mm average labial band marks both the marginal incision and the level of alveolar crest repositioning for crown lengthening.

P0739.t: A digitally guided dual technique for both gingival and bone resection during crown lengthening surgery
P0739.kf: Technique report: a digitally guided dual technique uses a printed gingivectomy guide and an alveolectomy guide, designed so the alveolar crest lies 3 mm from the planned gingival margin, to guide soft and bone resection in esthetic crown lengthening; described in one patient.

P0740.t: A Standardized Approach for the Early Restorative Phase After Esthetic Crown-Lengthening Surgery
P0740.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0740.kf: Case series of two esthetic crown-lengthening cases proposing a standardized early restorative protocol: abutments prepared supragingivally 3 weeks after surgery with provisionals progressively modified (contact point shifted 1 mm coronally at set visits) to condition papillae; final impression chosen at about 6 …

P0741.t: Aesthetic crown lengthening: classification, biologic rationale, and treatment planning considerations
P0741.kf: Narrative review proposing a four-type classification of esthetic crown lengthening based on the relation of the alveolar crest to the planned gingival margin, with treatment sequences (including staged approaches for types II and III) and an esthetic blueprint with surgical guide.

P0742.t: Aesthetic Crown Lengthening Using Chu Aesthetic Gauges And Evaluation of Biologic Width Healing
P0742.j: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
P0742.kf: Clinical study of 15 patients (30 teeth needing crown lengthening plus 60 adjacent teeth) treated with Chu aesthetic gauges and followed for 6 months; biologic width re-established to original vertical levels by three months and stabilized by six months.

P0744.t: CAD/CAM techniques help in the rebuilding of ideal marginal gingiva contours of anterior maxillary teeth: A case report
P0744.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P0744.kf: Case report of a woman with gingival inflammation and asymmetric anterior maxillary gingival contours from crowns violating biological width, treated with 3D-printed template-guided crown lengthening and CAD/CAM interim crowns that induced 0.5 to 1.5 mm papilla growth.

P0745.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P0745.kf: Literature review with a clinical case on periodontal crown lengthening; wound-healing studies report about 3 mm of supragingival soft tissue rebounding coronal to the crest, requiring at least three months for vertical growth.

P0746.t: 3D-Printed Surgical Guide for Crown Lengthening Based on Cone Beam Computed Tomography Measurements: A Clinical Report with 6 Months Follow Up
P0746.kf: Clinical report of one patient with altered passive eruption treated by esthetic crown lengthening using a single 3D-printed guide designed from CBCT and intraoral scans for gingivectomy and osteoectomy, with a satisfactory outcome at 6 months.

P0748.t: Esthetic Crown Lengthening: Contemporary Guidelines for Achieving Ideal Gingival Architecture and Stability
P0748.kf: Review of protocols for esthetic crown lengthening; it reports that diode lasers may offer an advantageous compromise for gingival sculpting and that coronal gingival regrowth may be prevented by sufficient bone removal and flap management preserving gingival complex dimensions.

P0749.t: Relationship Between Crestal Bone Levels and Crown-to-Implant Ratio of Ultra-Short Implants With a Microrough Surface: A Prospective Study With 48 Months of Follow-Up
P0749.kf: Prospective cohort of 60 patients with atrophic ridges treated with 6-mm ultra-short microrough implants without grafting (47 patients, 66 implants followed, mean 48.5 months); clinical C/I ratio was 2.8 ± 0.6 at last follow-up, crestal bone level 1.0 ± 0.5 mm, success 96.9%.

P0750.kf: Narrative review with seven illustrative cases: authors conclude long-term stability of esthetic crown lengthening depends on accurate diagnosis and treatment planning, respecting biologic width, harmony of soft and hard tissue, and often combining orthodontic extrusion with surgery; final restorations are deferred …

P0751.t: Crown lengthening and restorative procedures in the esthetic zone
P0751.kf: Narrative review (authors state no systematic reviews and few controlled trials exist): recommends thinning tissues to minimize ostectomy, using split-thickness papillae and a thinned palatal flap, ostectomy by esthetic proportion parameters, and starting provisional restorations 3 weeks after surgery to condition …

P0754.t: Treatment of Gummy Smile of Multifactorial Etiology: A Case Report
P0754.kf: Case report of a 17-year-old with excessive gingival display from altered passive eruption and hyperactive lip, treated with esthetic crown lengthening then modified lip repositioning; the patient was satisfied at 1.5 years, though mouth breathing and recurrent inflammation persisted.

P0755.t: The prosthodontic concept of crown-to-root ratio: a review of the literature
P0755.kf: Critical literature review (Medline 1966–2003 plus manual search) on crown-to-root ratio for abutment evaluation of periodontally compromised teeth; it found a dearth of evidence-based research.

P0757.t: Nano-Layering Adds Strength to the Adhesive Interface
P0757.kf: Laboratory ultrastructural study (TEM, FIB-SEM, scanning probe microscopy) of a 10-MDP 3-step self-etch adhesive on dentin; it formed a submicron hydroxyapatite-rich hybrid layer and a 3D network of self-assembled nano-layering extending into the adhesive resin.

P0758.t: Influence of implant positioning in extraction sockets on osseointegration: histomorphometric analyses in dogs
P0758.kf: Histomorphometric study in six Labrador dogs with immediate implants placed centrally (control) or 0.8 mm deeper and more lingually (test) in mandibular sockets; at 4 months the buccal rough/smooth limit to crest distance was 2±0.9 mm vs 0.6±0.9 mm (P<0.05).

P0760.t: A critical review of diabetes, glycemic control, and dental implant therapy
P0760.kf: Systematic critical review of 16 longitudinal studies (≥10 patients) on implants in diabetes; failure rates ranged 0% to 14.3%, glycemic control was insufficiently reported in 13 studies, and the 3 interpretable studies showed no significant relationship between glycemic control and failure.

P0762.t: Effects of diabetes on the osseointegration of dental implants
P0762.j: Medicina Oral, Patología Oral y Cirugía Bucal
P0762.kf: Literature review on diabetes and implant osseointegration; experimental diabetes reduces bone-implant contact (reversible with insulin), and diabetic patients show higher failure rates, mostly in the first year of loading.

P0763.t: Glycemic control and implant stabilization in type 2 diabetes mellitus
P0763.kf: Prospective study of 10 non-diabetic individuals (12 implants) and 20 with type 2 diabetes (30 implants) followed by resonance frequency analysis for 4 months; those with HbA1c ≥8.1% had a greater maximum stability decrease and needed longer to return to baseline.

P0765.kf: PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 publications comparing diabetic and non-diabetic implant patients; marginal bone loss was significantly greater in diabetic patients (mean difference 0.20 mm, 95% CI 0.08–0.31; p = .001).

P0766.t: Challenging Paradigms: Update on the Use of Dental Implant Therapy for Patients with Diabetes Mellitus (Thematic Abstract Review)
P0766.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0766.kf: Thematic abstract review of studies on implants in diabetes: a 2-year series of 24 patients with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes reported 98.6% (1 year) and 96.6% (2 years) implant survival; a meta-analysis of 7 studies found no difference in failure by glycemic level, while a systematic review reported about 50% …

P0767.t: Does a higher glycemic level lead to a higher rate of dental implant failure?: A meta-analysis
P0767.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P0767.kf: Meta-analysis of 7 studies (252 patients, 587 implants) comparing well-controlled vs poorly controlled diabetes; no direct association between glycemic level and implant failure was found (RR 0.620, 95% CI 0.225-1.705), for early or late failure.

P0770.t: Group 3 ITI Consensus Report: Materials and antiresorptive drug-associated outcomes in implant dentistry
P0770.kf: ITI Group 3 consensus based on three systematic reviews; zirconia implants and transmucosal components showed outcomes up to 5 years comparable to titanium (mostly 1-piece implants), and low-dose bisphosphonate therapy did not increase early implant failure.

P0773.t: Peri-implantitis: Summary and consensus statements of group 3. The 6th EAO Consensus Conference 2021
P0773.kf: EAO 2021 consensus (group 3) based on two systematic reviews and one critical review; limited clinical data showed no difference between modified and non-modified surfaces in peri-implantitis, while emergence angle >30 with convex profile and restricted hygiene access were associated with increased risk.

P0774.t: Soft tissue management at implants: Summary and consensus statements of group 2. The 6th EAO Consensus Conference 2021
P0774.kf: EAO 2021 consensus (group 2) based on three systematic reviews and one critical review; soft tissue augmentation with immediate or delayed implants gave superior esthetics in the esthetic zone, had limited effect on marginal bone levels and PROMs, and keratinised mucosa gain improved gingival index, recession and …

P0775.t: Abutment Emergence Profile and Its Effect on Peri-Implant Tissues
P0775.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P0775.kf: Narrative continuing-education review: a larger abutment emergence profile compresses peri-implant soft tissue apically while a narrowed profile lets it drape coronally; the author recommends designing and testing the emergence profile in a screw-retained provisional, allowing 4 to 6 weeks for tissue maturation and …

P0780.t: Implant-abutment emergence angle and profile in relation to peri-implantitis: A systematic review
P0780.kf: Systematic review including three studies (168-349 implants); peri-implantitis prevalence was 16.7% and 24.8% at implant level, and bone-level implants with emergence angle above 30° or a convex emergence profile showed significantly higher prevalence.

P0785.t: Projection of Cervical Enamel into Molar Furcations
P0785.kf: Study of 474 extracted molars: cervical enamel projections toward the furcation were found on 28.6% of 304 mandibular molars and 17% of 170 maxillary molars; Grade III projections into the furcation occurred in 4.3% and 4.8%; early clinical observation linked them with about 90% of isolated mandibular bifurcation …

P0786.t: The relationship between cervical enamel projection and class II furcation defects in humans
P0786.kf: Clinical study of mandibular molars with class II furcation defects treated by guided tissue regeneration; cervical enamel projection was present in 82.1% of molars (Grade II most prevalent, 34.8%) and was associated with deeper baseline probing but greater post-treatment attachment gains.

P0788.t: Cervical Enamel Projections and Associated Pouch‐Like Opening in Mandibular Furcations
P0788.kf: Ex vivo microscopy (stereo, light, SEM) of 35 extracted mandibular molars with Grade III cervical enamel projections; 16 (45.7%) were fully covered by cementum, and a narrow pouch-like opening between cementum and enamel was seen in 15 of 16 (93.8%).

P0789.t: Survival and success of endocrowns: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0789.kf: Systematic review of 10 studies (3 clinical, 7 in vitro) with meta-analysis of clinical studies; 5-year survival was 91.4% for endocrowns vs 98.3% for conventional crowns and success 77.7% vs 94%, without significant differences.

P0791.t: Comparison of Fracture Strength of Endocrowns and Glass Fiber Post-Retained Conventional Crowns
P0791.kf: Laboratory comparison of fracture strength of endocrowns vs glass fiber post-retained conventional crowns on endodontically treated molars; the clinical relevance statement reports better mechanical performance, lower cost and less clinical time for endocrowns.

P0792.t: Influence of No-Ferrule and No-Post Buildup Design on the Fatigue Resistance of Endodontically Treated Molars Restored With Resin Nanoceramic CAD/CAM Crowns
P0792.kf: In vitro fatigue study of 45 extracted molars with no ferrule restored with resin nanoceramic CAD/CAM crowns (4-mm buildup, 2-mm buildup or endocrown, n=15): survival 53%, 87% and 87% (not significantly different); post-fatigue load-to-failure 2969 N, 2794 N and 2606 N (not different).

P0797.t: Influence of Occlusal Thickness and Radicular Extension on the Fracture Resistance of Premolar Endocrowns from Different All-Ceramic Materials
P0797.kf: In vitro study of 90 root-canal-treated premolars restored with lithium disilicate, polymer-infiltrated ceramic or high-translucency zirconia endocrowns with 2 mm or 4.5 mm occlusal reduction or 4.5 mm plus 2 mm radicular extension; lithium disilicate values were 62.55, 45.80 and 74.27 MPa respectively.

P0798.t: Influence of Ceramic Thickness and Ceramic Materials on Fracture Resistance of Posterior Partial Coverage Restorations
P0798.kf: In vitro study of 40 extracted molars with 1 mm or 2 mm lithium disilicate or leucite-reinforced partial coverage restorations luted with resin cement; material significantly affected fracture resistance (p<0.001) but thickness did not (p=0.074), with 2-mm lithium disilicate at 2505 N.

P0801.t: Current options concerning the endodontically-treated teeth restoration with the adhesive approach
P0801.kf: Critical review of adhesive approaches for endodontically treated teeth, covering partial vs full coverage, ferrule, post type and postless options such as endocrowns; there is consensus that remaining tooth structure is key to survival, but evidence on post type and avoiding posts is contradictory.

P0804.t: Strength comparison of anterior teeth restored with ceramic endocrowns vs custom-made post and cores
P0804.kf: 3D finite element analysis of maxillary central incisors restored with metal post-core and ceramic crown, leucite endocrown or lithium disilicate endocrown under 100 N; leucite endocrown stress (47.5 MPa) approached its tensile strength, while lithium disilicate stresses were 4 times lower.

P0805.t: Effect of Full Coverage, Endocrowns, Onlays, Inlays Restorations on Fracture Resistance of Endodontically Treated Molars
P0805.j: Journal of Dental and Oral Health
P0805.kf: In vitro study of 50 maxillary first molars (intact or endodontically treated with lithium disilicate full crowns, endocrowns, onlays or inlays); mean failure loads were 985, 1076, 989, 908 and 638 N, with full crowns 90% restorable and inlays 30%.

P0806.t: Preparation Ferrule Design Effect on Endocrown Failure Resistance
P0806.kf: In vitro study of mandibular third molar endocrowns (n=12 per group) with 0, 1 or 2 mm ferrule: failure load was lower without ferrule (638.5 N) than with 1 mm (1101.0 N) or 2 mm (956.3 N), but failure stress did not differ; catastrophic failures were 10/12, 8/12 and 12/12.

P0807.t: Fracture Resistance and Microleakage of Endocrowns Utilizing Three CAD-CAM Blocks
P0807.kf: In vitro study of 30 endodontically treated molars (n=10 per group) restored with endocrowns: resin nanoceramic had higher fracture resistance (1583.28 N vs 1340.92 N feldspathic and 1368.77 N lithium disilicate) and more favorable failures, but greater dye penetration (2.80 mm vs 1.11 and 1.91 mm).

P0810.t: Guidelines for the preparation of CAD/CAM ceramic inlays and partial crowns
P0810.kf: Narrative guideline article describing, with 3D drawings, preparation forms for CAD/CAM ceramic inlays and partial crowns; the authors state special preparation rules are needed for lasting success, e.g. margins ending near 90 degrees, reduction following the tooth's outer shape, and no parallel-walled isthmus because …

P0811.t: Effect of Endocrown Pulp Chamber Extension Depth on Molar Fracture Resistance
P0811.kf: In vitro study of 36 mandibular third molars (n=12 per group) with endocrown pulp chamber extensions of 2, 3 and 4 mm: mean failure load 843.4 N, 762.8 N and 943.5 N; catastrophic fractures 8/12, 11/12 and 10/12.

P0813.t: Clinical Behavior of Ceramic, Hybrid and Composite Onlays. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P0813.j: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
P0813.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 articles (27 quantitative): estimated onlay survival was 94.2%; survival decreased with follow-up duration and with composite as onlay material, and composite survival was significantly poorer than hybrid or ceramic (p = 0.003).

P0816.t: Finite element and Weibull analyses to estimate failure risks in the ceramic endocrown and classical crown for endodontically treated maxillary premolar
P0816.kf: 3D finite element and Weibull analysis of an endodontically treated maxillary premolar restored with a CEREC ceramic endocrown or classical crown, validated by fatigue testing; endocrown dentin and cement stresses were lower, overall failure probabilities similar, and fatigue fracture resistance 1,446 vs 1,163 MPa.

P0817.t: Evaluation of failure risks in ceramic restorations for endodontically treated premolar with MOD preparation
P0817.kf: Finite element/Weibull and acoustic emission analyses of an endodontically treated premolar with MOD preparation restored with CEREC inlay, endocrown or conventional crown; failure probability under normal biting was 95%, 2% and 2% respectively.

P0818.t: Estimation of the Failure Risk of a Maxillary Premolar with Different Crack Depths with Endodontic Treatment by Computer-aided Design/Computer-aided Manufacturing Ceramic Restorations
P0818.kf: Finite element/Weibull analysis of an endodontically treated cracked maxillary premolar restored with CAD/CAM onlay, endocrown or crown; failure probabilities were 27%, 2% and 1% with a shallow crack and 70%, 10% and 2% with a deep crack.

P0819.t: Composite Resin Core Buildups With and Without Post for the Restoration of Endodontically Treated Molars Without Ferrule
P0819.kf: In vitro fatigue study of 30 endodontically treated molars without ferrule (n=15 per group): core buildup with dual-cure Multicore HB (859.4 N mean fracture load) versus Multicore Flow plus fiber post (796.13 N) did not differ; none survived all 185,000 cycles and posts were linked to initial marginal gap failures.

P0820.t: Biomechanical behavior of endodontically treated premolars using different preparation designs and CAD/CAM materials
P0820.kf: In vitro study of 48 ferrule-free endodontically treated premolars restored with 2.5-mm or 5-mm deep endocrowns or 5-mm post&crown in composite or lithium disilicate; all survived 1,200,000 chewing cycles, and only in 2.5-mm endocrowns did composite give significantly higher load-to-failure.

P0821.t: Adhesive restoration of anterior endodontically treated teeth: influence of post length on fracture strength
P0821.kf: In vitro study of 48 endodontically treated maxillary incisors with 2 mm ferrule restored with 10-mm or 5-mm fiber posts or endocrowns, with ceramic or composite crowns; post presence, length and crown material had no significant effect on fracture resistance, and endocrowns showed more repairable fractures.

P0823.t: Restoration of severely damaged endodontically treated premolars: The influence of the endo-core length on marginal integrity and fatigue resistance of lithium disilicate CAD-CAM ceramic endocrowns
P0823.kf: In vitro study of 48 premolars cut at the CEJ restored with lithium disilicate overlays, endocrowns with 2-mm or 4-mm endo-cores, or post-and-core crowns; four overlays debonded during thermo-mechanical loading, while endocrowns performed equivalently to crowns after stepwise fatigue.

P0824.t: New material perspective for endocrown restorations: effects on mechanical performance and fracture behavior
P0824.kf: In vitro study of 42 endodontically treated molars with endocrowns of conventional composite, bulk fill, adhesive-modeled composite or lithium disilicate; none failed in fatigue and load-to-fracture was similar, but lithium disilicate showed more irreparable root fractures.

P0826.t: Endocrown restorations: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0826.kf: PRISMA systematic review of 8 studies (3 clinical trials, 5 in vitro) with meta-analysis of in vitro studies; clinical success of endocrowns ranged 94 to 100%, and endocrowns showed higher fracture strength overall (p=0.03) but not in posterior-only analysis (p=0.07).

P0830.t: Vonlays: a conservative esthetic alternative to full-coverage crowns
P0830.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P0830.kf: Case report introducing the 'vonlay', a monolithic lithium disilicate onlay with extended buccal veneer, used to restore posterior teeth in one patient as a less invasive alternative to full-coverage crowns; authors report from experience under 1% annual failure for premolars with sufficient enamel.

P0838.t: Digital workflow for the rehabilitation of the excessively worn dentition
P0838.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0838.kf: Case report describing a step-by-step digital workflow for rehabilitating an excessively worn dentition; the authors conclude the workflow aims to give faster, more predictable treatment, though combining digital and conventional procedures is still needed for complex cases.

P0839.t: A biometric approach to predictable treatment of clinical crown discrepancies
P0839.kf: Technique article introducing color-coded aesthetic measurement gauges that set a 78% width-to-length proportion for maxillary anterior teeth to quantify tooth size discrepancies and guide crown lengthening or restorations; illustrated with clinical cases and by the gauge's inventor.

P0840.t: A dental esthetic checklist for treatment planning in esthetic dentistry
P0840.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P0840.kf: Practical article presenting a seven-point dental esthetic checklist (midline, vertical and horizontal axes, central incisor symmetry, incisal edge line, smile line, profile and phonetics) for treatment planning, from an AEGD program; authors report it broadened residents' view to dentofacial harmony.

P0842.t: Analysis of Select Facial and Dental Esthetic Parameters
P0842.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0842.kf: Cross-sectional photographic study of 106 Caucasian adults with healthy dentitions; the average smile had coinciding midlines, an average smile line, teeth displayed to the second premolar, incisal curve parallel to the lower lip, and mean tooth and lip arcs of 9 and 13 degrees.

P0843.t: Anatomic crown width/length ratios of unworn and worn maxillary teeth in white subjects
P0843.kf: Measurement study of standardized images of 146 extracted maxillary anterior teeth and premolars from white subjects; central incisors were widest (9.10 to 9.24 mm), and width/length ratios ranged from 73% (unworn canines and laterals) to 87% (worn central incisors).

P0844.t: An overview of treatment considerations for esthetic restorations: a review of the literature
P0844.kf: Literature review (Medline 1986-2006 plus manual search) of biocompatibility, marginal adaptation, color, patient selection, technique sensitivity and failure of tooth-colored restorations; the author concludes prognosis hinges predominantly on choice of material, precise technique and patient selection.

P0845.t: The Influence of Restorative Procedures on Esthetic Outcomes in Implant Dentistry: A Systematic Review
P0845.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0845.kf: Systematic review of 58 records (15 RCTs, 6 cohort, 37 case series) on prosthodontic factors and implant esthetics; meta-analysis was not possible, facial malpositioning consistently increased mucosal recession, and no esthetic differences were established for abutment platform, all-ceramic vs metal-ceramic, or cement …

P0850.t: Evaluation of the golden proportion in the natural dentition: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0850.kf: PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of 6 included studies (from 566 retrieved) on tooth width ratios; evidence supporting the golden proportion in natural smiles was lacking.

P0852.kf: Historical overview of the past 100 years of aesthetic dentistry, highlighting aesthetic rules based on natural parameters, tooth whitening, adhesion-supported restorative materials, advances in orthodontics and periodontal and maxillofacial surgery, and recent digital technologies.

P0853.t: Geometric and Mathematical Proportions and their Relations to Maxillary Anterior Teeth
P0853.j: The Journal of Contemporary Dental Practice
P0853.kf: Cross-sectional analysis of standardized frontal smile images of 376 dental students; the golden proportion between central and lateral incisors occurred in 31.3% of men and 27.1% of women, RED proportion was not constant, and golden percentage was fairly constant (23%, 15%, 12%).

P0856.t: Implant placement in the esthetic area: criteria for positioning single and multiple implants
P0856.kf: Review combining clinical experience and literature on implant placement in the esthetic area; it concludes immediate placement can succeed esthetically but is technique sensitive, post-extraction immediate loading is feasible in infected sites, and shoulder-less abutments allow more tissue space.

P0857.t: Interdisciplinary management of anterior dental esthetics
P0857.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P0857.kf: Article describing an interdisciplinary (restorative, orthodontic, periodontic) approach to diagnosing anterior dental esthetic problems, beginning with esthetics and encompassing structure, function and biology.

P0858.t: Is the timing of implant placement and loading influencing esthetic outcomes in single-tooth implants?—A systematic review
P0858.kf: Systematic review of 18 RCTs (9 on placement timing, 9 on loading timing) with meta-analyses where comparable; no differences in midfacial recession or papilla level between immediate and early placement at 1 and 2 years, and loading timing did not significantly change mucosal margin or PES/WES.

P0860.t: Linear and profilometric changes of the mucosa following soft tissue augmentation in the zone of aesthetic priority: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0860.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies on soft tissue grafting at esthetic-zone implants; after immediate placement grafting reduced mid-buccal recession (0.34 mm) and increased thickness (0.66 mm), and after delayed placement reduced recession (0.17 mm) without significant thickness gain.

P0862.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P0862.kf: Article categorizing macroesthetic smile design criteria around two reference points, the facial midline and the amount and position of tooth reveal in various views and lip configurations.

P0863.t: Mathematical Tooth Proportions: A Systematic Review
P0863.kf: Systematic review comparing golden proportion, golden percentage and RED proportion; tooth proportions varied substantially in natural dentitions, no study supported a single formula, and the golden proportion occurred between central and lateral incisors only in some cases.

P0868.kf: Narrative review (PubMed/Medline search) of smile design principles covering facial and dental composition: midline, incisal edge position, central incisor width-to-length ratio about 4:5 (75-80%), zenith points, contacts, gingival levels and smile line; the author states there is no formula for anterior esthetics.

P0869.t: Proportional smile design using the recurring esthetic dental (red) proportion

P0870.t: Prosthetically Driven Techniques to Compensate Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Deficiencies
P0870.kf: Technique review with five clinical cases (ITI Forum, 2016): for minor-to-moderate peri-implant soft tissue deficiencies, crown morphology adaptations alone (facial transition line angles, increased interdental contours, long palatal contact lines) are recommended; for major deficiencies, pink ceramics may become …
