P0871.t: Restoring dentate appearance: a literature review for modern complete denture esthetics
P0871.kf: Literature review (1880 to present) of complete-denture esthetics found a limited amount of useful evidence-based information, falling into three areas: published guidelines, patient preference studies and studies of anatomic norms.

P0873.t: Single implant restorations: prosthetically induced soft tissue topography
P0873.kf: Technique article with three cases presenting the 'cervical contouring concept': the soft tissue design is planned on a modified soft tissue replica and transferred through custom abutment and provisional restoration, with about 6 months for soft tissue maturation in a similar case; authors state single implants are a …

P0874.t: Six Month Clinical Evaluation of Interdental Papilla Reconstruction with Injectable Hyaluronic Acid Gel Using an Image Analysis System
P0874.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P0874.kf: Prospective uncontrolled study of 10 patients (43 maxillary anterior sites) given up to five hyaluronic acid gel injections at 3-week intervals: at 6 months, 29 sites had complete papilla reconstruction and 14 improved by 39 to 96%.

P0875.t: Smile Analysis: The Photoshop® Smile Design Technique: Part I
P0875.kf: Technique article (part 1 of 2) describing smile analysis elements and a step-by-step digital method using Adobe Photoshop 'tooth grids' to design and show proposed smiles, said to take about three to four minutes; width-to-length ratios of 75 to 80% are most often cited.

P0876.kf: Narrative review of smile design principles (facial, lip, gingival and dental components; central incisor width about 75% to 80% of height; smile line, buccal corridor, midline); the author notes ideal-model guidelines may not give the most natural smile and that natural smiles are not necessarily symmetric or perfect.

P0880.t: The facial flow concept: An organic orofacial analysis-the vertical component
P0880.kf: Clinical report with one 44-year-old patient proposing the 'facial flow' concept: a facial flow line through glabella, nose bridge, philtrum and chin defines a green side (midline cant following the flow) and red side (opposing), used instead of a strict facial midline in smile design.

P0882.t: The principles of visual perception and their clinical application to denture esthetics
P0882.kf: Narrative article applying principles of visual perception to denture esthetics (tooth arrangement, shade selection and the effect of lipstick); the author concludes that perceptual principles can free dentists from confusion in esthetics and be applied by all.

P0883.t: Tooth preparation for ceramic veneers: when less is more
P0883.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0883.kf: Technique article presenting a step-by-step 'mock-up driven' protocol for conservative ceramic veneer preparation (prepared through a bis-acryl mock-up, minimum 0.3 mm labial and about 1.5 mm incisal reduction); the authors conclude it produces considerably less invasive preparations than traditional approaches, which …

P0884.t: Peri-implant Soft Tissue Conditioning with Provisional Restorations in the Esthetic Zone: The Dynamic Compression Technique
P0884.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P0884.kf: Technique report with two cases (single implant and adjacent implants): the dynamic compression technique conditions peri-implant soft tissue with a screw-retained provisional that is first slightly overcontoured to apply pressure and then undercontoured to let tissue fill; final restorations were placed at 4 and 6 …

P0885.t: A biometric approach to aesthetic crown lengthening: part I--midfacial considerations
P0885.kf: Technique article with one case introducing color-coded gauges (Proportion, Sounding, Crown Lengthening Gauges) that use a 78% width-to-length proportion and a 3-mm dentogingival complex to determine how much bone to remove in esthetic crown lengthening; final restorations were cemented 6 months after surgery.

P0903.t: Influence of width of keratinized tissue on the prevalence of peri-implant diseases: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0903.kf: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 21 studies (15 cross-sectional): peri-implantitis affected 10.5% to 44% of implants with KT <2 mm or 0 mm vs 5.1% to 8% with ≥2 mm or >0 mm; BOP, plaque, MBL and recession favored KT ≥2 mm.

P0915.t: Decontamination of biofilm-contaminated implant surfaces: An in vitro evaluation
P0915.kf: In vitro study of 123 biofilm-contaminated implants in simulated intrabony defects: air-polishing and rotating titanium brushes removed more biofilm than gauze wiping; chemical adjuncts gave no relevant benefit over saline, and no method removed biofilm completely.

P0917.t: Dental Implant Failure Rates and Associated Risk Factors
P0917.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0917.kf: Retrospective cohort of consecutive patients (1982–2003): failure was 8.16% in the maxilla vs 4.93% in the mandible; age 60–79 (RR 2.24), smoking (RR 1.56), diabetes (RR 2.75), head and neck radiation (RR 2.73) and postmenopausal estrogen therapy (RR 2.55) raised failure risk.

P0919.t: Incidence of First Implant Failure: A Retroprospective Study of 27 Years of Implant Operations at One Specialist Clinic
P0919.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P0919.kf: Retroprospective single-clinic study of 8,528 patients with 39,077 implants (1986–2012): 10.0% of patients had one or more failures; first failure was more frequent in upper jaws, within 1 year of surgery (69%), and with turned vs moderately rough surfaces.

P0920.t: Multifactorial evaluation of implant failure: a 19-year retrospective study
P0920.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0920.kf: Retrospective study of 879 patients with 2,796 implants (1991–2009): 150 implants in 91 patients failed; 57.3% were early failures, mainly from inflammation (47%), and 42.7% late, mainly from overloading (53%).

P0933.t: Attached gingiva: histology and surgical augmentation
P0933.kf: Narrative review with cases: keratinized attached gingiva increases resistance to injury and stabilizes the gingival margin; apically positioned flaps, free gingival grafts and subepithelial connective tissue grafts augment it predictably and durably.

P0940.t: Free Gingival Graft to Increase Keratinized Mucosa after Placing of Mandibular Fixed Implant-Supported Prosthesis
P0940.kf: Case report of an edentulous patient lacking interforaminal keratinized mucosa: a palatal free gingival graft placed after a mandibular fixed implant prosthesis promoted peri-implant health, hygiene and comfort at 2 and 12 months.

P0942.t: Mucogingival surgery with free gingival graft (strip technique) for augmentation of the attached gingival tissues: report of three cases
P0942.j: Journal of IMAB - Annual Proceeding (Scientific Papers)
P0942.kf: Report of three cases (Miller class II to IV recessions, mandibular anterior): the strip technique for free gingival graft, splitting the palatal graft longitudinally, gave a mean attached gingiva gain of 4.33 mm at 4 months with initial healing complete in two weeks.

P0944.t: Use of platelet concentrates in oral and maxillofacial surgery: an overview
P0944.kf: Critical overview of autologous platelet concentrates (PRP, PRF) in oral and maxillofacial surgery: they may stimulate soft- and hard-tissue regeneration via growth factors, but quality varies between donors and consensus on efficacy has not been reached.

P0949.t: Healing and remodeling of connective tissue graft around implants with poor keratinized mucosa. Influence of provisionalization timing (delayed vs immediate) using BOPT abutments. A clinical observational controlled pilot study
P0949.j: University of Milan, Doctoral Program XXIX Cycle in Oral Sciences

P0951.t: How Thick Is the Oral Mucosa around Implants after Augmentation with Different Materials: A Systematic Review of the Effectiveness of Substitute Matrices in Comparison to Connective Tissue Grafts
P0951.kf: Systematic review of 7 clinical studies comparing xenogeneic collagen or acellular dermal matrices with connective tissue grafts around implants: all increased mucosal thickness; four studies found no significant difference and three favored CTG; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.

P0954.t: Bonding lithium disilicate ceramic to feather-edge tooth preparations: a minimally invasive treatment concept
P0954.kf: Clinical report of 235 teeth (136 anterior, 99 posterior) restored with monolithic lithium disilicate crowns bonded to feather-edge preparations: one molar crown fractured after 3 years, with no biological or technical complications.

P0956.t: Durability and Weibull Characteristics of Lithium Disilicate Crowns Bonded on Abutments with Knife‐Edge and Large Chamfer Finish Lines after Cyclic Loading
P0956.kf: In vitro study of 20 pressed lithium disilicate molar crowns bonded on epoxy abutments after 1,200,000 load cycles: fracture strength did not differ between knife-edge (1655 ± 353 N) and large chamfer (1618 ± 263 N); Weibull modulus was lower for knife-edge (5.48 vs 7.68).

P0957.t: Minimally invasive vertical preparation design for ceramic veneers: a multicenter retrospective follow-up clinical study of 265 lithium disilicate veneers
P0957.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P0957.kf: Multicenter retrospective study of 265 lithium disilicate veneers with feather-edge margins in 53 patients (mean 54.4 months): survival was 99.63%, with one adhesive failure after trauma and mostly Alfa ratings for color, surface, discoloration and marginal integrity.

P0980.t: Comparison of general and aesthetic effects between flapless and flap techniques in dental implantation a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
P0980.kf: Meta-analysis of 14 RCTs: flapless and flap techniques had similar survival, BOP, keratinized mucosa width and crestal bone loss, while flapless surgery reduced probing depth (WMD −0.37), day-1 pain (WMD −1.66) and better preserved papillae.

P0983.t: Soft Tissue Response in Posterior Teeth Adjacent to Interdental Single Implants: A Controlled Randomized Clinical Trial Comparing Intrasulcular vs Trapezoidal Incision
P0983.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0983.kf: RCT of 40 patients with single interdental posterior implants: intrasulcular vs trapezoidal incision showed no differences in probing depth, recession or papilla of adjacent teeth; recession, scar formation and papilla index changed significantly over 1 year in the whole sample.

P0985.t: Initial Crestal Bone Loss After Implant Placement with Flapped or Flapless Surgery—A Prospective Cohort Study
P0985.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0985.kf: Randomized study of 80 patients (195 implants): at 12 months, flapped placement showed mean bone loss of 0.55 ± 0.57 mm vs a slight mean gain of 0.09 ± 0.49 mm with flapless placement (P < .001).

P0986.t: Minimal invasiveness at dental implant placement: A systematic review with meta-analyses on flapless fully guided surgery
P0986.kf: Meta-analyses of 5 RCTs (124 participants, 449 implants): flapless static computer-aided placement had less angular deviation (MD -3.88°), less pain and shorter surgery than flapped freehand/partially guided placement, but a 12% intraoperative complication rate and 7% inability to place.

P0991.t: Impact of immediate interim restoration on peri-implant tissues around immediately placed single dental implants in the esthetic region: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0991.kf: Meta-analysis of 16 studies (836 immediately placed single implants in the esthetic region): immediate interim restoration did not significantly affect mid-facial mucosal level (MD 0.01), papilla levels or marginal bone loss, but improved esthetic outcomes and PROMs.

P0992.t: Accuracy and Reliability of Cone Beam Computed Tomographic Measurements of the Bone Labial and Palatal to the Maxillary Anterior Teeth
P0992.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P0992.kf: Study of 18 immediate-implant candidates comparing presurgical CBCT with direct post-extraction measurements: mean labial bone was 0.50 ± 0.32 mm direct vs 0.76 ± 0.37 mm on CBCT; correlation was 0.795, improving when bone exceeded 1 mm.

P0994.t: Immediate implant placement in compromised sockets: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P0994.kf: Meta-analysis of 43 studies (4825 sockets): immediate implants in compromised vs noncompromised sockets showed no significant differences in survival (RR 0.992), marginal bone level at ≤12 months (MD 0.033) or esthetic parameters.

P1000.t: Buccal bone thickness around single dental implants in the maxillary esthetic zone
P1000.kf: Meta-analysis of 2 RCTs and 12 cohort studies: buccal bone thickness around single anterior maxillary implants did not differ significantly by placement protocol (early, immediate, delayed) or loading protocol; descriptive data suggested graft material may influence it.

P1003.t: Classification of Sagittal Root Position in Relation to the Anterior Maxillary Osseous Housing for Immediate Implant Placement: A Cone Beam Computed Tomography Study
P1003.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1003.kf: Retrospective CBCT review of 100 patients (600 maxillary anterior teeth): sagittal root positions were Class I in 81.1%, Class II 6.5%, Class III 0.7% and Class IV 11.7%.

P1012.t: Differences in Dental Implant Survival between Immediate vs. Delayed Placement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P1012.kf: Meta-analysis of 10 studies (6 RCTs): survival was 97.4% for 341 immediate vs 97.5% for 359 delayed implants (RR 0.99; 95% CI 0.96, 1.02), with no significant difference.

P1016.t: Effect of splinting and interproximal contact tightness on load transfer by implant restoration
P1016.kf: Photoelastic in vitro model of three mandibular implants: non-splinted crowns with heavier interproximal contacts increased tensile stresses between implants, while splinted restorations shared occlusal loads and distributed stresses more evenly.

P1017.t: Effect of the buccal gap width following immediate implant placement on the buccal bone wall: A retrospective cone-beam computed tomography analysis
P1017.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1017.kf: Retrospective CBCT study of 51 grafted immediate-implant sites at maxillary central incisors (≥1 year): buccal bone was thicker with gaps >2 mm than ≤2 mm (1.9 ± 0.9 vs 0.5 ± 0.6 mm), and gap width was the only predictor of buccal wall thickness.

P1019.t: Effectiveness of immediate implant placement into defective sockets in the esthetic zone: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1019.kf: Single-arm meta-analysis of 23 studies (630 immediate implants in defective esthetic-zone sockets): survival was 98.1%, MBL 0.72 mm at 12 months, recession 0.25 mm at 12 months and PES 12.34 at 12 months.

P1020.t: Effects of modified abutment characteristics on peri-implant soft tissue health: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1020.kf: Systematic review of 13 RCT investigations: zirconia abutments showed less BOP increase over time than titanium (WMD -26.96), while abutment macro-design, surface topography and manipulation had no significant influence on peri-implant inflammation.

P1022.t: Radiological evaluation of marginal bone loss at tooth surfaces facing single Brånemark implants
P1022.kf: Radiological follow-up of 58 adults with 71 single Brånemark implants up to 3 years after crown installation: bone loss at adjacent tooth surfaces occurred mainly before crown placement, was largest next to upper lateral incisors and increased as implant-tooth distance decreased.

P1024.t: Esthetic Outcome of Implant Supported Crowns With and Without Peri-Implant Conditioning Using Provisional Fixed Prosthesis: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
P1024.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1024.kf: RCT of 20 single bone-level implants in the esthetic zone: soft tissue conditioning with provisional crowns (dynamic compression technique) gave a mean combined modPES/WES of 16.7 vs 10.5 without a provisional at 1 year, with similar bone loss.

P1025.t: Esthetic Outcomes Following Immediate and Early Implant Placement in the Anterior Maxilla—A Systematic Review
P1025.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1025.kf: Systematic review of 50 studies (33 case series): immediate (type 1) placement showed midfacial recession >1 mm in 9% to 41% of sites (median 26%), whereas two early-placement studies reported no such sites; meta-analysis was not possible.

P1035.t: Immediate Placement and Provisionalization of Implants Into Sites With Periradicular Infection With and Without Antibiotics: An Exploratory Study
P1035.kf: Exploratory randomized study of 13 subjects receiving immediate implants with provisionalization in infected sites (8 placebo, 5 antibiotics): one implant failed in each group.

P1036.t: Group 5 ITI Consensus Report Implant placement and loading protocols
P1036.kf: ITI consensus based on two systematic reviews: five consensus statements per review and twelve clinical recommendations; Type 1A (immediate placement and loading) in the anterior maxilla under favorable conditions was considered predictable with high survival.

P1041.t: Immediate implant placement in fresh extraction sockets using the open healing technique and tissue level implants
P1041.kf: Series of 42 immediate tissue-level implants in 40 patients with socket grafting and open healing: 4-year survival was 100% and success 95.2%, with no significant crestal bone differences among augmentation materials.

P1047.t: Immediate or Early Placement of Implants Following Tooth Extraction: Review of Biologic Basis, Clinical Procedures, and Outcomes
P1047.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1047.kf: Review of 31 articles (1990–June 2003): immediate and delayed-immediate implants had survival comparable to healed ridges; defects ≤2 mm healed by spontaneous fill with rough-surface implants, while larger defects or damaged walls required membranes and grafts.

P1049.t: Immediate positioning of a definitive abutment versus repeated abutment replacements in post-extractive implants: 3-year follow-up of a randomised multicentre clinical trial
P1049.kf: Multicentre RCT of 25 post-extractive immediately restored maxillary premolar implants: at 3 years bone loss was 0.34 mm with definitive abutments vs 0.55 mm with repeatedly replaced provisional abutments (significant 0.2 mm difference); success was 100% in both groups.

P1050.t: Immediate versus delayed implant placement after anterior single tooth extraction: the timing randomized controlled clinical trial
P1050.kf: Multicenter RCT of 124 subjects: immediate implants needed bone augmentation more often (72% vs 43.9%), had more wound failure (26.1% vs 5.3%), deeper probing depths at 1 year and more inadequate pink esthetic scores (42% vs 19%) than delayed placement.

P1051.t: Immediate, early (6 weeks) and delayed loading (3 months) of single implants: 4-month post-loading from a multicenter pragmatic randomised controlled trial
P1051.kf: Multicenter pragmatic RCT of 81 patients randomized to immediate, early (6 weeks) or conventional (3 months) loading: up to 4 months post-loading no implant or prosthesis failed and no complications occurred.

P1052.t: Immediate, immediate-delayed (6 weeks) and delayed (4 months) post-extractive single implants: 1-year post-loading data from a randomised controlled trial
P1052.kf: RCT of 210 patients: 1 year post-loading, failures were 6% immediate, 6.2% immediate-delayed and 1.6% delayed (not significant); bone loss was similar, and aesthetic scores were higher with immediate (12.52) and immediate-delayed (12.49) than delayed (11.78) placement.

P1053.t: Implant design and intraosseous stability of immediately placed implants: a human cadaver study
P1053.kf: Human cadaver study of implants placed immediately in mandibular premolar sockets: the tapered-effect implant had higher ISQ than the Ø 4.1 mm solid screw implant (P <0.01) and was comparable to the Ø 4.8 mm implant.

P1060.t: Optimizing Esthetics for Implant Restorations in the Anterior Maxilla: Anatomic and Surgical Considerations
P1060.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1060.kf: Narrative review of anatomic and surgical factors for esthetic anterior maxillary implants. The authors describe ideal 3D implant position (comfort and danger zones) and recommend avoiding oversized implants, low-trauma soft tissue handling, guided bone regeneration when the facial wall is missing, and submerged or …

P1063.t: Outcomes of regenerative treatment with rhPDGF‐BB and rhFGF‐2 for periodontal intra‐bony defects: a systematic review and meta‐analysis
P1063.kf: Meta-analysis of 7 studies (one at low risk of bias): rhPDGF-BB increased linear defect fill (0.95 mm) and CAL gain (0.34 mm) versus carrier alone, and rhFGF-2 increased percentage defect fill (21.22%).

P1064.t: Immediate placement of dental implants into fresh extraction socket in the maxillary anterior region: a case report

P1065.t: Peri-implant bone changes following tooth extraction, immediate placement and loading of implants in the edentulous maxilla
P1065.kf: Prospective study of 20 patients with 118 immediately loaded maxillary implants (59 in sockets, 59 in healed sites): survival was 100% and mean marginal bone level -0.35 mm at 18 months, unaffected by socket vs healed placement.

P1070.t: Resonance frequency analysis of implants placed in condensed bone
P1070.kf: Human cadaver split-mouth study: insertion torque and ISQ correlated in edentulous jaws (r = 0.63 untreated, r = 0.82 condensed) and in untreated extraction sockets (r = 0.78), but not in condensed extraction-socket bone (r = 0.15).

P1072.t: Ridge Alterations Post-extraction in the Esthetic Zone: A 3D Analysis with CBCT
P1072.kf: Prospective CBCT study of 39 patients over 8 weeks after flapless anterior extraction: thin facial walls (≤1 mm) showed a median vertical bone loss of 7.5 mm vs 1.1 mm for thick walls, with central areas most at risk.

P1073.t: Ridge Preservation After Tooth Extraction With Buccal Bone Plate Deficiency Using Tunnel Structured β-Tricalcium Phosphate Blocks: A 2-Month Histological Pilot Study in Beagle Dogs
P1073.kf: Beagle pilot (6 dogs) with buccal-deficient premolar sockets: at 2 months, tunnel β-TCP blocks gave greater coronal (3.2 ± 0.5 vs 1.2 ± 0.3 mm) and middle ridge widths and more woven bone (62.4% vs 26.8%) than extraction alone.

P1077.t: Selection criteria for immediate implant placement and immediate loading for single tooth replacement in the maxillary esthetic zone A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1077.kf: Systematic review of 68 articles (mean 37.2 implants per study, 2.8-year follow-up) on Type 1A single implants in the maxillary esthetic zone: all used highly selective criteria; studies before 2012 reported lower survival (-1.9 percentage points).

P1087.t: The effectiveness of immediate implant placement for single tooth replacement compared to delayed implant placement: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1087.kf: Meta-analysis of 3 RCTs and 5 non-randomized studies (473 single implants): survival was lower for immediate (94.9%) than delayed placement (98.9%) (RR 0.96), all early failures; probing depth and pink aesthetic scores were similar.

P1094.t: Efficacy of different surgical techniques for peri-implant tissue preservation in immediate implant placement: a systematic review and meta-analysis
P1094.kf: Meta-analysis of 11 RCTs on immediate implants: connective tissue grafts improved facial gingival level (MD = -0.51) and bone grafts reduced horizontal buccal resorption (MD = -0.59), whereas flapless surgery and palatal positioning gave no significant improvements.

P1095.t: Management of the extraction socket and timing of implant placement: Consensus report and clinical recommendations of group 3 of the XV European Workshop in Periodontology
P1095.kf: European Workshop consensus based on four systematic reviews, yielding 23 consensus statements and 12 clinical recommendations graded with a modified GRADE tool, with evidence mostly from single-tooth extraction and replacement.

P1106.t: Bone healing and soft tissue contour changes following single-tooth extraction: a clinical and radiographic 12-month prospective study
P1106.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1106.kf: Prospective 12-month study of 46 patients after single premolar or molar extraction, assessed with study casts, linear radiography and subtraction radiography: major changes of the extraction site occurred during the first year.

P1110.t: Changes in alveolar process dimensions following extraction of molars with advanced periodontal disease A clinical pilot study
P1110.kf: Pilot CBCT study of 17 molars extracted for advanced periodontitis: after 6 months, central crest width at -1 mm decreased by 0.59–0.72 mm buccally, mandibular buccal/lingual plate heights decreased 0.56 to 1.38 mm, and no significant volumetric loss occurred.

P1113.t: Dimensional changes of buccal bone plate in immediate implants inserted through open flap, open flap and bone grafting and flapless techniques: A cone-beam computed tomography randomized controlled clinical trial
P1113.kf: Three-arm RCT of 45 patients with immediate maxillary premolar implants: flap-graft, flap-nograft and flapless-nograft techniques gave similar buccal bone changes and near-complete gap fill at 6 months (residual vertical gap 0.27 mm); flapless was less painful.

P1123.t: Soft Tissue Dimensions Following Tooth Extraction in the Posterior Maxilla: A Randomized Clinical Trial Comparing Alveolar Ridge Preservation to Spontaneous Healing
P1123.kf: RCT of 35 patients after maxillary molar extraction: at 6 months, alveolar ridge preservation resulted in thinner crestal gingiva (-1.16 mm) and thinner buccal and palatal gingiva at implant shoulder level than spontaneous healing, with similar MGJ change.

P1130.t: Association of Connective Tissue Grafts in Immediate Implants Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P1130.kf: Systematic review of 5 RCTs (245 subjects), 4 in meta-analysis: CTG with immediate implants gave a non-significant mean buccal gingival level difference of 0.09 mm (95% CI −0.54 to 0.72) versus no graft.

P1132.t: Crestal Ridge Width Changes When Placing Implants at the Time of Tooth Extraction With and Without Soft Tissue Augmentation After a Healing Period of 6 Months: Report of 24 Consecutive Cases
P1132.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1132.kf: 24 consecutive patients with immediate maxillary anterior implants: the first 12 (no graft) lost an average of 1.063 mm of labial volume at 6 months, whereas the next 12 receiving a tunneled subepithelial CTG gained 0.34 mm.

P1133.t: Effects of Connective Tissue Grafting on the Facial Gingival Level Following Single Immediate Implant Placement and Provisionalization in the Esthetic Zone: A 1-Year Randomized Controlled Prospective Study
P1133.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1133.kf: RCT of 20 patients with immediate placement and provisionalization: at 1 year, facial gingival level change was -0.70 mm without vs -0.25 mm with subepithelial CTG (significant), and all implants remained osseointegrated.

P1135.t: Immediate implant placement with or without connective tissue graft A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1135.kf: Systematic review of 5 RCTs and 3 NRSs (409 implants): CTG with immediate placement improved vertical mid-facial soft tissue change by 0.41 mm and lowered the risk of ≥1 mm asymmetry (RR 12.10); PES, bone level and probing depth did not differ.

P1136.t: Immediate implant placement, reconstruction of compromised sockets, and repair of gingival recession with a triple graft from the maxillary tuberosity: A variation of the immediate dentoalveolar restoration technique
P1136.kf: Clinical report of a variation of the immediate dentoalveolar restoration technique: immediate implant placement with a triple graft (cancellous and cortical bone plus soft tissue) from the maxillary tuberosity to rebuild the buccal wall and repair recession in one session. The authors list donor-site access and …

P1141.t: Single immediate implant placement in the maxillary aesthetic zone with and without connective tissue grafting: Results of a 5-year randomized controlled trial
P1141.kf: RCT of 60 patients with immediately placed and provisionalized maxillary anterior implants ± tuberosity CTG: at 5 years mid-buccal mucosa level change was −0.6 mm without vs 0.1 mm with graft (p = .008); survival was 96.7% in both groups.

P1145.t: Evaluation of Buccal Alveolar Bone Dimension of Maxillary Anterior and Premolar Teeth: A Cone Beam Computed Tomography Investigation
P1145.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1145.kf: CBCT study of 43 implant patients: median buccal bone thickness 1 mm below the crest was 1.13 mm at first premolars and 0.83 mm at anterior teeth, and few anterior teeth had buccal bone >1 mm.

P1150.t: A New Concept in Maintaining the Emergence Profile in Immediate Posterior Implant Placement: The Anatomic Harmony Abutment
P1150.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P1150.kf: Technique report proposing the anatomic harmony abutment for immediate molar implant placement: flapless tooth removal, then a chairside custom composite healing abutment that seals the site and preserves the emergence profile. The author reports typical healing at 3 months and a final restoration at 1 year, and …

P1154.t: Flapless Postextraction Socket Implant Placement, Part 3: The Effects of Bone Grafting and Provisional Restoration on Soft Tissue Color Change—A Retrospective Pilot Study
P1154.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1154.kf: Retrospective pilot of 23 patients with flapless immediate implants: mean gingival color difference (ΔE) versus contralateral teeth was 1.9–2.6, with about 80% of sites below the visibly perceptible threshold.

P1156.t: Lingualized Flapless Implant Placement into Fresh Extraction Sockets Preserves Buccal Alveolar Bone: A Cone Beam Computed Tomography Study
P1156.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1156.kf: CBCT study of 14 patients with lingualized flapless immediate implants and nonocclusal loading at single maxillary incisor sites: buccal plate resorption at 6 months was not significant.

P1160.t: Tissue Dimensional Changes in Single-Tooth Immediate Extraction Implant Placement in the Esthetic Zone: A Retrospective Clinical Study
P1160.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1160.kf: Retrospective study of 77 patients (80 flapless immediate implants): buccopalatal contraction over 6 months was greatest with a healing abutment alone, smaller with bone graft or provisional, and minimal with provisional plus bone graft.

P1161.t: Early implant placement with simultaneous guided bone regeneration following single-tooth extraction in the esthetic zone: a cross-sectional, retrospective study in 45 subjects with a 2- to 4-year follow-up
P1161.kf: Cross-sectional retrospective study of 45 early-placed single implants with simultaneous GBR (2–4 years): all were successful, none showed facial mucosal recession, and mean shoulder-to-first-bone-contact distance was 2.18 mm.

P1163.t: Effectiveness and clinical performance of early implant placement for the replacement of single teeth in anterior areas: A systematic review
P1163.kf: Systematic review of 19 articles (140 patients): Type 3 placement showed survival comparable to Type 4 (95% vs 100%), and Type 2 and Type 3 showed minimal complications and high aesthetic scores.

P1166.t: Primary and Secondary Stability of Implants in Postextraction and Healed Sites: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
P1166.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1166.kf: RCT of 40 patients receiving premolar/molar implants immediately or 12 weeks post-extraction, followed up to 12 months: success was 100% in both groups and ISQ did not differ, but crestal bone loss was greater for postextraction implants (0.68 ± 0.43 vs 0.40 ± 0.26 mm, P = .02).

P1171.t: Immediate Implant Placement and Provisionalization in the Esthetic Zone Using a Flapless or a Flap-Involving Approach: A Randomized Controlled Trial
P1171.kf: RCT of 39 patients with immediate single implants and provisionalization in the esthetic zone, flapless vs flap: flapless showed less mesiobuccal (0.11 vs 0.43 mm) and distobuccal recession at 3 months, with no other significant differences at 3, 6 or 12 months.

P1173.t: Immediate implant placement with flap or flapless surgery A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1173.kf: Meta-analysis of 5 RCTs (140 single immediate implants, 6–12 months follow-up): flapless surgery yielded 0.48 mm (95% CI 0.13–0.84) less horizontal buccal bone change, with no difference in implant survival (RR 1.00).

P1180.t: Esthetic Outcomes and Tissue Stability of Implant Placement in Compromised Sockets Following Immediate Dentoalveolar Restoration: Results of a Prospective Case Series at 58 Months Follow-up
P1180.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1180.kf: Prospective case series of 18 patients treated with immediate implants and immediate dentoalveolar restoration in compromised sockets, followed 58 months: soft tissue dimensions were 12.85 mm at baseline and 12.79 mm at follow-up, with no recession and slightly increased papillae.

P1181.t: Accuracy of freehand versus guided immediate implant placement A randomized controlled trial
P1181.kf: RCT of 61 patients (80 immediate implants) comparing freehand vs static guided surgery: guided placement had lower crestal (0.34 vs 1.13 mm mesiodistal), apical and angular deviations (0.83° vs 6.09°), while depth deviation did not differ significantly.

P1182.t: Freehand vs. computer-aided implant surgery a systematic review and meta-analysis—part 1 accuracy of planned and placed implant position
P1182.kf: Meta-analysis of 55 studies: mean angular/entry/apex deviations were 7.46°/1.56 mm/2.22 mm freehand, 2.57°/0.72/0.88 mm fully guided static CAIS and 3.67°/1.01/1.36 mm dynamic CAIS; CAIS differed significantly from freehand.

P1183.t: Guided versus freehand single implant placement A 3-year parallel randomized clinical trial
P1183.kf: 3-year RCT of 60 sub-crestal platform-switched implants in 18 patients: guided surgery by a non-expert vs freehand by a skilled operator showed a non-significant MBL change difference of 0.11 ± 0.22 mm (p = 0.61).

P1184.t: Static computer-aided, partially guided, and free-handed implant placement A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
P1184.kf: Systematic review of 10 RCTs: static computer-aided placement had lower angular (MD 4.41°), coronal (MD 0.65 mm) and apical (MD 1.13 mm) deviations than freehand (8 studies, 878 implants); survival up to 12 months was >98% and comparable.

P1186.t: Immediate implant placement in fresh sockets versus implant placement in healed bone for full-arch fixed prostheses with conventional loading
P1186.j: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P1186.kf: Retrospective study of 41 patients with 512 implants for full-arch fixed prostheses placed in fresh sockets or healed bone (mean follow-up 44.9 months): 9 non-immediate and 2 immediate implants failed, all in the maxilla; success was 97.8% in both groups.

P1192.t: A prospective cohort study of immediate implant placement into posterior compromised sockets with or without primary wound closure of reactive soft tissue
P1192.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1192.kf: Prospective study of 33 immediate implants in posterior compromised sockets with or without reactive soft tissue as primary closure: survival was 100%; buccal bone height and keratinized mucosa decreased less with closure, while MBL and soft tissue changes did not differ at 1 year.

P1197.t: The Effect of Vertical Implant Position in Relation to Adjacent Teeth on Marginal Bone Loss in Posterior Arches: A Retrospective Study
P1197.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1197.kf: Retrospective study of 139 patients with posterior implants adjacent to a tooth (mean follow-up 4.42 years): placement more than 3 mm apical to the adjacent CEJ was associated with greater bone loss mesially (0.57 mm) and distally (0.83 mm).

P1198.t: Clinical and Radiographic Evaluation of the Papilla Level Adjacent to Single-Tooth Dental Implants. A Retrospective Study in the Maxillary Anterior Region
P1198.kf: Retrospective evaluation of 52 papillae around 27 anterior maxillary single implants in 26 patients: with contact point–bone crest distance ≤5 mm the papilla was present almost 100% of the time, and ≤50% when ≥6 mm.

P1201.t: Incidence of inter-proximal papilla between a tooth and an adjacent immediate implant placed into a fresh extraction socket: 1-year prospective study
P1201.kf: Prospective study of 46 immediate implants with single crowns: survival was 100% at 12 months, and the papilla was significantly present when implant–tooth distance was 3–4 mm and contact point–bone distance 3–5 mm (P<0.05).

P1202.t: Papilla height in relation to the distance between bone crest and interproximal contact point at single-tooth implants: A systematic review
P1202.kf: Systematic review of 12 studies of anterior maxillary single-implant crowns: contact point–bone distance ranged 2–11 mm, and partial or complete papilla fill (Jemt 2–3) ranged from 56.5% to 100% of cases.

P1205.t: A systematic review on the influence of the horizontal distance between two adjacent implants inserted in the anterior maxilla on the inter‐implant mucosa fill
P1205.kf: Systematic review including 4 studies of adjacent anterior maxillary implants: horizontal inter-implant distance ranged 2.01–4.0 mm, and inter-implant mucosa filled more than half the space in 21% to 88.5% of cases.

P1207.t: The Effect of Interimplant Distance on Peri-implant Bone and Soft Tissue Dimensional Changes: A Nonrandomized, Prospective, 2-Year Follow-up Study
P1207.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1207.kf: Nonrandomized prospective 2-year study of 30 patients with adjacent platform-switched conical-connection implants at about 2, 3 or >4 mm apart: marginal and midproximal bone loss (e.g. 0.27, 0.23 and 0.44 mm at 24 months) did not differ significantly between groups.

P1208.t: The Effect of Interimplant Distance on the Height of the Interimplant Bone Crest When Using Platform-Switched Implants
P1208.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1208.kf: Radiographic evaluation of 41 pairs of platform-switched implants placed less than 3 mm apart in 37 patients: mean vertical bone resorption was 0.62 mm, horizontal 0.60 mm, and 0.24 mm of bone height was preserved above the inter-implant line.

P1211.t: A prospective, randomized, controlled study using OsseoSpeed™ implants placed in maxillary fresh extraction socket: soft tissues response
P1211.kf: Multicenter RCT of 93 patients randomized to cylindrical or conical/cylindrical OsseoSpeed implants in maxillary fresh sockets: over 3 years mean gingival zenith change was 0.23 mm, and 79% and 72% of mesial and distal papillae were >50%/complete.

P1218.t: Immediate implant placement with immediate or delayed provisionalization in the maxillary aesthetic zone A 10-year randomized trial
P1218.kf: 10-year RCT of 40 immediate maxillary aesthetic-zone implants with immediate or delayed provisionalization: mesial/distal MBL changes were −0.47/−0.49 mm vs −0.58/−0.41 mm (not significant), implant survival was 100% and restoration survival 88.9% vs 87.5%.

P1224.t: Immediate implant placement with or without immediate provisionalization: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P1224.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 7 RCTs (323 single immediate implants, 12 to 60 months follow-up) on immediate provisionalization. In intact alveoli, immediate provisionalization gave 0.87 mm (95% CI 0.57; 1.17) less apical migration of the midfacial soft tissue; survival, papillary and marginal bone changes …

P1226.t: Osteointegration of Tissue-Level Implants With Very Low Insertion Torque in Soft Bone: A Clinical Study on SLA Surface Treatment
P1226.kf: Clinical series of 11 Straumann SLA tissue-level implants placed in soft bone with insertion torque below 10 Ncm and slight mobility: all passed a 35 Ncm reverse torque test at 4–6 months and remained functional after 28.5 months.

P1228.t: Single Dental Implant Restoration: Cemented or Screw-Retained? A Systematic Review of Multi-Factor Randomized Clinical Trials
P1228.kf: Systematic review of 8 studies comparing cemented and screw-retained single implant restorations: the primary outcomes MBL and BOP did not differ (p = 0.5813 and 0.8093), and clinical, technical and biological outcomes were comparable.

P1236.t: Predicting bone and soft tissue alterations of immediate implant sites in the esthetic zone using clinical parameters
P1236.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1236.kf: Regression analysis of 36 non-grafted immediate implant sites from an RCT at 12 months: gingival phenotype was the only parameter associated with both mid-buccal recession and buccal ridge reduction; flap elevation and older age were linked to interproximal recession.

P1237.t: Predictors of inter-proximal and midfacial recession following single implant treatment in the anterior maxilla: a multivariate analysis
P1237.kf: Retrospective cohort of 97 patients with anterior maxillary single implants: ridge re-contouring surgery (OR ≥ 3.4) and preoperative tooth bone level predicted interproximal recession, while midfacial recession was associated only with a buccal shoulder position (OR = 17.2).

P1238.t: The effect of placing a bone replacement graft in the gap at immediately placed implants: a randomized clinical trial
P1238.kf: RCT of 86 immediate anterior maxillary implants with or without DBBM-C gap grafting: at 16 weeks buccal horizontal crest reduction was 1.1 mm (29%) with graft vs 1.6 mm (38%) without (P = 0.02), more pronounced with thin buccal plates.

P1241.t: Esthetic, clinical and patient‐centered outcomes of immediately placed implants (Type 1) and early placed implants (Type 2): preliminary 3‐month results of an ongoing randomized controlled clinical trial
P1241.kf: RCT of 38 patients randomized to immediate (Type 1) or early (Type 2) placement; 32 completed 3-month follow-up with 100% survival, mid-facial soft tissue loss of 0.54 vs 0.47 mm (P > 0.05) and about 1 mm papilla reduction in both.

P1243.t: Minimally Invasive Single Implant Treatment (M.I.S.I.T.) based on ridge preservation and contour augmentation in patients with a high aesthetic risk profile: one‐year results
P1243.kf: Prospective case series of 50 high-risk patients (47 examined at 12 months) treated with flapless ridge preservation, delayed implant, provisional crown and connective tissue graft (M.I.S.I.T.). All implants survived; mean bone loss was 0.48 mm; mid-facial recession in the recession group was reduced by 0.9 mm (2/3 of …

P1245.t: Immediate Placement of Implants into Infected Sites: A Systematic Review
P1245.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1245.kf: Systematic review of animal and human studies on immediate implant placement into infected sites (32 studies identified, 5 more by hand search). The authors conclude high survival rates support successful osseointegration after meticulous debridement and 0.12% chlorhexidine rinse; antibiotic benefits remain unproven …

P1256.t: Immediate Placement of Implants Into Infected Sites: A Systematic Review of the Literature
P1256.kf: Systematic review (12 publications included, animal and human studies) on immediate implant placement into infected sites. The authors conclude implants can be placed into sites with periapical and periodontal infection after thorough debridement, usually with guided bone regeneration; systemic antibiotics were used …

P1257.t: Retrospective evaluation of implant‐supported full‐arch fixed dental prostheses after a mean follow‐up of 10 years
P1257.kf: Retrospective study of 709 patients with 869 full-arch implant-supported FDPs (4,797 implants), mean follow-up 10.7 years: cumulative implant survival was 93.3% at 10 and 87.1% at 20 years; 47.8% of prostheses had technical complications.

P1263.t: Efficacy of rehabilitation with different approaches of implant‐supported full‐arch prosthetic designs: A systematic review
P1263.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies in periodontitis-related edentulism: cumulative 5-year implant loss was 1.85% for fixed and 4.45% for removable full-arch prostheses; peri-implantitis affected 10%–50% of fixed-prosthesis patients.

P1265.t: Modern Approach to Full Arch Immediate Loading: The Simonpieri Technique with PRF and i‐PRF
P1265.j: Platelet Rich Fibrin in Regenerative Dentistry: Biological Background and Clinical Indications

P1267.t: Periodontal regeneration of dehisence defects using a modified perforated collagen membrane. A comparative experimental study
P1267.kf: Study in 8 dogs of 16 dehiscence defects treated with β-TCP plus perforated or occlusive collagen membranes: both achieved complete periodontal regeneration, but perforated membranes showed denser, more mature bone and significantly higher bone surface area.

P1272.t: A randomized controlled study comparing guided bone regeneration with connective tissue graft to re‐establish buccal convexity: One‐year aesthetic and patient‐reported outcomes
P1272.kf: Single-blind RCT of 42 patients with anterior maxillary single implants and horizontal defects (21 per group): PES did not differ between GBR (10.11) and CTG (10.48), but the Mucosal Scarring Index was significantly lower with CTG (1.10 vs 2.53).

P1281.t: Effectiveness of Lateral Bone Augmentation on the Alveolar Crest Dimension
P1281.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 clinical studies of lateral ridge augmentation: the simultaneous approach produced a significant defect height reduction (WMD −4.28 mm, 95% CI −4.88 to −3.69), with grafts plus barrier membranes associated with superior outcomes.

P1282.t: Membranes for guided tissue and bone regeneration
P1282.kf: Narrative review of GBR/GTR membranes from expanded PTFE to resorbable and platelet-rich fibrin membranes, describing improved mechanical properties and degradation rates and the incorporation of calcium phosphates and growth factors.

P1285.kf: Narrative review defining osteoinduction, osteoconduction and osseointegration. The authors conclude they are interrelated but not identical: osteoinduction is part of normal bone healing and accounts for most new bone, while osteoconduction and osseointegration also depend on the response to the foreign material, and …

P1295.t: The Influence of the Bucco‐Palatal Distance on Sinus Augmentation Outcomes
P1295.kf: Prospective cohort of 21 patients (24 sinuses; 20 analyzed) undergoing sinus augmentation with particulate allograft, with biopsies at 6 months. Mean vital bone was 22.71 +/- 19.08%; vital bone was inversely related to bucco-palatal sinus distance (R2 = 0.141; P<0.001); one sinus infection (96% success).

P1322.t: Simultaneous Hard and Soft Tissue Augmentation for Implants in the Esthetic Zone: Report of 37 Consecutive Cases
P1322.kf: Retrospective report of 37 maxillary anterior defects with buccal plate loss treated with FDBA, rhPDGF, GBR membranes and pediculated connective tissue grafts (12 immediate implants): all sites healed uneventfully, and 36 implants were stable and successful at 6 and 12 months.

P1327.t: Contour Management of Implant Restorations for Optimal Emergence Profiles: Guidelines for Immediate and Delayed Provisional Restorations
P1327.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1327.kf: Narrative review with guidelines on contour management of provisional implant restorations, defining critical and subcritical contours. The authors conclude that for immediate implants the critical contour should support the gingival margin while a concave subcritical contour provides regenerative space; in delayed …

P1331.t: Treatment of intrabony defects with modified perforated membranes in aggressive periodontitis: a 12-month randomized controlled trial
P1331.kf: 12-month split-mouth RCT of 15 aggressive periodontitis patients with paired intrabony defects treated with xenograft plus perforated or standard collagen membrane: PPD, CAL and defect depth improved similarly, but perforated sites gained additional linear (0.4 mm) and percentage (6.4%) defect fill from 6 to 12 months.

P1333.t: In situ shell technique for edentulous ridge augmentation
P1333.kf: Technique report of a two-stage in situ shell approach using an autogenous bone plate, allograft mixed with injectable PRF and a resorbable membrane; in the presented cases sufficient bone regenerated to place implants in an ideal position.

P1342.t: Collagen-Based Biomaterials for Tissue Engineering Applications
P1342.kf: Narrative review of collagen-based biomaterials for tissue engineering (sources, cross-linking, combinations with other biopolymers and applications). The authors conclude collagen remains the protein of choice for biomaterials because of its biocompatibility and low immunogenicity, with current research aimed at …

P1345.t: Minimal invasiveness in the surgical treatment of intraosseous defects A systematic review
P1345.kf: Systematic review of 13 trials on invasiveness of intraosseous defect surgery: single flaps reduced postoperative pain versus double flaps, membranes increased chair time and pain, and enamel matrix derivative with grafts reduced pain.

P1370.t: Non‐Carious Cervical Lesions Associated With Gingival Recessions: A Decision‐Making Process
P1370.kf: Clinical study of 94 patients with NCCLs and single gingival recessions treated with one of five procedures chosen by the relationship between maximum root coverage level and the lesion: patient and periodontist esthetic satisfaction was very high 1 year after all treatments.

P1381.t: The accuracy of static computer‐aided implant surgery: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P1381.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 clinical studies (2,238 implants, 471 patients) of static computer-aided implant surgery: mean error was 1.2 mm at entry, 1.4 mm at apex and 3.5° angular, with better accuracy in partially than fully edentulous cases.

P1382.t: Autoclaving-induced dimensional changes of three-dimensional printed surgical guides An in vitro study
P1382.kf: In vitro study of 50 3D-printed surgical guides from five resin/printer combinations: printing itself caused significant dimensional changes in all, and both steam autoclaving cycles produced minor but significant shrinkage in some combinations, while one resin showed no changes.

P1383.t: Impact of radiographic field-of-view volume on alignment accuracy during virtual implant planning: A noninterventional retrospective pilot study
P1383.kf: Retrospective pilot study of 15 participants: reducing CBCT field of view gave the largest mean (0.10 ± 0.33 mm) and maximum (1.44 mm) alignment discrepancies with artifacts, while precision decreased with smaller FOV but not with operator expertise.

P1384.t: Accuracy of dental implant placement with or without the use of a dynamic navigation assisted system: A randomized clinical trial
P1384.kf: RCT of 60 partially edentulous patients randomized to dynamic navigation or freehand placement: angular deviation was 4.02° vs 7.97° (p < .001) and most linear deviations were lower with navigation, which took 14 minutes longer; pain and satisfaction were similar.

P1385.t: Fabrication, workflow and delivery of reconstruction: Summary and consensus statements of group 4. The 6th EAO Consensus Conference 2021
P1385.kf: Consensus report (6th EAO Conference, group 4) assessing four systematic reviews. Limited evidence (49 non-randomized studies) shows excellent outcomes of all-ceramic implant crowns up to 3 years; monolithic crowns chip less than veneered; evidence on CAD-CAM production and computer-assisted surgery time/cost is …

P1389.t: Current state of the art of computer‐guided implant surgery
P1389.kf: Narrative review of computer-guided implant surgery. The authors conclude no decisive evidence shows computer-assisted surgery is superior to conventional procedures for safety, outcomes, morbidity or efficiency; inaccuracies are reported, most with bone-supported guides, and accuracy depends on cumulative errors from …

P1391.t: Diagnosis and Treatment Approaches to a "Gummy Smile"
P1391.kf: Narrative review of the diagnosis and treatment of excessive gingival display (gummy smile). The authors stress that identifying the etiology (lip length or mobility, crown length, altered passive eruption, vertical maxillary excess) must precede treatment, with options including gingivectomy or crown lengthening, lip …

P1392.t: The diagnosis and treatment of the gummy smile
P1392.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P1392.kf: Narrative review with five illustrative case reports on diagnosing and treating the gummy smile due to altered passive eruption (Coslet types 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B), where treatment ranges from gingivectomy to flap with osseous resection. The authors conclude esthetic crown lengthening is a powerful procedure that is …

P1393.t: Gummy Smile and Short Tooth Syndrome - Part 2: Periodontal Surgical Approaches in Interdisciplinary Treatment
P1393.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P1393.kf: Narrative review (Part 2) with two illustrated cases on periodontal surgical approaches to gummy smile and short tooth syndrome, contrasting a biological approach (re-exposing the CEJ) with a restorative approach. The authors conclude that misdiagnosing altered eruption can cause esthetic and periodontal failures, so …

P1395.t: Gummy Smile and Short Tooth Syndrome--Part 1: Etiopathogenesis, Classification, and Diagnostic Guidelines
P1395.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P1395.kf: Narrative review (Part 1) proposing an adult classification of gummy smile and short tooth syndrome causes and a six-step diagnostic process. The authors conclude treatment must start from a complete diagnosis of the etio-anatomical causes, often multidisciplinary, and that a pleasing smile can be achieved even …

P1397.t: Gummy Smile: Mercado-Rosso Classification System and Dynamic Restructuring with Hyaluronic Acid
P1397.kf: Clinical-experience report proposing the Mercado-Rosso classification of gummy smile into three types (lack of maxillary support, levator muscle imbalance, zygomatic muscle overactivity) with a hyaluronic acid filler treatment for each. The authors state that the treatment maintains 70 to 80% of its effectiveness at …

P1398.t: Gummy smiles: Etiologies, diagnoses & formulating a clinically effective treatment protocol
P1398.kf: Narrative review of the etiologies and diagnosis of gummy smile and a treatment protocol, focused on orthodontic approaches (such as miniscrew-based intrusion) for moderate to severe cases. The authors conclude gummy smile is a subjective clinical observation rather than a cephalometric measurement, so soft and hard …

P1399.t: The Effect of Healing Abutment Reconnection and Disconnection on Soft and Hard Peri-implant Tissues: A Short-Term Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
P1399.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1399.kf: RCT of 16 patients (21 implants) receiving a permanent abutment at placement or a healing abutment disconnected twice: survival was 100%, and 6-month marginal bone loss was 0.13 mm vs 0.28 mm, with no significant difference in mucosal dimensions.

P1400.t: Influence of the fixed implant‐supported provisional phase on the esthetic final outcome of implant‐supported crowns: 3‐year results of a randomized controlled clinical trial
P1400.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1400.kf: RCT of 20 anterior maxillary implants randomized after reopening to a provisional phase with dynamic compression soft tissue conditioning or no provisional phase: all implants survived at 3 years, modified PES differed significantly between groups (P = .018), while WES did not (P = .194).

P1403.t: Immediate loading of occluding definitive partial fixed prostheses vs non-occluding provisional restorations - 3-year post-loading results from a pragmatic multicentre randomised controlled trial
P1403.kf: Multicentre RCT of 40 partially edentulous patients immediately loaded with occluding definitive or non-occluding provisional fixed prostheses: at 3 years bone loss was 1.13 vs 1.03 mm, failures and complications did not differ significantly, but chair time and visits were significantly lower with definitive …

P1404.t: Facial Gingival Tissue Stability Following Immediate Placement and Provisionalization of Maxillary Anterior Single Implants: A 2- to 8-Year Follow-up
P1404.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1404.kf: Follow-up of 35 immediately placed and provisionalized anterior maxillary single implants (mean 4 years, range 2–8.2): all implants remained in function, papillae regenerated over time, but facial gingival recession continued and was smaller with thick biotypes.

P1405.t: Gingival recontouring by provisional implant restoration for optimal emergence profile: report of two cases
P1405.kf: Two-case report of gingival recontouring with a provisional implant restoration fabricated on a trimmed soft tissue cast: after 4 to 6 weeks the peri-implant gingiva reformed in harmony with the adjacent dentition.

P1406.t: Immediate occlusal loading of Brånemark implants applied in various jawbone regions: a prospective, 1-year clinical study
P1406.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1406.kf: Prospective 1-year study of 41 patients with 127 immediately occlusally loaded Brånemark implants: 22 implants were lost (cumulative success 82.7%), with 66% success in the posterior maxilla vs 91% elsewhere and more losses in bruxers (41% vs 12%).

P1407.t: Implant and prosthesis survival rates of full-arch immediate prostheses supported by implants with and without bicortical anchorage: Up to 2 years of follow-up retrospective study
P1407.kf: Retrospective study of 392 hydrophilic Morse taper implants supporting full-arch immediate prostheses, with or without bicortical anchorage, followed up to 24 months: overall implant survival was 99.7% and prosthesis survival 100%; bicortical implants had significantly higher primary stability.

P1408.t: Influence of the loading protocol and platform switching in two-implant bar-retained overdentures: 3-year results from a randomized controlled equivalence clinical trial
P1408.kf: Equivalence RCT of 32 patients with two-implant bar-retained mandibular overdentures loaded immediately or at 3 months: mean bone level change was −0.96 ± 0.89 mm, equivalent for platform switching but smaller with immediate loading when baseline was implant placement (p = .017).

P1410.t: Immediate loading: From biology to biomechanics. Report of the Committee on Research in Fixed Prosthodontics of the American Academy of Fixed Prosthodontics
P1410.kf: Committee report reviewing animal and human evidence on immediate loading: high survival is reported for many but not all modalities, and favorable bone response may result from biomechanically sound designs.

P1411.t: One-piece zirconia oral implants for single-tooth replacement: Three-year results from a long-term prospective cohort study
P1411.kf: Prospective cohort of 65 patients with one-piece zirconia implants and immediate temporization: at 3 years six posterior implants were lost (cumulative survival 90.8%), mean bone loss was 1.45 mm, and 22% lost more than 3 mm.

P1413.t: The role of primary stability for successful immediate loading of dental implants. A literature review
P1413.kf: Literature review of MEDLINE articles (1979–2010) concluding that primary stability is the core issue for immediate loading and depends on bone density and quality, implant shape, design, surface and surgical technique.

P1414.t: Stability of the Mucosal Topography Around Single-Tooth Implants and Adjacent Teeth: 1-Year Results
P1414.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1414.kf: Case series of 10 single-tooth implants treated with GBR and connective tissue grafting: 1 year after prosthesis insertion buccal soft tissue shrinkage averaged 0.6 mm, papilla volume increased by 0.375 mm, and no papilla lost volume.

P1416.t: 3‐D tooth movement adjacent to single anterior implants and esthetic outcome. A 14‐ to 20‐year follow‐up study
P1416.kf: Follow-up of 30 patients with anterior maxillary single-implant crowns after 14–20 years: adjacent teeth moved 0–2.5 mm, mostly incisally and palatally; incisal movement >1 mm occurred in 30% and was associated with lower anterior facial height ≥70 mm.

P1417.t: Lifelong Craniofacial Growth and the Implications for Osseointegrated Implants
P1417.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1417.kf: Observational case presentations of partially edentulous implant restorations followed more than 20 years: continued adult craniofacial growth was associated with occlusal changes, open contacts from tooth migration, labialization of anterior implant crowns and progressive gingival margin discrepancies.

P1422.t: Clinical effectiveness of mechanical-chemical tissue displacement methods
P1422.kf: Comparison of gingival displacement cords: racemic epinephrine and aluminum sulfate cords did not differ and both were more effective than nonmedicated cord, while Hemodent saturation approximately doubled hemostasis success of any cord.

P1423.t: Exposing the gingival margin: a systematic approach for the control of hemorrhage
P1423.kf: Technique report describing a systematic approach to exposing the gingival margin before impression: first control hemorrhage, then use moist astringent cords, hemostyptic syringe or surgical trimming depending on the clinical situation. The authors conclude consistent deflection can be achieved without iatrogenic …

P1424.t: Disinfection of alginate impression material using disinfectants as mixing and soak solutions
P1424.kf: In vitro study of alginate specimens prepared and soaked with chlorhexidine gluconate or sodium peroxysulphate solutions, then infected and incubated: chlorhexidine gluconate proved an effective alginate disinfectant when used as mixing liquid and post-setting solution.

P1427.t: Multi-unit implant impression accuracy: A review of the literature
P1427.kf: Literature review of 59 studies (3 clinical, rest in vitro) on multi-unit implant impressions: 11 of 15 found no PVS–polyether difference, splinting results were split (13 vs 13), 12 of 25 favored pickup over transfer, and 20–25° angulation reduced accuracy.

P1431.t: Accuracy of Implant Impressions for Partially and Completely Edentulous Patients: A Systematic Review
P1431.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1431.kf: Systematic review of 76 studies (4 clinical, 72 in vitro): splinted impressions were more accurate in both edentulous (15 vs 1 studies) and partially edentulous patients, and open-tray was more accurate in completely edentulous cases; impression material had no effect.

P1432.t: Accuracy of 3 different impression techniques for internal connection angulated implants
P1432.kf: In vitro study of 6 internal-connection implants at 0, 15 and 25 degrees: at 25° the splinted technique was most accurate (0.39 ± 0.05 mm) and snap-fit least (0.85 ± 0.09 mm), with no splinted–nonsplinted difference at 0°.

P1433.t: The accuracy of implant impressions: a systematic review
P1433.kf: Systematic review of 41 in vitro studies: of 17 splint vs nonsplint comparisons 7 favored splinting, 3 nonsplint and 7 no difference; 10 of 11 found no difference between polyether and VPS.

P1438.kf: Narrative review of implant impression techniques. The authors suggest using a rigid open custom tray with pick-up copings and polyvinyl siloxane, noting studies show pick-up copings are more accurate than transfer types and that splinting gives no statistically significant improvement, and describe methods to …

P1439.t: Accuracy of digital implant impressions in clinical studies: A systematic review
P1439.kf: Systematic review of 8 clinical studies (10 to 39 patients) of digital implant impressions: the oldest study showed the highest linear deviation (1000 ± 650 µm), while others reported 360 ± 46 µm to 40 ± 20 µm.

P1440.t: Comparative Review of Gingival Retraction Agents
P1440.kf: Narrative comparative review of gingival retraction agents (aluminum-salt astringents versus epinephrine vasoconstrictors). The authors conclude astringent metal salts should be preferred because therapeutic effect is similar with fewer systemic adverse effects, and that tetrahydrozoline and oxymetazoline merit …

P1441.t: Accuracy of two impression techniques with angulated implants
P1441.kf: In vitro study of open- and closed-tray addition silicone impressions of 3-implant casts with 0–15 degree convergence or divergence: angle errors did not differ between techniques (P=.22), and the combined effect of technique, angulation and implant number was not significant (P=.19).

P1442.kf: Narrative review of gingival retraction techniques, classified as mechanical, chemo-mechanical, cordless and surgical (including laser), with newer modalities. The authors conclude clinicians should know the different methods and products for different clinical scenarios, sometimes combining methods, and note …

P1443.t: A Practical Guide to Use and Methods of Disinfection of Alginate Impression Materials
P1443.kf: Narrative practical guide to using and disinfecting alginate impression materials. The authors conclude recommended disinfection protocols must be followed to prevent cross-contamination and avoid dimensional change, because prolonged immersion causes liquid absorption, swelling and an ill-fitting prosthesis.

P1446.t: The accuracy of different dental impression techniques for implant‐supported dental prostheses: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P1446.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 79 studies (77 experimental, 1 RCT, 1 retrospective; 75 in vitro) on the accuracy of conventional and digital implant impressions; meta-analysis covered 62 studies with high heterogeneity. The authors conclude the evidence level is low and lacks in vivo data to derive clinical …

P1447.t: Effect of Multiple Use of Impression Copings on the Accuracy of Implant Transfer
P1447.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1447.kf: In vitro study of 40 polyether impressions of a 5-implant cast using copings cleaned and sterilized up to 10 times: only θy in the open-tray technique was influenced by repeated use (P = .02).

P1448.t: Effect of Multiple Use of Impression Copings and Scanbodies on Implant Cast Accuracy
P1448.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1448.kf: In vitro study reusing one set of impression copings for 10 polyether impressions and one set of scanbodies for 10 scans of a two-implant model: most repetition cycles showed no significant differences, with sporadic significant deviations for some casts and scan 2.

P1449.t: Accuracy of Implant Impressions with Different Impression Coping Types and Shapes
P1449.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1449.kf: In vitro study of 40 polyether impressions on two five-implant models comparing direct and indirect techniques and two coping shapes (Implantium versus Replace Select). The less retentive Replace Select coping showed smaller 3D displacement (0.16 and 0.19 mm vs 0.28 and 0.26 mm; p<.001), while direct versus indirect …

P1450.t: Accuracy of Impression Techniques for Implants. Part 2 – Comparison of Splinting Techniques
P1450.kf: In vitro study (24 polyether impressions, implants at 90 and 65 degrees) comparing splinting techniques for pick-up impression copings. Mean angular difference from the control was 1.019 degrees unsplinted, 0.747 and 0.516 degrees with floss-and-acrylic splints, and 0.325 degrees with a prefabricated acrylic bar, …

P1451.t: Final Impressions: A Review of Material Properties and Description of a Current Technique
P1451.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P1451.kf: Narrative review of physical properties of final impression materials (polyvinyl siloxane versus polyether) and a described one-step/double-mix technique with double-cord gingival displacement for esthetic rehabilitation. The authors conclude impression quality plays a major role in prosthetic success and recommend …

P1456.t: Viability of fibroblasts in cell culture after treatment with different chemical retraction agents
P1456.kf: Cell culture study of four chemical retraction agents on V-79 fibroblasts: 25% aluminium chloride damaged all cultures within 1 min, while tetrahydrozoline damaged 60% of cells after 10 min, significantly less than other agents.

P1457.t: The segmental impression technique: A straightforward solution to a difficult problem
P1457.kf: Dental technique report describing a segmental (sectional tray) impression technique for multiple tooth preparations, giving extra working time by capturing each 3 to 4 tooth segment separately with light-body PVS before picking up all segments. The authors call it a useful procedure for simplifying definitive …

P1458.t: Effect of impression coping and implant angulation on the accuracy of implant impressions: an in vitro study
P1458.kf: In vitro study of 40 VPS impressions of a 3-analog master cast (parallel and 10° angulated) using pick-up or transfer copings of long or short length: pick-up copings showed a significantly lower error rate than transfer copings, while coping length and angulation had no significant effect.

P1459.t: Accuracy of a proposed implant impression technique using abutments and metal framework
P1459.kf: In vitro study of 3-implant casts at 0, 30 and 40 degrees comparing an abutment-framework open-tray technique with closed-tray and resin-splinted open-tray impressions: open-tray techniques gave significantly smaller vertical gaps, and only the abutment-framework technique was unaffected by angulation.

P1461.t: Gingival Displacement in the Vertical and Horizontal Dimension under the Condition of Mild Gingivitis—A Randomized Clinical Study
P1461.kf: Randomized clinical study of 40 probands with induced mild gingivitis receiving 3M Astringent Retraction Paste (22) or double-cord technique with aluminum chloride (18) on upper premolars: horizontal displacement was comparable and vertical displacement somewhat better with cords.

P1463.t: Digital evaluation of the accuracy of impression techniques and materials in angulated implants
P1463.kf: In vitro study of 180 impressions of models with parallel, 10° or 20° angulated implants using splinted direct or indirect techniques and PE, VPS or VPES: mean deviations were 0.205–0.359° and 22.56–33.33 μm, with VPS-direct most accurate and VPES-indirect least accurate.

P1465.t: Effect of subgingival depth of implant placement on the dimensional accuracy of the implant impression: An in vitro study
P1465.kf: In vitro study of open-tray impressions (n=15 per material) of implants at 0, 2 and 4 mm subgingival depth: depth had no effect with VPS, but with polyether the 4-mm-deep implant showed greater horizontal distortion than the 0-mm implant (P=.02), eliminated by a 4-mm coping extension.

P1467.t: Axial displacements in external and internal implant‐abutment connection
P1467.kf: In vitro study of external butt-joint vs internal conical connections measuring axial abutment displacement after 30 Ncm tightening and 1,000,000 loading cycles: internal conical connections showed more axial displacement with impression copings than external connections.

P1468.t: Accuracy of digital versus conventional implant impressions
P1468.kf: In vitro study of 30 gypsum models from conventional closed-tray impressions versus 30 milled models from digital impressions of a single implant, compared with a reference model. Accuracy was comparable except in fossae (P<0.001) and vertical implant position (P=0.020), where gypsum models were more apical (0.088 mm) …

P1469.t: Accuracy Comparison of Implant Impression Techniques: A Systematic Review
P1469.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1469.kf: Systematic review of 32 in vitro studies (2009–2013): 8 of 14 favored open over closed tray (6 similar), and all 14 splinting studies advocated splinted techniques.

P1470.t: Dimensional accuracy and surface detail reproduction of two hydrophilic vinyl polysiloxane impression materials tested under dry, moist, and wet conditions
P1470.kf: In vitro study of 102 impressions of ADA-type dies with two hydrophilic VPS materials under dry, moist and wet conditions: dimensional change was ≤0.005%, but surface detail declined in moist and wet conditions (wet: 47% Aquasil and 11% Reprosil satisfactory).

P1471.kf: Narrative review of dental impression materials and techniques, conventional and digital. The authors' key points are that conventional techniques remain widely used and reviewing them improves outcomes, while digital dentistry is well established and clinicians should become familiar with it; some cited studies found …

P1473.t: Evaluation of impression accuracy for osseointegrated implant supported superstructures
P1473.kf: In vitro study of 4 implant impression techniques (tapered, squared, squared splinted and squared with lateral extension copings): dimensional accuracy was high, with a statistically significant but maximum distortion difference of only 0.31%.

P1474.t: Evaluation of material waste, dimensional stability, and detail reproduction of polyvinyl siloxane impression materials mixed with different mixing tips
P1474.kf: In vitro study of six polyvinyl siloxane impression materials (regular and light-body) mixed with T-Mixer vs helical mixing tips (n=10). The T-Mixer reduced material waste; Virtual Light with T-Mixer showed lower dimensional change (0.53 ±0.58%) than with the helical tip (1.09 ±0.43%).

P1476.t: Effect of Implant Angulation, Connection Length, and Impression Material on the Dimensional Accuracy of Implant Impressions: An In Vitro Comparative Study
P1476.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1476.kf: In vitro comparison of open-tray pick-up implant impressions using addition silicone and polyether with different impression coping connection lengths and implant angulations. Impressions of angulated implants were significantly less accurate than those of parallel implants.

P1477.t: 인상용 트레이의 종류와 인상용 코핑의 연결고정이 임플랜트 주모형의 정확성에 미치는 영향
P1477.j: 구강회복응용과학지 (Journal of Dental Rehabilitation and Applied Science)
P1477.kf: In vitro study of open-tray implant impressions with three tray types (custom resin, plastic-metal, polycarbonate stock), with or without coping splinting (10 specimens per group). Tray type made no significant difference, while pattern-resin splinting gave more accurate master casts (p<0.05).

P1479.t: Master Cast Accuracy in Single-Tooth Implant Replacement Cases: An In Vitro Comparison. A Technical Note
P1479.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1479.kf: In vitro comparison of 20 impressions using sandblasted, adhesive-coated square impression copings vs 20 using gold machined UCLA abutments as copings for a single implant. Rotational position changes of the implant replica hexagon were significantly less variable with the UCLA abutments.

P1481.t: Clinical study evaluating the discrepancy of two different impression techniques of four implants in an edentulous jaw
P1481.kf: Clinical study of 10 edentulous jaws with four implants each, comparing transfer and splinted pick-up impressions. Mean discrepancies were 192 μm (±96), 282 μm (±97) and 366 μm (±114) for scan bodies 2–4, rising with span length; fit was clinically favourable with splinted pick-up casts.

P1482.t: Patients' preferences when comparing analogue implant impressions using a polyether impression material versus digital impressions (Intraoral Scan) of dental implants
P1482.kf: Clinical study of 30 consecutive patients with 41 Straumann tissue-level implants in the non-aesthetic zone, each receiving both polyether impressions and intraoral scans. Preparatory activities, taste and overall preference significantly favoured the intraoral scan.

P1483.t: Altered Vertical Dimension of Occlusion: A Comparative Retrospective Pilot Study of Tooth- and Implant-Supported Restorations
P1483.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1483.kf: Retrospective pilot study of 30 patients whose VDO was increased by 3 to 5 mm, comparing natural-tooth and implant-supported fixed restorations over a mean 66 months. All patients adapted; more bone loss and tooth failures occurred with natural dentition and more mechanical complications such as porcelain fractures …

P1484.t: Dental implants three-dimensional position affected by late facial bone growth: follow-up of 12 to 15 years
P1484.kf: Three adult patients (aged 38 to 60 at implant placement) followed for 12 to 15 years. Continued craniofacial growth led to infraocclusion of implant-supported crowns and diastemas.

P1485.t: Restoration of the extremely worn dentition
P1485.kf: Clinical review (1984) of the etiology, occlusal vertical dimension evaluation and restoration of extremely worn dentitions, classifying patients into three treatment categories. The authors state there is no definitive evidence that wear reduces vertical dimension, and that arbitrary increases should be avoided and …

P1486.t: Vertical and Horizontal Dimensions of Implant Dentistry: Numbers Every Dentist Should Know
P1486.kf: Narrative CE article on vertical and horizontal dimensions for implant dentistry. The authors state a cement-retained restoration needs at least 8 mm of crown height space (ideal 9 to 12 mm), single implants should be 1.5 to 2 mm from adjacent teeth and implants at least 3 mm apart, and these parameters should be …

P1487.t: Full Mouth Rehabilitation With Dental Implants for a Patient With Skeletal Class III Malocclusion: A Case Report
P1487.kf: Case report of a 42-year-old man with skeletal Class III malocclusion, worn maxillary teeth and periodontally compromised mandibular teeth, treated with orthodontics, two-jaw orthognathic surgery, 8 immediately placed implants and full-mouth fixed rehabilitation; at 2 years implants were osseointegrated without …

P1488.t: Clinical considerations for increasing occlusal vertical dimension: a review
P1488.kf: Narrative review of clinical considerations for increasing occlusal vertical dimension. It reports that a minimal increase is generally advised, up to a 5 mm increase can be justified, and permanent increase appears safe with usually interim symptoms.

P1489.t: Safety of increasing vertical dimension of occlusion: A systematic review
