P1489.kf: Systematic review (PubMed through August 2011) of 902 retrieved studies, of which 9 met inclusion criteria; magnitude, method, occlusion scheme and adaptation period were identified as relevant. Permanent VDO increase was judged safe and predictable, with self-limiting negative signs.

P1490.t: Clinical Indications for Altering Vertical Dimension of Occlusion
P1490.kf: Narrative review (with an additional commentary on determining occlusal vertical dimension) on clinical indications for altering vertical dimension of occlusion. The authors state vertical dimension can often be increased if reconstruction starts with condyles in centric relation and stays within each patient's …

P1496.t: Clinical performance of direct composite resin versus indirect restorations on endodontically treated posterior teeth: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1496.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 studies (2 RCTs, 3 prospective, 17 retrospective) comparing direct composite and indirect restorations on endodontically treated posterior teeth. Over 2.5 to 3 years, low-quality evidence suggested no difference in tooth survival or restorative success.

P1503.t: Marginal adaptation of CAD-CAM onlays: Influence of preparation design and impression technique
P1503.kf: In vitro study of CAD-CAM nanoceramic resin onlays comparing a 1.2-mm modified shoulder preparation with flat cuspal reduction, scanned directly or from stone dies. The conventional preparation had smaller mean marginal discrepancy (59 ±50 μm vs 69 ±58 μm, P<.001); indirect scanning gave the smallest buccal …

P1506.t: Simplified treatment of severe dental erosion with ultrathin CAD-CAM composite occlusal veneers and anterior bilaminar veneers
P1506.kf: Single case report of full-mouth rehabilitation of severe dental erosion in a 32-year-old man using ultrathin CAD-CAM composite occlusal veneers on posterior teeth, a 2 mm increase in vertical dimension, and bilaminar (palatal composite plus labial ceramic) veneers anteriorly. Treatment was completed within 1 month; …

P1509.t: Internal vs. external connections for abutments/reconstructions: a systematic review
P1509.kf: Systematic review of internal vs external implant connections regarding implant-level impression accuracy and technical complications. For impression accuracy, seven in vitro studies were included and no clinical study was found.

P1510.t: Group 1 ITI Consensus Report: The role of bone dimensions and soft tissue augmentation procedures on the stability of clinical, radiographic, and patient-reported outcomes of implant treatment
P1510.kf: ITI consensus based on two systematic reviews: buccal bone wall thickness decreased by 0.3 to 1.8 mm after implant placement in healed sites, and BBW <1.5 mm was associated with more vertical bone loss; connective-tissue-grafted sites showed stable soft tissue margins from 1 to 5 years.

P1519.t: Keratinized mucosa around implants in partially edentulous posterior mandible: 10‐year results of a prospective comparative study
P1519.kf: Prospective 10-year study of 128 consecutive patients (98 completed) with one posterior mandibular implant placed within keratinized or alveolar mucosa. Absence of keratinized mucosa was associated with more plaque, greater soft-tissue recession and more sites requiring additional surgical and/or antibiotic treatment.

P1520.t: The Significance of Keratinized Mucosa on Implant Health: A Systematic Review
P1520.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies (7 cross-sectional, 4 longitudinal) on keratinized mucosa width around implants. Significant differences were found in plaque index (WMD = −0.27), modified gingival index (WMD = −0.48), mucosal recession (WMD = −0.60 mm) and attachment loss (WMD = −0.35 mm).

P1521.t: Significance of keratinized mucosa around dental implants: a prospective comparative study
P1521.kf: Prospective comparative study of 15 edentulous patients with four mandibular overdenture implants each (36 evaluated), comparing implants with at least 2 mm keratinized mucosa (19) versus none (17) over 12 months. Implants with keratinized mucosa had significantly lower TNF-alpha total amounts and lower plaque and …

P1522.t: Is there a need for keratinized mucosa around implants to maintain health and tissue stability?
P1522.kf: Systematic literature review of 19 publications (17 human, 2 animal) on keratinized mucosa around implants. Heterogeneity precluded statistical analysis; in 5 of 12 human studies an inadequate (<2 mm) width was associated with significantly higher plaque scores.

P1525.t: Composite veneers: The direct–indirect technique revisited
P1525.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P1525.kf: Clinical article reviewing the direct-indirect composite veneer technique (composite layered on the tooth without bonding, removed, heat-tempered, finished extra-orally, then luted) with a step-by-step case. The authors conclude it combines operator control and single-visit delivery with improved material properties …

P1526.t: Effect of Accelerated Aging on the Color Stability of Light-cured Resin Cement and Flowable Composite Through Porcelain Laminate Veneer
P1526.j: Journal of Islamic Dental Association of IRAN
P1526.kf: In vitro study (4 groups of 5 specimens) of colour change after accelerated aging of light-cured resin cement and flowable composite, alone or under 1-mm feldspathic ceramic. Z350 flowable composite showed the highest colour change (P<0.001), and porcelain-covered groups changed significantly less than uncovered …

P1527.t: Fracture Localisation of Porcelain Veneers with Different Preparation Designs
P1527.j: Open Access Macedonian Journal of Medical Sciences
P1527.kf: In vitro loading to failure of porcelain veneers on maxillary central incisors with feather, bevel or incisal overlap–palatal chamfer preparations. Feather preparations fractured mostly incisally (66.7%), while bevel preparations fractured mostly in combined locations (53.6%).

P1528.t: Influence of Different Types of Resin Luting Agents on Color Stability of Ceramic Laminate Veneers Subjected to Accelerated Artificial Aging
P1528.kf: In vitro study of 80 molars with IPS e.max Ceram laminate veneers (0.5 and 1.0 mm) bonded with light-cured, conventional dual or self-adhesive dual cement and aged for 580 h. Colour change was greatest for 0.5-mm veneers with light-cured cement and lowest for 1.0-mm veneers with conventional dual cement (p<0.05).

P1529.t: Incisal preparation design for ceramic veneers: A critical review
P1529.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P1529.kf: Critical review (MEDLINE/Ovid through March 2017) of incisal preparation designs for ceramic veneers. In vitro studies showed palatal chamfer increases ceramic fracture risk and butt joint least affects tooth strength; clinical studies identified incisal ceramic as the most common fracture site.

P1530.t: Survival Rates for Porcelain Laminate Veneers with Special Reference to the Effect of Preparation in Dentin: A Literature Review
P1530.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P1530.kf: Literature review of 24 clinical papers on porcelain laminate veneer survival. Survival rates were rarely 100%, with reasonable evidence that preparation into dentin adversely affects survival.

P1534.t: A comparison of the marginal and internal fit of porcelain laminate veneers fabricated by pressing and CAD-CAM milling and cemented with 2 different resin cements
P1534.kf: In vitro study of 20 pressed (VITA PM9) and 20 CAD-CAM milled (VITA Blocs Mark II) laminate veneers cemented with RelyX Veneer or Variolink-N. Fabrication method and cement significantly affected cervical marginal gap and internal gap (P<.001); pressed veneers with RelyX Veneer had the lowest gaps and incisal gaps …

P1535.t: A Meta-Analysis of the Most Indicated Preparation Design for Porcelain Laminate Veneers
P1535.kf: Meta-analysis of in vitro studies on veneer preparation design: compared with unprepared teeth, fracture strength fell by 76.53 N with feathered incisal edge and 102.82 N with palatal chamfer preparations, while butt joint showed no significant difference (p = 0.37); ceramic fractures were more frequent with chamfer.

P1536.t: The Success of Dental Veneers According To Preparation Design and Material Type
P1536.j: Open Access Macedonian Journal of Medical Sciences
P1536.kf: Literature review (PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus) of veneer survival by preparation design and material. Incisal overlap preparation seemed to have the most predictable outcome, and composite veneers were considered less durable than porcelain veneers.

P1537.t: An up to 50-year follow-up of crown and veneer survival in a dental practice
P1537.kf: Retrospective single-operator practice study of 223 indirect restorations in 47 patients, reviewed annually for up to 50 years. Mean metal-ceramic crown survival was 47.53 years (95% CI 45.59-49.47), with 6 failures (3.9%) from periapical periodontitis; other restoration types had 100% survival.

P1538.t: A comparison of the film thickness of two adhesive luting agents and the effect of thermocycling on their μTBS to feldspathic ceramic
P1538.kf: In vitro study of a dual-cured resin cement vs a flowable resin bonded to HF-etched, silanized feldspathic ceramic (n=8). Luting agent did not affect μTBS (p= 0.4467); thermocycled specimens showed higher bond strength (20.5 ± 8.6 MPa) than dry ones (13.9 ± 4.7 MPa), and film thicknesses were similar.

P1539.t: Effectiveness of Combination of Dentin and Enamel Layers on the Masking Ability of Porcelain
P1539.kf: In vitro study of bilayer enamel/dentin porcelain disks (0.5 to 1 mm, n=10) over A2 and C4 backgrounds. Thinner disks were more translucent, monolayers were more translucent than bilayers, and dentin porcelain was less translucent than enamel porcelain of the same thickness.

P1542.t: Current Protocols for Resin-Bonded Dental Ceramics
P1542.kf: Narrative review concluding that the longevity of resin-bonded ceramic restorations depends on the resin-ceramic interface, and that ceramic type determines the protocol: HF etching plus silane for silica-based ceramics and polymer-infiltrated ceramic networks; air-particle abrasion plus phosphate-monomer primer for …

P1543.t: Effect of a modified laminate veneer preparation design on absolute margin discrepancy and marginal overhang
P1543.kf: In vitro study of CAD-CAM ceramic veneers on a typodont tooth with feather edge, shoulder, or shoulder-with-wings preparations (n=20). The shoulder-with-wings design produced the smallest cervical absolute margin discrepancy and overhang, and proximal values comparable with the shoulder design.

P1544.t: Degree of conversion of a flowable composite light-activated through ceramics of different shades and thicknesses
P1544.kf: In vitro FTIR study (n=5) of a flowable composite light-activated through IPS Classic ceramic discs (A1, A3; 0.5 to 1.0 mm). The no-ceramic control had the highest degree of conversion (71.9± 1.7); 0.5 and 0.7 mm A1 ceramics gave the highest interposed values (64.6±1.2 and 64.4) and 0.7 and 1 mm A3 the lowest.

P1545.t: Influence of bruxism on survival of porcelain laminate veneers
P1545.j: Medicina Oral, Patología Oral y Cirugía Bucal
P1545.kf: Clinical study of 323 porcelain laminate veneers in 70 patients, 170 of them in patients with bruxism. Of 13 fractures and 29 debondings, 8 fractures and 22 debondings were related to bruxism.

P1546.t: Effect of luting agent on the load to failure and accelerated-fatigue resistance of lithium disilicate laminate veneers
P1546.kf: In vitro study of 40 maxillary central incisors with lithium disilicate veneers luted with adhesive resin cement or restorative composite after thermo-mechanical aging. Composite-luted veneers had higher fatigue survival (mean load 1165N vs 762.5N) and load to failure (927.59N vs 629.4N, p=0.01).

P1550.t: Survival of Porcelain Laminate Veneers with Different Degrees of Dentin Exposure: 2-year Clinical Results
P1550.kf: Prospective clinical study of 125 porcelain laminate veneers in 28 patients over 2 years: 11 (8.8%) failed, giving 91.2% cumulative survival. Veneers bonded with severe dentin exposure failed more often than those on enamel or minimal dentin exposure (p < 0.05).

P1552.t: Color stability of ceramic laminate veneers cemented with light-polymerizing and dual-polymerizing luting agent: A split-mouth randomized clinical trial
P1552.kf: Split-mouth randomized trial in 10 participants with 0.3-mm no-preparation ceramic veneers on second premolars cemented with light- vs dual-polymerizing cement. Colour change did not differ significantly (P>.05) up to 24 months (median ΔE* 2.31 vs 1.57), and marginal discoloration appeared by 2 years in both.

P1553.t: Minimal invasive microscopic tooth preparation in esthetic restoration: a specialist consensus
P1553.kf: Specialist consensus on minimally invasive microscopic tooth preparation. Recommendations include microscope use for 0.1 mm accuracy, diagnostic wax-up and restorative-space guides, supragingival or equigingival margins with 0.3-0.5 mm mini-chamfer, enamel-confined design, and immediate dentin sealing (IDS) to reduce …

P1554.t: Minimally invasive veneers: current state of the art
P1554.kf: Narrative review of preparation and success parameters for ceramic veneers. The authors report success rates of 75% to 100% in studies from 18 months up to 20 years, and conclude minimum-thickness veneers may be a conservative alternative, with no-preparation veneers indicated only in selected cases.

P1556.t: Marginal and internal fit of porcelain laminate veneers: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1556.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 studies (2 clinical, 19 in vitro). Pressed and milled veneers did not differ in marginal gap (MD -4.53 μm, P=.600); pressed veneers had smaller internal gap (MD -40.56 μm, P=.030), and butt joint gave lower marginal gaps than palatal chamfer (MD -14.02 μm, P=.002).

P1557.t: Effect of exposure time on curing efficiency of polymerizing units equipped with light-emitting diodes
P1557.kf: In vitro study of two composites cured with three LED units and one QTH unit for 20, 40 or 60 s (five specimens per group). LED units were as effective as QTH, and microhardness increased significantly when exposure rose from 20 to 40 s.

P1558.t: Minimal exposure time of different LED-curing devices
P1558.kf: In vitro study of five composites cured in three 2-mm increments (n=9) with seven LED units at 7 mm distance simulating a class II cavity. Bluephase, Bluephase C8, Smartlite PS and Translux Power Blue cured all composites sufficiently within manufacturer-recommended times (10-20s).

P1559.t: High-Power LED Units Currently Available for Dental Resin-Based Materials—A Review
P1559.kf: Review of 21 of 1822 screened studies on high-power LED curing units, identifying 32 marketed units (≥2000 up to 6000 mW/cm2), most emitting 2000–3000 mW/cm2. Reports suggested that lower irradiance with longer exposure outperforms other combinations.

P1560.t: CAD/CAM Ceramic Restorative Materials for Natural Teeth
P1560.kf: Narrative review of CAD/CAM ceramics for natural teeth. The authors conclude that long-term success of CAD/CAM glass-ceramic restorations is well proven, preliminary data on polymer-infiltrated ceramic network restorations look promising, and long-term clinical data on monolithic zirconia are still awaited.

P1561.t: Early clinical performance of resin cements in glass-ceramic posterior restorations in adult vital teeth: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1561.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 3 prospective randomized or quasirandomized trials comparing self-adhesive and conventional resin cements for posterior glass-ceramic restorations. No significant differences in tooth or restoration integrity were found at 1 year.

P1562.t: Comparison of mechanical properties of different reinforced glass-ceramics
P1562.kf: In vitro comparison of HS10PC lithium disilicate with IPS e.max Press LT/HT and IPS Empress Esthetic (85 specimens per material). e.max HT had the highest and Empress Esthetic the lowest flexural strength (P<.001); after 1 200 000 masticatory cycles HS10PC showed less ceramic wear than the others (P=.003).

P1564.t: Wear of human enamel opposing monolithic zirconia, glass ceramic, and composite resin: An in vitro study
P1564.kf: In vitro pin-on-disk test (6 specimens per group, 25 N, 4800 cycles) of enamel opposing monolithic zirconia, glass ceramic, composite resin and enamel. Enamel wear depth was lower with zirconia (Dmax 2.17 ±0.80 μm) and composite (1.70 ±0.92 μm) than with glass ceramic (8.54 ±2.31 μm) and enamel (10.72 ±6.31 μm) …

P1565.t: Ceramic Restorations Worn Against Different Occlusal Antagonist (In Vitro Study)
P1565.j: IOSR Journal of Dental and Medical Sciences
P1565.kf: In vitro chewing-simulator study of 60 full-contour zirconia or e.max-pressed-on-zirconia discs worn against natural teeth, PFM crowns or zirconia crowns (49 N, 75000 cycles). E.max showed significantly higher wear than zirconia; teeth wore more than ceramic antagonists but not significantly.

P1567.t: The effect of hydrofluoric acid and resin cement formulation on the bond strength to lithium disilicate ceramic
P1567.kf: In vitro study of 63 lithium disilicate blocks etched with 1%, 5% or 10% HF and luted to dentin with light-cured cements with or without UDMA (n = 10). 10% HF gave higher μTBS than 1% for the UDMA-free cement (p < 0.05), and 6-month water aging generally decreased bond strength.

P1568.t: The Effect of Hydrofluoric Acid Concentration and Heat on the Bonding to Lithium Disilicate Glass Ceramic
P1568.kf: In vitro study of 104 lithium disilicate specimens etched with 5% or 10% HF, with or without prior heating of the acid and/or ceramic (n=13). Without heat treatment, 5% HF gave significantly lower micro-shear bond strength than 10% HF (p<0.05), and heat treatment increased values for 5% HF.

P1569.t: Effects of ceramic primers and post-silanization heat treatment on bond strength of resin cement to lithium disilicate-based ceramic
P1569.kf: In vitro micro-shear study (n = 10) of five ceramic primers, with or without 100 °C heat treatment, bonding RelyX ARC to lithium disilicate. Primer heating did not improve bond strength, and Clearfil Ceramic Primer (used without HF etching) yielded the lowest bond strength.

P1570.t: Preparing Porcelain Surfaces for Optimal Bonding
P1570.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P1570.kf: Narrative review (Compendium CE article) of porcelain intaglio surface treatment, noting no clear consensus. The author's generalizations: low-pressure sandblasting then 60 to 120 seconds of 9% to 10% HF for conventional stackable porcelain; 5% HF for 60 seconds for IPS Empress; silica coating for alumina/zirconia; …

P1571.t: Acid etching surface treatment of feldspathic, alumina and zirconia ceramics: a micro-morphological SEM analysis
P1571.kf: In vitro SEM study of 45 feldspathic, alumina and zirconia ceramic specimens (15 each), 30 of which were etched with 40% HF gel for 2 min. Etching produced micro-morphological surface changes in all three ceramic types.

P1572.t: Wear Evaluation of Prosthetic Materials Opposing Themselves
P1572.kf: In vitro two-body wear test (n=10) of gold alloy, two lithium disilicates, pressed feldspathic porcelain, zirconia and three composites, each opposing the same material for up to 120,000 cycles. Gold alloy vertical wear did not differ significantly from Ceram.X Universal, Enamel Plus Function, IPS e.max CAD and …

P1573.t: Mechanical stability of dental CAD-CAM restoration materials made of monolithic zirconia, lithium disilicate, and lithium disilicate-strengthened aluminosilicate glass-ceramic with and without fatigue conditions
P1573.kf: In vitro study (n=15) of CAD-CAM zirconia, lithium disilicate and lithium disilicate-strengthened aluminosilicate glass-ceramic (N!ce), with or without 1 200 000-cycle aging. Non-aged flexural strength was 1136 ±162 MPa for zirconia vs 304 ±34 and 202 ±17 MPa; aging reduced both glass-ceramics (14.6% and 14.5%) but …

P1574.t: A multicenter randomized controlled clinical pilot study of buccally micro-veneered lithium-disilicate and zirconia crowns supported by titanium base abutments: 1-year outcomes
P1574.kf: Multicenter randomized pilot study of 60 subjects with buccally micro-veneered lithium-disilicate (n = 30) or zirconia (n = 30) implant crowns on titanium base abutments. At a mean 13.2 ± 2.4 months, implant survival was 98.3% and restoration survival 100%; two minor chippings occurred in lithium-disilicate crowns, …

P1576.t: Mechanical properties of zirconia reinforced lithium silicate glass-ceramic
P1576.kf: In vitro comparison of Vita Suprinity (zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate) and IPS e.max CAD (lithium disilicate). Suprinity had significantly higher fracture toughness (2.31±0.17 MPa·m0.5), flexural strength (443.63±38.90 MPa), elastic modulus and hardness (P<0.001), but a higher brittleness index (lower …

P1577.t: Wear properties of dental ceramics and porcelains compared with human enamel
P1577.kf: In vitro two-body wear test (n=10, 120000 cycles against zirconia cusps) of human enamel, Type III gold and five ceramics. Gold wear depth (0.223 mm) was closest to enamel (0.217 mm); milled unglazed Celtra Duo wore most (0.320 mm), significantly more than gold or enamel (P<.05).

P1578.t: Three-body wear potential of dental yttrium-stabilized zirconia ceramic after grinding, polishing, and glazing treatments
P1578.kf: In vitro three-body wear study (8 specimens per group, 50,000 cycles) of enamel opposing zirconia, lithium disilicate and feldspathic porcelain with rough, smooth or glazed surfaces. Smooth zirconia caused the least enamel wear (1.26 ±0.55 mm2), and glazed groups the most (zirconia 5.58 ±0.66 mm2).

P1579.t: Wear of enamel opposing zirconia and lithium disilicate after adjustment, polishing and glazing
P1579.kf: In vitro chewing-simulator study (n=8, 400,000 cycles) of adjusted, polished or glazed zirconia and lithium disilicate vs veneering porcelain and enamel. Veneering porcelain caused the most opposing enamel wear (2.15 ± 0.58 mm3), while polished lithium disilicate and zirconia caused the least (0.36 ± 0.09 and 0.33 ± …

P1582.t: Comparison of the mechanical properties of translucent zirconia and lithium disilicate
P1582.kf: In vitro comparison of 5Y-ZP (Katana UTML), 3Y-TZP (Katana HT) and lithium disilicate (e.max CAD). Flexural strength was 688 ±159, 1194 ±111 and 450 ±53 MPa respectively; bond strength (P=.155) and opposing enamel wear (P=.533) did not differ, and 5Y-ZP showed no measurable material wear.

P1585.t: Wear behavior of human enamel against lithium disilicate glass ceramic and type III gold
P1585.kf: In vitro ball-on-flat friction-wear test (n=5) of human enamel opposing lithium disilicate or Type III gold. Gold had a significantly lower steady-state friction coefficient (P=.009) and caused less enamel wear damage, with abrasive wear predominating against lithium disilicate.

P1586.t: In vitro wear of four ceramic materials and human enamel on enamel antagonist
P1586.kf: In vitro two-body wear test (n=8, 100,000 cycles) of styli made of four ceramics and enamel against flattened enamel. Aadva zirconia had the smallest stylus losses and caused significantly lower antagonist enamel wear than GN-Ceram, Porcelain AAA and enamel styli.

P1587.t: Wear behavior of pressable lithium disilicate glass ceramic
P1587.j: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research Part B: Applied Biomaterials
P1587.kf: Laboratory pin-on-disk study of pressable lithium disilicate disks with different surface finishes worn against alumina pins at different loads. Surface finish and load significantly affected friction and wear, and wear volumes and friction coefficients increased with load.

P1589.t: Monolithic lithium disilicate complete single crowns with feather-edge preparation design in the posterior region: A multicentric retrospective study up to 12 years
P1589.kf: Multicentric retrospective study of 627 pressed monolithic lithium disilicate posterior single crowns with feather-edge margins in 335 patients (mean follow-up 48.17 months, range 6 to 144). Nine crowns failed by bulk fracture (97.93% survival) and four teeth were extracted.

P1590.t: Ultrathin CAD-CAM Ceramic Occlusal Veneers and Anterior Bilaminar Veneers for the Treatment of Moderate Dental Biocorrosion: A 1.5-Year Follow-Up
P1590.kf: Case report of one patient with moderate dental biocorrosion restored with ultrathin CAD-CAM lithium disilicate occlusal veneers (posterior) and bilaminar veneers (maxillary anterior). At 1.5 years the authors report conservation of tooth tissue, esthetics and effective restoration of wear.

P1591.t: Current status on lithium disilicate and zirconia: a narrative review
P1591.kf: Narrative review of lithium disilicate and zirconia properties and applications, based on the literature and the authors' clinical experience. Available data, sometimes conflicting, highlight their optical and esthetic properties, biocompatibility, mechanical resistance, reduced thickness and favourable wear behaviour.

P1592.t: Two-body Wear Performance of Zirconia Opposing e.max Ceramic
P1592.j: University of Illinois at Chicago (MS thesis, Oral Sciences)

P1595.t: Effects of crystal refining on wear behaviors and mechanical properties of lithium disilicate glass-ceramics
P1595.j: Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials
P1595.kf: In vitro study of experimental lithium disilicate glass-ceramics with different crystal sizes vs heat-pressed and ingot controls (n=8–10), with chewing-simulator loading at 350 N. The medium-crystal group (G3) had the highest flexural strength, hardness, elastic modulus, fracture toughness and wear resistance, while …

P1596.t: (Digitally Oriented Materials): Focus on Lithium Disilicate Ceramics
P1596.kf: Narrative review of lithium disilicate ceramics (properties, manufacturing, in vitro and in vivo survival data). The authors conclude it is one of the most promising materials in digital dentistry owing to optical properties, mechanical resistance, versatility and manufacturing options.

P1600.t: Effect of Thermocycling, Surface Treatments and Microstructure on the Optical Properties and Roughness of CAD-CAM and Heat-Pressed Glass Ceramics
P1600.kf: In vitro study of 48 A2 samples of heat-pressed and milled feldspathic, lithium disilicate and zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate glass-ceramics, glazed or polished and thermocycled 10,000 times. Translucency and opalescence differed between pressed and milled ceramics (p < 0.001) and decreased after thermocycling, …

P1601.t: Impact of crystallization firing process on the microstructure and flexural strength of zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate glass-ceramics
P1601.kf: In vitro study of 140 discs of Vita Suprinity and Celtra Duo zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate, fired or unfired (n=30). Fired Celtra Duo had the highest characteristic strength (251.25MPa) and unfired Suprinity the lowest (106.95MPa); crystallization firing was needed to crystallize zirconia.

P1602.t: Machinability: Zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate glass ceramic versus lithium disilicate glass ceramic
P1602.j: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials/Journal of mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
P1602.kf: In vitro simulated dental grinding of zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS) and lithium disilicate with coarse diamond burs. ZLS required higher grinding forces and energy (p < 0.05), and edge chipping of about 20-100 μm occurred in both, increasing with material removal rate (p < 0.01).

P1604.t: Microstructural and Mechanical Characterization of CAD/CAM Materials for Monolithic Dental Restorations
P1604.kf: In vitro study of monolithic posterior crowns and bars (n = 10) of lithium disilicate, ZLS, Cerasmart and Vita Enamic. ZLS and lithium disilicate crowns had significantly higher fracture strength than the hybrid materials (p < 0.0001), and lithium disilicate had the highest flexural strength.

P1605.t: Zirconia-Reinforced Lithium Silicate (ZLS) mechanical and biological properties: a literature review
P1605.kf: Literature review with a structured multi-database search (937 records, 71 papers included) on zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate. Vita Suprinity PC and Celtra Duo were similar in composition, microstructure and properties; ZLS is reported biocompatible with fracture resistance able to withstand physiological …

P1608.t: Long‐term outcomes of maxillary single‐tooth implants in relation to timing protocols of implant placement and loading: Systematic review and meta‐analysis
P1608.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of maxillary single-tooth implants in the aesthetic zone with ≥3 years follow-up. Meta-analyses of 7 controlled trials found no significant differences for immediate vs delayed loading (p = .306 and p = 1.000) or early vs delayed placement (p = .600).

P1609.t: Does the timing of implant placement and loading influence biological outcomes of implant‐supported multiple‐unit fixed dental prosthesis—A systematic review with meta‐analyses
P1609.kf: Systematic review of 14 studies (6 RCTs, 5 cohort studies, 3 case series) on timing of implant placement and loading for multiple-unit implant FDPs with ≥3 years follow-up. All combinations except IPIL showed implant survival >90%, and a meta-analysis of 3 RCTs found no survival difference between DPIL and DPDL (p = …

P1611.t: Comparison of loupes versus microscope-enhanced CAD-CAM crown preparations: A microcomputed tomography analysis of marginal gaps
P1611.kf: In vitro study of 18 extracted molars whose crown preparations were refined with loupes or a microscope (up to ×10.0) and restored with milled ZLS crowns, assessed by micro-CT. Mean marginal gap was 145.0 ±259.6 μm with loupes vs 35.6 ±110.6 μm with the microscope (P<.001).

P1612.t: Ridge alterations following tooth extraction with and without flap elevation: an experimental study in the dog
P1612.kf: Dog study (5 mongrel dogs) comparing hard tissue healing 6 months after distal-root extraction of mandibular premolars with full-thickness flap elevation on one side and flapless extraction on the other, allocated randomly. Removal of a single root caused a marked change in the edentulous ridge.

P1625.t: A Comparative Study of Two Techniques Used for Determining the Seated Condylar Position in Human Subjects

P1626.t: The effect of a Lucia jig for 30 minutes on neuromuscular re-programming, in normal subjects
P1626.kf: Electromyographic study of masseter and temporal muscles in 42 healthy dentate adults with a Lucia jig in place for 0 to 30 minutes. No statistically significant differences in muscle activity were found between time periods, although activation decreased in most periods.

P1629.t: Cantilever rests: An alternative to the unsupported distal cantilever of osseointegrated implant-supported prostheses for the edentulous mandible
P1629.kf: Technique report: additional posterior implants support the distal cantilever of a mandibular implant prosthesis through unconnected cantilever rests, so the framework is attached only to the anterior implants. The author states this should avoid flexure-related microdamage and reduce cantilever torque.

P1632.t: Impact of abutment geometry on early implant marginal bone loss. A double-blind, randomized, 6-month clinical trial
P1632.kf: Double-blind RCT of 77 implants in 25 patients comparing cylindrical vs concave abutments in healed bone. Early marginal bone loss at 6 months was significantly greater with cylindrical (-0.6 ± 0.7 mm) than concave abutments (-0.4 ± 0.6 mm) (p = .030).

P1634.t: Does platform switching really prevent crestal bone loss around implants?
P1634.kf: Review of platform switching literature covering human radiographic, animal histological and finite element studies. It found a shortage of published data in all three categories and an incompletely clarified mechanism of action.

P1635.t: Influence of the Size of the Microgap on Crestal Bone Changes Around Titanium Implants. A Histometric Evaluation of Unloaded Non‐Submerged Implants in the Canine Mandible
P1635.kf: Animal study: 60 implants in 5 hounds, 3 months, unloaded. Crestal bone loss was greater with screw-retained than laser-welded abutments (1.65 to 1.72 mm vs 1.06 to 1.28 mm). Microgap size (<10, 50 or 100 micrometres) had no significant influence.

P1636.t: Factors Affecting Implant Failure and Marginal Bone Loss of Implants Placed by Post-Graduate Students: A 1-Year Prospective Cohort Study
P1636.kf: Prospective cohort of 130 implants placed and restored by post-graduate students, 1-year follow-up: survival 96.15%, success 94.62%, mean marginal bone loss 0.53 mm. Diabetes and implant depth significantly affected bone loss; no variable significantly affected survival.

P1637.t: Prosthetic factors influencing the prevalence of peri-implant diseases and marginal bone loss in static computer-assisted implant sites: A cross-sectional study
P1637.kf: Cross-sectional study of 115 patients with 417 implants placed by static computer-assisted surgery and loaded >1 year: 57.8% had mucositis and 4.8% peri-implantitis. Removable-prosthesis implants had higher peri-implantitis odds (OR 2.16, 95% CI 1.003-4.63), and MBL was linked to contact level, emergence angle, …

P1639.t: Ten-year outcome of zirconia ceramic cantilever resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses and the influence of the reasons for missing incisors
P1639.kf: Clinical study of 108 zirconia ceramic single-retainer cantilever RBFDPs replacing incisors in 87 patients, mean observation 92.2±33 months. Six debondings and 1 restoration loss occurred; 10-year survival was 98.2% and success 92.0%.

P1641.t: All-ceramic resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses: Treatment planning, clinical procedures, and outcome
P1641.kf: Narrative review of single-retainer all-ceramic resin-bonded FDPs. Cited data: a randomized trial of zirconia RBFDPs showed a 5-year complication-free rate of 93.3% and 100% survival; 94.4% survival at 10 years for alumina ceramic. The authors consider them a viable modality when correctly indicated.

P1643.t: Resin-Bonded Bridges − the Problem or the Solution? Part 1: Assessment and Design
P1643.kf: Narrative review (part 1 of 2) on resin-bonded bridge assessment and design. It cites a 5-year survival of 87.7% (systematic review) and 80.4% at 10 years (771-bridge prospective study), with failures mostly in the first four years, and stresses careful case selection and design.

P1646.t: Deep-learning performance in identifying and classifying dental implant systems from dental imaging: a systematic review and meta-analysis
P1646.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 studies (from 1,293 records) on deep learning identification of implant systems from panoramic and periapical radiographs. Accuracy ranged from 70.75% to 98.19%, with an overall weighted accuracy of 92.16% (95% CI 90.8%-93.5%).

P1647.t: Systematic review evaluating the influence of the prosthetic material and prosthetic design on the clinical outcomes of implant-supported multi-unit fixed dental prosthesis in the posterior area
P1647.kf: Systematic review of 32 studies (42 arms) on posterior implant FDPs: estimated 3-year survival was 98.3% for PFM, 97.5% veneered zirconia, 98.9% monolithic/micro-veneered zirconia and 97.0% lithium disilicate, without significant differences; veneered restorations had significantly more fracture and chipping (p < .01).

P1667.t: New Resorbable Membrane Materials for Guided Bone Regeneration
P1667.kf: Narrative review of new resorbable GBR membrane materials (modified collagen, aliphatic polyesters, platelet-rich fibrin, silk), mostly supported by animal and in vitro studies. The authors conclude new materials aim to overcome drawbacks of commercial membranes and need further research before commercialization.

P1678.t: Zirconia toughened mica glass ceramics for dental restorations
P1678.kf: Laboratory study of mica glass ceramic composites with 0 to 20 wt.% yttria-stabilized zirconia. With 20 wt.% YSZ, Vickers hardness was 9.2GPa, elastic modulus 125GPa and indentation toughness 3.6MPa·m, with chemical solubility well below the permissible limit.

P1679.t: Dental cutting behaviour of mica-based and apatite-based machinable glass-ceramics
P1679.kf: Laboratory weight-load cutting tests with an air-turbine diamond point on Macor-M, Bioram-M, a composite typodont tooth and bovine enamel. Increasing load generally decreased cutting speed and increased cutting volume; Macor-M gave the maximum and Bioram-M the minimum cutting volume.

P1680.t: Enhanced dental cutting through chemomechanical effects
P1680.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P1680.kf: Laboratory study cutting Macor with diamond and carbide burs (six burs per irrigant) using coolant water with mouthwash additions. Carbide cutting rates reached 0.66 mm/s (1:10) vs 0.21 with water, and diamond 0.21 (1:5) vs 0.09 (P < .001).

P1681.t: Factors and clinical outcomes for standard and mini-implants retaining mandibular overdentures: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1681.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 7 publications comparing mini-implants and standard implants retaining mandibular overdentures. Mini-implants had fewer abutment adjustments (RR 0.23), retentive element replacements (RR 0.41), occlusal adjustments (RR 0.53) and overdenture fractures (RR 0.46), and lower plaque …

P1694.t: Minimal invasiveness in nonsurgical periodontal therapy
P1694.kf: Review of minimally invasive nonsurgical periodontal therapy (MINST). Reviewed papers report PPD reductions and CAL gains of 2 to 4 mm at 6 months to 5 years for intrabony defects and 1.5 to 3 mm at 2-6 months for full-mouth results, with reduced radiographic defect depth.

P1695.t: Occlusion for the class III jaw relations patient
P1695.kf: Narrative review of occlusion in the class III (macrognathic) patient. The author concludes that cusp-fossa, cusp-to-cusp and crossbite relations can coexist and be stable, that lack of anterior guidance produces balanced-type occlusion, and that 0.5 to 1 mm interocclusal rest distance is adequate.

P1697.t: Occlusal Concepts in Full Mouth Rehabilitation: An Overview
P1697.j: The Journal of Indian Prosthodontic Society
P1697.kf: Narrative overview of occlusal concepts in full mouth rehabilitation (gnathologic, freedom in centric, PMS, twin-stage and others). The authors favour posterior disocclusion and cusp-to-fossa contacts but conclude that no set rule applies to all patients.

P1699.t: Effects of dietary consistency on craniofacial and occlusal development in the rat
P1699.kf: Rat study of dietary consistency: moderate differences in diet hardness were related to significant differences in maxillary width and other measures of facial size.

P1701.t: An evidence-based assessment of occlusal adjustment as a treatment for temporomandibular disorders
P1701.kf: Critical review of 11 experiments (413 subjects with bruxism, TMD, headache/TMD or chronic cervical pain) on occlusal adjustment. Overall, occlusal adjustment did not show greater therapeutic efficacy than the control or contrasting therapy.

P1702.t: Application of the functionally generated path technique in designing an implant-supported fixed prosthesis with CAD-CAM technology: A dental technique
P1702.kf: Technique report describing a digital functionally generated path (FGP) method using an intraoral scanner, design software and a removable FGP wax table to design an implant-supported fixed prosthesis (one 79-year-old patient). The authors state it can reduce chairside time and replicate the existing occlusal scheme.

P1703.kf: Survey of Academy of Prosthodontics fellows (100 of 146 responded, 68.5%) on attributes of centric relation. Moderate-to-strong agreement held that CR is a clinically determined, repeatable, tooth-contact-independent physiologic maxillomandibular relationship, while evidence on disc and condyle position was judged …

P1705.t: Osseoperception: active tactile sensibility of osseointegrated dental implants
P1705.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1705.kf: Study of 62 subjects with single-tooth implants opposing natural teeth who bit on copper foils of 0 to 200 µm. Mean 50% tactile threshold was 20.2 ± 10.9 µm with a slope of 29 ± 15, and sandblasted acid-etched surfaces were significantly more sensitive than titanium plasma-sprayed surfaces.

P1706.t: Eskimo and Indian field studies in Alaska and Canada
P1706.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P1706.kf: 1936 uncontrolled field study of Eskimo and Indian groups. The author interprets that dental caries did not occur in groups living on native diets adequately reinforced with minerals and activators, and that nutritional deficiencies can produce marked changes in physical development within a single generation.

P1707.t: Timeless Principles in Esthetic Dentistry: A Four-Stage Protocol
P1707.kf: Technique report presenting the Dawson Academy four-stage protocol for esthetic restorations: functional-esthetic analysis, three-dimensional treatment planning, prototype restorations and definitive restorations. The authors state predictable, durable results come only from a reproducible protocol honoring functional …

P1709.t: Effects of unilateral posterior missing-teeth on the temporomandibular joint and the alignment of cervical atlas
P1709.kf: Radiographic study of 89 patients with unilateral posterior missing teeth vs 20 controls. The missing-teeth group had lower articular eminence inclination (42.28° vs 46.66°), smaller cranio-cervical angle (99.81° vs 103.27°) and fewer occlusal planes passing through the C1–C2 intersection (28.9% vs 65%).

P1710.t: Gnathology and Pankey-Mann-Schuyler: fulfilling the requirements of occlusion in oral rehabilitation
P1710.j: Medical College of Ohio / University of Toledo (Master's and Doctoral Projects)

P1711.t: Identifying occlusal overload and how to deal with it to avoid marginal bone loss around implants
P1711.kf: Review of 7 clinical human studies identified by PubMed search on occlusal overloading and peri-implant bone loss. Occlusal overloading was positively associated with peri-implant marginal bone loss.

P1712.t: Influence of unilateral tooth loss in the temporomandibular joint and masseter muscle of rabbits
P1712.j: Oral Surgery, Oral Medicine, Oral Pathology and Oral Radiology
P1712.kf: Rabbit study (n=8) of unilateral tooth extraction assessed by bone scintigraphy and masseter histochemistry at 6 and 12 weeks. TMJ bone metabolism differed significantly between extraction (39.96%) and nonextraction sides (60.04%) at 12 weeks (P < .05).

P1713.t: Influence of occlusal factors on treatment outcome: a study of 109 consecutive patients with mandibular implant-supported fixed prostheses opposing maxillary complete dentures
P1713.kf: Examination of 109 consecutive patients with Brånemark mandibular fixed implant prostheses opposing maxillary complete dentures (mean 8 years in function). Most were very satisfied; 61% had bilateral balanced occlusion, mean bone loss was 0.5 mm, and occlusal variables showed no or only weak correlations with outcomes.

P1714.t: Malocclusion in the modern Alaskan Eskimo
P1714.kf: Cross-sectional study of 100 Eskimo children in Kotzebue, Alaska: 82 per cent had malocclusion with high caries and tooth loss. Maxillary intercanine and intermolar widths did not differ between normal occlusions and malocclusions; Class I jaw relationships predominated.

P1715.t: Evidence-based considerations for removable prosthodontic and dental implant occlusion: a literature review
P1715.kf: Literature review (descriptive, not systematic) of removable prosthodontic and implant occlusion. The authors conclude little scientific evidence supports a direct cause-effect relationship between occlusal factors and deleterious biological outcomes for osseointegrated implants; support for occlusal theories rests on …

P1725.t: The bases for using a particular occlusal design in tooth and implant-borne reconstructions and complete dentures
P1725.kf: Systematic review (1966-2006) of studies on occlusal design for crowns, complete and partial removable prostheses and implant reconstructions, yielding 1315 studies. Lingualised posterior occlusion was preferred for complete dentures, while little evidence specified occlusal or superstructure design for fixed tooth or …

P1726.t: The difficult relationship between occlusal interferences and temporomandibular disorder – insights from animal and human experimental studies
P1726.kf: Review of animal and human experimental studies on occlusal interference and TMD. In double-blind randomised human experiments, subjects without TMD history adapted fairly well, whereas those with a TMD history developed significantly more clinical signs and stronger symptoms.

P1728.t: The importance of centric occlusion in diagnosis and treatment planning
P1728.kf: Opinion article (1960) arguing that centric occlusion, the first tooth contact at the terminal hinge position, is fundamental to diagnosis and treatment planning. A recording in one test patient is used to illustrate that eccentric closure can cause pathologic wear.

P1730.t: Missing Posterior Teeth and Risk of Temporomandibular Disorders
P1730.kf: Analysis of 741 individuals aged 21–60 with missing posterior teeth (386 with and 355 without TMD). In logistic regression, gender (OR = 1.59), number of missing posterior teeth (OR = 0.51) and number of quadrants with missing posterior teeth (OR = 7.71) were associated with TMD (P < 0.01).

P1731.t: Studies of biologic parameters for denture design. Part III: Effects of occlusal adjustment, base retention, and fit on masseter muscle activity and masticatory performance
P1731.kf: EMG and masticatory performance tests in 20 denture wearers before and after correcting occlusal prematurities and improving retention with denture adhesive or soft reline. These modifications did not significantly alter chewing performance or masseter muscle activity.

P1732.t: Concepts of occlusion in prosthodontics: A literature review, part II
P1732.j: The Journal of Indian Prosthodontic Society
P1732.kf: Narrative review (part II) of nonbalanced complete-denture occlusal concepts (e.g. neutrocentric, lingualized, lineal, monoplane). The authors conclude that choice of scheme depends on jaw relation, ridge resorption, displaceable tissues, neuromuscular control, patient attitude and esthetics, with health of the …

P1733.t: Concepts of occlusion in prosthodontics: A literature review, part I
P1733.j: The Journal of Indian Prosthodontic Society
P1733.kf: Narrative review of complete denture occlusion concepts. Available research has not identified a superior tooth form or occlusal scheme for comfort, mastication, phonetics and esthetics in edentulous patients.

P1734.t: An effective pattern of occlusion in complete artificial dentures
P1734.kf: Opinion article (1951) recommending, for complete dentures, 33-degree anatomic posterior teeth modified by selective grinding, correct centric relation and shallow guiding inclines. The author states this provides maximum masticatory efficiency without jeopardizing retention or stability.

P1735.t: The Development of Nonanatomic Denture Occlusion: Part III
P1735.kf: Historical narrative review (part III of four) tracing nonanatomic denture-tooth designs from the mid-1930s to the early 1950s. By that period the general preference for posterior denture occlusion had shifted from anatomic to nonanatomic teeth and all major manufacturers listed at least one nonanatomic design.

P1736.kf: Technique-oriented overview of the history of lingualized occlusion for complete dentures and common misconceptions. The authors state the basic tenet is that maxillary lingual cusps contact in centric and eccentric positions while maxillary buccal cusps do not; they present a 21-step arrangement technique.

P1737.t: Interventions for replacing missing teeth: 1- versus 2-stage implant placement
P1737.kf: Cochrane systematic review of 5 RCTs (239 patients) comparing 1- vs 2-stage implant placement. Meta-analyses showed no statistically significant differences in prosthesis or implant failures, though trends, especially in fully edentulous patients, favoured 2-stage implants.

P1738.t: Submerged or non-submerged healing of endosseous implants to be used in the rehabilitation of partially dentate patients: A multicenter, randomized controlled clinical trial
P1738.kf: Multicenter RCT of 84 patients with 115 posterior FPDs on Astra Tech implants placed with one-stage or two-stage protocols. Early failures were <2% in both groups, and first-year bone loss was 0.02 ± 0.38 mm vs 0.17 ± 0.64 mm, with near-zero additional loss in year two.

P1739.t: Two-part implants inserted in a one-stage or a two-stage procedure. A prospective comparative study
P1739.kf: Randomized study of 40 edentulous patients receiving two IMZ implants in the anterior mandible for overdentures via one-stage (n = 20) or two-stage (n = 20) surgery. Mean first-year bone loss was 0.6 mm in both groups, with no striking clinical differences.

P1742.t: The Buccal Fat Pad for Closure of Oroantral Communication
P1742.kf: Case report of a 70-year-old woman on bisphosphonate therapy with maxillary sinusitis and oroantral communication after implant insertion, closed with a buccal fat pad. Healing was uneventful without dehiscence, infection or necrosis.

P1745.t: Effect of dental implant therapy on the preservation of orofacial tissues: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1745.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies comparing implant-supported prostheses with conventional prostheses or no therapy. Pooled analyses showed no benefit for alveolar bone resorption in the posterior mandible or anterior maxilla, but a significant benefit for masseter muscle thickness.

P1749.t: Sensitivity of Resonance Frequency Analysis for Detecting Early Implant Failure: A Case-Control Study
P1749.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1749.kf: Retrospective evaluation of 3,786 implants identified 20 early failures in pristine bone. Immediate (OR = 4.27) and 4-month ISQ values (OR = 9.20) were significantly related to failure, but immediate ISQ misclassified 55% of failures.

P1751.t: Accuracy of CAD-CAM systems for removable partial denture framework fabrication: A systematic review
P1751.kf: Systematic review of 7 articles (2 clinical, 5 in vitro) on accuracy of CAD-CAM removable partial denture frameworks. Frameworks showed clinically acceptable discrepancies (<311 μm); PEEK fitted better than cast metal, and laser-sintered Co-Cr had the highest discrepancies.

P1753.t: Blood Flow Alterations in the Anterior Maxillary Mucosa as Induced by Implant-Retained Overdenture
P1753.kf: Comparative study of 9 maxillary complete denture wearers opposing mandibular implant-retained overdentures vs 4 opposing complete dentures, using laser Doppler flowmetry. Initial mucosal blood flow fell to 103 BPU with IRO vs 183 BPU with CD, and 1-year anterior maxillary bone volume loss was 7.3 ± 1.3% vs 2.6 ± 1.7%.

P1756.t: Treatment effect of implant‐supported fixed complete dentures and implant overdentures on patient‐reported outcomes: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P1756.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 prospective studies (1457 edentulous patients): patient-reported outcomes improved with large effect sizes for implant-supported fixed complete dentures (1.68) and implant overdentures (1.26), with no significant difference between them (p = .165).

P1757.t: Clinical performance of implant supported mandibular overdentures with cantilever bar and stud attachments: A retrospective study
P1757.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1757.kf: Retrospective 5-year study of 103 patients with two-implant mandibular overdentures (ball, cantilevered Dolder bar or Locator): implant survival 100%, mean bone loss 0.22 mm; ball attachments had more prosthetic complications, bars fewer attachment replacements and post-insertion visits.

P1759.t: Effect of 2-implant mandibular overdenture with different attachments and loading protocols on peri-implant health and prosthetic complications: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
P1759.kf: Bayesian network meta-analysis of 16 RCTs (599 participants, 1198 implants) on 2-implant mandibular overdentures: marginal bone loss and probing depth did not differ significantly among attachment systems and loading protocols; implant survival ranged from 91.2% to 100%.

P1761.t: Effects of repeated use of tungsten carbide burs on the surface roughness and contact angles of a CAD-CAM PMMA denture base resin
P1761.kf: In vitro study of 40 CAD-CAM PMMA denture base disks: new tungsten carbide burs produced higher Ra (1.3 μm) and lower contact angles than used burs (Ra 0.93 μm, contact angle 80 degrees); thermocycling lowered contact angles of used-bur specimens.

P1762.t: Factors affecting flexural strength of 3D-printed resins: A systematic review
P1762.kf: Systematic review of 19 studies on 3D-printed resins (provisional, denture base, occlusal device, orthodontic, denture teeth, surgical guide): most factors studied—fillers/nanofillers, printing orientation, layer thickness, post-polymerization time/temperature, rinsing time—significantly affected flexural strength.

P1764.t: Implant survival/success and peri-implant outcomes of titanium-zirconium mini implants for mandibular overdentures: Results from a 1-year randomized clinical trial
P1764.kf: 2×2 factorial RCT of 74 patients (296 titanium-zirconium mini implants) retaining mandibular overdentures: 1-year survival/success 100%, mean marginal bone loss 0.89 (±0.75) mm; flapless surgery gave better soft-tissue results but slightly higher bone-loss risk.

P1768.t: Longitudinal Oral Health-Related Quality of Life in maxillary mini dental implant overdentures after 3 years in function
P1768.kf: Multicenter prospective cohort of 31 patients with 5-6 flapless one-piece mini implants for maxillary overdentures: 164 of 204 MDIs (78.4%) remained at 3 years; OHIP-14 improved from 21.3 at baseline to 7.3 at final prosthesis connection, but less with multiple implant losses.

P1771.t: Mandibular two-implant overdentures with CAD-CAM milled bars with distal extensions or retentive anchors: A randomized controlled trial
P1771.kf: Non-inferiority RCT of 40 edentulous patients (38 at 1 year) with mandibular 2-implant overdentures on CAD-CAM milled bars with distal extensions or retentive anchors: 100% implant survival, no difference in bone level change (p = .754), chewing efficiency, bite force or OHIP; subjective chewing favoured bars.

P1772.t: Mandibular two-implant-retained overdenture: prosthetic design and fabrication protocol
P1772.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P1772.kf: Technique report with one case (67-year-old woman): mandibular overdenture retained by 2 freestanding implants with Locator abutments, a metal-reinforcing framework and laboratory pick-up of attachments. The patient expressed satisfaction at the recall appointment.

P1773.t: Maxillary bar overdentures on four or six posterior implants: 10-year results from a randomized clinical trial
P1773.kf: RCT of 66 patients with augmented maxillae randomized to bar overdentures on four or six posterior implants (46 completed 10 years): implant survival 100% vs 96.7%, mean bone loss 0.41 vs 0.70 mm, with no significant differences in clinical parameters or satisfaction.

P1775.t: Maxillary implant overdentures on two or four implants. A prospective randomized cross-over clinical trial of implant and denture success and survival
P1775.kf: Randomized cross-over trial of 24 participants with maxillary overdentures on four implants loaded in pairs: implant survival after loading 93.8% (mean 3.1 years), denture survival 100% and success 95.8%; 23 of 24 preferred the 4-implant overdenture.

P1776.t: Mechanical properties of 3D-printed prosthetic materials compared with milled and conventional processing: A systematic review and meta-analysis of in vitro studies
P1776.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 76 in vitro studies: 3D-printed polymers had lower flexural strength, hardness and fracture load than conventional processing; versus milling, only flexural strength was significantly lower (Hedge g=-3.88), with similar marginal discrepancy, trueness and internal fit.

P1777.t: Milled Bar Overdentures — Protocol and Procedures
P1777.kf: Technique report (laboratory perspective) on milled-bar implant overdentures, with one illustrated case. The author states that a verification index, tooth set-up and an internal metal framework are essential and that following this protocol produced a successful case.

P1778.t: Occlusion and Attachments: The Underlying Scheme for Successful Overdentures
P1778.kf: Technique-oriented narrative article by a dental technician on occlusion and attachments for overdentures. The author states lingualized occlusion works best for implant overdentures by relieving off-axis stress, and that a reinforcing metal bar helps prevent fracture of resin overdentures.

P1779.t: Prosthodontic management of endodontically treated teeth: Factors determining post selection, foundation restorations and review of success & failure data
P1779.kf: Narrative review of post selection, foundation restorations and success/failure data for endodontically treated teeth. Its treatment summary: anterior teeth with significant coronal damage need a post/core plus full coverage crown, with cast post and core considered best; posterior teeth with minimal damage may need …

P1781.t: Short strategic implants for mandibular removable partial dentures: One-year results from a pilot randomized crossover abutment type study
P1781.kf: Pilot randomized crossover study of 12 RPD wearers given two 6 mm short implants at mandibular molar sites with ball or dome abutments: 1-year implant survival 100%, success 90.9%, mean bone loss -1.2 mm, no group differences; 82% finally chose the ball abutment.

P1784.t: Changes in Peri-Implant Tissues Subjected to Orthodontic Forces and Ligature Breakdown in Monkeys
P1784.kf: Split-mouth study in 5 cynomolgus monkeys testing repetitive mechanical trauma with or without ligature-induced peri-implantitis: bone-to-implant contact differed significantly between healthy and diseased sites, but mechanical trauma showed no histologic effect on peri-implant bone loss.

P1785.t: Titanium implants and lateral forces. An experimental study with sheep
P1785.kf: Sheep study of 20 titanium implants in the forehead loaded with a 250–350 g horizontal pull from orthodontic elastics for 3 months: histology showed no signs of infection or bone loss around the implants.

P1786.kf: Narrative review of the basic science of bone healing (orthopaedic). It states bone regeneration is a complex process with interacting biologic mechanisms and that impaired healing complicates as many as 10% of all fractures; better understanding of biology and mechanics can target therapies.

P1793.t: Effects of Occlusal Overload on Peri-Implant Tissue Health: A Systematic Review of Animal-Model Studies
P1793.kf: Systematic review of animal studies on occlusal overload of non-splinted titanium implants: two high-risk-of-bias controlled studies found no tissue breakdown from overload without plaque, but with plaque accumulation overload played a key role (PD change 5.3 mm; DIB 6.0 mm).

P1794.t: Occlusal trauma and excessive occlusal forces: Narrative review, case definitions, and diagnostic considerations
P1794.kf: Narrative review: occlusal trauma and excessive forces do not initiate periodontitis or attachment loss; weak evidence suggests they may increase connective tissue loss when plaque-induced periodontitis coexists, and data do not support abfraction as a cause of gingival recession.

P1796.t: Histological evaluation of peri-implant bone at implants subjected to occlusal overload or plaque accumulation
P1796.kf: Monkey study (4 animals, Astra Tech implants) over 18 months: 6 of 8 overloaded implants became loose, 2 losing osseointegration completely, whereas plaque-accumulation implants stayed osseointegrated with mean histologic marginal bone loss of 2.4 mm.

P1797.t: Histological, histomorphometrical, and radiological evaluation of an experimental implant design with a high insertion torque
P1797.kf: Minipig study (10 animals, 80 implants) comparing an experimental high-insertion-torque implant design with Astra Tech implants: radiological and histomorphometric analyses showed significantly more bone loss, larger marginal defects and lower peri-implant bone fraction around the experimental implants.

P1801.t: Influence of bone parameters on peri-implant bone strain distribution in the posterior mandible
P1801.j: Medicina Oral, Patología Oral y Cirugía Bucal
P1801.kf: Finite element models based on CT of 75 posterior mandibular sites under a 200 N oblique load: maximum strains in crestal cortical and cancellous bone were 1.56–2.62-fold and 3.49–5.31-fold higher with low-density (150 HU) than high-density (850 HU) cancellous bone.

P1805.t: The Causes of Early Implant Bone Loss: Myth or Science?
P1805.kf: Review of six hypothesized causes of early crestal implant bone loss: biologic width reformation, a microgap at or below the bone crest, occlusal overload and the implant crest module were judged the most likely causes, with surgical trauma and peri-implantitis possibly contributing.

P1806.kf: Systematic review (726 titles; 16 clinical and 25 animal studies screened): all clinical studies were excluded for high risk of bias; included animal studies showed no overload–bone loss association without inflammation, while overload aggravated tissue breakdown with inflammation.

P1807.t: Occlusal overload with dental implants: a review
P1807.kf: Review: animal studies have not identified the biological threshold for peri-implant bone fatigue failure, clinical studies link parafunction with implant failure, and evidence does not support avoiding high crown-to-implant ratios, cantilevers or non-splinted designs for fear of overload.

P1809.t: Complete arch site classification for all-on-4 immediate function
P1809.kf: Classification (Class A to D) of complete-arch sites for all-on-4 immediate function, applied to 100 consecutive arches (retrospective, short-term): every arch received 4 implants and was immediately loaded; 83.3% of maxillae were Class A or B and 78.2% of mandibles were Class B or C; 2 zygomatic implant cases.

P1810.t: Optimal number of oral implants for fixed reconstructions: a review of the literature
P1810.kf: Literature review of 29 studies (26 datasets) on implant-supported fixed prostheses in edentulous jaws: almost no RCTs compared implant numbers; 5-year-plus survival averaged 90% to 100%, with a clear tendency to plan 4 to 6 implants per prosthesis.

P1812.t: Peri-Implant Bone Alterations under the Influence of Abutment Screw Preload Stress. A preclinical in vivo study
P1812.kf: Rabbit femur study (20 rabbits) of abutment screw preload without occlusal loading: implants with sustained 35 or 70 Ncm preload had significantly less bone-to-implant contact and bone volume than controls and temporarily tightened screws over 4–10 weeks.

P1813.t: Peri-Implant Bone Loss and Overload: A Systematic Review Focusing on Occlusal Analysis through Digital and Analogic Methods
P1813.kf: Systematic review of 7 clinical studies (4 cohort, 2 cross-sectional, 1 case-control) quantifying occlusal load: four reported a positive correlation between overload and crestal bone loss; all had moderate to serious risk of bias.

P1814.t: Periimplant diseases: where are we now? – Consensus of the Seventh European Workshop on Periodontology
P1814.kf: Seventh European Workshop consensus: peri-implant mucositis resembles gingivitis, whereas peri-implantitis may differ from periodontitis in lesion extent, cell composition and progression; surface roughness may influence biofilm but there is no evidence it influences peri-implantitis development.

P1816.t: Fixture design and overload influence marginal bone loss and future success in the Brånemark® system
P1816.kf: Clinical study of Brånemark fixtures: standard fixtures had clearly higher failure rates than self-tapping fixtures before and after loading, with no bone-loss difference among successful fixtures; in 93 patients, excessive bone loss (>1 mm) after year one and/or fixture loss correlated well with overload.

P1817.t: Ratios of Cantilever Lengths and Anterior-Posterior Spreads of Definitive Hybrid Full-Arch, Screw-Retained Prostheses: Results of a Clinical Study
P1817.kf: Retrospective analysis of 130 patients (193 arches, 774 immediately loaded implants, mostly 4 per arch) with full-arch hybrid prostheses followed up to 48 months: implant survival 99.5%, one definitive prosthesis fracture; mean CL/AP ratios of 0.84–0.90 were not associated with prosthetic repairs.

P1824.t: The Effect of Static Load on Dental Implant Survival: A Systematic Review
P1824.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1824.kf: Systematic review of 36 studies (28 animal, 8 human) on static loads such as prosthesis misfit and orthodontic forces: no apparent detrimental effect of static loading on osseointegrated dental implants was found.

P1825.t: The Influence of Controlled Occlusal Overload on Peri-implant Tissue. Part 3: A Histologic Study in Monkeys
P1825.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1825.kf: Monkey study of inflammation-free implants with supra-occluding prostheses 100, 180 or 250 microns too high: bone resorption tended to increase at 180 microns or more, suggesting a tissue-breakdown threshold of approximately 180 microns.

P1830.t: Bruxism and dental implant treatment complications: a retrospective comparative study of 98 bruxer patients and a matched group
P1830.kf: Retrospective matched comparison of 98 bruxers (from 2670 implant patients at one clinic) with non-bruxers: odds ratio of implant failure in bruxers was 2.71 (95% CI 1.25, 5.88), and bruxers had a higher prevalence of mechanical complications.

P1831.t: Bruxism and dental implant failures: a multilevel mixed effects parametric survival analysis approach
P1831.kf: Retrospective study of 10 096 implants in 2670 patients at one specialist clinic (analysis on 3549 implants in 994 patients). Failure was 24/185 implants in bruxers vs 155/3364 in non-bruxers; in the multilevel survival model bruxism was a significant risk factor (HR 3.396, 95% CI 1.314 to 8.777, P = 0.012).

P1832.t: Incidence of diurnal and nocturnal bruxism
P1832.kf: Questionnaire survey of 1,052 university students: 30.7% reported present or past bruxism (21.2% present). Diurnal bruxism was more frequent than nocturnal; men reported more diurnal and women more nocturnal bruxism; diurnal bruxists were more responsive to stress.

P1833.t: A systematic review of the survival and complication rates of implant supported fixed dental prostheses with cantilever extensions after an observation period of at least 5 years
P1833.kf: Systematic review with meta-analysis of five cohort studies: estimated 5- and 10-year survival of implant-supported cantilever FDPs was 94.3% and 88.9%; veneer fracture (10.3%) and screw loosening (8.2%) were the commonest 5-year complications, and bone level changes did not differ from end-abutment FDPs.

P1836.t: Clinical and radiographic evaluations of implant-supported cantilever fixed partial dentures replacing maxillary anterior teeth: A randomized clinical trial
P1836.kf: RCT of 14 patients missing two maxillary central incisors and one lateral incisor, restored on 2 implants with cantilever or conventional FPDs: at 24 months implants adjacent to the cantilever had significantly greater marginal bone loss (1.8 mm) and sulcus depth (2 mm), both within typical ranges.

P1837.t: Clinical and radiographic outcomes of implant-supported zirconia fixed dental prostheses with cantilever extension: A proof-of-principle study with a follow-up of at least 1 year
P1837.kf: Proof-of-principle study of 30 patients with 34 screw-retained full-zirconia posterior cantilever prostheses on 37 implants (mean loading 2.6 years): no implants lost, bone levels unchanged (0.92 to 0.96 mm), mucositis in 22 cases; screw loosening and chipping occurred once in 4 patients.

P1840.t: Performance of zirconia ceramic cantilever fixed dental prostheses: 3-Year results from a prospective, randomized, controlled pilot study
P1840.kf: Randomized pilot study of 21 patients with tooth-supported zirconia or metal-ceramic cantilever FDPs replacing one tooth: 3-year survival was 100% in both groups, with 6 complications needing aftercare (4 zirconia, 2 metal-ceramic) and similar periodontal parameters.

P1845.t: To what extent does the crown–implant ratio affect the survival and complications of implant‐supported reconstructions? A systematic review
P1845.kf: Systematic review of prospective studies (≥4 years): only two articles were included; reconstructions with crown–implant ratios above 2 had 94.1% survival, and crestal bone loss seemed unaffected by C/I ratio except in one study showing more loss with ratios <1.

P1846.t: Is there an effect of crown‐to‐implant ratio on implant treatment outcomes? A systematic review
P1846.kf: Systematic review with meta-analysis of 8 studies (10 study groups) of single-tooth, nonsplinted implants with crown-to-implant ratios from 0.86 to 2.14. Implant survival was above 99% per year and mean peri-implant bone change below 0.1 mm per year, with few biological or technical complications.

P1847.t: The Effect of Crown-to-Implant Ratio on the Clinical Outcomes of Dental Implants: A Systematic Review
P1847.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1847.kf: Systematic review of clinical trials (≥1 year): regression found no significant correlation between anatomical crown-to-implant ratio and survival (P = .905), marginal bone loss (P = 0.33) or prosthetic complications (P = .67), nor between clinical ratio and survival or bone loss.

P1852.t: Biological and Technical Complications of Splinted or Nonsplinted Dental Implants
P1852.kf: Literature review of splinted vs nonsplinted restorations on adjacent implants: no evidence that either design gives higher implant survival; each has its own complications, with compelling evidence that splinted restorations generally have fewer technical complications.

P1853.t: Clinical Evaluation of Marginal Bone Level Change Around Multiple Adjacent Implants Restored with Splinted and Nonsplinted Restorations: A 10-Year Randomized Controlled Trial
P1853.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1853.kf: Split-mouth RCT of 44 patients (132 posterior maxillary external-hex implants, 114 analysed): at 10 years bone loss was 1.2 mm with splinted and 1.3 mm with nonsplinted cemented restorations, a statistically significant 0.1 mm difference.

P1854.t: The Effect of Splinting Implant-Supported Restorations on Stress Distribution of Different Crown-Implant Ratios and Crown Height Spaces
P1854.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P1854.kf: Photoelastic model study of splinted three-implant restorations loaded at 30°: microstrain rose significantly as C/I ratio increased from 1:1 to 1:1.5, and C/I ratios of 1:1.75 and 1:2 (crown height space ≥15 mm) caused abutment screw fracture and crown dislodgement.

P1868.t: Effect of the vertical and horizontal distances between adjacent implants and between a tooth and an implant on the incidence of interproximal papilla
P1868.kf: Cross-sectional study of 48 patients (96 implant-implant and 80 tooth-implant sites): the papilla was absent 100% of the time with 2 or 2.5 mm lateral spacing and mostly present at 3–4 mm; contact point-to-bone distances of 3 mm (implant-implant) and 3–5 mm (tooth-implant) favoured papilla presence.

P1869.t: Hyaluronic acid gel as a nonsurgical approach for the interdental papillary defects: A systematic review
P1869.kf: Systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of 18 studies (213 participants, 696 papillary defects): hyaluronic acid injection achieved complete papilla reconstruction in 47% (CI 35–59%) of sites and partial reconstruction in 49%, with increased satisfaction and no significant pain.

P1885.t: Papilla Formation in Response to Computer-Assisted Implant Surgery and Immediate Restoration
P1885.kf: Retrospective analysis of 9 patients (23 computer-guided, immediately restored implants; mean follow-up 545 days): bone level rose by a mean 0.047 mm, and contact point-to-bone distances of 2.39/3.93 mm gave 91%/71% papilla fill between implants and between implant and tooth.

P1891.t: The effect of the distance from the contact point to the crest of bone on the presence or absence of the interproximal dental papilla
P1891.kf: Cross-sectional study of 288 sites in 30 patients: the papilla was present almost 100% of the time when the contact point-to-bone crest distance was 5 mm or less, 56% at 6 mm, and 27% or less at 7 mm or more.

P1896.t: Vertical Distance from the Crest of Bone to the Height of the Interproximal Papilla Between Adjacent Implants
P1896.kf: Cross-sectional study of 136 interimplant papillae in 33 patients from five private offices: mean soft-tissue height from bone crest to papilla tip between two adjacent implants was 3.4 mm (range 1 mm to 7 mm).

P1897.t: The use of PEEK in digital prosthodontics: A narrative review
P1897.kf: Narrative review (1990–2020) of PEEK in CAD-CAM prosthodontics: many in vitro studies point to PEEK's favourable properties, and its use has been recommended for a wide range of CAD-CAM fixed and removable prostheses.

P1901.t: Anti-infective treatment of peri-implant mucositis: a randomised controlled clinical trial
P1901.kf: Double-blind RCT of 29 patients with peri-implant mucositis: mechanical debridement plus 0.5% chlorhexidine or placebo gel reduced BOP and probing depth with no difference between groups; complete BOP resolution at 3 months occurred in 38% of implants.

P1903.t: Association between smoking and peri-implant diseases: A retrospective study
P1903.kf: Retrospective study of 117 patients (450 implants, mean 8.0 years in function): 31.6% of patients had peri-implantitis; ever smokers >23 pack-years had significantly higher peri-implantitis risk (p = .002), and smoking cessation >21 years was linked to lower disease risk.

P1904.t: At which bone level are implants explanted?
P1904.kf: Analysis of 192 implants explanted for peri-implantitis from 161 patients in 12 offices: excluding early failures, mean survival was 9.5 ± 5.8 years and bone loss at explantation 7.0 ± 2.7 mm (66.2%); late failures were removed at 57.7% bone loss in maxilla and 73.7% in mandible.

P1906.t: Changes in peri-implant soft tissue levels following surgical treatment of peri-implantitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P1906.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 investigations: reconstructive peri-implantitis surgery caused significantly less mucosal recession than access flaps (WMD -1.35 mm) and limited recession over time (0.389 mm), whereas resective surgery produced 1.21 mm; reconstructive approaches gave greater radiographic bone …

P1908.t: Clinical Outcomes of Using Lasers for Peri-Implantitis Surface Detoxification: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P1908.kf: Systematic review of seven human prospective trials and two animal studies: meta-analysis found a 0.00 mm (95% CI -0.18 to 0.19) difference in probing depth reduction between laser and conventional non-surgical treatment of peri-implantitis.

P1909.t: Clinical, microbiological and biochemical impact of a supportive care protocol with an air‐polishing device, after surgical treatment of peri‐implantitis: Randomized clinical trial
P1909.kf: RCT of 30 patients after access-flap peri-implantitis surgery: over 12 months of supportive care, ultrasonic PEEK-tip debridement plus glycine air polishing reduced probing depth (−0.84 ± 0.43 mm) significantly more than ultrasonics plus rubber-cup polishing (+0.18 ± 0.73 mm; p < .001).

P1910.t: Combined surgical therapy of peri-implantitis evaluating two methods of surface debridement and decontamination. A two-year clinical follow up report
P1910.kf: Randomized study of 24 patients (26 advanced peri-implantitis defects) treated with implantoplasty and augmentation, decontaminated by Er:YAG laser or plastic curets/saline: at 24 months BOP reduction (75.0% vs 54.9%) and CAL change (1.0 vs 1.2 mm) did not differ significantly.

P1913.kf: Narrative review of dental implant success/failure literature. Key points: actual failure rates are likely higher than published rates; roughened collars, microthreads and platform switching help bone maintenance; bone augmentation does not significantly increase implant success; reduced-diameter implants (3.75 mm or …

P1915.t: Effect of mechanical and antiseptic therapy on peri-implant mucositis: an experimental study in monkeys
P1915.kf: Monkey study (9 cynomolgus) of ligature-induced peri-implant mucositis: mechanical cleansing alone or with chlorhexidine reduced PD (to 1.7 and 2.1 mm vs 2.5 mm untreated) without significant difference between treatments, and both left minimal histologic inflammation.

P1918.t: Evaluation of the implant disease risk assessment (IDRA) tool: A retrospective study in patients with treated periodontitis and implant-supported fixed dental prostheses (FDPs)
P1918.kf: Retrospective study of 79 treated periodontitis patients with implant FDPs in function ≥5 years: peri-implantitis affected 12% at moderate and 27% at high IDRA risk (OR 2.727, 95% CI 0.793-9.376, not significant); AUC was 0.613.

P1920.t: Four-year follow-up of combined surgical therapy of advanced peri-implantitis evaluating two methods of surface decontamination
P1920.kf: 4-year follow-up of a randomized study of 17 patients with advanced peri-implantitis treated with implantoplasty and augmentation: BOP reduction (85.2% curets/saline vs 71.6% Er:YAG laser) and CAL gain (1.5 vs 1.2 mm) were not influenced by the decontamination method.

P1921.t: Group 4 ITI Consensus Report: Risks and biologic complications associated with implant dentistry
P1921.kf: ITI Group 4 consensus based on four systematic reviews: BOP alone is insufficient to diagnose peri-implantitis; peri-implantitis prevalence in augmented sites is low; after peri-implantitis treatment with supportive care about three-quarters of implants remain at 5 years.

P1922.t: Impact of the method of surface debridement and decontamination on the clinical outcome following combined surgical therapy of peri-implantitis: a randomized controlled clinical study
P1922.kf: RCT of 32 patients (38 advanced peri-implantitis defects) treated with implantoplasty and augmentation: at 6 months Er:YAG laser decontamination gave no greater BOP reduction (47.8% vs 55.0%) or CAL gain (1.5 vs 2.2 mm) than plastic curets/saline; bone fill was comparable.

P1924.t: A systematic review of implant outcomes in treated periodontitis patients
P1924.kf: Systematic review of 27 longitudinal publications: patients with treated periodontitis had lower implant success and survival and more bone loss and peri-implantitis than periodontally healthy patients, with a higher tendency for implant loss after severe periodontitis.
