P1929.t: Peri‐Implant Diseases and Biologic Complications at Implant‐Supported Fixed Dental Prostheses in Partially Edentulous Patients
P1929.kf: Single-center retrospective study of 71 partially edentulous patients (100 FDPs, 222 implants; mean follow-up 3.3 years): cumulative implant survival 99.1%; peri-implantitis affected 5% of implants and peri-implant mucositis 84.10%.

P1930.t: Restoration contour is a risk indicator for peri‐implantitis: A cross‐sectional radiographic analysis
P1930.kf: Cross-sectional radiographic analysis of 83 patients (168 implants, mean follow-up 10.9 years): in bone-level implants, peri-implantitis prevalence was 31.3% with emergence angle >30° vs 15.1% with ≤30°, and 37.8% with a convex profile plus >30°; no association for tissue-level implants.

P1933.t: Microbial Characteristics of Peri-Implantitis: A Case-Control Study
P1933.kf: Case-control study of 85 peri-implantitis patients and 69 healthy-implant controls: P. gingivalis, P. intermedia (OR 15.1), T. forsythia (OR 13.3) and F. nucleatum were significantly associated with peri-implantitis, whereas A. actinomycetemcomitans and Staphylococcus species were rare.

P1935.t: Microbiome associated with peri-implantitis versus periodontal health in individuals with a history of periodontal disease
P1935.kf: 16S rRNA sequencing study of 10 treated periodontitis patients comparing peri-implantitis and healthy dental sites: diseased microbiomes were less diverse, with Prevotella and Porphyromonas most discriminative for disease and Actinobacillus and Streptococcus associated with health.

P1936.t: Microbiota associated with peri-implantitis—A systematic review with meta-analyses
P1936.kf: Meta-analysis of 12 cross-sectional studies (1233 participants, 1513 implants): peri-implantitis was associated with S. epidermidis (OR 10.28), F. nucleatum (7.83), T. denticola (6.11), T. forsythia (4.25), P. intermedia (3.79) and P. gingivalis (2.46), but not A. actinomycetemcomitans, S. aureus or C. rectus.

P1940.t: Influence of implant neck and abutment characteristics on peri‐implant tissue health and stability. Oral reconstruction foundation consensus report
P1940.kf: Consensus based on two systematic reviews: marginal bone level changes were not influenced by abutment material and were similar for one- and two-piece implants at 1 year; rough-collar implants had better bone levels than machined collars, and titanium abutments showed greater BOP increases than zirconia.

P1941.t: Non-surgical peri-implantitis treatment with or without systemic antibiotics: a randomized controlled clinical trial
P1941.kf: RCT of 37 peri-implantitis patients: non-surgical treatment with or without systemic amoxicillin plus metronidazole reduced pocket depth (2.28 vs 1.47 mm at 12 weeks, difference not significant); 81% of sites still bled and only two implants met success criteria.

P1943.t: Nonsurgical cleaning potential of deep-threaded implants and titanium particle release: A novel in vitro tissue model
P1943.kf: In vitro model of 60 dyed implants (apically vs fully tapered) in horizontal defects with porcine soft tissue: cleaned surface ranged from 17.1% to 45.5%; erythritol air-powder waterjet cleaned best on apically tapered implants and left minimal titanium residues, whereas curettes released the most (152.0 ± 75.5).

P1949.t: Prevalence and risk/protective indicators of peri-implant diseases: a university-representative cross-sectional study
P1949.kf: Cross-sectional study of 99 patients (458 implants): peri-implantitis prevalence was 56.6% at patient and 27.9% at implant level; risk indicators included smoking (OR 3.59), moderate/severe periodontitis (2.77), plaque (3.49) and vestibular malposition (2.85), while interproximal cleaning was protective (OR 0.27).

P1950.t: Prevalence of peri-implantitis in patients not participating in well-designed supportive periodontal treatments: a cross-sectional study
P1950.kf: Retrospective cross-sectional study of 134 patients (478 implants, mean loading 4.43 years) without regular maintenance: peri-implantitis affected 20% of patients and 8.8% of implants, mucositis 48.5% and 40%; smoking (OR 2.57) and lack of keratinized mucosa (OR 3.89) were associated with peri-implantitis.

P1951.t: Prevention and management of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis: A systematic review of outcome measures used in clinical studies in the last 10 years
P1951.kf: Systematic review of 159 clinical studies on preventing or managing peri-implant diseases: PPD and BOP were reported in 89% and 87%, whereas composite outcomes (26%), adverse events (8%) and patient-reported outcomes (6%) were rare; only 36% clearly defined a primary outcome.

P1953.t: Primary prevention of peri-implantitis: Managing peri-implant mucositis
P1953.kf: Consensus report based on four systematic reviews: weighted mean prevalence was 43% for peri-implant mucositis and 22% for peri-implantitis; lack of supportive therapy raised peri-implantitis risk, and adjunctive antiseptics, antibiotics or air-abrasion did not improve professional plaque removal.

P1954.t: Reconstruction of Peri-implant Osseous Defects: A Multicenter Randomized Trial
P1954.kf: Multicenter RCT of 63 patients with circumferential peri-implant defects: open flap debridement plus porous titanium granules gave 3.6/3.6 mm radiographic defect fill vs 1.1/1.0 mm with debridement alone at 12 months (P < 0.0001), but complete resolution (30% vs 23%) and PPD reduction were similar.

P1955.t: Reconstructive Procedures for Treating Peri-implantitis: A Systematic Review
P1955.kf: Systematic review of 12 studies (1 RCT plus case series): meta-analysis showed weighted mean radiographic defect fill 2.17 mm, PD reduction 2.97 mm, CAL gain 1.65 mm and BOP reduction 45.8%, with great variability in outcomes.

P1960.t: Re-osseointegration following reconstructive surgical therapy of experimental peri-implantitis. A pre-clinical in vivo study
P1960.kf: Dog study (6 Labradors) of reconstructive surgery for experimental peri-implantitis: smooth-surface implants showed significantly greater radiographic bone gain, lesion resolution and re-osseointegration than moderately rough implants, while bone substitute benefits were overall small.

P1962.t: Study on the immunopathological effect of titanium particles in peri-implantitis granulation tissue: A case–control study
P1962.kf: Case-control histology study of 39 peri-implantitis and 35 periodontitis biopsies: titanium particles were present in all peri-implantitis specimens without macrophage engulfment or foreign body reaction; peri-implantitis tissue showed more macrophages (CD68) and neovascularization (VEGF) than periodontitis.

P1964.t: Surface decontamination protocols for surgical treatment of peri-implantitis: A systematic review with meta-analysis
P1964.kf: Systematic review of 16 RCTs on implant surface decontamination in surgical peri-implantitis therapy: no method was clearly superior; Er:YAG laser added no PPD reduction (WMD -0.24 mm), while systemic amoxicillin or azithromycin improved treatment success (RR 1.84) but not PPD reduction.

P1965.t: Surgical Management of Peri-Implantitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Treatment Outcomes
P1965.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 articles (12 case series) on surgical peri-implantitis treatment: weighted mean PD reduction ranged from 2.04 mm (resection) to 3.16 mm (GBR), and radiographic bone fill was 2.1 mm with bone grafting or GBR over 3 to 63 months.

P1966.t: Surgical peri-implantitis treatment with and without guided bone regeneration. A randomized controlled trial
P1966.kf: RCT of 40 patients with contained intraosseous peri-implantitis defects: at 12 months access flap alone vs with xenograft and collagen membrane gave PD reduction 4.2 vs 3.7 mm, bone gain 1.7 vs 2.4 mm and success 90% vs 85%, with no significant differences.

P1972.t: What is the influence of implant surface characteristics and/or implant material on the incidence and progression of peri-implantitis? A systematic literature review
P1972.kf: Systematic review: dog meta-analyses showed modified surfaces had greater bone loss (0.44 mm) and infiltrated connective tissue (0.75 mm) during peri-implantitis progression, but clinical data from 7605 patients with 26,188 implants showed no significant differences in peri-implantitis incidence among surfaces.

P1973.t: Crestal Bone Loss and Oral Implants
P1973.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P1973.kf: Consensus meeting plus review of 10 studies on three moderately rough modern implant brands (≥10 years): BOP and probing depth were weak indicators of crestal bone loss, and peri-implant infection with bone loss leading to removal or surgery averaged 2.7% over 7 to 16 years.

P1985.t: Novel impacts of saliva with regard to oral health
P1985.kf: Narrative review of saliva physiology and its roles in oral health. The authors conclude proteomics advances have expanded understanding of salivary proteins, saliva-based diagnostics are developing rapidly, and general knowledge of saliva physiology is important in clinical practice.

P1986.t: The Relationships Between Tooth‐Supported Fixed Dental Prostheses and Restorations and the Periodontium
P1986.kf: Narrative review: subgingival restorations are associated with increased gingival index, BOP, probing depth and attachment loss, but intracrevicular margins do not cause periodontal disease; inflammation and bone loss occur with direct and indirect restorations only with large overhangs.

P1987.t: Periodontal ligament formation around different types of dental titanium implants. I. The self-tapping screw type implant system
P1987.kf: Monkey study (7 animals) with self-tapping titanium implants placed in contact with retained root tips: after 3 months new cementum was deposited on implant surfaces contacting the retained roots, while osseointegration occurred elsewhere and on implants without root contact.

P1988.t: Periodontal ligament formation around titanium implants using cultured periodontal ligament cells: a pilot study
P1988.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P1988.kf: Pilot dog study (3 dogs) of titanium implants seeded with cultured autologous periodontal ligament cells: after 3 months some implant surfaces showed a cementum-like layer with inserting collagen fibers.

P1989.t: Titanium Implants with a True Periodontal Ligament: An Alternative to Osseointegrated Implants?
P1989.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P1989.kf: Monkey study of titanium implants placed near retained apical root portions: implants in close contact with retained roots developed a cementum layer with inserting collagen fibers, whereas implants without root contact showed typical osseointegration.

P1991.t: Some periodontal tissue reactions to orthodontic tooth movement in monkeys
P1991.kf: Monkey study (5 animals) of incisors moved labially through the alveolar envelope and premolars moved distally: at every second labially moved incisor the gingival margin shifted apically, but displacement was small and accompanied by attachment loss at only 2 teeth, which showed gingival inflammation.

P1993.t: The link between periodontitis and Alzheimer’s disease – emerging clinical evidence
P1993.kf: Review: pre-clinical and clinical studies show associations between periodontal disease and Alzheimer's disease, with recent evidence suggesting a bi-directional relationship, but a causal relationship has yet to be established.

P1997.t: Use of cone beam computed tomography in implant dentistry: current concepts, indications and limitations for clinical practice and research
P1997.kf: Narrative review: no data show that preoperative CBCT reduces intraoperative complications or improves implant survival; postoperative CBCT should be limited to specific complications, and peri-implantitis should be assessed clinically and with periapical radiographs.

P2006.t: Digital technology in fixed implant prosthodontics
P2006.kf: Narrative review of digital technology in fixed implant prosthodontics. The authors conclude single-unit monolithic implant crowns with intraoral scanning and virtual design may be considered in place of conventional manufacturing, but a complete digital approach for implant-supported fixed prostheses has not been …

P2008.t: Evolution of loading protocols in implant dentistry for partially dentate arches
P2008.kf: Narrative review of implant loading protocols for partially dentate arches. The authors state the literature is of varying quality but suggest implant survival is not affected by placement or loading protocol with careful assessment, with insertion torque above 25 Ncm and/or ISQ above 60 recommended for accelerated …

P2011.t: Screw retained vs. cement retained implant-supported fixed dental prosthesis
P2011.kf: Review of screw- versus cement-retained implant FDPs including recent systematic reviews: the retention type might not influence overall prosthesis survival but may be responsible for certain complications; a decision tree for selection is presented.

P2016.t: Consensus Statements and Recommended Clinical Procedures Regarding Optimizing Esthetic Outcomes in Implant Dentistry
P2016.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2016.kf: Consensus statements (ITI Group 3) from three systematic reviews on esthetics. Midfacial recession of 1 mm or more occurred in 9% to 41% (median 26%) of immediate placements at 1 to 3 years; most data are case series; early placement is the option of choice in most instances; soft tissue defect resolution after …

P2017.t: Ridge preservation techniques for implant therapy
P2017.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2017.kf: Systematic review of 37 human studies (1999–2008): ridge preservation procedures were effective in limiting horizontal and vertical post-extraction ridge alterations, with no technique shown superior and no conclusive evidence of improved ability to place implants.

P2020.t: Surgical protocols for ridge preservation after tooth extraction. A systematic review
P2020.kf: Systematic review of 14 publications (9 pooled in meta-analyses): control sites without ridge preservation showed significantly greater bone height reduction than treated sites (WMD = −1.47 mm; 95% CI −1.982 to −0.953; P < 0.001).

P2021.t: Fracture Resistance of Zirconia Restorations with a Modified Framework Design
P2021.kf: In vitro study of 24 veneered zirconia crowns: final fracture resistance was 3519.42±1154.96 N with standard 0.5 mm copings and 3570.01±1224.33 N with modified copings (P=0.9); most specimens showed mixed failure.

P2024.t: Tooth preparations for complete crowns: an art form based on scientific principles
P2024.kf: Literature review of complete crown preparations: recommends 10 to 20 degrees total occlusal convergence, a minimum occlusocervical dimension of 4 mm for molars and 3 mm for other teeth, a ratio of 0.4 or greater, and auxiliary grooves or boxes when these features are missing.

P2025.t: The peri‐implant phenotype and implant esthetic complications. Contemporary overview
P2025.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2025.kf: Overview: keratinized mucosa width, mucosal thickness, supracrestal tissue height and buccal bone are linked to implant esthetics and health, but the literature does not allow point-by-point evidence-based recommendations for each component.

P2026.t: The significance of surgically modifying soft tissue phenotype around fixed dental prostheses: An American Academy of Periodontology best evidence review
P2026.kf: Systematic review: no controlled studies on tooth sites were found; meta-analysis of 5 implant studies showed soft tissue phenotype modification increased tissue thickness (WMD 0.98 mm) and reduced mucosal recession (WMD 0.36 mm), without significant effects on BOP, PD, PES or marginal bone loss.

P2027.t: A Beginning Guide for Dental Photography: A Simplified Introduction for Esthetic Dentistry
P2027.kf: Narrative review/guide to dental photography for esthetic dentistry. Key points: dental photography is a simple tool needed for high-level predictable esthetic dentistry; the author recommends a DSLR camera with an 85 to 105 mm macro lens, symmetrical flash lighting, and set exposure parameters (shutter speed 1/125, …

P2035.t: Platform-switching implants and bone preservation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
P2035.j: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P2035.kf: Meta-analysis of 25 studies (17 RCTs, 8 prospective; 1098 patients, 2310 implants): platform-switched implants had significantly less crestal bone loss than regular-platform implants (-0.41 mm, 95% CI -0.52 to -0.29) but no difference in failure (RR 1.10).

P2037.t: Platform switching and marginal bone‐level alterations: the results of a randomized‐controlled trial
P2037.kf: RCT of 31 patients (80 posterior maxillary implants; 69 analysed) restored with 3.8-mm abutments on 3.8 (control), 4.3, 4.8 or 5.5 mm platforms: mean bone loss was 0.99, 0.82 and 0.56 mm for the 4.3, 4.8 and 5.5 mm platform-switched groups.

P2040.t: Soft tissue changes and crestal bone loss around platform‐switched implants placed at crestal and subcrestal levels: 36‐month results from a prospective split‐mouth clinical trial
P2040.kf: Prospective split-mouth trial (23 patients, sides allocated by coin toss; 46 implants): platform-switched implants placed 2 mm subcrestally versus crestally. At 36 months crestal bone loss was 0.3 vs 0.45 mm; bleeding on probing and probing depth showed no significant differences, and survival was 100% in both groups.

P2041.t: Crestal Bone Level Around Tissue-Level Implants Restored with Platform Matching and Bone-Level Implants Restored with Platform Switching: A 5-Year Randomized Controlled Trial
P2041.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2041.kf: RCT of 100 patients (202 posterior implants): 5-year marginal bone level change was 0.61 ± 0.73 mm for platform-matched tissue-level implants versus -0.20 ± 0.75 mm for platform-switched bone-level implants (mean difference 0.85 mm, P < .001); survival 98% and 96.1%.

P2042.t: A 5-Year Esthetic RCT Assessment of Anterior Maxillary Single-Tooth Implants with Different Abutment Interfaces
P2042.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2042.kf: RCT of 141 patients with immediately provisionalized anterior maxillary single implants: 5-year marginal bone loss was -0.16 mm for conical, -0.92 mm for flat-to-flat and -0.81 mm for platform-switched interfaces (P < .0005), with minimal mucosal zenith change and similar papillae.

P2045.t: Effect of Microthreads and Platform Switching on Crestal Bone Stress Levels: A Finite Element Analysis
P2045.kf: 2D finite element model of a 5 mm mandibular premolar implant loaded at 100 N: the microthread model had 29% greater crestal bone stress (31.61 MPa oblique, 9.31 MPa vertical) than the smooth-neck implant (24.51 and 7.20 MPa).

P2046.t: In Vitro Bacterial Leakage at the Implant-Abutment Connection of Two Dental Implant Systems with Internal Connection
P2046.kf: In vitro E. coli leakage test of 22 implants with 30 Ncm abutment torque: microleakage occurred in 20% of conical-connection samples after 6 h to 2 days and in 50% of slip-joint samples after 3 to 7 days.

P2048.t: Evaluation of peri-implant bone loss around platform-switched implants
P2048.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P2048.kf: Prospective study of 131 implants in 45 patients: 75 received a healing abutment 1 mm narrower than the platform (platform switching) vs matching-diameter controls. At 12 months after loading, mean vertical bone loss was 0.95 ± 0.32 mm (test) vs 1.67 ± 0.37 mm (control).

P2050.kf: Narrative review of PubMed literature (1990–2014) on implant-abutment connections (external hex, internal hex, Morse taper), describing inherent differences in design characteristics and clinical applications.

P2051.t: Platform switching: biomechanical evaluation using three-dimensional finite element analysis
P2051.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2051.kf: 3D finite element analysis of external-hex implant single crowns (regular platform, platform-switched, wide platform) under 100 N axial or oblique load: platform switching reduced von Mises stress in peri-implant bone by 17.5% (axial) and 9.3% (oblique) and gave lower bone and implant stresses than the other models.

P2052.t: Bone Response to Loaded Implants With Non‐Matching Implant‐Abutment Diameters in the Canine Mandible
P2052.kf: Histologic study in five dogs (12 implants each, placed at, 1 mm above or 1 mm below the crest; submerged vs non-submerged; 6 months post-loading) of a platform-switched Morse taper configuration: marginal bone remained near the top of the implants under both healing conditions.

P2053.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2053.kf: Topological shape optimization combined with 2D/3D finite element analysis of dental implants: designs with a taper and larger crestal radius at the shoulder showed significantly lower peak stresses under axial and oblique loads than a commercial implant model.

P2056.t: Influence of Vertical Soft Tissue Thickness on Crestal Bone Changes Around Implants with Platform Switching: A Comparative Clinical Study
P2056.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2056.kf: Prospective comparative study of 80 platform-switched implants (40 in thin mucosa of 2 mm or less, 40 in thick mucosa): crestal bone loss at 1 year was 1.18 mm (thin) vs 0.22 mm (thick), P < .001, with 100% survival. Platform switching did not prevent bone loss in thin tissue.

P2066.t: Preservation of crestal bone by implant design. A comparative study in minipigs
P2066.kf: Minipig study (12 animals) comparing three bone-level implant designs placed at crest level or 1 mm above: no differences at 4 weeks; at 12 weeks, at crest level, Astra OsseoSpeed and Straumann Bone Level implants preserved more crestal bone than NobelReplace Tapered Groovy (P < 0.01).

P2067.t: Platform switching minimises crestal bone loss around dental implants: truth or myth?
P2067.kf: Systematic review of 15 clinical studies (PubMed/Google Scholar to December 2013) on platform switching: seven studies reported that platform-switched implants did not minimise crestal bone loss compared with non-platform-switched implants.

P2068.t: Platform Switching for Marginal Bone Preservation Around Dental Implants: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
P2068.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 controlled studies (1,239 implants): marginal bone loss was significantly less around platform-switched than platform-matched implants (mean difference -0.37 mm; 95% CI -0.55 to -0.20), with no difference in implant failure; an abutment mismatch of 0.4 mm or more gave a more …

P2069.t: Bone and Soft Tissue Response in Bone-Level Implants Restored with Platform Switching: A 5-Year Clinical Prospective Study
P2069.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2069.kf: Prospective single-arm study of 67 bone-level implants restored with platform switching, followed 5 years: mean marginal bone level change was -0.28 ± 0.45 mm from baseline to 5 years, and papilla tip-to-contact point distance went from 2.08 mm to 1.31 mm.

P2073.t: Impact of platform switching on interproximal bone levels around 8.5 mm implants in the posterior region; 5-year results from a randomized clinical trial
P2073.kf: RCT of 80 patients with 8.5 mm posterior implants (platform-switched vs platform-matched), 5 years after loading: interproximal bone loss was 0.38 ± 0.61 mm vs 0.41 ± 0.47 mm (p = 0.201), with comparable survival, clinical parameters and satisfaction.

P2078.t: The flat and step (F and S) pontics. Novel pontic designs for periodontally reconstructed sites
P2078.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2078.kf: Technique article describing flat (F) and step (S) pontic designs that contact a wide mucosal area of a periodontally reconstructed ridge without excessive pressure, to reduce inflammation and ease cleaning.

P2079.t: The Implant Biologic Pontic Designed Interface: Description of the Technique and Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Evaluation
P2079.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2079.kf: Retrospective CBCT evaluation of 65 patients (383 implants, 219 pontic sites) with zirconia prostheses and modified ovate pontics at 3 years: implant and prosthesis survival 98.7% and 100%; mean ridge mucosa thickness 2.32 ± 0.57 mm (maxilla) and 2.20 ± 0.62 mm (mandible).

P2081.t: Bonding between layering materials and zirconia frameworks
P2081.kf: Literature review of in vitro studies on bond strength between layering materials and zirconia frameworks, covering comparisons with metal-ceramics, thermal expansion mismatch, press-on ceramics, liners and cooling time; few studies addressed indirect composites.

P2084.kf: Laboratory-perspective article on modern metal-ceramic restorations (high-gold alloy framework, fine-leucite porcelain, vertically reduced framework). The author concludes new metal-ceramic systems can rival all-ceramic restorations in esthetics and, given the short clinical history of all-ceramics, remain the choice …

P2087.t: Clinical discrimination between autoglazed and polished porcelain surfaces
P2087.kf: Prosthodontists, general dentists and students (six per group) rated 12 porcelain-fused-to-metal crowns, autoglazed or air-abraded and polished, in two phases: groups differed in outline sharpness, porosity, reflectance, dullness and overall esthetics in phase 1, but only in dullness in phase 2 (p < .01).

P2088.t: Fabrication of Zirconia‐Reinforced Lithium Silicate Ceramic Restorations Using a Complete Digital Workflow
P2088.kf: Case report describing fabrication of monolithic zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS) restorations through a completely digital workflow: powder-free intraoral scanning, generatively fabricated working model and laboratory CAD/CAM.

P2096.t: Lithium-zirconium silicate glass-ceramics for restorative dentistry: Physicochemical analysis and biological response in contact with human osteoblast
P2096.kf: Laboratory study of lithium-zirconium (LZS) and lithium-zirconium-alumina (LZSA) silicate glass-ceramics: LZS showed higher fracture toughness and Young's modulus and higher osteoblast proliferation and mineralization than LZSA.

P2097.t: Present status and future directions: The restoration of root filled teeth
P2097.kf: Narrative review of restoring root filled teeth: current research largely lacks appreciation of occlusal factors, and the clinical relevance of minimally invasive endodontic and restorative concepts remains largely unanswered by clinical data.

P2098.t: Evaluation of fiber posts vs metal posts for restoring severely damaged endodontically treated teeth: a systematic review and meta-analysis
P2098.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of four RCTs (3 to 7 years follow-up): fiber posts had significantly higher survival than metal posts (RR 0.57, 95% CI: 0.33 to 0.97, P = .04), with no difference in success, post debonding or root fracture.

P2099.t: Post and core build-ups in crown and bridge abutments: Bio-mechanical advantages and disadvantages
P2099.kf: Narrative review of post and core biomechanics arguing that a post's main function is to help prevent the abutment from fracturing at the crown/ferrule margin level, essentially improving the ferrule effect, rather than mainly retaining the core.

P2100.t: The effect of type post, crown, and ferrule presence on stress distribution of maxillary central incisors with weakened roots: finite element analysis
P2100.kf: 2D finite element analysis of maxillary central incisors with weakened roots (metal-ceramic vs alumina crowns, glass fiber vs cast post, no ferrule vs 2 mm ferrule): cast post-and-cores concentrated stress at the post-dentin interface, fiber posts gave more homogeneous stress, and ferrule improved stress distribution.

P2101.t: Ferrule-Effect Dominates Over Use of a Fiber Post When Restoring Endodontically Treated Incisors: An In Vitro Study
P2101.kf: In vitro fatigue study of 45 decoronated endodontically treated bovine incisors restored with bonded glass-ceramic crowns. The ferrule groups survived significantly more cycles than the no-ferrule group (p = 0.001); adding a fiber post made no significant difference (p = 0.884), and 100% of failures with posts were …

P2103.t: Quality guidelines for endodontic treatment: consensus report of the European Society of Endodontology
P2103.kf: Consensus quality guidelines (European Society of Endodontology) covering history, diagnosis, vital pulp management, root canal treatment steps, surgical endodontics and trauma. They recommend outcome assessment at 1 year and treat a lesion persisting beyond a 4-year assessment period as post-treatment disease.

P2104.t: Effect of different composite core materials on fracture resistance of endodontically treated teeth restored with FRC posts
P2104.kf: In vitro study of 40 endodontically treated premolars restored with quartz fiber posts and four core materials: Clearfil Photo Core and MultiCore Flow gave significantly higher fracture resistance than LuxaCore Z-Dual and Tetric N-Ceram (p<0.05), in line with flexural modulus ranking.

P2105.t: Fracture Strength and Stress Distribution in Premolars Restored with Cast Post-and-Cores or Glass-Fiber Posts Considering the Influence of Ferule
P2105.kf: In vitro study of 40 decoronated mandibular premolars restored with cast post-and-cores or glass-fiber posts, with or without ferrule, plus FEA: fracture strength did not differ between post types, and ferrule presence increased fracture strength with both.

P2106.t: An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses Evaluating the Success Rate of Prosthetic Restorations on Endodontically Treated Teeth
P2106.kf: Umbrella review of 14 systematic reviews/meta-analyses (118 studies) on prosthetic restoration of endodontically treated teeth. From low-risk-of-bias reviews, fiber posts had a higher success rate than metal posts with similar root fracture rates; the authors conclude single crowns and endocrowns are among the most …

P2107.t: Evidence-based treatment planning for the restoration of endodontically treated single teeth: importance of coronal seal, post vs no post, and indirect vs direct restoration
P2107.kf: Narrative appraisal of evidence on coronal restoration of single endodontically treated teeth (coronal seal, post vs no post, indirect vs direct), noting that recent reviews of clinical trials on post placement or crowning are inconclusive.

P2108.t: Rethinking ferrule – a new approach to an old dilemma
P2108.kf: PubMed-based literature review of ferrule effect components (width, partial ferrule, tooth type, lateral loads, 2 mm height rule), deriving a risk-assessment classification of teeth by achievable ferrule effectiveness.

P2110.t: Fiber Posts and Tooth Reinforcement: Evidence in the Literature
P2110.kf: Industry-linked narrative review (two authors disclose consultancy to a fiber post supplier) on fiber posts and tooth reinforcement. The authors conclude there is compelling evidence that fiber posts can reinforce tooth structure, that failures are more often non-catastrophic, and that success falls drastically …

P2112.t: Influence of remaining coronal thickness and height on biomechanical behavior of endodontically treated teeth: survival rates, load to fracture and finite element analysis
P2112.kf: In vitro study of 72 bovine teeth (fiber post vs cast post and core; 0 vs 2 mm coronal height; thickness below vs above 1 mm) under 1.5 million fatigue cycles plus FEA: teeth without remaining coronal structure had lower survival (p=0.001), and thickness above 1 mm increased load to fracture (p=0.0043).

P2113.t: Post-endodontic restorative treatments and their mechanical behavior: A narrative review
P2113.kf: Narrative review of classic literature on post-endodontic restorative treatments, noting that rigid metallic post-and-cores might now be considered a limited option and that glass-fiber posts bring advantages but raise concerns over guidelines and indications.

P2114.t: Degree of conversion and adhesion of methacrylate-based resin cements with phosphonic or phosphoric acid acrylate to glass fiber posts at different regions of intraradicular dentin
P2114.j: Journal of Adhesion Science and Technology
P2114.kf: In vitro study of 24 endodontically treated teeth with glass fiber posts luted with Multilink Automix (phosphonic acid acrylate) or RelyX Unicem 2 (phosphoric acid acrylate): degree of conversion was 67 ± 8.2% vs 26 ± 8.8% (p < 0.001), and push-out bond strength was higher coronally than apically for both.

P2115.t: Evaluation of the sealing capability and morphological fit of prefabricated dowels and fiber-reinforced composite resin: An in vitro study
P2115.kf: In vitro study of 50 maxillary central incisors: fiber-reinforced composite resin dowels had significantly thinner resin cement layers than prefabricated dowels (cervical 197.0 vs 311.0 μm; apical 57.3 vs 131.6 μm) and higher push-out strength (22.98 vs 16.49 N/mm, P<.05).

P2117.t: Influence of remaining coronal tooth structure on fracture resistance and failure mode of restored endodontically treated maxillary incisors
P2117.kf: In vitro study of 60 maxillary central incisors with cast post-and-cores and metal crowns: a 2-mm ferrule missing one interproximal wall had significantly lower fracture resistance (697 N) than a complete 2-mm ferrule (932 N); 3 and 4 mm walls gave 844 N and 853 N.

P2124.t: “Ferrule Comes First. Post Is Second!” Fake News and Alternative Facts? A Systematic Review
P2124.kf: Systematic review of 7 RCTs and 1 prospective trial (minimum 5 years): 2 of 3 studies supported the ferrule effect, 7 of 8 showed no post effect, and 5 studies had high risk of bias.

P2127.t: An in vitro study evaluating the effect of ferrule design on the fracture resistance of endodontically treated mandibular premolars after simulated crown lengthening or forced eruption methods
P2127.kf: In vitro study of 40 mandibular first premolars with simulated crown lengthening or forced eruption and fiber post-and-cores: mean fracture loads ranged from 1.01 kN (no buccal ferrule) to 0.73 kN (crown lengthening, 2.0 mm buccal ferrule); ferrule length mattered (P = 0.012), method did not (P = 0.699).

P2129.t: Evaluation of the fracture resistance of root filled thin walled teeth restored with different post systems
P2129.kf: In vitro study of 80 thin-walled endodontically treated maxillary canines: fracture resistance was highest with cast posts, followed by glass-fiber and I-TFC posts, and lowest with composite resin only (p < 0.05).

P2132.t: Cast metal vs. glass fibre posts: A randomized controlled trial with up to 3 years of follow up
P2132.kf: RCT of 54 participants (72 teeth with no remaining coronal wall, metal-ceramic crowns) followed up to 3 years: survival of glass fibre and cast metal posts was similar (97.1% vs 91.9%; p=0.682), with four failures.

P2133.kf: Narrative overview of post-and-core history, failure causes and systems (custom cast, prefabricated metal, ceramic, fibre-reinforced), with one fibre-post case. Authors conclude many materials and techniques exist, and each clinical situation should be evaluated individually.

P2134.t: Effect of ferrule and post placement on fracture resistance of endodontically treated teeth after fatigue loading
P2134.kf: Fatigue-loading laboratory study of endodontically treated teeth: avoiding extra removal of sound tooth structure, rather than placing a fibre post, protected against catastrophic failure; when some ferrule is preserved, a fibre post may improve retention and fatigue resistance.

P2136.t: Resistance to compression of weakened roots subjected to different root reconstruction protocols
P2136.kf: In vitro study of 40 human anterior roots: non-weakened roots with a glass fiber post had higher fracture resistance than weakened roots reconstructed with incremental composite, accessory fiber posts or anatomic posts, which were similar to each other.

P2139.t: A retrospective case series evaluating the outcome of implants with low primary stability
P2139.kf: Retrospective case series of 156 patients with 169 implants placed with low primary stability (follow-up up to 9.28 years): cumulative survival was 94.74% (implant level) and 94.33% (patient level); all 7 failures occurred in the advanced surgery group (p = 0.005).

P2140.t: Diagnosis of implant stability and its impact on implant survival: a prospective case series study
P2140.kf: Prospective case series of 4114 consecutive SLA Straumann implants: survival was 99.1% for 3899 clinically stable implants vs 97.2% for 213 unstable implants (rotation when tightening the healing cap).

P2142.t: Excess cement and the risk of peri‐implant disease – a systematic review
P2142.kf: Systematic review of 26 publications (945 subjects, 1010 cemented implant restorations): peri-implant disease prevalence ranged from 1.9% to 75%, with 33–100% of cases associated with excess cement; abutment type and cement medium had no significant influence.

P2143.t: The Positive Relationship Between Excess Cement and Peri‐Implant Disease: A Prospective Clinical Endoscopic Study
P2143.kf: Endoscopic study of 39 consecutive patients with peri-implant disease signs (42 test implants) and 20 control implants without inflammation: excess cement was found at 34 test sites and at none of the controls.

P2144.t: Influence of Apico‐Coronal Implant Placement on Post‐Surgical Crestal Bone Loss in Humans
P2144.kf: Retrospective chart review of 55 patients (134 implants) followed to 12–18 months: on the mesial aspect, 67.3% of implants were subcrestal at placement but only 17.7% at prosthetic delivery, while supracrestal positions rose from 13.3% to 46.9%.

P2146.t: Peri-implant disease: current understanding and future direction
P2146.kf: Narrative review of peri-implant disease. Authors conclude implant treatment requires planned ongoing maintenance; smoking and previous periodontitis raise risk; no gold standard peri-implantitis treatment exists; the key to peri-implant health is continuous assessment and individualised supportive treatment.

P2148.t: Systemic Antibiotic Prophylaxis to Reduce Early Implant Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P2148.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (11 studies): antibiotics significantly reduced early implant failure (RR = 0.30, 95% CI: 0.19–0.47), a single preoperative dose sufficed vs no antibiotic (RR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.21–0.53), and pre- vs pre+postoperative regimens did not differ.

P2152.kf: Narrative review of osseoperception: tooth loss removes periodontal mechanoreception, and implant-supported prostheses restore jaw function more appropriately than complete dentures, with improved psychophysiological discrimination and oral stereognosis.

P2155.t: Clinical Uses of Platelet-Rich Fibrin in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P2155.kf: Narrative review of platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) uses in oral and maxillofacial surgery. Authors report that most studies favor PRF over controls and show promising results, but there is no standard PRF protocol and more randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm surgical indications.

P2156.t: Comparison between PRP, PRGF and PRF: lights and shadows in three similar but different protocols
P2156.j: European Review for Medical and Pharmacological Sciences
P2156.kf: Narrative comparison of PRP, PRGF and PRF protocols, highlighting PRF's simpler production without manipulation, which reduces the chance of operator-related protocol errors.

P2157.t: Current Knowledge and Perspectives for the Use of Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) and Platelet-Rich Fibrin (PRF) in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Part 1: Periodontal and Dentoalveolar Surgery
P2157.kf: Narrative review of PRP and PRF in periodontal and dentoalveolar surgery (extraction, mucogingival surgery, GTR, intrabony defects, GBR), noting the literature is contradictory, dense for PRP and still limited for PRF subfamilies.

P2158.t: Drugs and diseases: Summary and consensus statements of group 1. The 5th EAO Consensus Conference 2018
P2158.kf: EAO consensus statements (5th Consensus Conference 2018) from systematic reviews on platelet concentrates, antiresorptive drugs and titanium particles. Evidence is weak: PRF may limit post-extraction ridge resorption; low-dose oral bisphosphonates were not associated with increased implant loss; evidence does not …

P2160.t: Platelet rich fibrin is not a barrier membrane! Or is it?
P2160.kf: Narrative review arguing that PRF lacks occlusivity, stiffness and space maintenance and therefore does not meet barrier membrane criteria, although there is evidence that PRF membranes significantly improve wound healing.

P2161.t: Platelet-rich plasma for periodontal regeneration in the treatment of intrabony defects: a meta-analysis on prospective clinical trials
P2161.j: Oral Surgery Oral Medicine Oral Pathology and Oral Radiology
P2161.kf: Meta-analysis of prospective clinical trials (21 included, 18 meta-analyzed) on PRP for intrabony defects: attachment level gain WMD 0.58 mm (95% CI 0.24 to 0.91) and bone level WMD 0.76 mm (95% CI 0.21-1.31), but no significant PPD difference (WMD 0.55 mm, P=.09).

P2162.t: The application of injectable platelet-rich fibrin in regenerative dentistry: A systematic scoping review of In vitro and In vivo studies
P2162.kf: Systematic scoping review (2000 to December 2021) identifying 18 in vitro, 5 animal, 6 case report and 31 clinical studies on injectable PRF, which reported anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial and regenerative effects for wound, periodontal, bone, cartilage and pulp regeneration.

P2164.t: Use of platelet-rich fibrin in regenerative dentistry: a systematic review
P2164.kf: Systematic review of 35 human RCTs (to May 2016): PRF was most studied for intrabony defects and gingival recessions with mostly favorable soft tissue results and reduced third-molar dry sockets tenfold; little or no data addressed bone formation in GBR, sinus lifting or peri-implantitis.

P2166.t: RPA clasp design for distal-extension removable partial dentures
P2166.kf: Descriptive article presenting the RPA clasp (mesial rest with circumferential retentive arm) as an alternative to the RPI clasp for distal-extension RPDs, giving essentially the same tooth release.

P2167.t: Evaluation of removable partial denture frameworks fabricated using 3 different techniques
P2167.kf: Clinical study in 9 participants, each receiving RPD frameworks made by analog, combined analog-digital and fully digital (intraoral scan, selective laser melting) pathways, rated by 5 clinicians: digital was significantly better than analog (P<.001) and combined (P<.001); analog beat combined (P=.008).

P2168.t: Implant-assisted removable partial dentures as an alternative treatment for partial edentulism: a review of the literature
P2168.kf: PubMed-based literature review of implant-assisted removable partial dentures, indicating that combining implants with RPDs is a cost-efficient protocol that can address problematic aspects of RPD treatment.

P2169.t: Clinical Performance of Implant Crown Retained Removable Partial Dentures for Mandibular Edentulism—A Retrospective Study
P2169.kf: Retrospective study of 18 implant-crown-retained RPDs (60 implants) vs 24 magnet-retained implant overdentures (94 implants), median follow-up 46.6 months: implant survival was 98.3% vs 92.5%, and cumulative survival at 96 months 98.3% vs 83.1%.

P2171.t: Science in the Practice of Clinical Dentistry
P2171.kf: Narrative article explaining how clinicians can interpret dental research: study designs and evidence hierarchy, publication bias, statistical versus clinical significance, forest plots, confidence intervals, power and efficacy versus effectiveness. The author concludes clinical dentistry data are sometimes …

P2180.t: A New Method Using Autogenous Impacted Third Molars for Sinus Augmentation to Enhance Implant Treatment: Case Series with Preliminary Results of an Open, Prospective Longitudinal Study
P2180.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2180.kf: Prospective case series of six patients receiving lateral sinus elevation with particulate autogenous impacted third molar material: first-year peri-implant bone resorption averaged up to 0.63 mm, bone remained stable up to 5 years, and histology showed osteoconductive osteogenesis.

P2210.t: Rubber dam in endodontics - an overview of recent advances
P2210.kf: Narrative overview of recent advances in rubber dam materials, arguing that rubber dam is obligatory in endodontics and that newer variations make it easier to use, countering common reasons for not using it.

P2212.t: Accuracy of Intraoral Scanners for Recording the Denture Bearing Areas: A Systematic Review
P2212.kf: Systematic review of 18 studies (8 clinical, the rest laboratory) on intraoral scanner accuracy for denture-bearing areas: accuracy differed among scanners, with influencing factors including artificial markers, scanner head size, scanning strategy and operator experience.

P2213.t: In vitro scanning accuracy using different aids for multiple implants in the edentulous arch
P2213.kf: In vitro study (10 intraoral scans per scan-aid variant, three designs and three colors) on a six-implant edentulous maxillary model: the beige irregular scan aid had the highest trueness and differed significantly from unsplinted scans, while precision was heterogeneous and decreased with the aid.

P2214.t: Enhancing intraoral scanner accuracy using scan aid for multiple implants in the edentulous arch: An in vivo study
P2214.kf: In vivo study of 87 implants in 22 edentulous patients scanned with and without a scan aid using CS3600 and TRIOS3: the aid reduced CS mean linear deviation from 189 to 135 μm (p = .001) but not TRIOS (165 μm both), and improved successful scan-body recognition with both scanners.

P2215.t: The ability of marginal detection using different intraoral scanning systems: A pilot randomized controlled trial
P2215.kf: Pilot RCT of 30 patients needing inlays/onlays, randomized to one of three intraoral scanners (Aadva, True Definition, Trios): no significant inter-scanner differences in margin detection were found, whereas all margins were clearly visible on conventional impression controls.

P2217.t: A guide for maximizing the accuracy of intraoral digital scans. Part 1: Operator factors
P2217.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2217.kf: Narrative guide classifying operator factors that affect intraoral scanner accuracy, including system selection, scanning head size, calibration, scanning distance, ambient temperature, humidity and lighting, operator experience, scanning pattern, scan extension and rescanning.

P2218.t: A guide for maximizing the accuracy of intraoral digital scans: Part 2—Patient factors
P2218.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2218.kf: Narrative guide classifying patient factors that affect intraoral scanner accuracy, including tooth type, interdental spaces, arch width, palate, wetness, existing restorations, edentulous areas, and implant distance, position, angulation, depth and scan body selection.

P2219.t: Evaluation of implant abutment screw tightening protocols on reverse tightening values: An in vitro study
P2219.kf: In vitro study of 50 Neoss implants (five tightening protocols, n=10, 32 Ncm): mean reverse tightening values were 21.49 to 22.57 Ncm for the first four protocols and 25.51 Ncm for the tighten/counter-tighten-twice-then-tighten protocol (P<.05).

P2221.t: Monolithic hybrid abutment crowns (screw-retained) versus monolithic hybrid abutments with adhesively cemented monolithic crowns
P2221.kf: Pilot RCT of 20 subjects with single implants restored with screw-retained monolithic lithium disilicate hybrid abutment crowns or cemented crowns on hybrid abutments, 36 months: one cemented restoration failed (Ti-base adhesion loss); survival, FIPS, OHIP, treatment time and satisfaction did not differ significantly.

P2224.t: Cuspal deflection and microleakage in premolar teeth restored with bulk-fill flowable resin-based composite base materials
P2224.kf: In vitro study of 24 premolars with Class II cavities: mean total cuspal deflection was 11.26 μm with oblique incremental GrandioSO vs 4.63 μm (SDR) and 4.73 μm (x-tra base) bulk-fill flowable bases (P=0.007, P=0.005); cervical microleakage did not differ.

P2226.t: Randomized clinical trial evaluating the effect of splinting crowns on short implants in the mandible 3 years after loading
P2226.kf: RCT of 20 patients with two 7-mm implants in the posterior mandible, randomized to splinted (n=11) or non-splinted (n=13) cemented crowns, 3 years: implant and restoration survival was 100% in both groups; success was 84.6% non-splinted vs 86.4% splinted.

P2228.t: Mechano‐adaptive Responses of Alveolar Bone to Implant Hyper‐loading in a pre‐clinical in vivo model
P2228.kf: Mouse study (66 mice randomized to normal or hyper-loading of maxillary implants) using FEA, µCT, histology and remodeling assays: hyper-loaded implants experienced a 3.6-fold increase in occlusal force compared with controls.

P2232.t: Short implants compared to implants in vertically augmented bone: a systematic review
P2232.kf: Systematic review of four RCTs (15 to 30 per group, 1–5 years): implant survival was similar in vertically augmented bone vs short implants (95.09% vs 96.24%), with more surgical complications after augmentation (56 vs 18 patients).

P2233.t: Systematic review of short- (5–10 years) and long-term (10 years or more) survival and success of full-arch fixed dental hybrid prostheses and supporting implants
P2233.kf: Systematic review of 18 studies on full-arch fixed hybrid prostheses: short-term (5–10 years) survival was 93.3–100% for prostheses and 87.89–100% for implants, while true long-term studies were scarce and at risk of bias.

P2234.t: Implant Survival and Crestal Bone Loss Around Extra-Short Implants Supporting a Fixed Denture: The Effect of Crown Height Space, Crown-to-Implant Ratio, and Offset Placement of the Prosthesis
P2234.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2234.kf: Study of 34 patients with 45 extra-short implants (≤6.5 mm) supporting posterior mandibular fixed dentures, mean follow-up 2 years: no implants were lost; mean crown-to-implant ratio was 2.4, and bone loss correlated significantly only with crown height space.

P2235.t: Short implants (≤8mm) compared to standard length implants (>8mm) in conjunction with maxillary sinus floor augmentation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
P2235.j: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P2235.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of three low-risk-of-bias studies (≥3 years): no significant differences in implant survival, marginal bone loss or patient satisfaction between short (≤8 mm) implants and standard implants with lateral-window sinus floor augmentation.

P2236.t: The Effect of Crown/Implant Ratio and Crown Height Space on Stress Distribution in Unsplinted Implant Supporting Restorations
P2236.j: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
P2236.kf: Photoelastic model study with strain gauges on unsplinted implant restorations: at 30° loading, microstrain rose significantly as C/I ratio increased from 1:1 to 1:1.5 (P < .001), and C/I ratios of 1:1.75 and 1:2 led to abutment screw fracture; failures occurred at CHS >15 mm.

P2238.t: One-Year Results of a Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial of Immediately Loaded Short Implants Placed in the Lower Posterior Single Molar Using a Complete Digital Workflow
P2238.kf: Randomized controlled trial, 52 patients, immediately loaded single implants in the posterior mandible via a fully digital workflow (short 6.6-8.5 mm vs 10 mm long; 19 long and 27 short analyzed), 1-year follow-up. No significant differences in ISQ, marginal bone loss or soft tissue parameters.

P2242.t: The Influence of Crown-to-Implant Ratio on Short Implant Marginal Bone Loss
P2242.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2242.kf: Retrospective cohort of 59 patients with 118 short (4 × 7 mm) external-connection implants at 36 months: mean MBL was 0.67 ± 0.63 mm and mean C/I ratio 2.53 ± 0.79, with a weak non-significant inverse correlation between them (r = -0.081; P = .383).

P2243.t: Influence of Crown/Implant Ratio on Marginal Bone Loss: A Systematic Review
P2243.kf: Systematic review of 13 human studies (minimum 6 months follow-up) on crown/implant ratio: a significant negative association between C/I ratio and marginal bone loss was found (P = 0.012).

P2245.t: Short Implants (5 to 8 mm) Versus Longer Implants (>8 mm) with Sinus Lifting in Atrophic Posterior Maxilla: A Meta‐Analysis of RCTs
P2245.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2245.kf: Meta-analysis of seven RCTs (554 implants): short (5–8 mm) implants and longer implants with sinus lifting had similar survival (RR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.97–1.03), while short implants had significantly fewer complications (RR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.37–0.90).

P2247.t: Long‐term effectiveness of 6 mm micro‐rough implants in various indications: A 4.6‐ to 18.2‐year retrospective study
P2247.kf: Retrospective study of 55 patients with 74 six-mm micro-rough implants after 4.6–18.2 years: survival was 93.2% (all losses in mandibular free-end sites), success 89.2%, mean MBL 0.029 mm; smoking significantly reduced survival (hazard ratio 36.25).

P2250.t: Short Dental Implants Retaining Two-Implant Mandibular Overdentures in Very Old, Dependent Patients: Radiologic and Clinical Observation Up to 5 Years
P2250.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2250.kf: Follow-up of 19 very old dependent patients (mean age 85.7 years) with two 8-mm Straumann implants retaining mandibular Locator overdentures: 5-year implant survival was 94.7% and mean peri-implant bone loss 0.17 mm per year.

P2259.t: Rehabilitation of posterior atrophic edentulous jaws: prostheses supported by 5 mm short implants or by longer implants in augmented bone? One-year results from a pilot randomised clinical trial
P2259.kf: Pilot split-mouth RCT in 30 patients (5-mm implants vs ≥10-mm implants in augmented bone), 1 year after loading: two long and one short implant failed, with no significant differences in failures or complications; mean bone loss was 1 mm vs 1.2 mm (statistically significant).

P2261.t: Influence of the Crown-Implant Connection on the Preservation of Peri-Implant Bone: A Retrospective Multifactorial Analysis
P2261.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2261.kf: Retrospective analysis of 246 implants in 101 patients in pristine maxillary bone: at 18 months, MBL was significantly higher around external than internal connections (0.714 vs 0.516 mm/year), and age and smoking were also related to MBL.

P2263.t: Short implants versus longer implants in vertically augmented posterior mandibles: a randomised controlled trial with 5-year after loading follow-up
P2263.kf: RCT of 60 patients (6.6-mm implants vs ≥9.6-mm implants in vertically augmented posterior mandibles), 5 years after loading: failures did not differ, augmented patients had more complications (25 in 21 vs 6 in 6 patients, P < 0.0001), and bone loss was 1.49 vs 2.34 mm.

P2264.t: Influence of the crown‐to‐implant length ratio on the clinical performance of implants supporting single crown restorations: a cross‐sectional retrospective 5‐year investigation
P2264.kf: Cross-sectional retrospective study of 70 patients with 100 posterior single-crown implants (mean follow-up 6.2 years): crown-to-implant ratio did not significantly affect survival (95.8% at 5 years), marginal bone loss or complications; smoking was significantly associated with implant failure and biological …

P2270.t: A systematic review on marginal bone loss around short dental implants (<10 mm) for implant‐supported fixed prostheses
P2270.kf: Systematic review with random-effects meta-regression of studies on short implants (<10 mm) supporting fixed prostheses: implant length had no significant effect on peri-implant marginal bone loss (P = 0.633).

P2271.t: Five-Year Survival of Short Single-Tooth Implants (6 mm): A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
P2271.kf: RCT of 96 patients with posterior single-tooth 6-mm vs 10-mm implants (86 recalled at 5 years): survival was 91% vs 100% (P = 0.036), while median marginal bone levels did not differ (-0.29 vs -0.15 mm).

P2274.t: Use of short implants (6 mm) in a single‐tooth replacement: a 5‐year follow‐up prospective randomized controlled multicenter clinical study
P2274.kf: Multicenter study of 60 SLA implants (30 6-mm, 30 10-mm) supporting single posterior crowns in 45 patients, 5 years: survival was 86.7% for 6-mm vs 96.7% for 10-mm implants.

P2278.t: Survival rates of short (6 mm) micro‐rough surface implants: a review of literature and meta‐analysis
P2278.kf: Review and meta-analysis of 12 studies on 690 Straumann 6-mm micro-rough implants (1–8 years follow-up): 25 implants failed in total, 14 of 266 in the maxilla and 5 of 364 in the mandible.

P2281.t: Marginal bone level and survival of short and standard‐length implants after 3 years: An Open Multi‐Center Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
P2281.kf: Multicenter RCT of 95 patients with 209 splinted posterior implants (6 mm vs 11 mm), 3 years after loading: bone was located 0.27 ± 0.40 mm and 0.44 ± 0.74 mm apical to the platform in test and control groups, with 0.04 mm gain vs 0.02 mm loss over follow-up.

P2284.t: Impact of platform switching on marginal peri‐implant bone‐level changes. A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P2284.kf: Systematic review of 15 RCTs and 7 prospective controlled cohort studies; a meta-analysis of 13 RCTs showed significantly less mean marginal bone change at platform-switched (0.49 mm) than platform-matched implants (1.01 mm).

P2288.t: An Overview of Systematic Reviews Related to Aspects of the Shortened Dental Arch and Its Variants in Adults
P2288.kf: Overview of nine systematic reviews (228 articles) on the shortened dental arch, AMSTAR-rated as five high and four medium quality: seven of nine drew positive conclusions that the SDA concept is functionally sound.

P2289.t: Attitudes Toward the Shortened Dental Arch Concept Among Swedish General Dental Practitioners
P2289.kf: Questionnaire survey of a random sample of 189 Swedish general dental practitioners (54% response, 102 clinicians): attitudes toward the shortened dental arch were generally positive for oral function and comfort, with small group differences but large individual variation.

P2291.t: Knowledge, perceptions and clinical application of the shortened dental arch concept among Malaysian government dentists
P2291.kf: Questionnaire survey of 326 Malaysian government dentists (84.0% response): most had good knowledge and perceptions of the shortened dental arch, but only 20.4% reported applying it clinically.

P2293.t: Signs and Symptoms Associated with TMD in Adults with Shortened Dental Arches
P2293.kf: Cross-sectional study of 725 Tanzanian adults with shortened dental arches and 125 controls: joint sounds were reported more often with only unilateral (17%) or no posterior support (10%), while pain, restricted mobility and clicking did not differ significantly.

P2294.t: The shortened dental arch: A review of the literature
P2294.kf: Literature review (Medline, 1966 onward) of the shortened dental arch, noting that dental arches comprising the anterior and premolar regions meet the requirements of a functional dentition.

P2295.t: The shortened dental arch concept: awareness and opinion of dentists in Victoria, Australia
P2295.kf: Mailed survey of 434 randomly selected dentists in Victoria, Australia: 61% of respondents were aware of the SDA concept, 78.4% believed it useful in clinical practice, and those with <20 years' experience were more aware (p = 0.004).

P2296.kf: Literature review of 83 articles on dentition and oral function: masticatory efficiency and ability are linked to tooth number, and a minimum of 20 teeth with nine to 10 pairs of contacting units (including anterior teeth) is associated with adequate efficiency and ability.

P2299.t: Implant survival after graftless sinus floor augmentation in highly atrophic maxillae: a randomized controlled trial in a split mouth study
P2299.kf: Split-mouth RCT in 10 edentulous patients (graftless membrane-lifted vs autograft/xenograft sinus augmentation; 59 implants; 57–88 months): bone gain was 6.20 vs 9.69 mm (p = 0.041) and implant survival 86.2% vs 96.7% (p < 0.001).

P2300.t: Influence of Lateral Window Dimensions on Vital Bone Formation Following Maxillary Sinus Augmentation
P2300.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2300.kf: Prospective study of 24 lateral-window sinus augmentations in 21 patients with allograft: mean vital bone at 6 months was 21.69% ± 16.30%, with a strong negative correlation between window dimensions and vital bone (r = -0.621; P = .0007).

P2301.t: Intraoperative complications and early implant failure after transcrestal sinus floor elevation with residual bone height ≤5 mm: A retrospective multicenter study
P2301.kf: Retrospective multicenter study of 430 patients with transcrestal sinus elevation at residual bone height ≤5 mm: early implant failure occurred in 12 cases (2.8%) and membrane perforation in 7.2%, both associated with wide bucco-palatal sinus width.

P2304.t: Long-term evaluation of osteotome sinus floor elevation and simultaneous placement of implants without bone grafts: 10-Year radiographic and clinical follow-up
P2304.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2304.kf: Retrospective 10-year follow-up of 34 Astra implants in 25 patients placed with osteotome sinus floor elevation without bone graft: mean marginal bone loss was 0.6 ± 0.8 mm and mean bone gain 2.6 ± 1.2 mm, with 100% survival in single-tooth and partially edentulous cases.

P2310.t: Repair of Large Sinus Membrane Perforations Using Stabilized Collagen Barrier Membranes: Surgical Techniques with Histologic and Radiographic Evidence of Success
P2310.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P2310.kf: Technique report on repairing large Schneiderian membrane perforations by stabilizing a collagen membrane outside the antrostomy and folding it inward as a new wall or pouch; used in 20 consecutive patients without procedural failures, with 6–9-month histologic/radiographic evidence of success.

P2312.t: Sinus augmentation procedure via the lateral window technique—Reducing invasiveness and preventing complications: A narrative review
P2312.kf: Narrative review of lateral-window sinus augmentation covering osteotomy techniques, one- vs two-stage indications, Schneiderian membrane integrity and management of intra- and post-operative complications.

P2313.j: The Journal of Implant & Advanced Clinical Dentistry
P2313.kf: Article proposing a five-class classification of sinus membrane perforations during crestal-approach sinus augmentation, each with corresponding management techniques, and defining sinus cavity space and sinus membrane space.

P2314.t: Six-year extension results of a randomized trial comparing transcrestal and lateral sinus floor elevation at sites with 3–6 mm of residual bone
P2314.kf: 6-year follow-up of a randomized trial (43 of 54 patients) comparing transcrestal vs lateral sinus elevation at 3–6 mm residual bone: implant survival was 100%; radiographic bone contact was 96% vs 100% (p = .036) and median distal MBL 0.3 vs 0 mm (p = .024).

P2323.t: Effect of alveolar ridge preservation interventions following tooth extraction: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P2323.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 RCTs (25 articles) comparing alveolar ridge preservation with socket grafting to extraction alone: pooled analysis showed less horizontal (1.99 mm), vertical mid-buccal (1.72 mm) and vertical mid-lingual (1.16 mm) bone resorption. No superior ARP approach could be determined; …

P2324.t: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Hard Tissue Outcomes of Alveolar Ridge Preservation
P2324.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2324.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 studies: alveolar ridge preservation reduced horizontal bone loss by 1.86 mm (95% CI = 1.44, 2.28) versus extraction alone, with effects modified by wound closure, graft type, membranes, growth factors and socket morphology.

P2325.t: Alveolar ridge preservation with guided bone regeneration or socket seal technique. A randomised, single-blind controlled clinical trial
P2325.kf: Single-blind RCT of anterior maxillary extraction sites (GBR, socket seal or unassisted healing; n = 14 per group): at 4 months, GBR and socket seal preserved buccal ridge height vs control, GBR limited mid-socket area loss (4% vs 13%, p = .01) and had fewer dehiscences at implant placement (57% vs 85%, p = .03).

P2326.t: Alveolar ridge preservation using autogenous whole‐tooth versus demineralized dentin grafts: A randomized controlled clinical trial
P2326.kf: RCT of 20 non-molar extraction sockets grafted with autogenous whole-tooth or demineralized dentin grafts under collagen membranes: at 6 months ridge width reduction was 0.85 ± 0.38 vs 1.02 ± 0.45 mm (p > .05), and all biopsies showed new bone formation.

P2327.t: Early implant placement with or without alveolar ridge preservation in single tooth gaps renders similar esthetic, clinical and patient‐reported outcome measures: One‐year results of a randomized clinical trial
P2327.kf: RCT of 75 patients needing anterior maxillary single extraction (DBBM-C with collagen matrix, DBBM-C with palatal graft, or spontaneous healing) before early implant placement: at 1 year post-loading (70 patients), mid-facial mucosal margin changes did not differ significantly.

P2331.t: Soft tissue contour and radiographic evaluation of ridge preservation in early implant placement: A randomized controlled clinical trial
P2331.kf: RCT, 75 patients, single maxillary incisor/premolar extraction: ridge preservation with xenograft plus collagen matrix or palatal graft versus spontaneous healing, implants at 8 weeks. Horizontal resorption was -0.9 and -1.0 mm versus -3.2 mm (p<.001); GBR was needed in 32% and 24% versus 72% (p=.001).

P2332.t: Efficacy of biologics for alveolar ridge preservation/reconstruction and implant site development: An American Academy of Periodontology best evidence systematic review
P2332.kf: AAP systematic review of 39 RCT articles on biologics (blood-derived products, EMD, rhPDGF-BB, rhBMP-2) for ridge preservation/reconstruction and implant site development: most showed results similar to conventional protocols, though biologics attenuated ridge atrophy vs unassisted healing or collagen sponges and …

P2333.t: Alveolar ridge preservation in the esthetic zone
P2333.kf: Narrative review of ridge preservation decision-making in the esthetic zone, describing three time-periods: soft-tissue preservation (6–8 weeks), hard- and soft-tissue preservation (4–6 months) and hard-tissue preservation (>6 months of healing).

P2336.t: Minimal invasiveness in the alveolar ridge preservation, with or without concomitant implant placement
P2336.kf: Systematic review of 26 studies on minimally invasive ridge preservation (flapless surgery, socket shield, socket sealing, biological agents) with or without immediate implants: most studies failed to show improvements in morbidity, esthetics or patient-related outcomes.

P2338.t: Bone Healing after Tooth Extraction with or without an Intervention: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
P2338.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2338.kf: Systematic review of nine RCTs: control sites lost 2.46 to 4.56 mm of ridge width vs 1.14 to 2.5 mm at grafted and/or membrane sites; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.

P2340.t: The Effects of Alveolar Ridge Preservation: A Meta‐Analysis
P2340.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2340.kf: Review and meta-analysis (64 studies qualitative, 18 quantitative): ridge preservation retained about 1.31 to 1.54 mm more bucco-oral width and 0.91 to 1.12 mm more height than unassisted healing, while vital bone differences were inconclusive.

P2341.t: The Pontic-Shield: Partial Extraction Therapy for Ridge Preservation and Pontic Site Development
P2341.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P2341.kf: Retrospective case series of 10 patients (14 partial extraction sites) showing how a modification of the socket-shield technique (pontic-shield) can develop pontic sites and preserve the ridge.

P2343.t: A decade of the socket-shield technique: a step-by-step partial extraction therapy protocol
P2343.j: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P2343.kf: Technique article presenting a reproducible step-by-step socket-shield protocol (specifications, instrumentation, procedures) for immediate implant placement and provisionalization in single-rooted teeth.

P2348.t: Postextraction Dental Implant in the Aesthetic Zone, Socket Shield Technique Versus Conventional Protocol
P2348.kf: RCT comparing socket-shield vs conventional immediate implants with immediate loading in the aesthetic zone: implant survival was 100% in both groups at 3 years, with better marginal bone values for socket-shield implants.

P2351.t: Current Evidence on the Socket-Shield Technique: A Systematic Review
P2351.kf: Systematic review of 23 studies on the socket-shield technique (mostly case reports; 18 with ≤12 months follow-up): complications occurred in 82.86% of implants in animal studies and 24.26% in clinical studies, mainly buccal/crestal bone loss.

P2352.t: Partial Extraction Therapies (PET) Part 1: Maintaining Alveolar Ridge Contour at Pontic and Immediate Implant Sites
P2352.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P2352.kf: Narrative review introducing the term partial extraction therapies (PET) - root submergence, socket-shield and pontic shield techniques that retain part of the tooth root to preserve the alveolar ridge - with a classification and guide to their application.

P2353.kf: Prospective study of a modified socket shield technique with immediate single implants and crowns: 30 patients, 40 implants, 1-year follow-up. All implants survived (100%), mean ISQ was 72.9 at placement and 74.6 at 1 year, no biologic complications occurred and prosthetic complications were 2.5%.

P2364.t: Importance of keratinized mucosa around dental implants: Consensus report of group 1 of the DGI/SEPA/Osteology Workshop
P2364.kf: DGI/SEPA/Osteology consensus based on two systematic reviews: reduced keratinized peri-implant mucosa width is associated with more biofilm, inflammation, discomfort, recession, marginal bone loss and peri-implantitis; data on mucositis incidence are inconsistent.

P2370.t: Minimal invasiveness in the transcrestal elevation of the maxillary sinus floor: A systematic review
P2370.kf: Systematic review of controlled clinical trials (19 articles, 15 studies) on reducing invasiveness of transcrestal sinus floor elevation; powered instruments reduced invasiveness versus manual osteotomes and mallet without affecting clinical effectiveness.

P2371.t: Soft Tissue Management Around Implants in the Esthetic Zone
P2371.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P2371.kf: Technique report with four illustrative cases (follow-up 1 to 4 years) on overbuilding the implant site in the esthetic zone using orthodontic extrusion, bone and connective tissue grafting, guided soft tissue augmentation and punch uncovering. The author concludes enhanced sites can be molded to an ideal gingival …

P2373.t: The influence of thin as compared to thick peri-implant soft tissues on aesthetic outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2373.kf: Meta-analysis of 34 studies (1508 patients, 1606 sites): final PES did not differ between thin (<2 mm) and thick soft tissues (MD 0.15), but thick tissues favoured PES change, papilla presence, less recession (-0.62 mm) and patient satisfaction.

P2375.t: Use of a cross-mounting buccal index to help transfer the spatial relationships of an interim prosthesis to the definitive implant-supported prosthesis
P2375.kf: Technique report describing a cross-mounting buccal index that uses a duplicate of the accepted interim restoration to select abutments and fabricate the framework of an implant-supported prosthesis without a new denture setup. The authors state it reduces chair and laboratory time and gives predictable prosthodontic …

P2379.t: To Splint or Not to Splint: The Current Status of Periodontal Splinting
P2379.j: Journal of the International Academy of Periodontology
P2379.kf: Narrative overview of periodontal splinting covering splint types, classification, indications, contraindications, rationale and effects on oral health, noting improved materials have reduced ill effects such as poor hygiene.

P2381.t: Effect of Splinting Mini-Implants on Marginal Bone Loss: A Biomechanical Model and Clinical Randomized Study with Mandibular Overdentures
P2381.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2381.kf: FEA plus RCT in 45 edentulous patients (90 immediately loaded mini-implants) retaining mandibular overdentures: unsplinted mini-implants showed higher bone stress (-118 vs -56.8 MPa) and a trend to greater 2-year bone loss (1.43 vs 0.92 mm) with more vertical bone loss.

P2383.t: Circumferential bone loss around splinted and nonsplinted immediately loaded implants retaining mandibular overdentures: A randomized controlled clinical trial using cone beam computed tomography
P2383.kf: RCT of 30 edentulous patients with 2 immediately loaded implants for mandibular overdentures (ball vs bar): at 3 years CBCT vertical bone loss was 1.36 mm with ball vs 1.0 mm with bar (significant), horizontal loss did not differ; survival 93.3% vs 100%.

P2384.t: Split-Mouth Comparison of Splinted and Nonsplinted Prostheses on Short Implants: 3-Year Results
P2384.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2384.kf: Randomized split-mouth study in 18 patients (82 short implants, 6-11 mm); at 3 years (15 patients) bone levels did not differ between splinted and nonsplinted implants >6 mm, while all screw loosening (5 patients) occurred on nonsplinted sides, mostly 6-mm implants.

P2389.t: The effect of implant‐abutment junction position on crestal bone loss: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
P2389.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2389.kf: Meta-analysis of controlled clinical trials (14 articles reviewed, 12 pooled) on apico-coronal implant position: in bone level implants, equi- vs subcrestal placement showed no significant crestal bone loss difference (WMD 0.15 mm early, 0.03 mm late), while supra- vs equicrestal favoured supracrestal (WMD -0.64 mm).

P2390.t: The prevalence of peri‐implant diseases around subcrestally placed implants: A cross‐sectional study
P2390.kf: Cross-sectional study of 200 patients with 657 subcrestally placed implants (median function 9.36 years): patient-level prevalence of peri-implant mucositis was 66.5% and peri-implantitis 15.0%; peri-implantitis was associated with history of periodontitis (OR 5.33).

P2400.t: Which dental implant surface is more effective in osteointegration: RBM surface versus SLA surface
P2400.j: Annals of Clinical and Analytical Medicine
P2400.kf: Clinical comparison of SLA versus RBM-surface implants of the same brand and design (4793 implants, 2005 patients): success was 96.06% for RBM and 96.53% for SLA, with no significant difference in osseointegration success.

P2401.t: On osseointegration in relation to implant surfaces
P2401.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2401.kf: Narrative review introducing a supplement on implant surfaces: osseointegration is redefined as a foreign-body protective reaction, and surfaces are characterized by micro/nanoroughness, chemistry and physical parameters, with moderately rough surfaces reported to show improved clinical results.

P2404.t: Implant surface roughness and bone healing: a systematic review
P2404.kf: Systematic review of animal studies (14 articles in the final selection from 5966 abstracts): almost all showed increased bone-to-implant contact with increasing surface roughness, and push-out strength was significantly related to roughness, though studies were too heterogeneous for pooled inference.

P2406.t: Histomorphometric analysis of the bone-implant contact obtained with 4 different implant surface treatments placed side by side in the dog mandible
P2406.j: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
P2406.kf: Dog study (5 animals) of 4 implant surfaces after 90 days unloaded: bone-implant contact was 41.7% machined, 48.9% TPS, 57.9% HA and 68.5% SBM; only SBM vs machined was statistically significant.

P2410.t: Implant surfaces beyond micron roughness. Experimental and clinical knowledge of surface topography and surface chemistry
P2410.kf: Narrative review of experimental and clinical evidence on implant surface topography and chemistry. Authors conclude moderately rough surfaces give the strongest bone response but randomized clinical studies found no significant differences versus minimally rough implants; nanotopography effects remain unproven, and …

P2413.t: Benchmark performance of anodized vs. sandblasted implant surfaces in an acute dehiscence type defect animal model
P2413.kf: Minipig acute buccal dehiscence model (2 and 8 weeks): moderately rough sandblasted acid-etched implants produced significantly more de novo crestal bone and higher osseointegration at 8 weeks than a gradient anodized implant; early nBIC was influenced by implant geometry.

P2414.t: A comparison of endosseous dental implant surfaces
P2414.kf: Review of human clinical reports with meta-analyses by surface type: high success was achievable with smooth, rough and HA-coated implants, but when clustered by indication, rough surfaces had significantly higher success except in single-tooth replacement; mandibular implants generally succeeded more than maxillary.

P2415.t: Immediately loaded machined versus rough surface dental implants in edentulous jaws: One-year postloading results of a pilot randomised controlled trial
P2415.kf: Pilot RCT of 50 edentulous patients with immediately loaded cross-arch prostheses on rough vs machined implants: 1 year after loading no prosthesis failed, two machined implants failed in one patient, and bone loss was -0.64 vs -0.68 mm (no significant difference).

P2416.t: Predicting osseointegration by means of implant primary stability
P2416.kf: Clinical study of 36 patients (63 immediately loaded, 43 delayed-loaded ITI implants) with RFA: RFA was not reliable to identify mobile implants, but stability was reliably determined at ISQ ≥47; all DL implants with ISQi ≥49 and IL implants with ISQi ≥54 osseointegrated at 1 year.

P2417.t: Surface characteristics of dental implants: A review
P2417.kf: Narrative review of implant surface roughness, wettability and surface energy: roughness parameters are candidate predictors of tissue response, and hydrophilic surfaces improve initial blood contact and wound healing, accelerating osseointegration.

P2419.t: Influence of implant surfaces on osseointegration
