P2419.kf: Literature review of in vitro and in vivo studies on micro- and nano-scale implant surface topographies and biomimetic molecule incorporation (e.g., peptides, BMPs) and their effects on bone formation and remodeling.

P2422.t: Principles and practice of periodontal microsurgery
P2422.kf: Brief review of periodontal microsurgery basics: magnification and instruments, hand positions, knot tying, clinical applications and esthetic effects, emphasizing passive wound closure and reduced tissue trauma.

P2426.t: Comparison of temperature increase in the pulp chamber during the polymerization of materials used for the direct fabrication of provisional restorations
P2426.kf: In vitro test of 5 direct provisional resins on a prepared molar: all were exothermic; mean pulp-chamber temperature during crown fabrication ranged from 37.76 °C (polyvinylethyl methacrylate) to 39.40 °C (polymethyl methacrylate), with PMMA highest for fabrication and reline.

P2432.t: Transitional custom abutments: optimizing aesthetic treatment in implant-supported restorations
P2432.kf: Technique report introducing transitional custom abutments: composite-modified temporary cylinders progressively adjusted intraorally to sculpt supraimplant tissue and emergence profile, illustrated with two cases. The author states the technique can compensate for compromised implant position or angulation and …

P2433.t: Treatment of peri-implant recession with a screw-retained, interim implant restoration: A clinical report
P2433.kf: Clinical report of a maxillary lateral incisor implant with recession exposing a zirconia abutment after an unsuccessful connective tissue graft; an undercontoured screw-retained interim restoration allowed coronal soft tissue migration and resolved the deficiency.

P2435.t: A systematic review of the influence of the implant‐abutment connection on the clinical outcomes of ceramic and metal implant abutments supporting fixed implant reconstructions
P2435.kf: Systematic review of 60 studies (≥3-year follow-up): estimated 5-year survival was 97.6% (SCs) and 97.0% (FDPs) with internal connections vs 95.7% and 95.8% with external connections; 5-year abutment failure ranged from 0.7% to 2.8% across connections.

P2436.t: The effect of zirconia or titanium as abutment material on soft peri‐implant tissues: a systematic review and meta‐analysis
P2436.kf: Systematic review of 9 studies (4 RCTs, 5 CCTs) directly comparing zirconia and titanium abutments: meta-analysis was feasible only for soft tissue color, which was significantly superior for zirconia; other outcomes showed no significant differences.

P2438.t: Osseointegration of dental implants in extraction sockets preserved with porous titanium granules – an experimental study
P2438.kf: Animal study in three minipigs: extraction sockets preserved with porous titanium granules (PTG, n=12), heat-oxidized white PTG (n=12) or left empty (sham, n=6), implants placed after 11 weeks. Bone-to-implant contact was 68.2% (PTG), 36.6% (white PTG) and 60.9% (sham), not significant; apical bone defects occurred in …

P2446.t: Outcomes of treatment and monitoring of posterior teeth with cracks: three-year results from the National Dental Practice-Based Research Network
P2446.kf: Practice-based network study of 2,858 patients with a cracked posterior tooth followed 3 years by 209 dentists: tooth survival exceeded 98% (37 extractions), restorative treatment failure was 14%, and about 80% of monitored teeth stayed on monitoring.

P2447.t: Accuracy of three digital workflows for implant abutment and crown fabrication using a digital measuring technique
P2447.kf: In vitro comparison of three digital workflows for implant custom abutments and zirconia crowns: all had mean marginal gaps below 120 μm; the full digital Atlantis workflow had significantly smaller marginal gaps, while the 3Shape split-file workflow had smaller internal fit.

P2448.t: A randomized controlled clinical trial comparing the use of displacement cords and aluminum chloride paste
P2448.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2448.kf: Split-mouth trial in 10 participants (4 maxillary premolars each) comparing aluminum chloride paste and displacement cord: mean displacement was 0.241 mm (paste) vs 0.282 mm (cord), with the paste gap 0.041 mm smaller (P = .014).

P2449.t: Comparative research of the subgingival impression quality by fixed prosthesis using one and double cord retraction technique
P2449.j: Journal of IMAB - Annual Proceeding (Scientific Papers)
P2449.kf: Clinical comparison of subgingival impression quality: 30 impressions (103 abutments) with one retraction cord versus 30 impressions (222 abutments) with double cord, rated by 10 technicians. Poor ratings were 41.7% with one cord versus 3.6% with two cords; the author concludes double-cord technique gives more …

P2451.t: Computer-aided evaluation of preparations for CAD/CAM-fabricated all-ceramic crowns
P2451.kf: Digital analysis of 75 upper first molar preparations for zirconia crowns by general practitioners: mean convergence angle was 26.7°, interocclusal reduction was insufficient in over 30%, and no preparation fulfilled all recommendations.

P2454.t: Gingival Retraction Methods: A Systematic Review
P2454.kf: Systematic review of 10 clinical/experimental studies (400 teeth) on gingival retraction methods: chemomechanical retraction was most common, results were heterogeneous, and no method was significantly superior for retraction achieved or clinical parameters.

P2455.t: Gingival Retraction Methods for Fabrication of Fixed Partial Denture: Literature Review
P2455.kf: Literature review of conventional and modern gingival retraction techniques for tooth- and implant-supported fixed prostheses, classifying them as mechanical, chemical or surgical.

P2459.t: Influence of preparation design on fracture resistance of different monolithic zirconia crowns: A comparative study
P2459.kf: In vitro study of 40 extracted premolars with monolithic traditional or translucent zirconia crowns: fracture resistance was highest for traditional zirconia with shoulder margin (2.903 kN) and lowest for translucent zirconia with feather-edge (1.523 kN).

P2461.t: Influence of the Gingival Condition on the Performance of Different Gingival Displacement Methods—A Randomized Clinical Study
P2461.kf: Randomized split-mouth cross-over study in 40 probands comparing double cord vs aluminum chloride kaolin paste displacement in healthy gingiva and induced mild gingivitis: gingivitis worsened sulcus representation with cords but not paste; marginal gingiva height changes were not clinically relevant.

P2463.t: Efficiency of Cordless Versus Cord Techniques of Gingival Retraction: A Systematic Review
P2463.kf: Systematic review of 7 in vivo studies comparing cord and cordless retraction: three of four studies on hemostasis (epigingival finish lines) found paste more efficient for bleeding control, while evidence on sulcus dilatation was contrasting.

P2464.t: Interaction between enamel, porcelain and a gold alloy: an in vitro wear study
P2464.j: The University of Adelaide, School of Dentistry

P2465.t: Advances in dental veneers: materials, applications, and techniques
P2465.kf: Literature review of ceramic and adhesive materials, applications and techniques for porcelain laminate veneers, focusing on parameters determining long-term success, correct application and clinical limitations.

P2466.t: Advances in materials and concepts in fixed prosthodontics: a selection of possible treatment modalities
P2466.kf: Overview of advances in fixed prosthodontics - adhesive techniques, translucent restorative materials, new polymers and CAD/CAM ceramics - with support for material selection from single-tooth restorations to fixed dental prostheses.

P2467.t: Aesthetic Rehabilitation of a Patient with Bruxism Using Ceramic Veneers and Overlays Combined with Four-Point Monolithic Zirconia Crowns for Occlusal Stabilization: A 4-Year Follow-Up
P2467.kf: Case report of a 66-year-old man with bruxism and tooth wear rehabilitated at increased vertical dimension with lithium disilicate veneers and overlays plus four-point monolithic zirconia crowns on canines and first molars; no complications after 4 years.

P2468.t: Treatment of Tooth Wear Using Direct or Indirect Restorations: A Systematic Review of Clinical Studies
P2468.kf: Systematic review of 16 clinical studies (minimum 6 months, up to 10 years) on direct and indirect restorations for extensive tooth wear, including metal-ceramic, gold, lithium disilicate, zirconia, PICN and composite; heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis.

P2469.t: Clinical performance of occlusal onlays made of lithium disilicate ceramic in patients with severe tooth wear up to 11 years
P2469.kf: Prospective non-randomized study of 7 patients with severe tooth wear restored with 103 bonded monolithic lithium disilicate occlusal onlays (up to 11 years, median 94.9 months): 100% survival, 3.9% marginal discoloration and 1% marginal crack, with no debonding or secondary caries.

P2470.t: Tooth wear: A systematic review of treatment options
P2470.kf: Systematic review (2003-2013) of minimally invasive treatments for generalized tooth wear analysing diagnostic waxing, occlusal positioning, vertical dimension increase, restoration and follow-up; composite resin and glass ceramic were each used definitively in 6 studies.

P2471.t: Occlusal onlays as a modern treatment concept for the reconstruction of severely worn occlusal surfaces
P2471.kf: Article describing principles of minimally invasive, defect-oriented treatment of severely worn occlusal surfaces with occlusal onlays, guided by a diagnostic wax-up and new preparation designs to preserve tooth structure.

P2472.t: The management of anterior tooth wear using gold palatal veneers in canine guidance
P2472.kf: Technique report with two clinical cases: localized anterior tooth wear managed with gold palatal veneers on maxillary canines (canine guidance) plus direct composite restorations, using the Dahl concept with a 5-6 mm bite increase. Posterior dento-alveolar compensation occurred within 18 weeks with a mutually …

P2475.t: Accuracy of mechanical torque-limiting devices for dental implants
P2475.kf: In vitro test of new mechanical torque-limiting devices from 6 implant manufacturers (5 per manufacturer, 10 measurements each): friction-style and spring-style devices did not differ in accuracy, and all delivered within ±10% of the target torque.

P2477.t: The Effects of High Insertion Torque Versus Low Insertion Torque on Marginal Bone Resorption and Implant Failure Rates
P2477.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 human and 6 quasi-randomized animal studies (591 implants): high vs low insertion torque showed no significant differences in bone resorption (human ES 0.13), implant failure (human RR 0.39, 95% CI 0.01-20.77) or BIC.

P2478.t: Clinical effect of the high insertion torque on dental implants: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2478.kf: Meta-analysis of 6 studies (389 patients, 651 implants): high insertion torque (≥50 Ncm) vs regular/low torque showed no significant difference in implant survival (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.06-4.06) or marginal bone loss (MD 0.15 mm).

P2481.t: Clinical Outcome of Dental Implants Placed with High Insertion Torques (Up to 176 Ncm)
P2481.j: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
P2481.kf: Prospective study of 48 patients with 66 tapered implants: 42 placed at maximum insertion torque >70 Ncm (mean 110.6, up to 176 Ncm) vs 9 at 30-50 Ncm; after 2-3 months of non-submerged healing all implants were clinically stable.

P2484.t: Inflammation and Trauma from Occlusion, Co-Destructive Factors in Chronic Periodontal Disease
P2484.kf: Conceptual (expert) article, drawing on animal and human histologic findings, proposing that inflammation and trauma from occlusion are co-destructive in the supporting periodontal tissues. The author concludes trauma from occlusion does not cause gingival inflammation or pockets, but combines with inflammation to …

P2485.t: The angular bone defect and its relationship to trauma from occlusion and downgrowth of subgingival plaque
P2485.kf: Post-mortem study of 64 human jaw sets (106 interdental spaces): attachment and crestal bone loss were related to apical downgrowth of subgingival plaque, angular defects occurred equally adjacent to traumatized and non-traumatized teeth, and infrabony pockets were always associated with plaque downgrowth.

P2487.t: Biologically guided implant therapy: A diagnostic and therapeutic strategy of conservation and preservation based on periodontal staging and grading
P2487.kf: Conceptual paper proposing that the new AAP/EFP periodontitis staging and grading system guide implant treatment planning, prioritizing maximal tooth conservation and alveolar bone preservation over restoratively driven rationale.

P2492.t: Masticatory function following implants replacing a second molar
P2492.kf: Pre-post study of 20 patients with a single second molar implant: masticatory performance rose from 67.8% to 84.3% after prosthesis insertion (P<0.0001), efficiency index increased 29%, and over 90% were functionally satisfied.

P2499.t: Periodontal regeneration versus extraction and dental implant or prosthetic replacement of teeth severely compromised by attachment loss to the apex: A randomized controlled clinical trial reporting 10-year outcomes, survival analysis and mean cumulative cost of recurrence
P2499.kf: 10-year RCT of 50 stage III/IV periodontitis patients with a tooth with attachment loss to or beyond the apex: survival was 88% with periodontal regeneration vs 100% with extraction and replacement, complication-free survival did not differ, and regeneration costs were significantly lower.

P2501.t: Strategic considerations in treatment planning: deciding when to treat, extract, or replace a questionable tooth
P2501.kf: Literature review (MEDLINE 1966-2009) of factors in deciding whether to maintain or extract and replace a questionable tooth; maintenance is suitable when the tooth is not extensively diseased, strategically valuable, in an intact arch, or when gingival preservation is paramount.

P2502.t: The ultimate guide to restoration longevity in England and Wales. Part 10: key findings from a ten million restoration dataset
P2502.kf: Analysis of 13,896,048 restorations from GDS claims in England and Wales (1990-2006): 32-42% survived to 15 years without re-intervention and 77.8-84.2% of restored teeth survived to extraction; larger restorations performed worse.

P2503.t: The ultimate guide to restoration longevity in England and Wales. Part 9: incisor teeth: restoration time to next intervention and to extraction of the restored tooth
P2503.kf: Analysis of 2,526,576 incisor restorations from GDS claims data (1990-2006): at 15 years, 35% survived without re-intervention and 81% of restored incisors survived without extraction.

P2516.t: Minimal invasiveness in vertical ridge augmentation
P2516.kf: Review of recent strategies to reduce invasiveness and complications in vertical ridge augmentation, covering treatment planning, surgical techniques, digital tools such as customized titanium meshes or blocks, and tissue engineering trends.

P2522.t: EMG evaluation of masseter muscle during maximum clenching in complete denture wearers after reducing the occlusal vertical dimension
P2522.j: International Journal of Applied Dental Sciences
P2522.kf: Within-subject study of 7 complete denture wearers using dentures at appropriate OVD and then at OVD reduced by about 3 mm: mean masseter EMG during maximum clenching was 435.35 uV vs 299.25 uV, a significant difference.

P2523.t: Changing Vertical Dimension: A Solution or Problem?
P2523.kf: Article explaining principles that make changes in vertical dimension of occlusion advantageous and predictable, and exposing misconceptions that lead to missed diagnoses, failures and unnecessary overtreatment.

P2524.t: Effect of occlusal vertical dimension on lip positions at smile
P2524.kf: Study of 30 dental students photographed at OVD +0 to +8 mm: increasing OVD significantly increased interlabial gap height, incisal edge-to-lower lip distance and display zone, and decreased smile index; smile width and upper lip distance did not change.

P2526.t: Effect Of Occlusal Splints At Different Vertical Dimensions On The Condylar Position and Muscle Activity In Worn Out Dentition - An In Vivo Study
P2526.j: International Journal of Dentistry and Oral Science
P2526.kf: Randomized crossover study of patients with moderate-severe attrition (four groups, n=10) using canine-to-canine or full-arch splints at 1 or 4 mm: masseter EMG fell from 263.10 μV to 134.7-147.15 μV with all splints (p<.001), with no significant change in condylar position.

P2528.t: A Literature Review of Vertical Dimension in Prosthodontics Theory and Practice - Part 1: Theoretical Foundations
P2528.kf: Literature review of the theoretical foundations of vertical dimension in prosthodontics, including its definition, measurement, relation to TMDs, and impact on lower facial proportions and aesthetics.

P2529.t: Full mouth rehabilitation of the patient with severely worn dentition: a case report
P2529.kf: Case report of a 77-year-old woman with severe wear, loss of anterior guidance and reduced vertical dimension, treated with an occlusal overlay splint to confirm a new VDO before interim and definitive fixed reconstruction, with satisfactory esthetic and functional results.

P2530.t: Increased Vertical Dimension of Occlusion: Signs, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment and Options
P2530.j: The Journal of Contemporary Dental Practice
P2530.kf: Narrative discussion of signs and symptoms of increased VDO (joint and muscle pain, speech and swallowing difficulty, tooth sensitivity, abnormal wear, elongated face) and treatment options including selective occlusal adjustment, orthodontic intrusion or orthognathic surgery.

P2531.t: The effect of increasing vertical dimension of occlusion on facial aesthetics
P2531.kf: Questionnaire survey of 96 general-practice patients whose OVD had been increased (72% response): 79.7% of respondents said they looked younger, and a panel of five judges rated 81.2% of reviewed patients as looking younger from before/after photographs.

P2533.t: Increasing vertical dimension: considerations and steps in reconstruction of the severely worn dentition
P2533.kf: Technique report with one illustrative case describing a chairside protocol to increase vertical dimension in severely worn dentition (composite stops on maxillary molars, then staged restoration). The author states a systematic approach can facilitate a successful, predictable outcome; opening 1 mm posteriorly gives …

P2534.t: Relationship of occlusal vertical dimension to the health of the masticatory system
P2534.kf: Review noting that earlier evidence on OVD changes and masticatory disorders came from case reports and uncontrolled studies; human and animal research shows good possibility of adaptation if increases are not extreme and the appliance covers most of the dentition.

P2537.t: Vertical dimension of occlusion: the keys to decision
P2537.j: international journal of stomatology & occlusion medicine
P2537.kf: Article proposing an optimal adaptive range rather than a single point for VDO, with a decision-making table relating overjet, overbite, prosthetic space, mandibular morphology, profile and skeletal type.

P2538.t: Potential for tooth fracture in restorative dentistry
P2538.kf: Article on tooth fracture risk in restorative dentistry describing fiber-optic transillumination and a predisposition index for evaluating fracture potential, especially in older patients.

P2542.t: Prospective clinical evaluation of mandibular implant overdentures: Part I--Retention, stability, and tissue response
P2542.kf: Prospective crossover study of 17 complete denture wearers given two anterior mandibular implants: implant overdentures were statistically superior to conventional dentures, O-ring attachments outperformed magnets for retention and stability, and soft tissue response improved slightly but significantly.

P2543.t: Is there a correlation between vestibular depth and shrinkage of free gingival graft: A descriptive-correlational study
P2543.kf: Descriptive-correlational study of 19 analysed patients receiving free gingival grafts for insufficient attached gingiva: at 6 months attached and keratinized gingiva width rose to 6.15 mm and 7.55 mm (p <0.001); the abstract is truncated before shrinkage and correlation results.

P2551.t: A method of transferring the subgingival contour of interim restorations to definitive restorations by using zirconia copings customized with casting wax
P2551.kf: Dental technique report (single illustrated case, 3-year view) describing how to transfer the adjusted subgingival contour of an interim crown or fixed partial denture to the definitive restoration using a zirconia coping or framework customized with casting wax. The authors state symmetrical gingival contours may be …

P2552.t: Adhesion to Zirconia: A Systematic Review of Current Conditioning Methods and Bonding Materials
P2552.kf: Systematic review of 86 publications (2013-2018; in vitro, clinical and one systematic review) on zirconia bonding: airborne-particle abrasion and tribochemical silica coating have the most evidence, physico-chemical conditioning increases adhesion, and contamination reduces it.

P2553.t: Adhesion to Zirconia Used for Dental Restorations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P2553.kf: Systematic review of 52 in vitro studies on bonding to zirconia: bond strength was significantly influenced by surface conditioning, cement type, test method and aging; after physical conditioning MDP-based cements gave the highest values (e.g., 34.2 MPa macrotensile without thermocycling).

P2558.t: Clinical Performance of All-Ceramic Dental Restorations
P2558.kf: Review of clinical performance of all-ceramic restorations: established silica-based and oxide-based ceramics show high long-term success on teeth and implants, while silica-based ceramics depend on resin bonding and have limited indications.

P2559.t: Clinical performance of monolithic zirconia crowns on titanium–zirconium reduced-diameter implants in the molar area: Interim data at three years of a randomized controlled trial
P2559.kf: RCT of 76 patients with 3.3 mm titanium-zirconium tissue-level implants for single molar crowns (monolithic zirconia vs PFM): at 3 years (59 patients) 14 implants were lost (11 fractures, 3 aseptic losses), giving 80% estimated survival; chipping occurred only with PFM.

P2563.t: Comparison of sandblasted, ground and melt-etched zirconia crowns regarding adhesion strength to resin cement
P2563.kf: In vitro tensile test of zirconia crowns (n = 6 per group) cemented with resin cement: adhesion strength was 5.2 MPa sandblasted, 7.3 MPa ground and 9.8 MPa after melt-etching with potassium hydrogen difluoride, all significantly different.

P2566.t: Early bond strength to low-pressure sandblasted zirconia: evaluation of a self-adhesive cement
P2566.j: The European Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
P2566.kf: In vitro shear bond test of self-adhesive resin cement on 30 sintered zirconia cylinders: low-pressure (1 bar) and standard (2.8 bar) air abrasion gave 16.01 and 16.24 MPa without significant difference, both better than untreated controls, but caused scratches and microcracks.

P2567.t: Effect of an internal coating technique on tensile bond strengths of resin cements to zirconia ceramics
P2567.kf: In vitro study of alumina-abraded zirconia with or without an internal coating of fused silica-based ceramic: silanization significantly improved tensile bond strength of Panavia F 2.0 and Superbond C&B to silica-based ceramic and to the internally coated zirconia.

P2568.t: Effect of framework design on crown failure
P2568.kf: In vitro load-to-failure study of premolar PFM and In-Ceram alumina crowns with standard or modified framework designs: design modification increased characteristic strength for both, and PFM groups were stronger than alumina groups, with modified PFM strongest.

P2569.t: Effect of Marginal Designs on Fracture Strength of High Translucency Monolithic Zirconia Crowns
P2569.kf: In vitro test of 90 high-translucency monolithic zirconia crowns: heavy chamfer margins had higher fracture loads (4226-4486 N) than light chamfer (2913-3211 N), while collar height had no significant effect.

P2571.t: Effect of Sandblasting Angle and Distance on Biaxial Flexural Strength of Zirconia-based Ceramics
P2571.j: The Journal of Contemporary Dental Practice
P2571.kf: In vitro study of 50 zirconia discs sandblasted with 110 μm alumina at 15 or 25 mm and 45° or 90°: biaxial flexural strength did not differ among groups (p = 0.40), but surface roughness differed significantly, highest at 15 mm/90° (0.51 μm).

P2573.t: Effect of simulated mastication on the surface roughness of three ceramic systems
P2573.kf: 3-body wear simulation (50,000 cycles) against enamel of 72 zirconia, lithium disilicate and feldspathic porcelain specimens with rough, smooth or glazed finishes: smooth porcelain became significantly rougher, and rough lithium disilicate became smoother.

P2574.t: Effect of Sintering on the Marginal and Internal Fit of CAD/CAM-fabricated Zirconia Frameworks
P2574.kf: In vitro study of KATANA CAD/CAM zirconia copings and 3-, 4- and 5-unit frameworks: marginal and internal fit of 3- and 4-unit frameworks was within clinical acceptance, with slightly larger gaps on the pontic side; the 5-unit framework had better marginal fit due to the central abutment.

P2575.t: Effect of thickness and surface modifications on flexural strength of monolithic zirconia
P2575.kf: In vitro test of monolithic zirconia discs at 1.3 and 0.8 mm (n = 7 per subgroup): 1.3 mm discs had significantly higher flexural strength, airborne-particle abrasion increased strength, and grinding followed by polishing did not affect it.

P2579.t: Effects of sandblasting distance and angles on resin cement bonding to zirconia and titanium
P2579.j: International Journal of Adhesion and Adhesives
P2579.kf: In vitro study of zirconia and titanium sandblasted at 5-15 mm and 45-90° before silane and RelyX Unicem bonding: angle significantly affected shear bond strength (75° best, not significantly different from 90°), while distance did not.

P2583.t: Fracture resistance of three porcelain-layered CAD/CAM zirconia frame designs
P2583.kf: In vitro test of 30 extracted premolars with porcelain-veneered zirconia crowns of three frame designs: anatomically guided frames resisted 1721.6 N vs 1004.6 N (PFM-like) and 1179.5 N (flat), a significant difference.

P2587.t: In vitro evaluation of shear bond strengths of resin to densely-sintered high-purity zirconium-oxide ceramic after long-term storage and thermal cycling
P2587.kf: In vitro study of 80 air-abraded Procera AllZirkon specimens: after 180-day storage and 12,000 thermal cycles, groups pretreated with a phosphate-monomer bonding/silane agent kept 15.45-16.85 MPa vs 9.45 MPa (Panavia alone) and 1.08 MPa (Single Bond/Ceramic Primer); aging reduced all bonds.

P2589.t: Influence of surface treatment on the wear of solid zirconia
P2589.kf: Pin-on-disk wear test of 50 Lava zirconia plates with five surface treatments against steatite: zirconia wear was <1 μm in most groups, antagonist wear was 81-85 μm for several treatments, and polished zirconia produced the smallest antagonist wear.

P2592.t: Manufacturing accuracy and volumetric changes of stereolithography additively manufactured zirconia with different porosities
P2592.kf: In vitro study of SLA additively manufactured zirconia bars (n = 20 per group) at 0%, 20% and 40% porosity: 40% porosity gave the highest accuracy and lowest volume change, changes were greatest in the z-axis, and volumetric changes ranged from -20.33% to +3.5%.

P2594.t: Monolithic Zirconia: An Update to Current Knowledge. Optical Properties, Wear, and Clinical Performance
P2594.kf: Review of monolithic zirconia: new ultra-translucent and multicolor zirconia has translucency reported as similar to more translucent lithium disilicate, causes minimal antagonist wear when polished, and short-term clinical studies up to 5-7 years show promising survival.

P2596.t: Monolithic Zirconia Partial Coverage Restorations: An In Vitro Mastication Simulation Study
P2596.kf: In vitro mastication simulation (1.2 million cycles) of 32 premolars with bonded monolithic 3Y-zirconia crowns, onlays and overlays using the APC protocol: no fractures occurred, one MODF onlay debonded, and MODF specimens showed marginal integrity issues at antagonist contact.

P2597.t: Outcome of bonded vs all-ceramic and metal-ceramic fixed prostheses for single tooth replacement
P2597.kf: Literature review (258 articles) comparing FDPs for single-tooth replacement: metal-ceramic FDPs show the highest survival, all-ceramic may be comparable with more chipping, resin-bonded FDPs do better anteriorly and as cantilevers, and inlay-retained/fiber-reinforced FDPs have compromised prognosis.

P2598.t: Pre-sintered Y-TZP sandblasting: effect on surface roughness, phase transformation, and Y-TZP/veneer bond strength
P2598.kf: In vitro study of Y-TZP sandblasted before or after sintering: veneer shear bond strength was 9.73 MPa post-sintering and 7.94 MPa pre-sintering vs 5.54 MPa untreated; pre-sintering sandblasting gave much rougher surfaces (Ra 1.59 μm) and more defects without higher bond strength.

P2599.t: Prospective Clinical Study of Zirconia-Based Posterior Four-Unit Fixed Dental Prostheses: Four-Year Follow-up
P2599.kf: Prospective study of 10 patients with 17 zirconia-based posterior four-unit FDPs over 4 years: three were lost to distal connector fractures (mean 25.3 months), chipping occurred in several, and cumulative survival was 76.5%.

P2602.t: Reliability and properties of core materials for all-ceramic dental restorations
P2602.kf: Review of zirconia as an all-ceramic core material, covering zirconia/alumina nanocomposites, low-temperature degradation, effects of sandblasting and heat treatment, bonding to porcelain and cement, translucency, biocompatibility and clinical survival.

P2603.t: Revolution of Current Dental Zirconia: A Comprehensive Review
P2603.kf: Comprehensive literature review (PubMed/Embase to October 2021) of dental zirconia types, properties, applications and cementation: new monolithic translucent zirconia shows enhanced esthetics and promising high survival, and cementation materials and methods have improved.

P2605.t: Influence of yttria content and surface treatment on the strength of translucent zirconia materials
P2605.kf: In vitro study of 160 discs of four translucent 4Y and 5Y zirconias with four surface treatments: 4Y was stronger than all 5Y materials regardless of treatment; alumina abrasion slightly strengthened 4Y but weakened 5Y, and 4Y had about 5% less transmittance.

P2606.t: A systematic review of the survival and complication rates of all‐ceramic and metal–ceramic reconstructions after an observation period of at least 3 years. Part II: fixed dental prostheses.
P2606.kf: Systematic review of cohort studies (≥3-year follow-up) estimating 5-year survival and complications of all-ceramic FDPs versus metal-ceramic FDPs using Poisson regression; nine all-ceramic FDP studies met inclusion criteria. The abstract is truncated before survival estimates.

P2608.t: All-ceramic or metal-ceramic tooth-supported fixed dental prostheses (FDPs)? A systematic review of the survival and complication rates. Part I: Single crowns (SCs)
P2608.kf: Systematic review of 67 studies (4663 metal-ceramic, 9434 all-ceramic single crowns): 5-year survival was 94.7% for metal-ceramic, similar to reinforced glass-ceramic (96.6%), alumina and zirconia crowns (92.1%), while feldspathic/silica-based crowns survived less; zirconia had more veneer fractures and retention loss.

P2612.t: A comparison of bond strength of layered veneering porcelains to zirconia and metal
P2612.kf: In vitro shear bond test of five veneering porcelains fired to Katana zirconia (n = 8): bond strengths ranged 22.0-30.9 MPa, with CER and EMX significantly lower than CZR; failures were cohesive in porcelain, and strong thermal expansion mismatch significantly affected bonding.

P2615.t: Comparative reliability analyses of zirconium oxide and lithium disilicate restorations in vitro and in vivo
P2615.j: The Journal of the American Dental Association
P2615.kf: Combined analyses: lithium disilicate crowns had the highest step-stress fatigue load-to-failure in vitro, 4-year clinical performance comparable to zirconia-based crowns at 7 years, and a randomized trial component showed wear resistance and enamel-friendly antagonist wear.

P2617.t: Surface roughness of zirconia for full-contour crowns after clinically simulated grinding and polishing
P2617.kf: In vitro study of 30 zirconia bars (glazed full-contour vs veneered and glazed) after simulated grinding and polishing: full-contour zirconia had significantly lower roughness, and fine-polished full-contour zirconia was not significantly different from glazed.

P2618.t: Survival and complications of monolithic ceramic for tooth-supported fixed dental prostheses: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2618.kf: Meta-analysis of 18 studies (1061 monolithic crowns, 104 FPDs): pooled biological and technical complication rates for single crowns were 1% and 2%; in 5 direct comparisons, monolithic and veneered restorations did not differ in survival (RR 0.68) or complications.

P2619.t: Effect of Thickness of Zirconia Ceramic on Its Masking Ability: An In Vitro Study
P2619.kf: In vitro study of 90 zirconia discs (0.4-2 mm) on white and black substrates: mean ΔE fell from 13.0 at 0.4 mm to 5.0 at 1 mm and 1.5 at 2 mm, compared with clinical (ΔE 5.5) and ideal (ΔE 2.6) thresholds.

P2620.t: Clinical evaluation of monolithic zirconia crowns for posterior teeth restorations
P2620.kf: Clinical study of 46 patients (49 posterior monolithic zirconia crowns) followed up to 96 weeks: marginal adaptation was rated excellent in all, CDA parameters did not change significantly over time, one antagonist crack occurred, and antagonist wear did not differ over time.

P2621.t: Resin cementation of zirconia ceramics with different bonding agents
P2621.kf: In vitro shear test of 35 zirconia specimens bonded with Variolink II after five pretreatments: sandblasting plus MDP-containing primers (Monobond Plus, Z-Prime Plus) gave the highest bond strengths and untreated controls the lowest (24-hour storage).

P2622.t: The effect of grinding on the mechanical behavior of Y-TZP ceramics: A systematic review and meta-analyses
P2622.j: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials/Journal of mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
P2622.kf: Systematic review of 30 laboratory studies (20 meta-analysed): grinding significantly decreased flexural strength and increased roughness of Y-TZP versus as-sintered, with effects varying by grinding tool, grit size and cooling; heterogeneity was high.

P2632.t: Translucency of IPS e.max and cubic zirconia monolithic crowns
P2632.kf: In vitro study of 80 monolithic molar crowns: translucency ranked UT1.0 > ST1.0 > UT1.5 > lithium disilicate 1.5 mm, with both cubic zirconias significantly more translucent than low-translucency lithium disilicate even at 1.5 mm.

P2636.t: Is there a potential for durable adhesion to zirconia restorations? A systematic review
P2636.kf: Systematic review of 134 publications (1998-2014, mainly in vitro with some clinical studies) on adhesion to zirconia: airborne-particle abrasion and tribochemical silica coating are reference pretreatments, adhesive monomers are needed for chemical bonding, and contamination and aging impair adhesion.

P2639.t: Fracture resistance of different metal substructure designs for implant-supported porcelain-fused-to-metal (PFM) crowns
P2639.kf: In vitro study of 18 implant-supported PFM crowns (6 per group) with three metal substructure designs after 300,000 loading cycles: fracture resistance was 111.13 ± 27.15 kg (minimum thickness), 236.13 ± 39.21 kg (conventional) and 188.63 ± 12.10 kg (wrinkled) (P<0.05). The conventional design performed best; the …

P2644.t: Analysis of tooth preparations for zirconia-based crowns and fixed dental prostheses using stereolithography data sets
P2644.kf: Retrospective digital analysis of 182 zirconia frameworks (305 abutments) prepared by German general practitioners: only 13 teeth (4.3%) met preparation requirements; mean total occlusal convergence was 17.9°, highest in molars (23.2°), and 92.5% had non-ideal finish lines.

P2646.t: Fracture resistance of a selection of full-contour all-ceramic crowns: an in vitro study
P2646.kf: In vitro axial load-to-fracture test of monolithic maxillary molar crowns of zirconia, lithium disilicate or feldspar ceramic: zirconia crowns had the highest fracture resistance independent of adhesive or conventional fixation.

P2649.t: Optical Properties and Microstructure of Nanocrystalline Cubic Zirconia Prepared by High-Pressure Spark Plasma Sintering
P2649.kf: Materials study of transparent 8 mol% yttria cubic zirconia made by high-pressure spark plasma sintering: oxygen vacancies and residual pores were the main defects, oxidizing annealing improved transparency, and fine pores scattered light.

P2654.kf: Narrative review of current and next-generation dental zirconias, describing efforts to increase translucency (less light-scattering alumina, added cubic phase) while preserving strength and toughness, plus refined powders, dopants, sintering protocols and surface treatments.

P2656.t: Zirconia Posterior Fixed Partial Dentures: A Prospective Clinical 3-year Follow-up
P2656.kf: Prospective trial of 30 patients with 3-/4-unit posterior zirconia-framework FPDs; 27 examined at mean 34.2 months showed 100% framework survival, one major chip, 96.3% cumulative success and no significant periodontal differences versus control teeth.

P2668.t: Recent advances in dental zirconia: 15 years of material and processing evolution
P2668.kf: Review of 15 years of dental zirconia research (Web of Science search returning 5102 articles in 31 topic groups): translucency is improved by lowering alumina and raising yttria (4Y-, 5Y-, >5 mol% PSZ with >50% cubic phase), at the cost of mechanical properties.

P2669.t: Translucent Zirconia in Fixed Prosthodontics-An Integrative Overview
P2669.kf: Integrative review of translucent zirconia (3Y-, 4Y-, 5Y-TZP) in fixed prosthodontics, covering light-conducting properties, strength trade-offs versus opaque zirconia, adhesive strategies and implant-supported restorations.

P2672.t: Development and characterization of ultra-high translucent zirconia using new manufacturing technology
P2672.kf: Review of ultra-high translucent zirconia (UHTZ) made with 'Cyclic CIP' and 'Plus Y Technology': despite extremely high translucency its flexural strength is reported comparable to 5Y, with improved milling chipping resistance, chemical durability and less opposing-tooth wear.

P2673.kf: In vitro comparison (n=20 for translucency and edge chipping) of Katana UTML, Lava Esthetic, Lava Plus 3Y-TZP and IPS e.max Press: edge toughness was 304, 394, 717 and 354 N/mm respectively; Katana UTML translucency was similar to lithium disilicate.

P2674.t: Effect of Sintering Time on The Marginal and Internal Fit of Monolithic Zirconia Crowns Containing 3-4 Mol% Y2O3
P2674.kf: In vitro preprint: 60 monolithic zirconia crowns (3Y-TZP generations 1 and 2, and 4Y-TZP) sintered with a long (about 7 hours) or speed (about 2 hours) protocol. All marginal gaps were clinically acceptable (<120 µm); speed sintering did not change marginal fit of 3Y-TZP but significantly increased marginal gap in …

P2677.t: Impact of High-Speed Sintering on Accuracy and Fit of 4 mol% Yttria-Stabilized Tetragonal Zirconia Polycrystals
P2677.kf: In vitro study of 108 4Y-TZP single-unit, three-unit and cantilever three-unit FDPs (n=12 per subgroup): high-speed sintered multilayer three-unit FDPs showed poorer accuracy than conventionally sintered ones (P ≤ .001 to .008), but fit effects were not clinically relevant.

P2682.t: Classification and Properties of Dental Zirconia as Implant Fixtures and Superstructures
P2682.kf: Review classifying dental zirconia for implant fixtures and superstructures into 12 types; higher yttria content gives higher translucency and lower strength, and mirror-polished zirconia rarely wears antagonist teeth and shows less bacterial adhesion.

P2683.t: Mechanical Properties of Translucent Zirconia: An In Vitro Study
P2683.kf: In vitro study of 23 specimens: high-translucent Y-TZP had flexural strength 427 (±59.5) MPa and fracture toughness 4.9 (±0.9) MPa.m1/2 versus 805 (±198.4) MPa and 8.9 (±1.1) MPa.m1/2 for low-translucent Y-TZP; aged high-translucent specimens reached 440 MPa.

P2684.t: Mechanical Properties of New Generations of Monolithic, Multi-Layered Zirconia
P2684.kf: In vitro 3-point bending of Katana HTML, STML and UTML multilayer zirconia (15 specimens per group, four layers, three thicknesses): HTML had significantly higher flexural strength and fracture toughness than STML and UTML, with no significant differences between layers or thicknesses.

P2685.t: Multilayer Super-Translucent Zirconia for Chairside Fabrication of a Monolithic Posterior Crown
P2685.kf: Case report of chairside CEREC fabrication of a monolithic posterior crown from multilayer super-translucent 4Y-TZP zirconia using superfast dry-milling and speed-sintering, within 60-75 min.

P2686.t: New high-translucent cubic-phase–containing zirconia: Clinical and laboratory considerations and the effect of air abrasion on strength
P2686.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P2686.kf: Laboratory pilot article on cubic-phase-containing translucent zirconia: five translucent and two traditional zirconias (N=5 each) were tested for flexural strength after 2-bar and 4-bar alumina air abrasion. Traditional zirconia did not lose significant strength, whereas translucent zirconias showed significant …

P2688.t: Structural investigations on the tetragonal to cubic phase transformations in zirconia induced by progressive yttrium additions
P2688.j: Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids
P2688.kf: Laboratory materials-science study of sol-gel yttria-zirconia powders with 5 to 100 wt.% Y3+ (XRD, Raman, Rietveld refinement). Yttrium additions beyond 20 wt.% stabilized only the cubic phase, tetragonal-stabilized compositions underwent tetragonal-to-monoclinic transition at 1500 °C, and cubic-stabilized …

P2689.t: Survey of the mechanical and physical behaviors of yttria-stabilized zirconia from multiple dental laboratories
P2689.kf: Double-blinded laboratory survey: 9 dental laboratories supplied 32 specimens from 17 zirconia blanks; 'posterior' zirconia strengths ranged 195–783 MPa, overlapping 'anterior' 320–768 MPa, while grouped by yttria content strengths were 584 (158) MPa for 3 mol% and 373 (104) MPa for 5 mol%.

P2691.t: Translucency of recent zirconia materials and material-related variables affecting their translucency: a systematic review and meta-analysis
P2691.kf: Systematic review of 53 in vitro studies (2010–2023): changing yttria content significantly affected zirconia translucency, and zirconias of the same generation varied, influenced by additives, point defects, microstructure, thickness, phase distribution and sintering conditions.

P2697.t: Clinical efficacy of methods for bonding to zirconia: A systematic review
P2697.kf: Systematic review of 8 clinical studies (>12 months) of bonded zirconia restorations: posterior inlay-retained FPDs had estimated survival of 12.1% at 10 years, 95.8% at 5 years and 100% at 20 months; anterior resin-bonded FPDs had 100% 3- to 10-year survival, with debonds in all studies.

P2699.t: Effect of ethyl cellulose coating as an evaluation agent against contamination on the bond strength of zirconia restorations: An in vitro study
P2699.kf: In vitro study of 72 4Y-TZP blocks: precoating with ethyl cellulose before saliva contamination, then removal with ethanol in an ultrasonic bath, gave significantly higher shear bond strength than other cleaning methods (P<.05), with surfaces similar to uncontaminated controls.

P2700.t: Effect of hydrofluoric acid concentration and etching duration on select surface roughness parameters for zirconia
P2700.kf: In vitro study of 100 zirconia disks: 40% HF significantly increased surface roughness (P<.01), 9.5% HF only after 15 minutes, and 5% HF produced no significant difference (P>.05).

P2707.t: Influence of Material and Technique on Occlusal Chipping of All-Ceramic Molar Crowns
P2707.j: University of Toronto (MSc thesis, Graduate Department of Restorative Dentistry)
P2707.kf: In vitro thesis study of 50 molar crowns on epoxy replicas (n=10/group) under 500,000-cycle fatigue loading: all monolithic CAD/CAM lithium disilicate and CAD-on crowns survived, while all PFM and hand-layered or heat-pressed veneered zirconia crowns failed (P<.001).

P2708.t: Influence of surface treatment on veneering porcelain shear bond strength to zirconia after cyclic loading
P2708.j: Indiana University School of Dentistry (MSD thesis, Department of Prosthodontics)
P2708.kf: In vitro master's thesis: 48 zirconia specimens (12 per group) with four surface treatments (control, heat treatment, airborne-particle abrasion, abrasion plus heat) bonded to veneering porcelain, half subjected to cyclic loading. Shear bond strength was not significantly affected by surface treatment; abrasion …

P2720.t: XRD2 micro-diffraction analysis of the interface between Y-TZP and veneering porcelain: Role of application methods
P2720.kf: XRD2 micro-diffraction of Y-TZP–veneering porcelain interfaces showed both monoclinic and tetragonal zirconia grains under almost all conditions, indicating destabilization of the tetragonal phase at the interface during veneering.

P2725.t: Cleaning Methods for Zirconia Following Salivary Contamination
P2725.kf: In vitro shear bond study of saliva-contaminated, particle-abraded zirconia (n=10 per group, 10,000 thermocycles): with contamination after MDP priming, water rinsing preserved bond strength; with contamination before MDP, particle abrasion or Ivoclean preserved it.

P2726.t: Durable bonding to mechanically and/or chemically pre-treated dental zirconia
P2726.kf: In vitro micro-tensile bond study (n=15-21/group) of two composite cements to IPS e.max ZirCAD after ageing up to 6 months: tribochemical silica sandblasting plus silane/MDP primer with Panavia F2.0 performed best, and sandblasting was indispensable for Panavia F2.0.

P2729.t: Efficacy of various cleaning solutions on saliva-contaminated zirconia for improved resin bonding
P2729.kf: In vitro study of saliva-contaminated air-abraded zirconia (28 disks, 5,000 thermocycles): Ivoclean and sodium hypochlorite cleaning gave shear bond strengths similar to uncontaminated and re-air-abraded groups (P>.05), whereas SDS and hydrogen peroxide did not.

P2734.t: MDP Salts: A New Bonding Strategy for Zirconia
P2734.kf: In vitro study of alumina-blasted zirconia: MDP-salt primer showed the highest tensile bond strength before and after thermocycling compared with MDP and MDP+silane (P < 0.05), with no difference in surface roughness.

P2735.t: Meta-analysis of bonding effectiveness to zirconia ceramics
P2735.kf: Meta-analysis of 1,371 zirconia bond-strength tests from 144 papers: combined mechanical and chemical pretreatment was crucial for durable bonding, cement choice was not determining after aging when composite cement was used, and macro-shear tests gave lower, less discriminative values.

P2738.t: Clinical esthetic comparison between monolithic high-translucency multilayer zirconia and traditional veneered zirconia for single implant restoration in maxillary esthetic areas: Prosthetic and patient-centered outcomes
P2738.kf: Clinical comparison in 30 participants each with monolithic high-translucency multilayer and veneered zirconia single implant crowns in maxillary esthetic areas: patient VAS did not differ (9.0 vs 9.0, P > 0.05), but professional WES was lower for monolithic crowns (7.5 vs 8.0, P < 0.05).

P2739.t: Effect of Yttria Content on the Translucency and Masking Ability of Yttria-Stabilized Tetragonal Zirconia Polycrystal
P2739.kf: In vitro comparison of Katana HT (3Y), STML (4Y), UTML (5Y) and lithium disilicate at 0.8 and 1.5 mm: translucency rose with yttria content but stayed below lithium disilicate; all zirconias masked normal dentin and titanium at 1.5 mm, none masked severely discolored dentin.

P2741.t: Masking ability of indirect restorative systems on tooth-colored resin substrates
P2741.kf: In vitro study (n = 5) of five indirect restorative systems cemented on ND3, ND8 and ND9 resin substrates: only layered zirconia (IPS e.max ZirCAD + IPS e.max Ceram) kept color differences below the acceptability threshold, and it had the lowest translucency.

P2742.t: Masking Ability of Monolithic and Layered Zirconia Crowns on Discolored Substrates
P2742.kf: In vitro colorimetric study of monolithic, bi-layer and tri-layer 3Y-TZP anterior crowns over eleven substrates: monolithic crowns had better masking ability than layered crowns, and masking was lowest on ND9 and metal substrates.

P2743.t: Optical and Mechanical Properties of Highly Translucent Dental Zirconia
P2743.kf: In vitro study of 1-mm specimens of five monolithic zirconias, two glass-ceramics and bovine teeth: 5 mol% yttria significantly improved translucency but remained below lithium disilicate; alumina below 0.05 wt.% enhanced translucency, and 0.05 wt.% Fe increased chroma without compromising mechanical properties.

P2744.t: Substrate masking ability of bilayer and monolithic ceramics used for complete crowns and the effect of association with an opaque resin-based luting agent
P2744.kf: In vitro study of eleven ceramic systems (n=10) over discolored resin and metal substrates: zirconia groups showed lower ΔE and translucency; monolithic groups had significantly higher ΔE than bilayers, reaching acceptability only with an opaque luting agent over shade A3.5.

P2750.t: Crystal growth behavior and phase stability of rare earth oxides (4 mol.% GdO1.5-4 mol.% SmO1.5) doped zirconia nanopowders
P2750.j: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
P2750.kf: Laboratory study of co-precipitated 4 mol.% GdO1.5–4 mol.% SmO1.5 doped zirconia nanopowders: they stayed single metastable tetragonal phase from 873 K to 1273 K, crystallite size rose from 11.98 to 18.90 nm, and annealed powders were phase-stable at 1573 K for 100 h.

P2751.t: Does air particle abrasion affect the flexural strength and phase transformation of Y-TZP? A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2751.kf: Systematic review of 44 in vitro studies (21 in meta-analysis): airborne-particle abrasion improved Y-TZP flexural strength regardless of abrasion parameters and aging (p≤0.05); after aging for 12h or more, abraded Y-TZP showed less monoclinic content than controls.

P2756.t: Influence of elapsed time between airborne-particle abrasion and bonding to zirconia bond strength
P2756.kf: In vitro study of 140 zirconia discs bonded 15 min to 72 h after 50-μm alumina abrasion: surface free energy fell significantly within 24 h, and tensile bond strength after 150 days with thermocycling ranged from 38.3 MPa (15 min) to 24.8 MPa (24 h).

P2765.t: Alternative framework designs for zirconia-ceramic crowns
P2765.kf: CAD/CAM design study using a replicated prepared maxillary first molar die, showing three alternative zirconia framework designs that the system software can create to support veneering porcelain.

P2766.t: Clinical Chipping of Zirconia All-Ceramic Restorations
P2766.kf: Narrative review of porcelain chipping on zirconia all-ceramic restorations: reported veneer porcelain fracture ranged from 0.9 to 29.1% in clinical reports from 2010 to 2013. Authors conclude chipping is a clinical challenge linked to occlusal factors, cooling rate after firing and excessive porcelain thickness from …

P2767.t: Effect of core design and veneering technique on damage and reliability of Y-TZP-supported crowns
P2767.kf: In vitro mouth-motion step-stress fatigue study of 84 veneered Y-TZP molar crowns: hand-layered conventional cores had higher reliability (0.99) than press-veneered (0.50); anatomic core design increased reliability for both (PM9 0.98, VM9 1.00) and reduced chip size.

P2768.t: Effect of frame design on the fracture strength of a zirconia crown and porcelain-faced crown
P2768.kf: Laboratory study of zirconia and porcelain-faced crowns: fracture strengths were 645.9 MPa with Frame Design 1, 759.5 MPa with Frame Design 2 and 989.7 MPa with Frame Design 3.

P2777.t: The effect of zirconia framework design on the failure of all-ceramic crown under static loading
P2777.kf: In vitro static loading of 20 premolar zirconia crowns: cutback anatomic framework design failed at 1,450.4 ± 175.7 N versus 1,170.1 ± 90.9 N for 0.5 mm even thickness (P<.05); even-thickness crowns failed cohesively in porcelain, cutback crowns mostly through the framework.

P2778.t: The influence of zirconia coping designs on the fracture load of all-ceramic molar crowns
P2778.kf: In vitro study of four zirconia coping designs for molar crowns under vertical and lateral loading: the conventional uniform-thickness coping showed the lowest fracture load, and the coping following cuspal configuration for even porcelain thickness showed the highest.

P2783.t: Flexural Strength and Morphological Study of Different Multilayer Zirconia Dental Materials
P2783.kf: In vitro study of three multilayer translucent Y-TZP zirconias (ZirCAD Prime, Cercon ht ML, Katana YML) using three-point bending of 2 × 2 × 16 mm bars. Mean flexural strength was 879.42 ± 107.36 MPa for ZirCAD Prime versus 701.63 ± 84.21 and 644.73 ± 82.07 MPa for the other two (significantly lower).

P2784.t: Flexural Strength of Two Multilayered and Monochromatic High Yttria Containing Zirconia Materials Following Different Sintering Parameters
P2784.kf: In vitro study of 300 monochrome and multilayer 5Y-PSZ specimens (n=15/group) sintered at 1,450–1,550°C for 10–135 minutes: the highest flexural strengths were 315.81 ± 18.91 MPa and 335.21 ± 36.18 MPa, with no significant difference between monochrome and multilayer material.

P2785.kf: Narrative biomaterials update on gradient multilayered zirconia (monophase and multiphase 3Y, 4Y and 5Y-TZP) with one anterior case at 6 months. Authors conclude multiphase multilayered zirconia is the first material combining different crystal phases in one body to mimic enamel and dentin, but further investigation …

P2788.t: Multilayer zirconia: Influence of positioning within blank and sintering conditions on the in vitro performance of 3-unit fixed partial dentures
P2788.kf: In vitro study of 3-unit ZirCAD Prime FPDs milled at three blank positions with varied sintering times: all survived thermocycling and mechanical loading, and fracture forces (1002 ±446 N to 1760 ±607 N) showed no significant overall group differences (P=.059).

P2789.t: New multi-layered zirconias: Composition, microstructure and translucency
P2789.kf: In vitro characterization of Katana UTML, STML and ML: UTML was 5Y-PSZ with ˜75 wt% cubic content, STML 4Y-PSZ with ˜65 wt% and ML 3Y-PSZ with <50 wt%; layers differed only in pigments, UTML and STML had similar translucency superior to ML, and only ML showed monoclinic phase after aging.

P2813.t: Enamel wear against monolithic zirconia restorations: A meta-analysis and systematic review of in vitro studies
P2813.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2813.kf: Systematic review of 25 in vitro articles (3 in meta-analysis): enamel wear against monolithic zirconia was within the statistically accepted level, and polished zirconia caused less enamel wear than glazed surfaces.

P2818.t: Two-body wear of monolithic, veneered and glazed zirconia and their corresponding enamel antagonists
P2818.kf: In vitro chewing-simulator study (N = 36, up to 1,200,000 cycles): polished monolithic zirconia caused the least enamel antagonist wear (27.3 ± 15.2 and 28 ± 11.1 μm) and glaze-ceramic zirconia the most (118 ± 30.9 μm), but 100% of polished-zirconia antagonists developed enamel cracks.

P2826.t: In-vitro performance and fracture strength of thin monolithic zirconia crowns
P2826.kf: In vitro study of 0.2 mm and 0.5 mm monolithic zirconia crowns (n=32 each), adhesively bonded or zinc phosphate cemented, under thermal cycling and mechanical loading: all 0.5 mm crowns survived, while four 0.2 mm adhesive crowns and all 0.2 mm cemented crowns failed.

P2827.t: Comparison of Chamfer and Deep Chamfer Preparation Designs on the Fracture Resistance of Zirconia Core Restorations
P2827.j: Journal of Dental Research, Dental Clinics, Dental Prospects
P2827.kf: In vitro study of 0.4 mm Cercon zirconia cores on epoxy dies (10 per group): deep chamfer margins had mean fracture resistance of 1426.10±182.60 N versus 991.75±112.00 N for chamfer, a statistically significant difference.

P2831.t: Effect of Preparation Design on the Fracture Resistance of Zirconia Crown Copings
P2831.kf: In vitro study of 0.4 mm zirconia copings (10 per design) on CrCo molar dies with five preparation designs: mean breaking load was 2286 N for shoulder, 2041 N shoulderless, 1752 N pronounced deep chamfer, 1722 N beveled shoulder and 1624 N slight chamfer (p < 0.01).

P2832.t: Evaluation of diamond rotary instruments marketed for removing zirconia restorations
P2832.kf: In vitro comparison of two zirconia-marketed diamond instruments and a conventional diamond on 3Y-TZP and 4Y-TZP: cutting times were 85 seconds (conventional), 100 seconds and 182 seconds, and higher load raised tip temperature (2 N: 24.6 °C, 6 N: 36.7 °C).

P2836.t: A retrospective analysis of 102 zirconia single crowns with knife-edge margins
P2836.kf: Retrospective private-practice evaluation of 102 feldspathic porcelain veneered-zirconia crowns on knife-edge margins (51 anterior, 51 posterior), mean follow-up 20.9 months: one tooth extracted for an unrelated endodontic problem, 2 minor veneer chippings and no zirconia core fractures.

P2841.t: Chemical Bonding to Novel Translucent Zirconias: A Mechanical and Molecular Investigation
P2841.kf: In vitro study of a 10-MDP cement (Panavia F 2.0) with 3Y-, 4Y- and 5Y-TZP: PO32- peaks persisted after thermocycling, and shear bond strengths were approximately 20 MPa after water storage and approximately 6 MPa after thermocycling, with no differences between translucent zirconias and control.

P2847.t: Influence of cement type and ceramic primer on retention of polymer-infiltrated ceramic crowns to a one-piece zirconia implant
P2847.kf: In vitro study of 100 Vita Enamic crowns on one-piece zirconia implants with various cements (n=5): MDP-containing cements showed higher retention, highest for Panavia 21 (605 ±82 N) and Panavia F 2.0 (318 ±28 N), versus Ketac Cem (196 ±34 N) and Temp Bond (127 ±13 N).

P2849.t: Long-term resin bonding to zirconia ceramic with a new universal primer
P2849.kf: In vitro study of 96 e.max ZirCAD disks: after 150 days and 37,500 thermal cycles tensile bond strength fell with conventional silane (e.g., 38.3 to 11.3 MPa) but not with the universal primer on silica-coated surfaces (44 to 36 MPa).

P2850.t: Bonding effectiveness to different chemically pre-treated dental zirconia
P2850.kf: In vitro micro-tensile study of CoJet-sandblasted IPS e.max ZirCAD with four primers/adhesives: Clearfil Ceramic Primer and Monobond Plus gave significantly higher bond strength than Scotchbond Universal and Z-PRIME Plus, and Clearfil Ceramic Primer was most stable after ageing.

P2852.t: Influence of surface treatment of contaminated zirconia on surface free energy and resin cement bonding
P2852.kf: In vitro study of saliva-contaminated air-abraded IPS e.max ZirCAD cleaned with water, phosphoric acid, Ivoclean or additional air abrasion: water and Ivoclean groups had significantly lower surface free energy, and additional air abrasion increased both surface free energy and resin bond strength.

P2854.t: Influence of cleaning methods on resin bonding to saliva‐contaminated zirconia
P2854.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2854.kf: In vitro study of saliva-contaminated alumina-blasted zirconia with two resin cements: AD Gel and additional alumina-blasting gave bond strengths not significantly different from uncontaminated controls before and after thermocycling, whereas water rinsing, phosphoric acid and Ivoclean did not give durable bonding.

P2857.t: Clinical and radiographic outcomes of zirconia dental implants—A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2857.kf: Systematic review of 6 observational cohort studies of commercial zirconia implants (mean follow-up ≥60 months): meta-analyses estimated 97.2% survival (277 implants, 221 patients), 1.1 mm marginal bone loss and 3.0 mm probing depth after 5 years of loading.

P2859.t: A 5-year randomized controlled trial comparing zirconia-based versus metal-based implant-supported single-tooth restorations in the premolar region
P2859.kf: RCT in 30 patients (63 premolar implants) comparing all-ceramic crowns on zirconia abutments with metal-ceramic crowns on metal abutments over 5 years: implant survival 100%, restoration survival 100% vs 97%, similar bone loss (p = .056), but better marginal adaptation for metal-ceramic (p = .025).

P2863.t: Designing abutments for cement retained implant supported restorations
P2863.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) on designing abutments for cement-retained implant restorations. The authors conclude no abutment meets all ideal criteria; custom abutments with the cement margin following the mucosal outline are preferred over stock abutments, gold cast to machined cylinders is the most …

P2866.t: The role of orthodontics in implant dentistry
P2866.kf: Narrative article explaining that orthodontic correction of tipped, drifted or over-erupted teeth aids prosthetic replacement, and that osseointegrated implants can provide additional anchorage in partially edentulous patients and later support restorations.

P2867.t: An interdisciplinary approach to treatment planning in implant dentistry
P2867.kf: Narrative article (BDJ implant series) with three illustrative cases on an interdisciplinary team approach to implant treatment planning, combining orthodontics, grafting, surgery and prosthodontics. The authors conclude that without an interdisciplinary approach final outcomes can be compromised, and a team approach …

P2868.t: Factors that affect individual tooth prognosis and choices in contemporary treatment planning
P2868.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) of factors affecting individual tooth prognosis versus extraction and implant replacement. The authors conclude prognosis of periodontally involved teeth is unreliable, implant replacement appears more predictable than surgical periodontal and endodontic techniques in their …

P2869.t: Treatment planning of implants in posterior quadrants
P2869.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) on treatment planning of implants in posterior quadrants: space, implant number and position, occlusion, prosthesis type and overall plan. The authors conclude implants are the treatment of choice for missing posterior teeth, and the authors prefer splinting multiple posterior …

P2870.t: Treatment planning of implants in the aesthetic zone
P2870.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) on treatment planning of implants in the aesthetic zone. The authors state aesthetic predictability depends on tissue loss at treatment start, hard and soft tissue deficiencies must be addressed before placement, recreating papilla between adjacent implants is not predictable, and …

P2871.t: Surgical guidelines for dental implant placement
P2871.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) of surgical guidelines for implant placement. The author states placement must be both biologically and restoratively driven, implants should only be placed after comprehensive examination and accurate diagnosis, and a deficient osseous ridge must be reconstructed before placement.

P2872.t: Immediate implant placement: treatment planning and surgical steps for successful outcomes
P2872.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) of immediate implant placement. The author concludes multi-centre studies have validated the predictability of placing implants at extraction when appropriately planned; bone substitutes next to small defects appear safe but do not predictably promote osseointegration, and …

P2873.t: Treatment planning of the edentulous maxilla
P2873.kf: Narrative review with illustrative cases (BDJ implant series) comparing fixed and removable implant prostheses for the edentulous maxilla. The authors state the number of implants depends on bone quality, anticipated force and arch form, and that removable restorations require more maintenance than fixed ones.

P2874.t: Treatment planning of the edentulous mandible
P2874.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) of treatment planning for the edentulous mandible. The authors conclude there are three main choices: a two-implant retained overdenture (cheapest initially but needing more maintenance), a hybrid fixed prosthesis, or metal-ceramic fixed units; fixed options give higher patient …

P2876.t: Screw versus cemented implant supported restorations
P2876.kf: Narrative review (BDJ implant series) comparing screw-retained and cemented implant restorations across aesthetics, retrievability, retention, passivity, provisionals, occlusion, immediate loading and planning. The authors conclude there is no clear advantage of one retention type over the other, but state a …

P2877.t: Influence of Liquid on the Tooth Surface on the Accuracy of Intraoral Scanners: An In Vitro Study
P2877.kf: In vitro study scanning a mandibular model 10 times per condition with Trios 3 and Primescan: wet tooth surfaces gave significantly higher RMS deviations than dry and blow-dry conditions (p < 0.001), with no difference between water and artificial saliva.

P2878.t: Interproximal Open Contacts Between Implant Restorations and Adjacent Teeth. Prevalence – Causes – Possible Solutions
P2878.kf: Literature review identifying 7 studies with a high prevalence of interproximal contact loss between implant prostheses and adjacent teeth: 18% to 66% in the maxilla and 37% to 54% in the mandible, more often mesially and as early as 3 months.

P2879.t: Direct composite resin fillings versus amalgam fillings for permanent posterior teeth
P2879.kf: Cochrane review of 8 RCTs; pooled parallel-group trials (921 children; 1645 composite and 1365 amalgam restorations) gave low-certainty evidence that composite had almost double the failure risk (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.52 to 2.35) and higher secondary caries risk (RR 2.14), but not more fractures (RR 0.87).

P2880.t: Failure Risk of Composite Resin and Amalgam Restorations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P2880.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 studies: failure proportions ranged from 0% to 50.0% for amalgam and 0% to 62.7% for composite resin, with no statistically significant difference in failure risk (RR: 0.96, 95% CI 0.68-1.34).

P2881.t: International consensus on the assessment of bruxism: Report of a work in progress
P2881.kf: International consensus update defining sleep and awake bruxism as masticatory muscle activities and concluding that, in otherwise healthy individuals, bruxism is a behaviour that can be a risk and/or protective factor rather than a disorder, assessable by self-report and electromyography.

P2882.t: Basic Erosive Wear Examination (BEWE): a new scoring system for scientific and clinical needs
P2882.kf: Describes the Basic Erosive Wear Examination (BEWE): the most severely affected surface in each sextant is scored on a four-level scale, and the cumulative score is classified into risk levels that guide management.

P2883.t: Recommendations and guidelines for dentists using the basic erosive wear examination index (BEWE)
P2883.kf: Guidance paper explaining how to screen tooth wear in general practice with the BEWE index, noting UK stakeholders acknowledged it can be recorded at the same time as the Basic Periodontal Examination, with examples for each BEWE score.

P2884.t: Survival Rate of Resin and Ceramic Inlays, Onlays, and Overlays: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
P2884.kf: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 clinical studies with >5 y follow-up: glass-ceramic and feldspathic inlays, onlays and overlays had estimated survival of 92% to 95% at 5 y (n = 5,811) and 91% at 10 y (n = 2,154); fractures/chipping (4%) were the most frequent failure.

P2885.t: Survival and Complications of Partial Coverage Restorations on Posterior Teeth—A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P2885.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2885.kf: Systematic review of 6 RCTs of posterior partial coverage restorations: 3-year survival was 89.3% for resin matrix ceramic and 93.7% for lithium disilicate, leucite-reinforced glass ceramic 96.1% to 98.3%, with no statistically significant differences between materials at 1-3 years.

P2886.t: Wear in Antagonist Teeth Produced by Monolithic Zirconia Crowns: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P2886.kf: Systematic review of 8 clinical studies (4 meta-analyzed): mean maximum antagonist wear against monolithic zirconia crowns was 95.45 μm, increasing by an estimated 6.13 μm per month, while the crowns themselves showed 58.47 μm mean maximum wear.

P2887.t: Comparative Wear of Opposing Natural Enamel by Different Ceramic Materials in Fixed Dental Protheses: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P2887.kf: Meta-analysis of 9 clinical studies (5 RCTs, 4 prospective; 203 patients; 6 to 24 months): monolithic zirconia (MD −1.32) and lithium disilicate (MD −0.45) caused significant opposing enamel wear, whereas feldspathic-veneered metal-ceramic did not (p = 0.06).

P2888.t: Mechanical behavior of endocrown vs. post-and-crown: a systematic review and meta-regression analysis
P2888.kf: Systematic review with meta-regression of 25 in vitro studies: load-to-fracture did not differ significantly between endocrowns and post-and-crown restorations; resin composite luting increased and oblique loading reduced load-to-fracture (p<0.05).

P2889.t: Large Language Model Influence on Diagnostic Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Trial
P2889.kf: Single-blind RCT of 50 physicians reviewing up to 6 clinical vignettes: median diagnostic-reasoning score was 76% with GPT-4 access versus 74% with conventional resources only (adjusted difference 2 percentage points; P=.60); the LLM alone scored 16 percentage points higher (P=.03).

P2890.t: Immediate Dentin Sealing: A Fundamental Procedure for Indirect Bonded Restorations
P2890.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2890.kf: Review of more than 30 articles on dentin bonding for indirect restorations recommending immediate dentin sealing (applying and polymerizing the bonding agent on freshly cut dentin before impression), which appears to improve bond strength and reduce gaps, bacterial leakage and dentin sensitivity.

P2891.t: Changes in Implant Surface Characteristics and Wettability Induced by Smoking In Vitro: A Preliminary Investigation
P2891.kf: In vitro study of five implant disk types (Ti-Mach, Ti-SLA, Ti-Alloy, Zirc-1, Zirc-2) exposed to simulated occasional or heavy tobacco smoking: smoke changed surface chemistry and wettability, improving hydrophilicity of titanium surfaces but worsening that of ceramic surfaces.

P2892.t: Smoking and Dental Implants: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
P2892.kf: Meta-analysis of 292 publications (35,511 implants in smokers, 114,597 in non-smokers): smokers had higher implant failure risk (OR 2.402, p < 0.001), significant in both maxilla and mandible, and greater marginal bone loss (MD 0.580 mm).

P2893.t: Smoking in relation to early dental implant failure: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2893.kf: Meta-analysis of 32 observational studies (59,246 implants; 14,115 patients): smoking was associated with early implant failure at implant level (OR 2.59, 95% CI 2.08–3.23) and individual level (OR 2.00), with higher maxillary risk (OR 5.90).

P2894.t: Comparative Influence of Marginal Design and Digital Scanning Accuracy on the Clinical Longevity of Ceramic Restorations: An Evidence-Based Approach. Consensus Statement From SSRD, SEPES, and PROSEC Conference on Minimally Invasive Restorations
P2894.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2894.kf: خط تراش افقی و عمودی از نظر بقا، موفقیت و سلامت پریودنتال تفاوت معناداری ندارند؛ اسکنر داخل دهانی برای اینله و آنله تک‌واحدی قابل‌اعتماد است اما شواهد آن برای ونیر ناکافی است.

P2895.t: Clinical survival and complication rate of ceramic veneers bonded to different substrates: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2895.kf: ونیرهای سرامیکی باندشده به انامل بالاترین بقا و موفقیت (هر دو ۹۹٪) را دارند؛ باند به کامپوزیت رزینی موجود موفقیت را تا ۷۰٪ و باند به دنتین با اکسپوژر شدید بقا را تا ۹۱٪ و موفقیت را تا ۷۴٪ کاهش می‌دهد.

P2897.t: The all-on-four treatment concept: Systematic review
P2897.j: Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry
P2897.kf: Systematic review of 24 studies of the all-on-four concept with at least three years in function: survival for more than 24 months was 99.8%, and biological complications such as peri-implantitis were reported in few patients after a mean two years.

P2898.t: Protocol for Removal of Clinically Relevant Contaminants from Glass Ceramic-based Restorations
P2898.kf: Expert working instruction (IAAD) summarizing in vitro literature on cleaning contaminated glass-ceramic bonding surfaces. Water, alcohol and acetone do not remove saliva; 35-37% phosphoric acid gel (30-60 s) or particulate cleaning paste (20 s) removes saliva or blood, while silicone residues require hydrofluoric …

P2899.t: The Esthetic Width in Fixed Prosthodontics
P2899.kf: Narrative proposing an 'esthetic width' approach for porcelain-fused-to-metal restorations, based on the biologic width: positioning preparation margins, reducing the metal framework and adapting marginal design, plus pontic and interdental designs, to avoid the gray 'umbrella effect'.

P2900.t: The Influence of Ferrule Design and Pulpal Extensions on the Accuracy of Fit and the Fracture Resistance of Zirconia-Reinforced Lithium Silicate Endocrowns
P2900.kf: In vitro study of 60 extracted maxillary molars with ZLS endocrowns (n = 10 per group): endocrowns without ferrule had higher fracture strength than 1 mm ferrule designs (p < 0.05) regardless of inlay depth, and all designs showed clinically acceptable marginal and internal fit.

P2901.t: Influence of Cementation Mode and Ferrule Design on the Fatigue Resistance of Monolithic Zirconia Endocrowns
P2901.kf: In vitro step-stress test (up to 1500 N) of CEREC zirconia endocrowns on 80 human molars (n = 20 per group): 88.8% passed, with no significant differences in fatigue resistance by ferrule design or cementation mode.

P2902.t: Effect of Preparation Design on Marginal Integrity and Fracture Resistance of Endocrowns: A Systematic Review
P2902.kf: Systematic review of 10 in vitro studies: endocrown marginal discrepancy increased with added preparation features, greater cavity depth and divergence, while fracture resistance increased with more occlusal reduction and cavity depth; meta-analysis was not possible.

P2903.t: Effect of scanning strategies on the accuracy of digital intraoral scanners: a meta-analysis of in vitro studies
P2903.kf: Meta-analysis of 15 in vitro studies: intraoral scan accuracy improved significantly under dry conditions (P < 0.001), with artificial landmarks (P ≤ 0.02) and an S-shaped pattern (P ≤ 0.01), while light type had no significant impact (P ≥ 0.16).

P2904.t: The Endocrown: A Different Type of All-Ceramic Reconstruction for Molars
P2904.j: Journal of the Canadian Dental Association
P2904.kf: Narrative description of the molar endocrown: a monolithic ceramic adhesive restoration with a butt-joint cervical margin and pulp-chamber preparation not extending into the root canals, leaving more robust remaining tooth substance.

P2905.t: Management of Grossly Decayed Mandibular Molar with Different Designs of Split Cast Post and Core
P2905.kf: Case report describing management of a grossly decayed mandibular molar with divergent roots using a multisection (split) cast post and core or a single cast post and core with an auxiliary post.

P2906.t: Effect of implant-supported or retained dentures on masticatory performance: A systematic review
P2906.kf: Systematic review of 18 articles: a mandibular implant overdenture with a maxillary complete denture significantly improved masticatory performance versus complete dentures in resorbed mandibles, whereas fixed implant partial dentures did not significantly outperform removable partial dentures for Kennedy Class I and …

P2907.kf: Systematic review of 41 publications (8 clinical, 33 in vitro; 1995–2018) concluding that endocrowns are a reliable alternative to post-retained restorations for molars and seem promising for premolars, with lithium disilicate and nanofilled composite resin standing out.

P2908.t: An investigation into the prevalence of combination syndrome
P2908.kf: Cross-sectional examination of 99 patients with maxillary complete dentures opposing mandibular anterior teeth (64 with mandibular RPDs): only 8 showed two features and 38 one feature (excessive anterior maxillary resorption) of Combination Syndrome.

P2909.t: Effect of different fiber post surface treatments on microtensile bond strength to composite resin
P2909.kf: In vitro microtensile study of glass fiber posts (10 groups, n=14): silanization had a significant effect on bond strength to composite resin, highest with 5-minute phosphoric acid plus silane, whereas 30% hydrogen peroxide or 35% phosphoric acid had no significant effect.

P2910.t: Rubber dam isolation for restorative treatment in dental patients
P2910.kf: Cochrane review of six RCTs (1342 participants, all at high risk of bias): pooled data from two studies (192 participants) suggested rubber dam may increase six-month survival of direct composite restorations of non-carious cervical lesions (OR 2.29, 95% CI 1.05 to 4.99).

P2911.t: Influence of enamel preservation on failure rates of porcelain laminate veneers
P2911.j: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
P2911.kf: Retrospective survey of 580 porcelain laminate veneers in 66 patients over up to 12 years: 42 (7.2%) failed with 86% cumulative survival; veneers bonded to dentin or with dentin margins were approximately 10 times more likely to fail, and crown lengthening raised risk 2.3 times.

P2912.t: What is the influence of the operator on the long-term survival of posterior partial lithium disilicate restorations in an undergraduate setting?
P2912.kf: Retrospective analysis of 637 posterior partial lithium disilicate restorations in 373 patients placed by undergraduates (median follow-up 70 months): 5- and 10-year survival were 89.1% and 77.6%; medium-to-high caries risk (HR 1.57) and approximal outline within 3 mm of bone (HR 1.52) predicted failure, academic year …

P2913.t: Influence of intraoral temperature and relative humidity on the dentin bond strength: an in situ study
