P2913.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2913.kf: In situ study of dentin fragments from 60 molars bonded at incisor and molar intraoral sites: the posterior site showed higher temperature and humidity, but the intraoral environment did not affect immediate microtensile bond strength of two etch-and-rinse adhesives.

P2914.t: Effect of blood decontamination methods on dentin bond strength across adhesive systems: a systematic review
P2914.kf: Systematic review of 15 in vitro studies (1,015 teeth): blood contamination consistently reduced dentin bond strength, most severely after adhesive polymerization; adhesive reapplication, phosphoric acid re-etching and sodium hypochlorite with antioxidants were most promising, but full recovery was not reliably …

P2915.t: Effect of contamination and decontamination methods on the bond strength of adhesive systems to dentin: A systematic review
P2915.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2915.kf: Systematic review of 62 in vitro articles: any blood or saliva contamination impaired resin bond strength to dentin; water-spray and reapplication of the bonding system could revert the impairment, whereas hemostatic agents are not recommended for blood decontamination.

P2916.t: Evaluation of different surface treatments on fiber post cemented with a self-adhesive system
P2916.kf: In vitro push-out test of 60 fiberglass posts with RelyX U200 (n = 10): silane (15.94 ± 6.5), blasting (13.13 ± 3.6), NH3 plasma (14.44 ± 4.0) and HMDSO plasma (13.23± 5.3) gave higher bond strength than control (9.65 ± 3.6), whereas 24% H2O2 did not.

P2917.t: Should the restoration of adjacent implants be splinted or nonsplinted? A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2917.kf: Meta-analysis of 19 studies (4215 implants, 2185 patients; mean follow-up 87.8 months): splinted and nonsplinted restorations did not differ significantly in marginal bone loss or prosthetic complications, but splinted implants had significantly higher survival (99.1% vs 96.5%).

P2918.t: The influence of prosthetic designs on peri-implant bone loss: An AO/AAP systematic review and meta-analysis
P2918.kf: AO/AAP meta-analysis: platform switching, internal (especially conical) connections, abutment heights ≥2 mm, one abutment-one time and nonsplinted implants were associated with less marginal bone loss, while screw- vs cement-retention (p = 0.51) and crown-to-implant ratio (p = 0.32) showed no difference.

P2919.t: Under pressure: Unraveling the impact of occlusal overload on peri-implant health–A systematic review
P2919.kf: Systematic review of 80 studies (2000–2023): marginal bone loss associated with occlusal factors ranged from approximately 0.65 mm to 1.20 mm, while traumatic occlusal forces produced 1.0 mm to 3.0 mm bone changes and peri-implantitis rates of 20% to 50%.

P2920.t: Clinical Outcomes of Pterygoid and Maxillary Tuberosity Implants: A Systematic Review
P2920.kf: Systematic review of 38 studies (3446 implants: 3053 pterygoid, 393 tuberosity; mean follow-up 61.0 months): 10-year cumulative survival was 92.5% for pterygoid and 96.9% for tuberosity implants, with failures concentrated in the first year; immediately loaded and splinted implants survived better.

P2921.t: Combine Conventional and Digital Methods to Maximize Shade Matching
P2921.j: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
P2921.kf: Narrative practical review of shade-taking methods (classical and 3D shade guides, digital photography, spectrophotometers). The authors report that using all three modalities together reduced shade remakes by 80% at their UCLA center, and conclude the tri-modality approach is the most accurate way to determine and …

P2924.t: Guide to Optimizing the Accuracy of Intraoral Implant Scans: A Review Article
P2924.kf: Review summarizing that operator experience, scanning distance, scanner head size, inter-implant distance, scanned area (full/half arch), implant depth and saliva or blood significantly affect accuracy of intraoral implant scans, though no optimum condition could be determined.

P2925.t: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity
P2925.kf: Phase 3 double-blind RCT of 2539 adults with obesity (excluding diabetes) over 72 weeks: mean weight change was -15.0%, -19.5% and -20.9% with tirzepatide 5, 10 and 15 mg versus -3.1% with placebo (P<0.001); adverse events were mainly gastrointestinal.

P2926.t: In Vitro Evaluation of the Retention of Zirconia-Based Ceramic Posts Luted with Glass Ionomer and Resin Cements
P2926.kf: In vitro tensile test of CosmoPost zirconia posts in 32 endodontically treated teeth (n=16): posts luted with resin cement (Variolink II, 228.1 ±36.8 N) resisted dislodgement significantly better than with glass ionomer (Fuji I, 121.8 ±17.4 N; p<0.05), failing adhesively at the cement/post interface.

P2927.t: Influence of Conventional Polymer, Hybrid Polymer and Zinc Phosphate Luting Agents on the Bond Strength of Customized Zirconia Post in Premolars - An In-Vitro Evaluation
P2927.kf: In vitro pull-out test of milled customized zirconia posts in 60 premolars: resin cement gave the highest bond strength (69.89 ± 4.81 non-thermocycled; 64.06 ± 4.36 thermocycled) and zinc phosphate the lowest (43.66 ± 5.02; 37.70 ± 5.10), and thermocycling reduced bonding.

P2928.t: Association between mandibular torus and parafunctional activity: A case control study
P2928.j: Journal of Stomatology, Occlusion and Medicine
P2928.kf: Case-control study of 100 individuals with mandibular torus and 100 age- and gender-matched controls: patients with bruxism were 4 times more likely to have mandibular torus, wear facets increased the risk 20 times, and both correlated with torus size.

P2929.t: Ultrasound analysis of the masseter and anterior temporalis muscles in edentulous patients rehabilitated with full-arch fixed implant-supported prostheses
P2929.kf: Prospective controlled study of 30 edentulous patients receiving full-arch fixed implant prostheses and 30 dentate controls: masseter and anterior temporalis thickness increased significantly at 1 and 6 months, asymmetry decreased, and differences from dentate controls were not significant at six months.

P2930.t: Electromyographic Evaluation of Muscle Activity in Patients Rehabilitated with Full Arch Fixed Implant-Supported Prostheses
P2930.kf: Study of 63 patients (30 edentulous receiving 204 immediately loaded implants with fixed provisional prostheses, plus dentate controls): surface EMG during clenching and mastication did not differ between groups, nor within the study group after 6 months.

P2931.t: Bruxism and dental implants: A systematic review and meta-analysis
P2931.kf: Meta-analysis of 27 studies (2105 implants in probable bruxers, 10,264 in non-bruxers): implants in probable bruxers had higher failure risk (OR 2.189; 95% CI 1.337, 3.583, p = .002), unaffected by follow-up time; marginal bone loss could not be analyzed.

P2932.t: Bruxism in implant-supported rehabilitations: a narrative review of clinical complications and management strategies
P2932.kf: Narrative review reporting that systematic reviews show a 2.2-4.7 fold increased implant failure risk in bruxers, finite element analyses show occlusal splints reduce stress concentration by 33-73%, and evidence linking bruxism to peri-implant bone loss is limited.

P2933.t: Sleep bruxism in individuals with and without attrition-type tooth wear: An exploratory matched case-control electromyographic study
P2933.kf: Exploratory matched case-control study of 16 individuals with pronounced attrition-type wear versus controls, with EMG over at least four nights: self- and partner-reported sleep bruxism were more common with attrition, but no jaw-muscle EMG measure differed significantly (P > 0.05).

P2934.t: European Academy of Neurology guideline on trigeminal neuralgia
P2934.kf: European Academy of Neurology guideline based on systematic review and GRADE: recommends the current TN classification, MRI with three high-resolution sequences, carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine as first-choice drugs, and microvascular decompression as first-line surgery in classical TN.

P2935.t: AAN-EFNS guidelines on trigeminal neuralgia management
P2935.kf: AAN-EFNS guideline based on systematic review: carbamazepine (stronger evidence) or oxcarbazepine (better tolerability) should be offered first-line; early surgery may be considered for refractory TN, with microvascular decompression possibly giving the longest pain freedom.

P2936.kf: Practical review recommending new TN diagnostic criteria, MRI with high-resolution trigeminal sequences, carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine as first-choice drugs, and microvascular decompression as first-line surgery when trigeminal neurovascular conflict is present.

P2937.t: Guidelines for the management of trigeminal neuralgia
P2937.kf: Summary of trigeminal neuralgia guidelines advocating a multidisciplinary team approach, care pathways for prompt diagnosis and treatment, long-term outcome data collection, and summary materials for patients.

P2938.t: Guidelines for the management of trigeminal neuralgia 2021
P2938.j: Faculty of Dental Surgery, Royal College of Surgeons of England
P2938.kf: Multidisciplinary UK guideline (modified Delphi, at least 90% approval) built from existing guidelines. Carbamazepine is first line (NNT 2; RR 5.87, 95% CI 3.58 to 9.61), oxcarbazepine the alternative; MR imaging is advised; MVD is strongly recommended ahead of stereotactic radiosurgery when neurovascular compression …

P2939.t: A randomized trial of Citanest with Octapressin for relief of pain associated with laser vaporization of the cervix
P2939.j: British Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
P2939.kf: Randomized trial of 50 women undergoing laser vaporization of the cervix: infiltration with 2 ml Citanest with Octapressin significantly reduced pain on the visual analogue scale versus no anaesthesia (P = 0.011), not quite significant on the verbal rating scale (P = 0.06).

P2940.t: Review of the Safety and Clinical Considerations of Vasoconstrictor Agents in Dental Anesthesia During Pregnancy
P2940.kf: PRISMA-based PubMed review (2000–2025) including six narrative reviews and three guidelines: epinephrine at low dental doses (1:100,000-1:200,000) was generally regarded as safe in pregnancy, levonordefrin lacked safety data, and felypressin was contraindicated due to oxytocic properties.

P2941.t: Oral Health Care During Pregnancy - A National Consensus Statement (rev. ed. 2026)
P2941.j: National Maternal and Child Oral Health Resource Center, Georgetown University
P2941.kf: National consensus statement from an expert workgroup meeting (October 18, 2011; revised edition 2026) stating that preventive, diagnostic and restorative dental treatment is safe throughout pregnancy, including radiographs, pain medication and local anesthesia, and that prenatal and oral health professionals should …

P2942.t: Conventional and Basal Implantology: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence, Clinical Decision-Making, and Future Perspectives
P2942.kf: The review concludes that current evidence is insufficient to recommend basal implants over conventional implants; it calls for long-term comparative studies and standardized outcomes.

P2943.t: Properties of 3D printed resins for definitive dental restorations: A systematic review
P2943.kf: Forty-two in-vitro studies evaluated seven definitive 3D-printed resins; overall mechanical and optical performance remained inferior to CAD-CAM composite resin blocks.

P2944.t: Clinical Evaluation of Zirconia Occlusal Veneer Fixed Partial Denture: A New Design for Posterior Resin-Bonded Fixed Partial Dentures (RBFPDs)
P2944.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2944.kf: Forty posterior zirconia occlusal-veneer FPDs were evaluated for 18 months; no debonding or recurrent caries occurred. Two complete fractures and one crack occurred in 5Y groups; differences were not statistically significant.

P2945.t: Veneer-retained Fixed Dental Prosthesis: A Clinical Report on Three Cases with Up to 5 Years Follow-up and Literature Review
P2945.j: Journal of Dentomaxillofacial Radiology, Pathology and Surgery
P2945.kf: Three patients received four lithium-disilicate veneer-retained fixed dental prostheses, with follow-up reported up to five years and no mechanical or biological complications. A literature review included seven earlier reports.

P2946.t: Managing Fractured Ceramic Restorations: Current Evidence and Best Practices—A Scoping Review
P2946.j: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
P2946.kf: 126 studies (119 in vitro, 7 reviews) on ceramic restoration repair were mapped; bond strength was the most frequently evaluated outcome and methodology was heterogeneous.

P2947.t: Partial time use of anterior repositioning splints in the management of TMJ pain and dysfunction: a one-year controlled study
P2947.kf: In 52 patients with painful disc displacement with reduction, nighttime repositioning splints (converted to stabilization splints after 3–4 months) reduced pain significantly earlier (from 15 days) than stabilization splints or no treatment; by 6 months and 1 year the groups no longer differed.

P2948.t: Impact of lateral occlusion schemes: A systematic review
P2948.kf: Across 26 studies, CGO was associated with narrower chewing and less masticatory-muscle EMG activity during clenching, GFO with wider mandibular movement and quicker chewing; during chewing EMG did not differ, and long-term studies showed no difference between the two schemes in patient comfort or restoration …
